f: Find her hands: they rest calmly, one on top of the other, on the arm of the chair.
Look behind her shoulders and find the far mountains, the water and a little bridge.

m.q: What mood is Mona Lisa in?
m.w: The corners of her lips are lifted just a little, and her look is quiet and kind. She sits relaxed, in no hurry.

x.q: How did Leonardo make the shadows on her face as soft as mist?
x.w: He painted one thin, see-through layer after another, so you cannot see where light turns into shadow. This is called sfumato.

Q12418.s: Leonardo worked on this portrait for many years and even took it with him to France. Today it lives in the Louvre, in Paris.
Q12418.i: Imagine: what would Mona Lisa whisper to you if you came a little closer?

f: Find the orange sun above the sea: it is small, but it is the brightest spot.
Find the orange glints on the water and the dark boats drifting in the haze.

m.q: What is the mood of this morning?
m.w: Everything is wrapped in grey-blue mist, the water is calm and the sun rises slowly.

x.q: Which colour helps the sun shine against the grey?
x.w: Warm orange sits next to cool grey-blue, so the sun seems to glow.

Q328523.s: A critic laughed at the title of this picture, and the word ‘Impressionists’ stuck to Monet and his friends. Monet painted fast to catch one moment.
Q328523.i: Imagine: what is the fisherman in the boat thinking as the sun comes up?

f: Find the thin stream of milk pouring from the jug.
Find the bread and the basket on the table: little bright dots shine on the crusts.

m.q: What is the girl feeling?
m.w: She looks down at the jug and her shoulders are relaxed. The room is quiet and warm.

x.q: Where does the soft light come from?
o: From the window on the left
From a candle on the table
x.w: The light comes from the window on the left. It lights her face, the bread and the wall.

Q167605.s: Vermeer painted tiny bright dots on the bread, so the crust looks crunchy. An ordinary minute in the kitchen becomes magical.
Q167605.i: Imagine: what will the girl make with the bread and the milk?

f: Find the big yellow lamp above the café terrace.
Find the stars in the dark blue sky: they look like flowers.

m.q: What is the mood of the night street?
m.w: Yellow light spills over the tables and the paving stones, and above it the blue sky is calm.

x.q: Which pair of colours makes the picture so bright?
x.w: Warm yellow light next to deep blue night: each colour makes its neighbour shine.

Q1025704.s: Van Gogh painted this in Arles, at night, right out in the street. He was proud that he used no black paint at all.
Q1025704.i: Imagine: what are the people at the tables talking about?

f: Find the man banging his head against a brick wall.
Find the man throwing roses to the pigs.

m.q: What is the mood of this picture?
m.w: People do ridiculous things and hardly anyone notices how funny it is.

x.q: What did Brueghel hide in this picture?
x.w: Every little scene is a proverb that people in the Netherlands knew. ‘Banging your head against a wall’ means stubbornly trying the impossible.

Q533619.s: People back then spotted the proverbs at once, the way we spot riddles. Some of them are still used today.
Q533619.i: Invent your own proverb and draw it word for word, like Brueghel.

f: Find the yellow house with green shutters.
Find the train far away, puffing smoke.

m.q: What is the mood of this street?
m.w: The walls glow yellow, the sky is deep blue and everything is full of sun.

x.q: Why did Van Gogh rent this house in Arles?
o: To open a bakery in it
To live there and invite painters
To start a dance school there
x.w: He dreamed of a house for his painter friends. Soon the painter Paul Gauguin came to stay.

Q2200610.s: Van Gogh used thick, bright strokes of paint, so everything in his pictures seems to glow.
Q2200610.i: Imagine: who lives in the rooms of the yellow house, and what are they doing?

f: Find the thin band on her forehead with a tiny jewel in the middle.
Find her red dress and the dark background behind her.

m.q: What is the lady’s face like?
m.w: Her lips are closed and her look is attentive, with no smile. She sits straight and proud.

x.q: Why is the jewelled band on the forehead called a ‘ferronnière’?
o: It is named after this picture
It was a fashionable queen's name
x.w: The picture was later called La Belle Ferronnière, and the thin band with a jewel was named after it.

Q656434.s: Leonardo painted faces very softly, almost without hard lines. That is why the lady on the dark background looks alive.
Q656434.i: Give the lady a name and tell us what she is thinking about.

f: Find the globe of the stars that the scholar is touching.
Find the open book and the carpet on the table.

m.q: What is the scholar feeling?
m.w: He leans toward the globe and reaches out to it. Light falls on his face, as if he is about to understand something.

x.q: What is painted in the small picture on the wall?
o: A portrait of a king in a crown
x.w: It is a picture inside the picture: baby Moses by the Nile. Vermeer liked to hide little stories like this.

Q544315.s: Vermeer mostly painted women, but here it is a scholar. The picture has a partner, The Geographer, and it seems to show the same man.
Q544315.i: Imagine: what discovery did the scholar make while looking at the stars?

f: Find the woman sewing by the door.
Find the two children playing on the pavement.

m.q: What is the mood of this little street in Delft?
m.w: Everyone is busy with quiet jobs, the walls are warm and the clouds are soft.

x.q: Which street did Vermeer paint?
o: A street in his town, Delft
x.w: Historians think this is a real street in Delft, where Vermeer lived. People even tried to find the house from old records.

Q586035.s: Vermeer painted only two views of a town: this one and View of Delft. He painted bricks and plaster so well that you see every little crack.
Q586035.i: Imagine: what game are the children playing, and what will the woman say?

f: On the left, in the shade, find the painter himself beside a big canvas.
Find the lady who has turned away and does not show her face.

m.q: What are the royal faces like?
m.w: They stand straight, look at us and hold themselves very proudly. Their shiny medals make them look important.

x.q: Whose idea did Goya copy by painting himself next to the royal family?
o: Leonardo, who painted the Mona Lisa
x.w: In Las Meninas Velázquez also painted himself in his studio beside the royal family. Goya admired Velázquez.

Q920030.s: Goya painted silk, ribbons and medals so they sparkle like real ones. He placed himself in the shadow, like a modest guest.
Q920030.i: Imagine: what is the smallest child thinking while everybody poses?

f: Find the woman in the hat: she is staring into space.
Find the man with the pipe sitting beside her, looking the other way.

m.q: What are the two of them feeling?
o: They are cross with each other
Each is sad, lost in thought
m.w: They sit side by side but look in different directions, with drooping shoulders. It feels like there is a gap between them.

x.q: How did Degas show that people feel alone even when sitting together?
o: They do not look at each other
They stand with their backs to us
x.w: The figures are pushed toward the edge and there is a lot of empty space next to them. So each one seems to be on their own.

Q1239950.s: Degas liked to paint as if he had caught a scene by chance, like a snapshot. He asked two friends, an actress and a painter, to pose.
Q1239950.i: Imagine: what is this woman silent about?

f: Find the grapes in the young man’s hand.
Find the wreath of leaves on his head and the fruit on the table.

m.q: How does this young man look?
m.w: His skin and lips look a little green, and his eyes are tired. That is why the picture is called Sick Bacchus.

x.q: Whom did Caravaggio paint as the god Bacchus?
x.w: It is a self-portrait: the painter showed himself as the god of grapes and parties. They say he was ill at the time.

Q2293936.s: Caravaggio painted fruit and grapes so exactly that you almost want to eat them. Later he became famous for strong light, like a spotlight in a dark room.
Q2293936.i: Imagine: which party is pale Bacchus going to, and what does he need to feel better?

f: Find the girl’s shiny silk dress: how many folds can you count?
Find the young man’s foot on the step of the stairs.

m.q: What do the young man and the girl feel before parting?
m.w: They hug tightly, but his foot is already on the step. It seems he is about to leave.

x.q: What did many Italians see in this picture?
o: A harvest festival in a village
x.w: It was painted in 1859, when Italy was fighting for freedom. To many, the lovers’ goodbye recalled those who left to fight for their country.

Q1195035.s: Hayez lived and worked in Milan, and this picture hangs there in the Brera gallery. He painted the silk so well that you can see its shine.
Q1195035.i: Imagine: where is the young man going, and when will he come back?

f: Find the bright green railing and shutters.
Peer into the dark room and find the boy in the shadow.

m.q: What is the mood of the people on the balcony?
m.w: They look in different directions and hardly notice each other. Each is busy with their own thoughts.

x.q: Who are the people in the picture?
o: The family of a rich neighbour
Actors from a famous Paris theatre
x.w: Manet asked his friends to pose. The lady seated on the left is the painter Berthe Morisot.

Q775407.s: Manet was inspired by Goya’s painting Majas on a Balcony. He boldly put bright green next to a dark room.
Q775407.i: Imagine: what did they see in the street, and why are they looking in different directions?

f: Find the people trying to bite a pancake hanging on a string.
Find the roast bird tied to the tree that grows instead of a mast.

m.q: What is the mood of the people in the boat?
o: Everyone is scared of a storm
m.w: They sing, eat and stretch their mouths up to the pancake. The boat drifts with no aim, and they do not care.

x.q: What does this boat have instead of a mast?
o: A tall flagpole with a flag
A long oar with a handle
x.w: A tree grows where the mast should be. It is a joke: the boat is built all wrong, just like the thinking of those on board.

Q405814.s: Bosch painted funny, strange scenes with a serious meaning. He wanted people to laugh and also think about their mistakes.
Q405814.i: Imagine: where is this boat sailing, and who is the captain?

f: On the right, find the man in a yellow cloak looking straight at us.
Find Mary and the baby in the centre, with an old ruin and a roof above them.

m.q: What is the mood of the people around the baby?
m.w: The wise men bow and kneel, and everyone else is looking at the baby.

x.q: Whom did Botticelli paint as the Wise Men?
o: Members of the rich Medici family
x.w: They were friends and relatives of the Medici, who ruled Florence. It looks like a family portrait inside a Bible story.

Q488825.s: Botticelli painted himself at the edge: he looks at us, as if inviting us into the picture.
Q488825.i: Imagine: what gift would you bring to the baby?

f: Find the lion lying at the saint’s feet.
Find the places where the picture is only drawn in brown and not painted.

m.q: What is Saint Jerome feeling?
o: He is cross with the lion
m.w: He kneels with his head bowed. His thin body is all focused.

x.q: Why does the picture look unfinished?
x.w: Leonardo left it unfinished. So we can see how he began: first a drawing in brown paint, then the colours.

Q972196.s: A legend says the lion became Jerome’s friend when the saint pulled a thorn from its paw. The picture was once even cut into pieces, but they were joined again.
Q972196.i: Imagine: what does the lion want to tell the saint?

f: Find the thin, see-through veil on her head.
Find her hands clasped together at the bottom of the picture.

m.q: What is this lady’s mood?
m.w: Her eyes are lowered, her lips closed and her hands folded. She seems gentle and serious.

x.q: How did the painter show that the veil is light?
o: With a plain grey stripe of paint
With tiny folds in thin cloth
He glued on a piece of real cloth
x.w: Rogier used a fine brush to paint tiny folds, so the cloth looks light and see-through.

Q2439462.s: Rogier van der Weyden painted in thin layers of oil paint. People in his portraits look quiet, real and alive.
Q2439462.i: Give this lady a name and say what she is thinking, with her eyes lowered.

f: Find the three people at the table in the dark room.
Find the bread and the plain food on the table.

m.q: What is the mood of this lunch?
o: A scary wait in the night
m.w: The room is dark, and the table holds plain food, no golden dishes. The people sit together and eat.

x.q: How old was Velázquez when he painted this?
x.w: Velázquez was born in 1599 and painted this at around eighteen, still in his home city of Seville.

Q2535473.s: As a teenager Velázquez loved painting plain food and ordinary people, very close and very true. Such pictures are called bodegones.
Q2535473.i: Imagine: what are the three at the table talking about?

f: Find the angel floating over Matthew, who seems to count on his fingers.
Find Matthew’s stool: one leg sticks out over the edge, right toward you.

m.q: What is Matthew’s face like?
m.w: His eyebrows are raised and his forehead wrinkled: he listens to the angel and writes. It seems he heard something important.

x.q: What does the light do in this picture?
o: Comes from a candle on the writing desk
x.w: Light falls from the side like a spotlight in a dark room. The rest sinks into shadow. That is how Caravaggio leads your eye.

Q2337873.s: Caravaggio first painted a different version, but the people who ordered it did not like it. They accepted this second one.
Q2337873.i: Imagine: what did the angel whisper to Matthew?

f: Find Mary: she sits in the meadow and bends toward the two children.
Find the soft hills and the blue distance behind her.

m.q: What can you feel in this group on the meadow?
m.w: Mary bends toward the children and looks at them kindly. The three figures nestle close together.

x.q: What shape do Mary and the children make together?
x.w: Mary’s head is at the top and the children are below, so the group forms a calm, steady triangle.

Q2343778.s: Raphael painted Mary with the baby many times and always gave the faces a soft, kind look. People loved him for his clarity and calm.
Q2343778.i: Imagine: what words does Mary whisper to the children?

f: Find Saint George in his shiny armour.
Find the carpet in front of Mary’s throne.

m.q: What is the old canon feeling?
m.w: He sits with a calm, serious face, and Saint George, his protector, stands beside him.

x.q: What does Canon van der Paele hold in his hands?
o: A sword and a heavy shield
x.w: The spectacles show that he is old. Van Eyck painted his wrinkles exactly as they were.

Q2480921.s: Van Eyck painted in thin layers of oil paint. So his metal shines, his cloth looks soft, and the wrinkles look like a real person’s.
Q2480921.i: Imagine: what does Mary kindly say to the old canon?

f: Find the girl in the red dress holding the glass.
Find the window with coloured panes.

m.q: What is the mood in this room?
m.w: The red dress is bright, the light is soft and the man leans toward the girl. It feels like a friendly chat.

x.q: What is special about the window?
o: It has heavy dark wooden shutters
It is filled with coloured glass
It is round like a porthole
x.w: In rich Dutch houses, windows had coloured glass with pictures. Vermeer painted its sparkle.

Q1169874.s: Vermeer loved light from a window on cloth and glass. His scenes look frozen for a second.
Q1169874.i: Imagine: what did the man whisper to the girl?

f: Find the man sitting on a stone with his hands tightly clasped.
Find the pale dawn sky behind him.

m.q: What is this man feeling?
m.w: He sits very still, his fingers clenched, his eyes fixed far away. Around him there are only cold stones.

x.q: Where and when does this happen?
o: In a shady garden at midday
On a ship in the dark of night
In a stony desert at dawn
x.w: The grey stones, cold sky and emptiness show that he is quite alone, with nobody near.

Q2354080.s: Kramskoi was one of the ‘Wanderers’, painters who took their exhibitions around Russian towns. He wanted people to see Christ as a person making a hard choice.
Q2354080.i: Imagine: what is he thinking about at dawn?

f: Find the two girls in pretty hats on the terrace.
Find the bright red and orange strokes: they make the picture warm.

m.q: What is the mood of a summer day on the terrace?
m.w: The girls sit close together, the colours are warm and the strokes are soft. Everything looks calm and pleasant.

x.q: How did Renoir show warm summer air?
o: With soft strokes and warm colours
With one grey paint, no colour
x.w: He used short, soft strokes and loved warm colours, so the picture seems to shimmer in sunny air.

Q630121.s: Renoir said pictures should be pretty, because the world already has enough unpleasant things. He loved to paint joy.
Q630121.i: Imagine: what are the two sisters whispering about on the terrace?

f: Find the people carefully carrying Jesus.
Find the places where the picture is only a sketch, without colours.

m.q: What are these people feeling?
m.w: They bend down and carry the body quietly and carefully. Their movements are slow and caring.

x.q: Why are there bare sketches without colours on the picture?
o: Sea water washed some of it away
The paint flaked off long ago
x.w: The master left it unfinished, so we can see how he began: first a drawing, then the colours.

Q1213160.s: Michelangelo loved sculpture best of all, so the people in his paintings look strong, as if carved from stone.
Q1213160.i: Imagine what else should be painted in the empty spot to finish the picture.

f: Find the blossoming almond branches against the blue sky.
Find the white and pink flowers: they look like little stars.

m.q: What feeling do these branches give?
m.w: The sky is bright, the flowers pale and the branches reach upward. It feels like spring is coming.

x.q: For whom did Van Gogh paint this picture?
o: For a school in a nearby town
For the king of a country
x.w: Van Gogh’s brother Theo had a baby son named Vincent. The painter made the blossoming branches as a gift for the baby.

Q1432536.s: Almond trees blossom among the first, at the very start of spring, a sign of new life. Van Gogh painted the branches big, like the Japanese prints he loved.
Q1432536.i: Make up a lullaby for the baby who was given this picture.

f: Find the book in Mary’s hand.
Find the far mountains behind her.

m.q: What is Mary feeling?
m.w: She bows her head, looks down at the baby and holds him carefully. Everything about her is calm.

x.q: What shape is this picture?
x.w: A round picture like this is called a tondo. Raphael fitted Mary and the baby into the circle so they look like one whole.

Q919294.s: Raphael painted it very young, at about twenty. It came to Russia and now hangs in the Hermitage in Saint Petersburg. It was moved from wood onto canvas.
Q919294.i: Imagine: which page is Mary reading, and what does the baby want to ask?

f: Find the two women who are fighting.
Find the man who watches the duel.

m.q: What can you feel in this duel scene?
m.w: The background is dark, the poses are sharp and everyone waits to see how the fight ends.

x.q: How did Ribera make the scene so tense?
o: Sharp light and a dark background
x.w: Bright light picks the figures out of the dark and the poses are sharp. It feels like something is about to happen.

Q3716086.s: Ribera was born in Spain but lived in Naples. He loved deep shadows and bright light, like Caravaggio.
Q3716086.i: Imagine: what started this duel, and who will win?

f: Find the soft grey beard and moustache on his face.
Find his big black beret and dark clothes.

m.q: What is this man’s face like?
m.w: His look is soft and clear and his face is calm. You can tell he is a kind and thoughtful man.

x.q: Who was Baldassare Castiglione?
o: A cook in a royal kitchen
A king of a far country
x.w: Castiglione was Raphael’s friend and wrote a famous book, The Courtier, about how to behave gracefully and politely.

Q546977.s: Raphael used very few colours, grey, brown and black, and the face comes alive. Later Rembrandt saw this painting and made a drawing of it.
Q546977.i: Imagine: what advice on good manners would he give you?

f: Find her long braid tied with a ribbon.
Find the fine patterns of interlaced lines on her dress.

m.q: What is the face of the girl in profile like?
m.w: She looks to the side, her face calm and without a smile. Her profile is clean and delicate.

x.q: What is this portrait drawn on?
o: On a big wall, in paint
On a wooden board, in oil
x.w: It is a drawing on parchment, in chalks and pen. The portrait is quite small.

Q2072801.s: This portrait was noticed only in our own time, and experts still argue whether Leonardo drew it. Many think he did.
Q2072801.i: Imagine what she is thinking about as she looks to the side.

f: Find the far bluish mountains behind the god.
Find the deer in the landscape.

m.q: What is the god’s mood?
m.w: He sits relaxed with a soft look. Nothing about him is hurried or worried.

x.q: Who was the young man in this picture at first?
o: A sailor from a big ship
x.w: At first the picture showed Saint John the Baptist, and later it was changed into the god Bacchus.

Q798034.s: Francesco Melzi was Leonardo’s pupil and friend. Leonardo’s followers learned to paint soft shadows like their master, a way called sfumato.
Q798034.i: Imagine: what party did Bacchus throw in these mountains?

f: Find the girl standing at the keyboard instrument, looking straight at us.
Find the picture of little Cupid on the wall.

m.q: What is the girl’s face like?
m.w: She has paused her music and calmly looks at the viewer. It is as if she waits to hear what you will say.

x.q: What is a virginal?
o: A wind instrument with a pipe
A string instrument with a bow
x.w: A virginal is a small keyboard instrument, a relative of the harpsichord. Its sound is gentle and delicate.

Q2624258.s: Vermeer painted very few pictures: about thirty-five are known. That is why each one is so precious.
Q2624258.i: Imagine: what tune will she play when she turns back to the instrument?

f: Find the high throne where Mary sits.
Find baby Jesus snuggled close to his mother.

m.q: What can you feel in the room where the mother holds her baby?
m.w: Mary holds the baby close, safe and tender. The room is quiet and warm.

x.q: Why is the painting called the Lucca Madonna?
o: It belonged to the Duke of Lucca
x.w: The painting belonged for a long time to the Duke of Lucca, and that gave it its name.

Q474409.s: Van Eyck painted in thin layers of oil paint, so his colours are deep and shining. He was one of the first great masters of oil painting.
Q474409.i: Imagine what baby Jesus wants to tell his mother.

f: Find Moses: he holds the stone tablets above his head.
Find his long grey beard and the light on his face.

m.q: What is Moses feeling?
m.w: He lifts the heavy tablets, his brows are drawn together and his face is in shadow. He has seen something that upsets him a lot.

x.q: What is written on the stone tablets?
o: A map of the desert with wells
x.w: The tablets hold the Ten Commandments, the main rules for life. In the story, Moses was so upset that he wanted to smash them.

Q325267.s: Rembrandt loved strong contrast of light and shadow: Moses’ face glows while everything around sinks into darkness.
Q325267.i: Imagine how Moses will explain to the people what happened.

f: Find Wally’s face against the plain light background.
Look at the lines: they are thin and sharp, as if drawn with a sharpened pencil.

m.q: What is Wally’s face like?
m.w: Her look is quiet and her lips are closed. She seems to be thinking of something far away.

x.q: How are Schiele’s pictures different from others?
o: Soft mist with no sharp lines
A mosaic of tiny coloured dots
x.w: Schiele loved a sharp, nervous line and unusual poses. That is how he showed a person’s feelings.

Q1555137.s: The famous Viennese painter Gustav Klimt supported young Schiele. Schiele painted many portraits where feelings show in the lines.
Q1555137.i: Imagine what Wally is thinking about.

f: Find the prickly flower in his hand: it is a thistle.
Find his cap and his long wavy hair.

m.q: What is the young painter’s face like?
m.w: He gazes into the distance, his brows are calm and his lips closed. You can see the young man is thinking about something.

x.q: For whom is it thought Dürer painted this portrait?
o: For a king in a castle
x.w: People think the portrait was sent to his bride, Agnes. The prickly flower may have meant faithfulness.

Q2428778.s: Dürer drew himself when he was only thirteen. This portrait is one of the earliest self-portraits painted in oil in northern Europe.
Q2428778.i: Imagine what he would tell his bride about the prickly flower.

f: Find baby Jesus in Mary’s arms.
Find the quiet landscape with hills behind them.

m.q: What does Mary feel, holding the baby in her arms?
m.w: She holds the baby carefully and looks at him with love. Everything around is calm.

x.q: Why is the painting called the Small Cowper Madonna?
o: The Madonna was called Lady Cowper
x.w: There were two pictures, both owned by Lord Cowper in England: a large one and a small one. This is the small one.

Q2607050.s: As a young man Raphael painted many Madonnas with babies. He gave faces a soft, kind look, and people loved him for it.
Q2607050.i: Imagine what baby Jesus wants to reach with his hand.

f: Find the woman in the striped dress washing the child.
Find the jug and the basin of water.

m.q: What is the woman’s mood?
m.w: She holds the child gently and both look at the little foot in the water. Everything is done quietly and kindly.

x.q: From where does the painter look at the scene?
o: From below, as if sitting on the floor
From above, as if standing higher
From a window of the house opposite
x.w: The view is high up, like in Japanese prints. That is why the carpet and its patterns look like flat shapes.

Q3172226.s: Mary Cassatt was an American who lived in France. She was a friend of Edgar Degas and showed her work with the Impressionists. She loved painting mothers and children most.
Q3172226.i: Imagine what the child says to its mother while she washes it.

f: Find the icon in the glittering frame carried above the crowd.
Find the golden dust over the road, with the sun shining through it.

m.q: What is the mood of the crowd?
m.w: Some walk with hope, others are worn out by the heat and the road. Repin showed many different faces.

x.q: What did Repin want to show?
x.w: Repin gathered in one picture people of every fate: peasants, beggars, townsfolk, priests. It became a portrait of a whole country.

Q2354033.s: Repin travelled to Kursk Province and painted real people. The picture is almost three metres wide, and Repin himself was one of the ‘Wanderers’.
Q2354033.i: Imagine the story of one person in the crowd: where is he going and what is he praying for?

f: Find the tall snowy peak far beyond the forest.
Find the waterfall tumbling among the greenery.

m.q: What is the mood of this landscape?
m.w: Soft golden light, huge mountains and thick greenery make nature look enormous and beautiful.

x.q: How did visitors look at this painting at its show in New York?
x.w: The painting is very big and detailed, full of plants. Visitors took opera glasses to see the small things.

Q334604.s: Frederic Edwin Church travelled to South America and sketched mountains and plants from life. Later he made the big painting in his studio from those sketches.
Q334604.i: Imagine: what would you hear if you stood in this forest?

f: Find Christ rising above the tomb, with angels beside him.
Find the guards below: they are asleep or just waking up.

m.q: What kind of morning is shown?
m.w: Christ rises in soft light, with angels nearby. Below everything is quiet, and above there is a glow.

x.q: What are the guards by the tomb doing?
o: Sleeping or waking up in wonder
x.w: They were guarding the tomb but fell asleep. The wonder happened while they slept.

Q677682.s: Raphael painted this when he was very young and still learning from the painter Perugino. Later he became the most famous painter in Rome.
Q677682.i: Imagine: what does a guard say to his friend when he wakes and sees the wonder?

f: Find the old pope in the red cap, sitting in his chair.
Find the grandson bowing low before the pope.

m.q: How does the pope look at his grandson?
m.w: He has turned his head and watches carefully, with a frown. He seems to wait for what the grandson will say.

x.q: Why does the picture look unfinished in places?
x.w: The picture stayed unfinished, so you can see how Titian painted: with free, bold strokes.

Q180632.s: Titian was the most famous painter in Venice, and popes and emperors posed for him. With the years he painted more and more freely, almost sweepingly.
Q180632.i: Imagine what the pope will say to his grandson when he stands up straight.

f: Find the man with the glass raised high: it is Rembrandt himself.
Find Saskia, the painter’s wife: she sits on his lap.

m.q: What is the mood of the couple?
m.w: The man laughs and raises his glass while his wife looks back at us. It looks like a noisy, happy party.

x.q: What story does the picture tell?
o: A master who built a ship
A son who wasted his money
x.w: It is the parable of the Prodigal Son. Rembrandt painted himself and his wife as cheerful revellers, as if acting out a scene.

Q1111394.s: Rembrandt painted himself all his life: dozens of his self-portraits survive. He looked in the mirror and learned to show feelings on a face.
Q1111394.i: Imagine: what does Rembrandt say to the guests as he raises his glass?

f: Find the book in Mary’s hands.
See how gently Mary holds the baby: find her hands.

m.q: What does Mary feel, bending toward the baby?
m.w: She bends toward the baby and holds him carefully. Her face is calm and her look is soft.

x.q: Why were small pictures like this of Mary and the baby ordered?
o: To hang at home and pray
x.w: Wealthy families hung such pictures in rooms for quiet prayer. That is why Raphael painted them especially tenderly.

Q2629134.s: Raphael painted this when he was very young, about twenty. People love his Madonnas for their soft faces and calm colours.
Q2629134.i: Imagine which story Mary is reading to the baby.

f: Find the big white collar on his dark clothes.
Find his eyes: he looks straight at you.

m.q: What is Juan’s look like?
m.w: He looks straight at us with his head up and shoulders back. He seems calm and full of dignity.

x.q: Who was Juan de Pareja to Velázquez?
o: A king of a far country
A sailor on a big ship
x.w: Juan helped Velázquez in his workshop and later became a painter himself. In 1650 Velázquez gave him his freedom.

Q4717953.s: When this portrait was shown in Rome, everyone praised it: it looked so alive. Velázquez used loose strokes that blend into a face when you stand back.
Q4717953.i: Imagine: what was Juan thinking while he posed?

f: Find John the Baptist pointing with his hand at a distant figure.
Find the small, faraway figure of Christ walking toward the people.

m.q: What are the people in the picture feeling?
m.w: Some peer into the distance, some are amazed, some have doubts. Different feelings show on their faces.

x.q: For how many years did Ivanov paint this picture?
x.w: Ivanov worked on it for almost twenty years and made hundreds of studies from life. He lived in Rome all that time.

Q4536026.s: This picture is huge: almost seven and a half metres wide. Today it hangs in the Tretyakov Gallery in Moscow.
Q4536026.i: Imagine what a person in the crowd whispers to their neighbour.

f: Find the painter’s brush and palette.
Find the sunflowers in the vase that he is painting.

m.q: What is Van Gogh’s face like while he paints?
m.w: He gazes hard at the sunflowers with his brush ready. You can see he is caught up in his work.

x.q: Who painted this picture?
o: His brother Theo, an art dealer
x.w: Gauguin lived with Van Gogh in Arles, and they painted each other. Here Gauguin painted Vincent at work.

Q2093283.s: Gauguin and Van Gogh lived and worked together in the Yellow House in Arles. Van Gogh’s sunflowers became his most famous pictures.
Q2093283.i: Imagine: what did Van Gogh say to Gauguin when he saw his portrait?

f: Find the woman reading a book with her head bowed.
Look at the folds of her dress: there are so many.

m.q: What is Mary Magdalene’s mood?
o: She is cross with the book
She is laughing at the book
m.w: Her head is bowed and her eyes rest on the page. It seems very quiet all around her.

x.q: What was this picture before?
o: A page from an old book
A drawing on a church wall
x.w: Once it was part of a big altarpiece with several saints. Later the picture was cut up, and only this part survives.

Q3039856.s: Rogier painted the folds of cloth with a fine brush, so they look like heavy real fabric. His pictures were loved for their clarity and calm.
Q3039856.i: Imagine what story is written in the book.

f: Find the little wanderer with a hat and a walking stick.
Find the rainbow over the mountains.

m.q: What feeling does this huge nature give?
m.w: The wanderer is tiny, while the mountains and sky are huge. The rainbow and soft light make everything calm and solemn.

x.q: How did Friedrich show that nature is enormous?
o: Only a huge sky, with no ground
A tiny person next to the mountains
A big crowd of people in a market square
x.w: A tiny figure beside mountains and sky helps you feel how huge nature is.

Q507120.s: Friedrich was a German Romantic painter. He loved painting people standing with their backs to us, gazing at mountains, mist or the sea.
Q507120.i: Imagine: what is the wanderer thinking as he looks at the rainbow?

f: Find the tall lamp stand by the couch.
Find her simple white dress.

m.q: What is her face like?
o: Sad, as if she had just cried
m.w: She looks at us and smiles a little. Her pose is relaxed and her face is calm.

x.q: What piece of furniture got its name from this lady?
o: A teapot with a long spout
A hat with a wide brim
x.w: Couches with a curved head end like this are called ‘récamiers’, after Madame Récamier.

Q2619037.s: David never finished this portrait: Madame Récamier got tired of waiting and asked the painter Gérard for another. Even unfinished, it is very famous.
Q2619037.i: Imagine what she is thinking as she rests on the couch.

f: Find Saint George in shining armour, riding his horse.
Find the dragon and the princess running away.

m.q: What is the mood as the knight rides at the dragon?
m.w: The horse charges forward, the knight raises his weapon and the sky is above him. It is full of movement and courage.

x.q: What did George do, according to the legend?
o: Built a castle on a hill
Saved a princess from a dragon
Found a treasure in a cave
x.w: In the legend George beat a dragon that frightened a town and saved a princess. He is seen as a brave protector.

Q2622161.s: Raphael painted this when he was very young, about twenty. The picture is small, but it is full of movement.
Q2622161.i: Imagine how the princess will thank the knight.

f: Find the bagpiper: he plays the bagpipe and everyone dances.
Find the couple dancing fast in the middle of the crowd.

m.q: What is the mood of the village party?
m.w: People dance, drink and chat at the tables, and everybody is having fun. It is a lively village festival.

x.q: Whom did Pieter Brueghel often paint in pictures like this?
o: Gods and heroes from old myths
x.w: Brueghel loved to show village life: feasts, work, games. That is why he was sometimes nicknamed ‘Peasant Brueghel’.

Q95562.s: Brueghel painted peasants full of life, with round faces and heavy shoes. His pictures show how people lived more than four hundred and fifty years ago.
Q95562.i: Imagine what tune the bagpiper is playing.

f: Find the quill in her hand.
Find her yellow jacket with white fur and the pearls.

m.q: What is the woman’s face like?
m.w: She has looked up from her letter and smiles softly at us. It seems she enjoys writing.

x.q: What did people write with in the 1600s?
x.w: Back then people wrote with a quill dipped in ink. Vermeer painted the quill in her hand very exactly.

Q914984.s: Vermeer liked to paint women reading or writing letters. Letters mattered a lot then, because there were no telephones.
Q914984.i: Imagine: who is she writing to, and what is in the letter?

f: Find Pierrot in white and Harlequin in a costume of diamonds.
Find the diamond pattern on Harlequin’s costume and the heavy curtain behind.

m.q: What is the mood of the two?
m.w: They walk slowly and gravely, with calm faces. It seems they are playing a part on a stage.

x.q: Who posed for Cézanne as Harlequin?
o: One of the kings of France
x.w: The painter’s son Paul posed as Harlequin.

Q3138984.s: Cézanne built pictures out of coloured shapes, like bricks. Many painters after him learned from him.
Q3138984.i: Imagine which party Pierrot and Harlequin are going to.

f: Find the girl with the guitar: she plays and smiles.
Find the picture hanging on the wall behind her.

m.q: What is the girl’s mood?
m.w: She plays and smiles a little, with her head turned to the side. It seems she enjoys playing.

x.q: What instrument does the girl have?
o: A big violin with a bow
x.w: It is an old stringed instrument like a guitar. In the Netherlands of the 1600s people played such instruments at home.

Q4358442.s: The picture is kept in England, at Kenwood House. Vermeer loved painting music: many of his pictures show people playing or listening.
Q4358442.i: Imagine the song the girl is singing.

f: Find the white snow lying all around and covering the girl.
Find the white dove.

m.q: What do you feel looking at the quiet white snow?
m.w: White snow, silence, a figure lying still. Everything is very calm and sad.

x.q: What does the legend of Saint Eulalia tell?
o: That she was a brave girl
That she became queen of a country
That she discovered a new island
x.w: According to the legend, Eulalia was very young and very brave. When she was gone, snow fell and covered her like a white blanket.

Q7401211.s: Waterhouse loved pictures about young heroines of legends and myths and painted them softly, almost like fairy tales. He was an English painter.
Q7401211.i: Imagine how the people of the town remembered brave Eulalia.

f: Find the three heroes on horseback: who is in the middle?
Find the bow and quiver of Alyosha Popovich, the youngest hero, on the right.

m.q: What is the mood of the heroes?
m.w: They stand on guard and look into the distance, ready to fight. Their faces are serious and sure.

x.q: What are the heroes doing in the picture?
o: Riding to a fair in the next town
x.w: They are watching for an enemy and defending their homeland. The bogatyrs are brave heroes of Russian epic songs.

Q4089077.s: Vasnetsov worked on this picture for about seventeen years. The heroes come from old Russian epic songs: Ilya Muromets, Dobrynya Nikitich and Alyosha Popovich.
Q4089077.i: Imagine whom the heroes spotted in the distance and what they will do.

f: Find the little white handkerchief in her hand.
Find her very wide pink dress.

m.q: What is the little infanta’s face like?
m.w: The girl stands straight and looks seriously at us. She knows this is an important portrait.

x.q: Who was this girl?
x.w: Margarita Teresa was the daughter of King Philip IV of Spain. She is the same girl as in Velázquez’s Las Meninas.

Q1130759.s: Del Mazo was Velázquez’s pupil and son-in-law, and learned from him to paint freely and softly. This portrait feels like a sequel to Las Meninas.
Q1130759.i: Imagine what the little princess did once her portrait was finished.

f: Find the white sails of the boats on the river.
Find the reflections of the boats in the water: they tremble in short strokes.

m.q: What is the mood of this day?
m.w: The sun is shining, the sails are white and the water sparkles. People are enjoying a happy day on the river.

x.q: How did Monet paint the sparkling water?
o: With one smooth flat blue fill
x.w: He put many short strokes side by side, so the water looks alive and shimmering.

Q3454959.s: Monet lived in the town of Argenteuil on the river Seine and often painted boats. Later he even had a floating studio.
Q3454959.i: Imagine: which boat will win the regatta, and what is it called?

f: Find the giraffe and the camel in the square.
Find the people in white and coloured turbans listening to the preacher.

m.q: How does the crowd listen?
m.w: People stand and sit all around with their heads turned to the preacher. They listen to him very closely.

x.q: How did Gentile Bellini know what eastern cities looked like?
o: He never left his own house
He saw it all in a dream
x.w: Bellini travelled to Constantinople and worked at the Sultan’s court. That is why clothes and buildings look eastern.

Q3910087.s: Gentile Bellini began this picture and his brother Giovanni finished it. Saint Mark is the patron saint of Venice, so Venetians loved such pictures.
Q3910087.i: Imagine what the giraffe thinks about the crowd.

f: Find the huge red horse rushing forward.
Find the workers trying to hold it back.

m.q: What can you feel on this building site of a new city?
m.w: The horses and people look like a whirlwind, the colours are bright and the lines are blurred. It feels like everything moves and roars.

x.q: What did the Futurist painters want to show?
o: Speed, machines and a new city
x.w: Futurists loved speed, factories and growing cities. The word ‘Futurism’ comes from ‘future’.

Q587514.s: Boccioni showed the building of a new part of the city. The picture is very big: about two metres tall and three wide. His strokes are short, so everything seems to tremble.
Q587514.i: Imagine what is being built on this site and what sounds you hear.

f: Find the fish and eggs on the table.
Find the little scene in the background: through an opening you can see Christ.

m.q: What is the mood of the girl in front?
m.w: She bends over her work and looks down, with a serious, tired face. An old woman behind her seems to be telling her something.

x.q: What is unusual about how the scenes are arranged?
o: Main scene far off, kitchen in front
It is split into two equal halves
x.w: Velázquez put the kitchen in front and showed the Bible scene through an opening in the distance. This trick is called a picture within a picture.

Q1087226.s: Velázquez painted this when he was about nineteen. He painted simple food and dishes so exactly that you feel you could touch them.
Q1087226.i: Imagine what Christ talks about with Martha and Mary in the small room far away.

f: Find the golden chain around her neck, with words running along it.
Find the book in her hand.

m.q: What is Lucrezia’s face like?
m.w: Her face is smooth and still, and her look is calm and cool. She carries herself with great dignity.

x.q: What is written on her necklace?
x.w: The necklace says in French that love has no end. Such mottoes were fashionable among rich people at that time.

Q1990128.s: Bronzino painted skin as smooth as porcelain, and cloth and jewels very sharply. He was the court painter of the Duke of Tuscany.
Q1990128.i: Imagine the story: who gave her such a necklace?

f: Find the women in the white, red and black dresses.
Find the path of moonlight on the water.

m.q: What is the mood of this night dance?
m.w: In the middle a couple whirls, the woman in red. On the left stands a pale girl, on the right a dark one. Joy and sorrow are side by side.

x.q: What did Munch want to show with three women in different dresses?
x.w: The woman in white shows youth, in red love, in black sorrow. That is how the painter told how life goes by.

Q3208135.s: This picture belongs to Munch’s big series, the Frieze of Life, about love, joy and sadness. He painted feelings, not only what the eye sees.
Q3208135.i: Imagine what music the dancers hear on this summer night.

f: Find the tall turban-like hat on her head.
Find the soft fur.

m.q: How does Isabella look?
m.w: She sits straight and looks calm and sure, dressed in rich cloth. This is how confident rulers look.

x.q: How old was Isabella when Titian painted her?
x.w: Isabella asked to be painted as she was in her youth. Titian made her face young, though she was over sixty.

Q3853901.s: Isabella d’Este was the Marchioness of Mantua, a clever ruler and a lover of art. She was called the ‘First Lady of the Renaissance’.
Q3853901.i: Imagine what question Isabella would ask you if you visited her.

f: Find the emperor: he is feeding the birds.
Find the beautiful walls and floor of the palace around the emperor.

m.q: What is the emperor’s mood?
m.w: He sits calmly, busy with his birds, as if he had forgotten the business of the state. Important matters do not worry him.

x.q: What did Honorius love most, according to the old story?
x.w: In the old story, the emperor had a favourite hen named Roma. When he was told ‘Rome has fallen’, he thought of her.

Q7733565.s: Waterhouse loved painting scenes from ancient Rome and Greece and painted them in great detail: marble, cloth, feathers.
Q7733565.i: Think up names for the emperor’s favourite birds.

f: Find the three heads of the king: on each he is turned differently.
Find his lace collar and pointed beard.

m.q: What is the king’s face like?
m.w: His look is thoughtful and serious and his lips are closed. You can tell he holds himself with dignity.

x.q: Why did van Dyck paint the same face three times?
o: So a sculptor could make a bust
Because the king had three heads
x.w: The picture was sent to Rome to the sculptor Bernini. From it he made a marble bust of the king.

Q3998985.s: Van Dyck was the court painter of King Charles I of England. A pointed beard like the king’s is still called a ‘Van Dyke’.
Q3998985.i: Imagine what the king is thinking while the sculptor waits for the picture.

f: Find the woman in the bright blue dress stretching after long hours of sewing.
Find the little mouse on the floor.

m.q: What is Mariana feeling?
m.w: She stretches, her back tired, and her face is sad. It seems she is weary of waiting.

x.q: What story is behind the picture?
o: A girl waits for her fiancé
A harvest festival in a village
x.w: The picture comes from a poem by Tennyson. A girl lives in a lonely house and waits for the one she loved. But he does not come.

Q4281369.s: Millais was one of the Pre-Raphaelites: they painted every little thing very brightly and exactly, like old paintings. See how the blue dress and the glass shine!
Q4281369.i: Imagine what Mariana writes in a letter to the one she is waiting for.

f: Find the two people by the window.
Find the spot where two faces have merged into one.

m.q: What do the two by the window feel?
m.w: The faces have joined, the figures press together, and there is nothing extra around them. It feels as if nobody else exists for them.

x.q: Why did Munch merge two faces into one?
o: To show how close they are
x.w: Munch painted not only what the eye sees but feelings too. Merged faces speak of closeness.

Q18891111.s: Munch painted The Kiss several times, changing colours and details. He was a Norwegian painter of feelings: love, joy and sadness.
Q18891111.i: Imagine how this evening by the window ends.

f: Find Saint Joseph: he has no beard.
Find Mary with the baby in her arms.

m.q: What is the mood of this family?
m.w: They lean toward each other and their faces are kind. You can see it is a close family.

x.q: What is unusual about Joseph in this picture?
o: He is the tallest in the family
x.w: Joseph was usually painted old and with a beard. Raphael painted him younger, without a beard.

Q2629419.s: Raphael painted this when he lived in Florence. The picture is now in the Hermitage in Saint Petersburg.
Q2629419.i: Imagine what Joseph will say to the baby.

f: Find Christ in the centre: he holds an orb in his hand.
Find John the Baptist and Mary Magdalene on the side wings.

m.q: What is the mood of the central part?
m.w: Christ blesses, with Mary and John beside him. The poses are calm and the figures still.

x.q: What is special about this triptych?
o: It is painted right on water
x.w: The wings fold shut like cupboard doors. Other pictures are painted outside, such as the sign of the family that ordered it.

Q24160.s: Rogier van der Weyden painted so finely in oil that folds and faces look like photographs. The altarpiece was ordered by the Braque family of Tournai.
Q24160.i: Imagine what you would paint on the closed doors of your own altarpiece.

f: Find the tiny figures: how many scenes can you count?
Find the tall houses and towers of the city.

m.q: What is the mood of this story in little scenes?
m.w: The figures are small, the colours muted and the scenes follow one after another. It is like a quiet story without words.

x.q: How did Memling fit so many scenes into one picture?
o: He put scenes in different corners of a city
He painted each scene on a separate sheet
He stretched the picture into a long ribbon
x.w: Each little scene happens in its own corner of the city. Your eye travels along the streets as if turning the pages of a book.

Q2446983.s: Hans Memling lived in the city of Bruges and painted very finely and in great detail. His pictures were loved for their calm and clarity.
Q2446983.i: Make up your own short story that goes along the streets of this city, from scene to scene.

f: Find the crutch the boy carries over his shoulder.
Find his smile and the bright sky with clouds behind him.

m.q: What is the boy’s face like?
m.w: He looks straight at us and smiles, with his head up. Despite his difficulties he looks bold and proud.

x.q: From where does the painter look at the boy?
o: From below, up against the sky
x.w: Ribera placed the boy against a big sky and showed him from below. That is why he looks strong and proud.

Q24118.s: Ribera was born in Spain but lived in Naples. He painted ordinary people as seriously and respectfully as kings.
Q24118.i: Imagine what the cheerful boy is thinking as he looks at us.

f: Find the little girl sitting right on the big dog.
Find the mother in a pretty dress on the sofa.

m.q: What is the mood of the family?
m.w: The mother sits relaxed, the children are nearby and the dog lies quietly. Everything looks cosy.

x.q: What does this picture tell about the Charpentier family?
o: That they came from another land
That they hardly ever left home
That they were friends of artists
x.w: The Charpentiers, a publisher and his wife, were friends of painters and welcomed them at home. Renoir painted their cosy drawing room.

Q686105.s: This picture made Renoir famous: it was shown at a big exhibition. People began to order portraits from him. It is now in the Metropolitan Museum in New York.
Q686105.i: Give the big dog a name and say what it likes.

f: Find the shadow on the wall: what does it look like?
Find Mary kneeling by the chest.

m.q: What does Mary feel on seeing the shadow on the wall?
m.w: She has lifted her head and looks at the shadow with her hands clasped. It seems she has become uneasy.

x.q: What does Jesus’s shadow on the wall look like?
x.w: The shadow of his stretched arms looks like a cross. The painter hints at the future without showing anything frightening.

Q949567.s: Hunt was a Pre-Raphaelite: he painted very sharply and brightly. He travelled to Palestine to paint real houses and clothes. That made the picture accurate.
Q949567.i: Imagine what Mary says to Jesus.

f: Find the old suit of armour.
Find the young man in the straw hat.

m.q: What is the mood of the scene?
m.w: Each is busy with their own thing. The young man looks ahead, the man smokes, the woman is far off. Nobody talks, and that makes the scene mysterious.

x.q: Does the picture tell a story?
x.w: Manet showed an ordinary moment in the studio and left a riddle. The viewer decides what the scene is about.

Q1245431.s: Manet painted freely, with broad strokes, and loved modern life, not only legends. Young Impressionist painters admired him.
Q1245431.i: Imagine whom they are waiting for at this lunch table and what they will talk about.

f: Find the big barrel and the branch sticking out above it.
Find the hunting horn.

m.q: What is the mood of this strange world?
m.w: The figures are silly and objects stand in the wrong places. It feels like a dream or a joke.

x.q: What does the word ‘intemperance’ mean?
o: When there is far too much of everything
When a person stays silent all day
When a person runs very fast
x.w: Intemperance is having too much food, drink or fun. Bosch painted such stories so people would laugh and think.

Q2091114.s: Bosch lived in the Dutch town of ’s-Hertogenbosch. He loved painting strange creatures and funny scenes with a lesson.
Q2091114.i: Imagine what advice a wise friend would give the people in this picture.

f: Find the big blocks of stone: stonemasons work here.
Find the canal in the distance: it is the Grand Canal of Venice.

m.q: What kind of day is shown in this yard?
m.w: People work or rest quietly and the sky has soft clouds. Everything is calm and simple.

x.q: What are such pictures with exact views of a town called?
x.w: A veduta is an exact view of a town. Canaletto painted Venice so well that you can still recognise it today.

Q2943415.s: Canaletto painted Venice very accurately, and tourists bought his pictures as souvenirs. Here he showed not the grand city but a simple working yard.
Q2943415.i: Imagine what will be built from these stones.

f: Find the three friends who fell asleep below.
Find the group of people walking along the road far away.

m.q: What is Jesus’s mood?
m.w: He kneels on the hill and prays, alone among the rocks. The poses and the light stress his loneliness.

x.q: What are Jesus’s friends doing?
x.w: They meant to stay awake but fell asleep while Jesus prayed. The painter shows them asleep below.

Q3884945.s: Mantegna loved to paint rocks like sculpture: hard, angular, with sharp edges. He admired ancient statues.
Q3884945.i: Imagine what Jesus prays about in the quiet of the night.

f: Find the knight in shining armour.
Find the lady tying a ribbon on the knight’s arm.

m.q: What is the lady feeling?
m.w: She sees him off on his way and carefully ties the ribbon. Her face is serious and tender.

x.q: What does the title ‘God Speed’ mean?
o: A wish for good luck on a journey
The name of an old castle by the sea
The name of the knight's fast horse
x.w: ‘God speed’ is an old English wish for good luck. People said it to those setting off on a journey or a big task.

Q17466708.s: Edmund Leighton painted knights and ladies of the Middle Ages. He loved painting old armour and dresses in great detail. The picture was painted in 1900, but it shows the past like a fairy tale.
Q17466708.i: Imagine where the knight is going and what he will bring back to the lady.

f: Find the city far away.
Find the dark, heavy sky above the city.

m.q: What do you feel looking at the quiet city under a dark sky?
m.w: The sky is dark, the distant city is still and the colours are muted. Everything is very quiet and sad.

x.q: Which city is painted?
x.w: It is Jerusalem, a city told about in the Bible. It is one of the oldest cities in the world.

Q5665712.s: Gérôme painted very sharply and smoothly, almost like a photograph. He loved unusual light and strong shadows.
Q5665712.i: Imagine what sounds you hear in this silence above the city.

f: Find the books: the whole figure is built from them.
Find the beard made of fluffy tails, the kind once used as dusters.

m.q: What do you feel looking at the man made of books?
m.w: A serious face is made from books, and that makes the picture funny. The painter loved jokes.

x.q: What is ‘The Librarian’ built from?
x.w: The figure is built of stacks of books and other library things. It is a joke about a person who lives among books.

Q17021187.s: Arcimboldo painted portraits out of vegetables, flowers, fruit and books. He was a court painter of emperors in Vienna and Prague.
Q17021187.i: Make up your own joke portrait: what would you be built from?

f: Find her big eyes: she glances back over her shoulder.
Find her crown and the dark sunset sky.

m.q: What is the Swan Princess’s mood?
m.w: She looks back over her shoulder with big eyes, and her look is uneasy and sad. Above her the dusky sky is like a fairy tale.

x.q: Which fairy tale is the heroine from?
o: The tale of Puss in Boots
x.w: She is the Swan Princess from Pushkin’s Tale of Tsar Saltan. Vrubel designed the sets for an opera based on this tale.

Q4503153.s: Vrubel painted in faceted strokes, as if the picture were assembled from pieces of mosaic or crystals. That makes everything shimmer.
Q4503153.i: Imagine what the Swan Princess is thinking as she looks back.

f: Find Archangel Michael with wings and a spear.
Find Michael’s face: it is calm.

m.q: What is Michael’s expression?
m.w: He looks down calmly with his spear raised. You can see he is brave and sure of victory.

x.q: For whom was this picture ordered?
x.w: The picture was ordered as a gift for King Francis I of France. Today it is in the Louvre in Paris.

Q594470.s: Raphael painted this near the end of his life, with help from his pupils. Archangel Michael is a brave protector who beats evil.
Q594470.i: Imagine what Michael says when evil has been beaten.

f: Find the old fortune teller holding the young man’s hand.
Look where the girls’ eyes are looking: not at the young man!

m.q: What is the young man’s mood?
m.w: He looks only at his hand and the fortune teller, and does not see what the others are doing. He is far too trusting.

x.q: What is really happening in the picture?
o: The girls are robbing the young man
They all sing a song together
x.w: The fortune teller distracts the young man while the girls quietly take his things. The painter shows it with glances, without words.

Q379906.s: Georges de La Tour painted smooth, calm figures, almost like sculptures, and loved candlelight. Here he shows a sly little scene.
Q379906.i: Imagine what happens when the young man notices something is missing.

f: Find the Milky Way: the wide band of stars across the sky.
Find the Moon and its reflection in the water.

m.q: How do the travellers feel on their night road?
m.w: There are dark woods and a night sky, and the travellers are lit by firelight. It is quiet, but you feel the road is hard.

x.q: What unusual thing did Elsheimer paint in the sky?
o: A giant face made of clouds
x.w: He painted the stars very exactly, and you can even recognise constellations. It is one of the first pictures with such a real night sky.

Q2381716.s: Elsheimer painted very small pictures on copper plates. He lived in Rome, and the great painter Rubens admired his work.
Q2381716.i: Make up a name for each bright star in this sky.

f: Find the two girls sitting on the grass and looking straight at us.
Find the hazelnuts and the bare feet.

m.q: What look do the girls have?
m.w: They smile and look at us in a friendly way. It all looks calm, like a warm day.

x.q: What is special about Bouguereau’s paintings?
o: They are very smooth, no strokes
They are only black and white
x.w: Bouguereau painted so smoothly that you hardly see any strokes. His people look polished and soft.

Q5971282.s: William-Adolphe Bouguereau was a French academic painter, one of the most famous of his time. He loved painting children and village girls.
Q5971282.i: Imagine what the girls plan to do with the hazelnuts.

f: Find the girl in the shiny satin dress, standing with her back to us.
Find the bed with its curtain behind.

m.q: How do you think this room sounds?
m.w: People sit and stand calmly, and faces are hidden or thoughtful. We cannot hear the words, and that makes the scene mysterious.

x.q: What is Ter Borch famous for?
o: The shine of silk and satin
x.w: Ter Borch could show how satin shines softly and falls in folds. His fabrics look real.

Q5227835.s: The title ‘Paternal Admonition’ was given later and may not be accurate. Nobody really knows what the people are saying, so you can invent the story yourself.
Q5227835.i: Imagine what the people in the room are talking about.

f: Find the big sword the boy holds in both arms.
Find the wide belt around his waist.

m.q: What is the boy with the sword’s face like?
m.w: He looks straight at us with his shoulders back. The boy is very serious, as if playing an important part.

x.q: Whose paintings did Manet love when he painted this one?
o: Van Gogh and the Dutch painters
x.w: Manet admired Velázquez and painted in his spirit: dark colours and a simple background.

Q1844748.s: Manet painted freely, with broad strokes, and young Impressionist painters admired him.
Q1844748.i: Imagine: who is the boy going to fight, and why?

f: Find the doctor gently holding Goya up.
Find the glass of medicine in the doctor’s hand.

m.q: How does Goya feel in the doctor’s arms?
o: Weak, but he trusts the doctor
m.w: Goya is pale and clutches the sheet while the doctor holds him. You can see he feels ill, but a friend is near.

x.q: Why did Goya paint this picture?
o: To sell it for a lot
x.w: At the bottom Goya wrote that he thanks his friend Arrieta, who saved him from a serious illness.

Q2736720.s: Goya was over seventy when he painted this. He was almost deaf by then, but he kept on painting.
Q2736720.i: Imagine what words the doctor says to Goya as he holds him.

f: Find the old wooden Rialto Bridge.
Find the gondolas on the canal.

m.q: What kind of life bustles in this city?
m.w: On the bridge, boats and balconies there are many people, all doing something. Venice feels alive and busy.

x.q: What is unusual about this bridge?
o: It is made of glass, like an aquarium
It is wooden, but now it is stone
x.w: Back then the Rialto Bridge was wooden. The stone bridge was built almost a hundred years later.

Q3817178.s: Carpaccio loved telling stories and showing lots of little details: clothes, houses, boats. His pictures show how Venice looked more than five hundred years ago.
Q3817178.i: Imagine where the gondolier is rushing and whom he is carrying.

f: Find the woman in the long dress covered in bright patterns.
Find the three women below with bowed heads.

m.q: What do the figures with bowed heads feel?
m.w: The figures bow their heads, their eyes closed, and everything is still. It feels as if all are quietly waiting for something good.

x.q: What is the pattern on the dress made of?
x.w: Klimt painted the dress like a mosaic: coloured dots, curls and gold. The dress and the background almost merge.

Q19883512.s: Klimt used real gold in thin leaves. That is why his pictures glitter like jewels.
Q19883512.i: Imagine what this woman is quietly waiting for.

f: Find the church with domes far away on the river bank.
Find how the evening sun colours the sky and the water.

m.q: What kind of evening did Levitan paint?
m.w: Warm evening light, smooth water and silence. It feels as if a far-off ringing floats over the river.

x.q: What does the title ‘Evening Bells’ mean?
o: The clinking of dishes in the kitchen
x.w: It is the ringing of church bells heard in the evening. We cannot hear it in the picture, but we can imagine it.

Q4110204.s: Isaac Levitan was a master of the ‘mood landscape’: he could show feelings in a landscape. His pictures are called quiet and poetic.
Q4110204.i: Imagine how this evening ringing sounds: high or low, fast or slow.

f: Find baby Jesus putting a little ring on a woman’s finger.
Find the angel playing the little organ.

m.q: What moment is shown in the middle of the altarpiece?
m.w: The baby puts on a ring, angels play music and everyone looks on tenderly. It is a lovely, quiet ceremony.

x.q: Where is this altarpiece still kept?
o: In Paris, in a big museum
In Moscow, in a big palace
In Bruges, in an old hospital
x.w: Memling painted it for Saint John’s Hospital in Bruges. It is still there, and the hospital has become a museum.

Q2446971.s: Hans Memling painted with very fine brushes, and you can see tiny details in his pictures: cloth, flowers, jewellery.
Q2446971.i: Imagine what tune the angel plays on the organ.

f: Find the red poppies: they are scattered like bright drops.
Find the woman with a parasol and the boy: they appear in the picture twice.

m.q: What kind of day is it?
m.w: The sun shines, the poppies are bright, there are clouds in the sky and people stroll slowly. Everything is light and kind.

x.q: How did Monet paint a whole field of poppies?
x.w: He put short red dabs on the green field, and from far away they join into a flowering meadow.

Q3231771.s: Monet painted this looking at a real meadow near the town of Argenteuil. The woman with the parasol and the boy are his wife Camille and son Jean.
Q3231771.i: Imagine what the mother and son talk about as they walk down the path.

f: Find the hilt of the sword: his hand rests on it.
Find his dark clothes against the dark background: the face looks brighter.

m.q: What is this man’s look like?
m.w: He looks from under his brows and his face is tense. His hand is on the sword: he is ready to defend himself at any moment.

x.q: What were Venetian painters like Titian famous for?
x.w: Venetians loved rich, beautiful colours. Titian is considered one of the greatest masters of colour.

Q3643957.s: The title ‘The Bravo’ was given later. We do not know for sure who the man was.
Q3643957.i: Give this man a name and a story.

f: Find King Frederick: he is playing the flute.
Find the sparkling candles: how many are there? They are reflected in the mirrors.

m.q: How do the courtiers listen?
m.w: Candlelight, dressed-up courtiers and everyone listening to the king. There is no chatter, only music.

x.q: What makes this picture look so ‘glowing’?
o: Bright sun in a big window
A roaring fire in a big fireplace
x.w: Menzel painted many candles and their reflections. The room seems to glow from inside.

Q944909.s: King Frederick the Great loved music, composed and played the flute himself. Adolph von Menzel was a German painter who painted a lot of the king’s life.
Q944909.i: Imagine what tune the king is playing.

f: Find the flag in the general’s hand.
Find his long hair, flying in the wind.

m.q: What does Bonaparte feel as he strides forward?
m.w: He glances back at his soldiers and strides forward with a flag and a sword. It is as if he calls: ‘Follow me!’

x.q: What did the painter want to show by painting Bonaparte this way?
o: That he likes to go fishing
That he got lost in the mountains
That he is brave and leads
x.w: Gros showed Bonaparte as a hero who goes ahead of everyone. Such portraits helped people remember him as a bold commander.

Q1282978.s: Gros was a pupil of David. He painted pictures full of movement and bright colour to show courage and energy.
Q1282978.i: Imagine what Bonaparte shouts to his soldiers.

f: Find his profile: nose, lips and chin drawn with a fine clear line.
Find his lowered eyes.

m.q: What feeling can you see in this profile?
m.w: He looks down, his face calm and sad. The profile is still, like on a coin.

x.q: Why is the portrait painted in profile?
o: That was how coins and medals showed faces
The painter could not draw a front view
The man turned away from the painter
x.w: A profile recalls the images on coins and medals. It makes the face look strong and noble.

Q2272723.s: Botticelli painted such portraits for the Medici family, who ruled Florence. His line is very smooth and beautiful.
Q2272723.i: Imagine what he is thinking about as he looks down.

f: Find his face: a tired, watchful look.
Find his dark clothes.

m.q: What is the emperor’s face like in the portrait?
m.w: His look is watchful but weary, with no smile. You can see the emperor has many heavy worries.

x.q: Who was Charles V?
o: A sailing king with a fleet
A court musician in a castle
x.w: Charles V ruled Spain, lands in Germany, the Netherlands and part of Italy. People said the sun never set on his lands.

Q2609585.s: Titian was the emperor’s favourite painter and painted him several times. He liked to show people as they really were.
Q2609585.i: Imagine what the emperor is thinking as he looks at us.

f: Find his greying beard and watchful eyes.
Find the light collar on his dark clothes.

m.q: What impression does this man make?
m.w: His eyes are watchful and his face is long and calm. You can tell he is used to thinking.

x.q: Why is there a question mark in the title?
o: Experts are unsure who is shown
The man in it asked something
x.w: We do not know for sure who is shown. El Greco may have painted himself, but it is hard to prove.

Q5712837.s: El Greco liked to stretch faces and figures, so they look tall and ‘spiritual’. He came from the island of Crete.
Q5712837.i: Imagine the man’s name and what he does.

f: Find the sleeping baby.
Find Joseph in the background: he is working.

m.q: What kind of evening is it in this house?
m.w: A soft, warm light glows, the baby sleeps and everyone is busy with quiet tasks. It is like a cosy home.

x.q: How did Rembrandt make the scene cosy?
o: With warm light in a dark room
x.w: He painted soft golden light and dark corners. The light gathers around the mother and baby.

Q3944474.s: Rembrandt showed the most important story as an ordinary family scene. There is a simple room, a hard-working father and a warm light. He loved ordinary people.
Q3944474.i: Make up a lullaby that Mary sings to the baby.

f: Find the little dog beside the boy.
Find where the boy is looking.

m.q: What connects the boy and the dog?
m.w: Beside the dog the boy looks calm and warm. You can see they are friends.

x.q: Whom did Murillo love to paint?
x.w: Murillo lived in Seville and often painted children from ordinary families. He painted them with warmth and kindness.

Q6025684.s: Murillo used soft, golden tones and kind faces. He was much loved in Spain, and his pictures of children are known all over the world.
Q6025684.i: Give the dog a name and say what the boy did with it this morning.

f: Find the huge red horse.
Find the boy on its back and the other bathers with horses in the distance.

m.q: What feeling does the red horse on the blue water bring?
m.w: The red horse glows against the blue water, and the boy sits calm and proud. It feels like something very important is happening.

x.q: Why is a red horse unusual?
o: The horse was painted with wall paint
The whole picture is wrapped in red
x.w: Petrov-Vodkin painted the horse bright red to look like fire and strength. He cared more about feeling than the real colour.

Q4247398.s: Petrov-Vodkin learned from icon painters and loved pure bright colours and simple big shapes. This picture became one of the best-known Russian paintings of the twentieth century.
Q4247398.i: Give the red horse a name and say where it will gallop after the bath.

f: Find the slim birch trees standing right in the water.
Find the sky with clouds reflected in the flood.

m.q: What do you feel in this picture?
m.w: The water has spread and sparkles, the sky is blue and the birches are pale. It feels as if all nature is waking up.

x.q: Why has the water spread over the meadows?
o: A heavy rain fell in summer
People flooded the field on purpose
x.w: In spring the snow melts and there is so much water that rivers flood their banks. In Russian this is called ‘big water’.

Q4109497.s: Isaac Levitan loved painting quiet Russian nature and could show moods: joy, calm, sadness.
Q4109497.i: Imagine which birds have come back in the spring.

f: Find the horseman on a horse crashing into the snow fortress.
Find the brightly dressed people on the white snow: how many colours do you see?

m.q: What is the mood of the winter festival?
m.w: Snow flies, the horse gallops and people laugh and shout. Everyone is caught up in a merry game.

x.q: What game is this?
o: Horse racing through a winter forest
A bear hunt in the snowy taiga
A winter game: storming a snow fort
x.w: In Siberia, at winter festivals people built a fortress of snow, and horsemen tried to break it. It is a game, not a real war.

Q4110459.s: Surikov was born in the Siberian town of Krasnoyarsk and painted this from childhood memories. He loved bright colours on white snow and big pictures with crowds of people.
Q4110459.i: Imagine who will win: the horseman or the defenders of the snow fortress.

f: Find Zinaida Yusupova’s face: where is she looking?
Find the soft, light brushstrokes: how do they make cloth and light?

m.q: What impression does the princess make?
m.w: Serov showed her directly and simply, with no extra decoration. She holds herself calmly and with dignity.

x.q: Who was Valentin Serov?
x.w: Serov painted portraits of famous people of his time: painters, actors, aristocrats. His portraits were thought very lifelike.

Q66988420.s: Serov painted quickly and freely, with fresh, light strokes, and his pictures seem full of air. Zinaida Yusupova was a princess, one of the richest and most beautiful women in Russia.
Q66988420.i: Imagine what the princess was thinking about while she posed.

f: Find the armour on the lady's chest: it shines.
Look at the big throne she sits on.

m.q: How does the woman on the throne feel?
m.w: She sits straight with her head held high. Her face is calm: strong, but not angry.

x.q: What kind of strength did Botticelli paint?
o: The strength of wind and storms
x.w: Here «fortitude» means courage and steadiness inside. That is why the lady in armour sits so calmly.

Q1109340.s: Botticelli loved soft, flowing lines and gentle faces. Even a lady in armour looks graceful in his hands.
Q1109340.i: Imagine what brave thing this lady did today.

f: Find the armour in the picture: soldiers wore it in battle.
Find the jester: he stands very proudly.

m.q: How does the jester carry himself?
o: Lazily, as if ready to nap
m.w: He stands straight and looks out with confidence. It seems the jester is playing a great warrior.

x.q: Who was the jester nicknamed Don John of Austria after?
x.w: The real Don John of Austria was a famous commander. The jester got his name as a joke, and the painting gently plays with that.

Q1114361.s: Velázquez painted court jesters with respect and warmth. He saw a real person with a character of his own in each one.
Q1114361.i: Imagine the funny story the jester tells the king.

f: Find the smallest children: they stand at the front.
Look at the altar: a cross stands on it, and everyone has gathered around.

m.q: What is the mood of the family?
m.w: The grown-ups look at the altar seriously and calmly. Nobody is shouting or playing.

x.q: What is this family doing in the painting?
o: Having lunch at a long table
x.w: This is the Vendramin family of Venice. They have gathered at an altar to pray together before a cross.

Q1133103.s: Titian lived in Venice and was famous for warm colours: golden, red and deep brown. Rich families asked him to paint their portraits.
Q1133103.i: Imagine what the smallest child is thinking while the grown-ups pray.

f: Find the firefighter: he is carrying the children.
Find the mother: she holds out her arms to the children.

m.q: What does the mother feel when she sees the children?
o: She is cross and walks away
m.w: The mother has dropped to her knees and reaches for her children. Her pose says: «You are safe, you are with me!»

x.q: Why is the painting filled with red-orange light?
o: It is a red sunset by the sea
It is a party full of candles
It is the glow of the fire
x.w: There is a fire in the house, and the firefighter carries the children out. The bright light of the flames lights up faces and clothes.

Q1175910.s: Millais belonged to the Pre-Raphaelites. They painted very precisely, down to tiny details, as if looking at everything through a magnifying glass.
Q1175910.i: Imagine what the firefighter says to the children when he sets them down.

f: Find the masts of the sailing boats: they are thin, like winter trees.
Find the man in a hat: he is quite small.

m.q: What is the mood of this harbour?
m.w: The boats stand still, the water is calm, and there are hardly any people. It feels as if time has stopped.

x.q: Why does the painter know this place so well?
o: He was born in this town
He sold fish in this port
x.w: Caspar David Friedrich was born in Greifswald, by the Baltic Sea. He painted the town of his childhood.

Q1545495.s: Friedrich loved silence and wide-open space. The people in his pictures are often small, and the world around them is huge and calm.
Q1545495.i: Imagine where one of the sailing boats will sail tomorrow morning.

f: Find the tall dark trees in the garden.
Find the people in hats: they have stopped to talk.

m.q: What is the mood of this garden?
m.w: People have stopped to talk, nobody is in a hurry, and the stone and trees bask in the light. Everything is quiet and slow.

x.q: Where is this garden?
o: In Rome, at the Villa Medici
In London, beside a big river
x.w: Velázquez was in Italy in 1630 and painted the garden of the Villa Medici in Rome. The picture is small, with quick, free brushstrokes.

Q1133844.s: Velázquez was painter to the Spanish king. In Italy he made small views of the Villa Medici garden. They are free and quick, almost like pictures made long after him.
Q1133844.i: Imagine what the people who stopped in the garden are talking about.

f: Find Cupid: he holds a yoke over the couple.
Find the ring: it is being put on the bride's finger.

m.q: What is the mood of this couple?
m.w: This is a wedding portrait: the couple sit side by side. Cupid beside them reminds us of love. The mood is solemn and tender.

x.q: What does the yoke over the couple's shoulders mean?
o: They will plough a field together
They are tired and need a rest
x.w: A yoke is a bar that joins two oxen in one team. Here it means that husband and wife are now together and will walk through life side by side.

Q2105277.s: Lorenzo Lotto painted portraits that hide little signs and riddles. You have to look carefully to find them.
Q2105277.i: Imagine what Cupid whispers to the groom and the bride.

f: Find the hammer in the young man's hand.
Find the ring on his finger.

m.q: What does the young man's look say?
o: He wants to play a prank
m.w: He looks calm and serious, with closed lips and a still face. This is how a reserved, attentive person looks.

x.q: What helped Netherlandish masters paint the tiniest details?
o: Strokes with a wide house brush
x.w: Netherlandish masters painted in oils in thin, see-through layers. This lets you paint the tiniest details: a ring, cloth, single hairs.

Q3399428.s: Rogier van der Weyden worked in Brussels. His portraits are precise and calm, and the faces in them seem alive.
Q3399428.i: Imagine why the young man holds a hammer.

f: Find the fan in the girl's hands.
Find her bracelet and her dark hair with a fringe.

m.q: What does the girl's expression say?
o: She is bored and keeps yawning
m.w: The girl has a light smile and a soft gaze. She looks content and relaxed.

x.q: Who posed for Renoir?
o: A flower seller from a market
x.w: Alphonsine Fournaise posed, the daughter of the owner of a restaurant on the Seine at Chatou. Renoir often painted his friends and acquaintances there.

Q3713925.s: Renoir loved to paint the joy of life: smiles, soft light, warm colours. His brushstrokes are light as down.
Q3713925.i: Imagine what the girl says as she waves her fan.

f: Find Max Schmitt: he sits in a narrow boat with oars.
Find the bridge over the river and the houses on the bank.

m.q: How does Max feel out on the water?
o: He rests calmly on the water
He is rushing and very nervous
He is laughing loudly at a joke
