m.w: The oars are still, the river is quiet, and Max looks calm. Everything around him is slow and peaceful.

x.q: Where is the painter himself hiding in the picture?
o: On the bridge, watching the water
In a boat far away, rowing
On the bank, resting under a tree
x.w: Thomas Eakins painted himself as a small rower far away. His name is even written on the side of the boat.

Q1913390.s: Eakins loved rowing himself and knew well how a rower holds the oars. He painted people doing what they love.
Q1913390.i: Think of a name for Max's boat and say where he will row next.

f: Find the woman who is pointing at Peter.
Find the soldier in a helmet.

m.q: What does Peter feel?
o: He is glad to meet friends
m.w: Peter presses his hand to his chest and looks away. He has been recognised, and he feels worried.

x.q: What did Peter say when he was recognised?
x.w: Peter was a friend of Jesus. He felt afraid and said he did not know Him. Afterwards he was very sad about it.

Q2270778.s: Caravaggio painted as if one bright spotlight were switched on in a dark room. The light picks faces and hands out of the dark.
Q2270778.i: Imagine what Peter says to his friend when they meet again.

f: Find the saint's brown robe: it has deep folds.
Find where the light touches his face.

m.q: What is the mood around Saint Francis?
o: Merry, like at a big party
Stormy, as if he is angry
m.w: The saint bows his head, and all around is dark and quiet. He seems lost in peaceful thoughts.

x.q: What did Saint Francis of Assisi love?
x.w: Francis lived very simply and loved animals, birds and all of nature. People called him a friend of the animals.

Q2275371.s: Caravaggio often painted saints as ordinary people in plain clothes. That makes them feel alive and close to us.
Q2275371.i: Imagine which bird Francis will meet when he steps out of the stillness.

f: Find the partridge: it hangs from a nail.
Find the knight's heavy iron gloves and the short crossbow bolt.

m.q: What is the mood of this still life?
o: Noisy, like a busy village fair
m.w: The things hang still against a plain wall, with no people and no movement. Everything is very quiet.

x.q: What was unusual about this painting in its time?
o: It is as big as a whole wall
There are no people, only things
It was painted with one colour
x.w: In 1504, pictures of only objects were very rare. This is one of the earliest, which makes it special.

Q2349652.s: Jacopo de' Barbari painted so precisely that you want to touch the partridge. Feathers, metal and wood all look different.
Q2349652.i: Imagine which knight left his gloves here and where he went.

f: Find the man's face: Raphael painted it very carefully.
Find where the light falls on his face: what is brightest there?

m.q: How does this man look?
m.w: His face is calm and his gaze steady, with no hurry at all. He seems ready to listen.

x.q: Who was Perugino to Raphael?
o: A neighbour who baked fresh bread
x.w: Perugino was a well-known painter. According to tradition, young Raphael learned from him.

Q2607072.s: Raphael painted faces softly and warmly, without harsh lines. That is why his people seem kind.
Q2607072.i: Imagine what Perugino is teaching young Raphael.

f: Find the man's face and his watchful eyes.
See how softly the light rests on his face.

m.q: What kind of face does the man show us?
o: With a frown and an angry look
m.w: His mouth is closed and his gaze is steady and attentive. He looks serious and focused.

x.q: How old was Raphael when he painted this portrait?
o: Not even ten years old yet
x.w: Raphael was born in 1483 and lived only 37 years. He painted this portrait when he was very young.

Q2629715.s: Raphael was one of the greatest painters of Italy. He lived a short life but made many pictures full of harmony.
Q2629715.i: Imagine what this man dreams about before he falls asleep.

f: Find the horse: it is rearing up.
Find the rider: he sits upright and holds the horse.

m.q: How does the rider carry himself?
m.w: The horse rears up, yet the rider sits straight and calm. This is how the painter showed his courage.

x.q: What does «equestrian portrait» mean?
o: A portrait of a horse alone
A portrait of a person on horseback
A portrait of a person on a ship
x.w: An equestrian portrait shows a person riding a horse. In the past, this was how noble people were shown: strong and brave.

Q2749266.s: Jacques-Louis David loved clear lines and firm shapes, like in ancient Rome. His figures stand tall, like statues.
Q2749266.i: Imagine the horse's name and why it reared up.

f: Find the face in profile: you see only one side.
Look at the smooth, even lines of the face and clothes.

m.q: How does this man seem?
m.w: He looks straight ahead, and his face is still and stern. This is how proud and important people look.

x.q: Why were people often painted in profile then?
o: It is easier to paint a smile
It shows the hair colour better
x.w: Italians followed ancient Roman coins and medals, where rulers were shown from the side. Such a portrait looked important.

Q2755121.s: Piero della Francesca loved geometry. His people seem built from smooth, calm shapes, and his light is soft and clear.
Q2755121.i: Imagine what this ruler is thinking as he looks ahead.

f: Find the four men: they sit close together and talk.
Find the rainbow: it seems to promise better times.

m.q: What is the mood of this meeting?
m.w: Four men sit close together and talk calmly. The rainbow behind them is like a sign of hope.

x.q: What are these people talking about?
o: About where to hold a ball
About how to end the war
x.w: This is Abraham Lincoln with three commanders aboard the steamer River Queen in 1865. They talked about how to end the war in America.

Q3023498.s: George Healy was an American portrait painter. He painted presidents and kings and liked to show people at important moments.
Q3023498.i: Imagine what Lincoln said at the end of the meeting.

f: Find Saint Paul's face: the light falls on it from the side.
Look at his beard: it seems completely real.

m.q: How does Saint Paul seem?
m.w: His gaze is thoughtful and his brows are slightly drawn together. He seems to be pondering important words.

x.q: What did the Apostle Paul do as he travelled the world?
o: Sold fruit at the busy markets
x.w: Paul went to many cities and wrote letters to the first Christians. People still read those letters today.

Q3075292.s: As a young man, Velázquez loved to paint people truthfully. He used real light and living faces, with no prettying up.
Q3075292.i: Imagine what Paul writes in his letter.

f: Find the big stone arches of the Colosseum.
Find the grass and plants growing on the old walls.

m.q: What is the mood of this view of the Colosseum?
m.w: The old walls bask in the sun, grass grows on them, and clouds drift above. All is quiet and peaceful.

x.q: What is the Colosseum?
o: An old royal castle in Denmark
A big lighthouse by the sea
x.w: The Colosseum is an ancient arena in Rome where thousands of spectators gathered. Today, beautiful ruins remain.

Q3079004.s: Eckersberg, a Danish painter, knew perspective very well. That is why his arches lead deep into the picture, like real ones.
Q3079004.i: Imagine who will walk through these arches in a minute.

f: Find the cat: she has arched her back.
Find the big ray fish hanging on a hook.

m.q: What does the cat feel?
m.w: Her back is arched and the cat is frozen, as if ready to leap away. That is how a wary cat behaves.

x.q: What is unusual about the painted ray?
o: It looks like a large bird
It looks a bit like a face
x.w: Seen from below, the ray seems to have «eyes» and a «smile». That is why it looks as if the fish has a face.

Q3212142.s: Chardin painted the simplest things: fish, jugs, saucepans. He presented this picture when he was accepted into the Royal Academy.
Q3212142.i: Imagine what the cat thinks about the fish and the oysters.

f: Find Mary: she bends toward the baby.
Find the angels all around: they surround Mary and the child.

m.q: What is the mood of this painting?
o: Tender and warm, like a hug
Noisy and playful, like a game
m.w: Mary bends toward the baby, and the angels' faces are gentle and quiet. Everything speaks of care.

x.q: Who are the seraphim?
o: Angels who stay closest to God
x.w: Seraphim are angels who, by tradition, stand closest to God. Painters put them around Mary to show her glory.

Q3213773.s: Botticelli lived in Florence and loved flowing lines that seem to dance. His figures are light, almost floating.
Q3213773.i: Imagine what the baby whispers to the angels.

f: Find the lady's face: her skin is smooth and pale.
Look at the cloth of her dress: it looks so soft you could touch it.

m.q: What is the lady's mood?
o: She is laughing out loud at us
She is cross and frowning hard
She is calm and a bit dreamy
m.w: Her face is smooth and calm, and her gaze is soft. There is neither loud laughter nor anger.

x.q: What is the painter Ingres famous for?
x.w: Ingres was a master of the outline: his figures seem traced with a gentle, clear line. He studied with David.

Q3292681.s: Ingres painted so smoothly that brushstrokes almost vanish. Lace, skin and cloth look precise and delicate in his pictures.
Q3292681.i: Imagine where the lady plans to go after the portrait.

f: Find the big white frilly collar: it is as round as a plate.
Find the marchesa's face: she looks straight at us.

m.q: What does the marchesa's gaze show?
o: Worry and a lot of confusion
m.w: She looks straight at us, with her head high and her shoulders straight. That is how confident people stand.

x.q: Where did Rubens paint this portrait?
o: In Antwerp, in his home city
In Madrid, at the king's court
x.w: Rubens lived in Italy for several years and painted wealthy people of Genoa. Marchesa Brigida came from a noble Genoese family.

Q3399422.s: Rubens loved rich shapes, warm colours and the shine of cloth. His people look alive and full of energy.
Q3399422.i: Imagine what party the marchesa put on this huge collar for.

f: Find the pope's face: it is lit softly.
Look at the pope's clothes: they are solemn.

m.q: How does the pope look?
m.w: The face is gentle and the look kind, with neither anger nor hurry. The pope seems like someone who knows how to listen.

x.q: Why did the pope come to Paris?
o: To open a brand new museum
x.w: In 1804 Pope Pius VII came to Paris to crown the emperor Napoleon. David, Napoleon's painter, portrayed the pope.

Q3399514.s: David was Napoleon's chief painter. He painted important events and people clearly and solemnly, as if on a stage.
Q3399514.i: Imagine what the pope is thinking as he looks at the painter.

f: Find the angels with musical instruments.
Find the angels who sing all together.

m.q: What is the mood of the angels?
m.w: The angels' faces are calm and bright, and they sing and play together, like a great choir. Everything is harmonious and festive.

x.q: What is Hans Memling famous for?
x.w: Memling lived in Bruges and painted very finely: gold embroidery, jewels, folds of cloth. You want to study every little detail.

Q3428050.s: Memling painted in oil in thin layers, so his colours glow like stained glass.
Q3428050.i: Make up the tune the angels are singing and hum it.

f: Find the women in long robes: they have gathered together.
Look at how they stand: they lean forward and listen.

m.q: What do the women feel?
m.w: The women stand and sit close together, leaning forward and holding still. They are afraid to miss a single word.

x.q: What was an oracle in ancient Greece?
o: A workshop where vases were made
A market where fish was sold
A place where gods gave answers
x.w: An oracle was a place in ancient Greece where people put questions to the gods. Priestesses passed on the answers.

Q5164607.s: Waterhouse loved the heroes of old legends and beautiful robes. His pictures look like fairy-tale scenes painted in soft colours.
Q5164607.i: Imagine the question the women asked the oracle.

f: Find baby Jesus: he is the brightest spot in the painting.
Find the Magi: they bow before the baby with their gifts.

m.q: What is the mood of this scene?
m.w: Many people gather around the baby, and all bow respectfully. Bright light and warm colours make the scene festive.

x.q: Who were the Magi?
o: Wise men who came with gifts
x.w: The Magi were wise men from the East. They followed a star and brought the baby gold, frankincense and myrrh.

Q5961888.s: Rubens lived in Antwerp and loved movement, rich shapes and warm colours. Years later he came back to this painting and made it bigger.
Q5961888.i: Imagine what gift you would bring to the baby.

f: Find the tall mountain with snow on top.
Find the tipis by the water and the horses beside them.

m.q: What is the mood of these mountains?
m.w: The mountains are huge, the water is calm, and the camp is quiet. Golden light makes everything peaceful.

x.q: Who lives in the tents by the lake?
o: The Shoshone people of the area
x.w: The painting shows a Shoshone camp: tipis, horses, a campfire. Bierstadt travelled to these mountains in 1859 and made sketches there.

Q7761325.s: Bierstadt loved huge views and golden light. His pictures showed people in the east of America how grand the nature of the West was.
Q7761325.i: Imagine the name of the dog by the camp and what it is doing.

f: Find Mary: she is being crowned.
Find the golden glows around the heads, the halos.

m.q: What is the mood of everyone around?
m.w: The faces are bright and calm, the colours clear and pure, with lots of gold. It looks like a joyful celebration in heaven.

x.q: Who was Fra Angelico?
o: A sailor who lived in Venice
x.w: «Fra» means «brother»: he was a monk and painted bright, joyful pictures. People nicknamed him «Angelic».

Q3797771.s: Fra Angelico loved pure bright colours and gold. The gold in his paintings is real gold leaf, shining like a jewel.
Q3797771.i: Imagine what Mary says when the crown is placed on her head.

f: Find Jesus and Mary: he is placing a crown on her.
Find the golden background: it shines behind the figures.

m.q: What does Mary feel as she is crowned?
o: Quiet joy and a modest heart
m.w: Mary bows her head a little: she accepts the crown quietly and modestly. Her face shows neither fear nor pride.

x.q: Why is the background of this painting golden?
o: No other paint could be found
x.w: Gold was precious and shone, so it was used for heavenly light. You see at once: this is not an ordinary place, but heaven.

Q3797775.s: Lorenzo Monaco was a monk and painter, like Fra Angelico. He loved fine flowing lines and light, delicate colours.
Q3797775.i: Imagine how everyone greets Mary when she stands up with her crown.

f: Find the woman in the black dress with a dark shawl.
Look at her face: it is pale and serious.

m.q: What is the woman's mood?
m.w: Her face is pale and serious, and the colours around her are dark. The picture is quiet and a little sad.

x.q: Where did Goya paint this picture?
o: On a wall in his own house
In a park, on a sheet of paper
On the deck of a big ship
x.w: Goya was no longer young and lived outside the city. He painted straight onto the walls of his house, and later the paintings were moved onto canvas.

Q4901871.s: In old age Goya painted quickly and boldly, in dark colours. His brushstrokes are free and strong.
Q4901871.i: Imagine what the woman is thinking in the quiet.

f: Find the boy: his face is brightly lit.
Find the monkey next to the boy.

m.q: What is the mood of this little scene?
m.w: The boy and the monkey make a funny, almost joking little scene. Warm light picks their faces out of the dark background.

x.q: Where did El Greco come from?
x.w: «El Greco» means «the Greek». He was born on the island of Crete and later lived in Italy and in Toledo, Spain.

Q5966793.s: El Greco painted long, stretched figures and bold bright colours. That is why you never confuse his pictures with others.
Q5966793.i: Imagine what the monkey wants to tell the boy.

f: Find the spiral staircase the girls are walking down.
Find the musical instruments in the girls' hands.

m.q: How do the girls come down the stairs?
o: Run down and laugh out loud
m.w: The girls come down slowly, one after another, and nobody hurries. It all feels like a quiet dream.

x.q: Who posed for the painter as these girls?
x.w: Daughters of the painter's friends posed, among them May Morris, along with his own daughter Margaret.

Q7737113.s: Burne-Jones loved fairy-tale, dreamy subjects and soft, muted colours. His pictures feel like dreams.
Q7737113.i: Imagine the tune the girls play as they come down the stairs.

f: Find the shepherd boy: his face is gentle and bright.
Find the lamb next to the boy.

m.q: How does the boy feel about the lamb?
o: He is scared and runs away
m.w: The boy rests his hand on the lamb and looks kindly. You can see he is protecting it.

x.q: What does «good shepherd» mean?
o: Someone who builds houses of stone
Someone who bakes bread every day
Someone who looks after his flock
x.w: A shepherd looks after sheep. A good shepherd protects every sheep, just as Jesus cares for people.

Q11694421.s: Murillo lived in Seville and loved painting children most of all. In his pictures they are warm and lively, in golden light.
Q11694421.i: Imagine the lamb's name and where they will go together.

f: Find the cup of tea in the lady's hands.
Find the flowerpot nearby and the bonnet on her head.

m.q: What is the mood in this room?
m.w: The lady sips her tea calmly, and the room is light and soft. Everything feels homely.

x.q: Who posed for Mary Cassatt in this picture?
o: A queen from a far-off land
x.w: Lydia, the painter's sister, posed. Mary Cassatt loved to paint the people close to her in ordinary home life.

Q12859910.s: Mary Cassatt was an American who lived in France and showed her work with the Impressionists. She loved to paint home scenes with women and children.
Q12859910.i: Imagine what news the lady shares over tea.

f: Find Rembrandt's face: a warm light falls on it.
Look into his eyes: they are calm and watchful.

m.q: What expression does Rembrandt's face have?
m.w: His eyes are calm and watchful. He looks as if he has thought a great deal and seen a great deal.

x.q: How many self-portraits did Rembrandt leave?
o: Just two or three in his life
About a hundred in his life
More than a thousand in a year
x.w: Rembrandt portrayed himself all his life: in paintings, etchings and drawings there are about a hundred. They show how he grew up and grew old.

Q2267759.s: Here Rembrandt is about fifty-five. The face is thickly painted and the background is dark. So the light seems to come from the face itself.
Q2267759.i: Imagine what Rembrandt, as Paul, writes in his letter.

f: Find Rembrandt's untidy curls.
Find the shadow on his face: it lies across his eyes.

m.q: How does the young Rembrandt seem?
m.w: He looks straight out with an attentive gaze. He seems to be studying himself.

x.q: How did Rembrandt paint the curls?
o: Drew them on top with pencil
x.w: While the paint was still wet, Rembrandt scratched the curls with the other end of his brush. This made thin, light lines.

Q3630753.s: Here Rembrandt is about twenty-two and lives in Leiden. Even then he loved to play with light and shadow.
Q3630753.i: Imagine what young Rembrandt thinks as he looks in the mirror.

f: Find the soldiers in their dress uniforms.
Look at how the people stand and where they look: who is the main person here?

m.q: What is the mood of this scene?
m.w: The people stand stiffly and nobody smiles. The scene is serious and tense.

x.q: What does this painting show?
o: A fairy tale about a dragon
A real event in 1830, in Java
A holiday parade in a square
x.w: This is a real event from 1830 on the island of Java. The Dutch general De Kock detained the Javanese prince Diponegoro. The painting was made soon afterwards.

Q17327791.s: Nicolaas Pieneman painted large pictures of important events. Later the Javanese painter Raden Saleh painted the same scene his own way: one story can look different.
Q17327791.i: Imagine what these people were saying a minute ago.

f: Find the children: they sing along with the grown-ups.
Find the jug: it stands near the family.

m.q: How does this family spend the evening?
m.w: Everyone sings and has fun together, even the children. There is noise, laughter and music all around.

x.q: What do the Dutch call a noisy, messy home?
x.w: The Dutch still say «a Jan Steen household» when a home is noisy and messy. Steen loved painting noisy, merry families.

Q17342250.s: Jan Steen made viewers smile: his pictures are full of funny little details. There is always something to look for and smile at.
Q17342250.i: Make up the song this family is singing.

f: Find Mary, Joseph and the baby Jesus.
Find the landscape behind them: trees and sky.

m.q: How does the family feel during the rest?
o: Worry, they are in a hurry
m.w: Mary, Joseph and the baby have stopped together and are in no hurry. Around them are greenery and soft light.

x.q: Why is the family resting on the road?
o: Heading to Egypt, to a safe place
Going to a fair in the next town
Coming home from a fishing trip
x.w: Mary and Joseph travelled to Egypt so that the baby would be safe. On the way they stopped to rest.

Q3936368.s: Titian loved painting trees, sky and distant hills in soft, warm colours. In his pictures the landscape is part of the story.
Q3936368.i: Imagine what Joseph tells the baby during the rest.

f: Find the straw hat: it has a feather and flowers on it.
Find the palette and brushes in her hand.

m.q: What kind of look does the painter have?
m.w: She looks straight at us with lively eyes and a light smile. You can tell she is glad to meet you.

x.q: Which painting inspired the painter?
x.w: In Antwerp she saw a portrait in a straw hat by Rubens and painted herself in a similar hat. The shadow of the brim falls softly on her face.

Q18719540.s: Vigée Le Brun was the portrait painter of the French queen Marie Antoinette. She painted her light, warm portraits with soft strokes.
Q18719540.i: Imagine what the painter will paint in her next picture.

f: Find the brightest patch of colour.
Find a curving line that runs across the picture.

m.q: What is the picture's mood like?
m.w: The lines swirl and the patches of colour crash into one another. The picture feels full of loud, fast music.

x.q: What did Kandinsky want to show with colour and line?
o: A portrait of an old friend
His home town seen from above
x.w: Kandinsky loved music and «heard» colours. He wanted colours and lines to sound like a melody. That is why there are no ordinary objects in the picture.

Q16543389.s: Kandinsky was one of the first painters to make fully abstract pictures. His «Compositions» are like concerts made of colour.
Q16543389.i: Imagine which instrument would play the brightest patch.

f: Find Jesus and Mary: he is placing a crown on her.
Look at the four saints below: which of them holds a book?

m.q: What is the mood of this coronation?
o: Playful, like a game of tag
m.w: Everything is calm and grand: the saints stand still, and the heavenly scene above is bright. It is a solemn celebration.

x.q: What is happening here?
o: Mary wins a prize for singing
Jesus places a crown on Mary
x.w: Jesus places a crown on his mother Mary: this is how she is honoured as queen of heaven. Angels gather around, and saints stand below.

Q1131263.s: Botticelli divided the picture into two «floors»: saints on earth below, a heavenly celebration above.
Q1131263.i: Imagine what the saints below whisper as they watch the heavenly celebration.

f: Find Mary: angels are lifting her toward the sky.
Find the people below: they look upward.

m.q: What do the people below feel?
m.w: The people raise their faces to the sky and watch in amazement. They are seeing a miracle.

x.q: What is happening to Mary in the painting?
o: She sails away on a ship
x.w: According to tradition, at the end of her life on earth the angels took Mary up to heaven. The painter shows her rising on the clouds.

Q4810381.s: Annibale Carracci founded a school in Bologna with his brother and his cousin. He wanted his pictures to be clear and easy to understand at first glance.
Q4810381.i: Imagine what Mary sees as she rises above the clouds.

f: Find the river: the bank and the sky are reflected in the water.
Find which colours Monet put in the sky.

m.q: What kind of day does the painting show?
m.w: The water is calm, the sky is light, and the colours are warm and bright. It is a quiet, sunny day by the river.

x.q: How did Monet paint?
o: With a tiny brush, hair by hair
x.w: Monet painted with short, quick strokes of different colours. Up close they are dabs, but from afar the water, sky and leaves come alive.

Q10315096.s: Monet wanted to catch a moment on the canvas: how light plays on water at that hour. That is why he often painted outdoors and quickly.
Q10315096.i: Imagine who will walk along this bank in a minute.

f: Find the boy: he is playing with toys on the ground.
Find the leftovers of lunch on the table: a cup, a coffeepot and fruit.

m.q: What is the mood in this garden?
m.w: Sunshine breaks through the leaves and falls in patches on the table and the ground. Everyone minds their own business, and it is quiet.

x.q: Who is the boy who is playing?
o: A little prince from a palace
x.w: This is Jean Monet, the painter's little son. Monet often painted his family in the garden of their house in Argenteuil.

Q18922918.s: Monet painted sunny patches and shadows with colourful strokes, not with grey paint. That is why his shadows are blue and violet.
Q18922918.i: Imagine what the boy is playing and what he is building.

f: Find the houses on the bank: they are reflected in the water.
Find the boat on the water.

m.q: What is the mood of this place?
o: Noisy and crowded, like a port
m.w: The water hardly moves, the houses stand in a row, and the sky is bright. It is quiet and peaceful here.

x.q: In which country did Monet paint this picture?
o: In France, in his native Paris
In Italy, on the canals of Venice
x.w: Monet visited the Netherlands in 1871 and spent several months painting the town of Zaandam: houses, canals, windmills.

Q20180920.s: Monet loved reflections in water. He painted houses and sky in strokes, and in the water they shimmer and tremble.
Q20180920.i: Imagine who lives in one of the houses by the water and what they are doing.

f: Find the actress's face: it is light against the dark background.
Look at her outfit and her hairstyle.

m.q: What is the actress like, judging by the portrait?
m.w: She looks calmly at us, with a clear face. You can tell the actress is used to being seen and carries herself with confidence.

x.q: Where did Antonia Zárate work?
o: On a theatre stage in Madrid
Aboard a big ship at sea
x.w: Antonia Zárate was a well-known actress in Madrid. Goya painted her portrait, as he did for many people he knew.

Q21728497.s: Goya was a court painter in Spain. With a few brushstrokes he could capture a lively gaze and a character.
Q21728497.i: Imagine what part the actress plays on stage this evening.

f: Find the huge whirl of clouds and snow.
Find the tiny people below: next to the storm they look very small.

m.q: What is the mood of this storm?
o: Mighty and wild, like a gale
m.w: The clouds twist into a huge spiral, while the people below are tiny. It feels as if the storm is stronger than everything.

x.q: What did Hannibal, the hero of this picture, do?
o: Drew a map of the whole world
x.w: Hannibal, a commander from Carthage, led his army with elephants over the Alps more than two thousand years ago. It was a hard and bold journey.

Q3646554.s: Turner loved storms, mist and light. He painted the sky as if the colours were swirling and glowing.
Q3646554.i: Imagine what a tiny soldier says as he looks at the huge storm.

f: Find the two babies: Jesus and little John.
Find Mary: the whole family has gathered around her.

m.q: What is the mood among Mary and her family?
m.w: Everyone has gathered close together, and the faces are soft and kind. You can see this is a close family.

x.q: Why is the painting called «The Pearl»?
o: The king found it the best
It was found inside a sea shell
x.w: King Philip IV of Spain thought this the most precious painting in his collection and called it «the Pearl». The name stuck.

Q427390.s: Raphael liked to arrange figures so that together they form a calm triangle. That is why his pictures feel so harmonious.
Q427390.i: Imagine what the babies Jesus and John play while the grown-ups talk.

f: Find Mary with the baby: they sit very close together.
Find the angel and little John beside them.

m.q: How do these people treat one another?
m.w: Mary and the children sit close, with soft faces and gentle gestures. You can see they love one another.

x.q: What can you see behind Mary?
o: A sea harbour full of ships
A dark room with no windows
x.w: Behind the figures Titian painted a landscape: trees, hills and sky. For Venetian painters, nature was as beautiful as people.

Q1112863.s: Titian was the leading painter of Venice. He mixed colours so that skin and cloth look warm and soft.
Q1112863.i: Imagine what gift the angel wants to give the children.

f: Find the yellow crescent moon and the stars. Each star has a glowing ring around it.
Find the tall dark cypress tree on the left. It looks like a green flame.

m.q: What is the mood of this night sky?
o: Calm and flat, like a lake
Empty and dark, with no stars
m.w: The sky twists into whirls and the stars shine in rings. It looks as if the sky is breathing and dancing.

x.q: Where did Van Gogh paint this picture?
o: Outdoors at night, under the sky
Indoors in the day, from memory
From a rooftop, with a telescope
x.w: He was staying in a hospital in Saint-Rémy and remembered the night sky outside his window. He invented part of the village.

Q45585.s: Van Gogh put on his paint in thick strokes. On the canvas it forms little ridges, like a pattern of ropes.
Q45585.i: Imagine: what song is the wind singing in these swirling clouds?

f: Compare the patterns: the man has black and white rectangles, the woman has circles and flowers.
Find the flowery meadow below. The pair seem to stand in a field of blossoms.

m.q: What do these two feel?
m.w: They hold each other, the woman's eyes closed and her cheek against his. The golden glow makes everything warm.

x.q: What is the golden shimmer in this picture made of?
x.w: Klimt stuck thin leaves of gold onto the canvas and painted over them. That is why the picture glitters.

Q698487.s: Klimt's father was a gold engraver, so the painter loved this shine from childhood.
Q698487.i: Invent a name for this golden garden.

f: Find the little patches of sunlight on the dresses and the ground. They shine through the leaves.
Find the dancing couples and the straw hats. How many couples can you see?

m.q: What is the mood of the guests at this party?
o: Tired, everyone wants to go home
Worried, as if rain is coming
m.w: Everyone smiles, chats and dances. Warm light and bright dresses make the party feel joyful.

x.q: Where did this dancing take place?
o: Inside a big striped circus tent
x.w: It was an open-air dance garden in Paris. That is why spots of light from the leaves fall on the people.

Q683274.s: Renoir painted it on the spot, and his friends posed for him. He wanted to catch the cheerful mood.
Q683274.i: Imagine: what music is playing while everyone dances?

f: Find the dark, prickly juniper bush behind the girl.
Look at her pale face and curly hair. Where is she looking?

m.q: What is the look on the girl's face?
m.w: Her lips are closed, and her gaze is calm and a little distant. She does not smile; she seems to be thinking.

x.q: Why is there a juniper bush behind the girl?
o: It grew outside the painter's window
In Italian, it sounds like her name
It is the garden of her family
x.w: In Italian a juniper is «ginepro», and the girl was called Ginevra. The painter hid a word game in the picture.

Q1267893.s: Leonardo softened edges like a smoky haze: this is «sfumato». It is his only painting in America.
Q1267893.i: Imagine: what is she thinking about as she looks at you?

f: Find the forest of long raised spears on the right.
Find the key to the city. The loser holds it out to the winner.

m.q: How did the winner greet the loser?
o: Coldly, as if to an enemy
m.w: The winner does not let his opponent kneel and puts a hand on his shoulder. It is a sign of respect.

x.q: Why is this picture also called «The Lances»?
o: Many tall lances stand on the right
The winner holds one very long lance
Lances lie on the ground at the front
x.w: Velázquez painted the spears in a thick crowd, and the picture was nicknamed after them. They also make the army look big.

Q1133420.s: In 1625 the city of Breda gave in after a long siege. Velázquez showed that a victory can be kind.
Q1133420.i: Imagine: what did the winner say as he put a hand on his shoulder?

f: Find where the path splits in front of the church, and the woman walking on it.
Look at the sky. It is deep blue, even though it is daytime.

m.q: What mood do the dark sky and the wavy lines create?
o: Cosy and sleepy, like a nap
m.w: The sky is deep blue and the church walls seem to sway. So the picture feels alive and a little restless.

x.q: What did Van Gogh do to make the church look alive?
o: Added smoke rising from the roof
x.w: The walls and roof bend a little, as if the church were moving. This is how Van Gogh showed his feelings.

Q1213917.s: Van Gogh painted this church in the town of Auvers-sur-Oise near Paris, where he was living then.
Q1213917.i: Imagine: where is the woman going along the path?

f: Find the pink shoe. It has flown off her foot and is sailing through the air!
On the left find the little statue with a finger to its lips. Where is the young man hiding?

m.q: What does the girl on the swing feel?
o: Tired, she wants to get down
m.w: She soars up in her frothy dress and boldly kicks off her shoe. It is a playful prank.

x.q: Who is pushing the swing?
o: An older man in the shadows
The young man in the bushes
Nobody, she swings on her own
x.w: An older man in the shade pulls the ropes. He does not see the young man hiding in the bushes.

Q2629559.s: Fragonard used soft pinks and greens. His style is called Rococo: light as lace.
Q2629559.i: Imagine: what will the older man say when he sees the shoe on the grass?

f: Find the painter from behind: he is at work. Where is the girl with the trumpet and the book?
Look at the big map on the wall. You can see its folds.

m.q: What is the mood in the studio?
m.w: The painter is busy and the girl poses calmly. Light flows softly from the window and everything feels still.

x.q: What is the painter painting on his canvas?
o: A wreath of leaves for her head
The big map on the back wall
x.w: He has only just started, with the wreath of leaves. The girl plays the muse of history, so she has a trumpet and a book.

Q588695.s: Vermeer loved this picture so much that he never sold it. He kept it all his life.
Q588695.i: Imagine: what will the painter's picture look like when it is finished?

f: Find the yellow sunset sky and the crooked trees with twisting branches.
In the distance look for the ruins of an old abbey on a hill.

m.q: What is the mood of this evening?
o: Warm and quiet, day is ending
Busy and noisy, full of people
m.w: The sun is setting, the sky is a warm yellow and all is still. It feels as if the day is tired and falling asleep.

x.q: What happened to this picture for many years?
o: Everyone thought it was a fake
It was lost at sea, then found
It was hidden in a castle for years
x.w: In 2013 experts proved it is a real Van Gogh. Then the painting was shown to everyone.

Q14866847.s: Van Gogh wrote about it to his brother Theo. He painted in Provence, where the sun is hot and bright.
Q14866847.i: Imagine: what do the birds do here when the sun goes down?

f: Find the spinning wheel on the left. It turns so fast you can hardly see the spokes!
Find the bright room at the back and the big tapestry on the wall.

m.q: How do the women in the front work?
m.w: They are busy: one spins, another winds the wool. You can see they work well together.

x.q: How did Velázquez show that the wheel spins very fast?
o: Painted it blurred, with no spokes
x.w: The wheel seems to tremble and melt away. The painter caught the movement, as a photo would.

Q984058.s: Hidden inside is the myth of Arachne, who argued with Athena about who weaves best. It is two pictures in one.
Q984058.i: Imagine: what pattern would you weave on a big tapestry?

f: Find the basket of fruit right on the edge of the table. It is about to fall towards us!
Find the hands reaching right out of the picture, as if towards you.

m.q: What do Jesus's friends at the table feel?
o: Worry that the food is cold
m.w: They spread their arms and rise from their chairs. You can see they are amazed and cannot believe their eyes.

x.q: What is unusual about Jesus in this picture?
o: He is young, with no beard
He has a shining golden halo
He is very old, with white hair
x.w: Jesus was usually painted with a beard. Caravaggio painted him young, which was bold.

Q318947.s: Caravaggio loved strong light from one side, like a spotlight in a dark room. It makes faces and hands bright against a dark background.
Q318947.i: Imagine: what would you say if you sat at this table?

f: Look at the lady's shiny white dress and her pink sash.
Find the green sofa with soft cushions where she lies.

m.q: What is the look on the lady's face?
o: Sad, as if about to cry
m.w: She looks straight at us, and the corners of her lips lift a little. Her pose is relaxed.

x.q: How many times did Goya paint the lady in this pose?
x.w: They are a pair and hang side by side in the Prado Museum. In the second she is dressed differently.

Q2735507.s: Goya was court painter to the Spanish king. He caught the shine of silk with light, quick strokes.
Q2735507.i: Imagine: what is the lady thinking as she looks at us?

f: Find the painter himself in the crowd. He carries a box of paints and brushes on his head.
Find the bright lightning in the sky and the red glow of fire.

m.q: What feelings can you see on the faces?
o: Fear, yet they help each other
Joy, as at a big festival
m.w: People cover their heads, hug their families and lift up those who fell. They are scared, but they do not leave each other.

x.q: What event is shown in the picture?
x.w: In the year 79 the volcano Vesuvius woke up and buried the Roman city of Pompeii in ash. People ran from the city.

Q2521909.s: Bryullov visited the ruins of Pompeii and spent years painting this huge picture. It is more than six metres wide.
Q2521909.i: Imagine: how did these people escape?

f: Find the lion sniffing the sleeping woman, and the big round moon.
Find the mandolin and the jug of water beside her.

m.q: What is this night like?
o: Busy, like a market in the sun
Calm and magical, like a dream
m.w: The moon shines evenly, the sand is still, the woman sleeps. The lion does not attack; everything is frozen like a dream.

x.q: Did Rousseau ever visit a real desert and see lions?
o: Yes, he sketched it on safari
No, he dreamed it up at home
Yes, he lived in a desert once
x.w: Rousseau hardly ever left France. He looked at lions in the zoo and in pictures, and imagined the rest.

Q1219263.s: Rousseau worked as a customs officer and taught himself to paint. That is why his pictures are simple, bright and like a fairy tale.
Q1219263.i: Imagine: what is the sleeping woman dreaming about?

f: Look at the lady's black dress and her very pale skin.
Find the thin golden straps on her shoulders and her head turned in profile.

m.q: How does this lady seem?
m.w: She stands straight, chin raised, head turned in profile. That is how proud and confident people look.

x.q: What did Sargent change in the picture after the exhibition?
o: He put her dress strap back up
He painted her skin a bit darker
He added flowers on the table
x.w: At first one strap slipped off her shoulder, and visitors did not like it. The painter painted it over.

Q2664039.s: The dark dress and pale skin make a strong contrast. Sargent liked to paint so that a person looked alive and striking.
Q2664039.i: Imagine: what is this lady thinking about?

f: Can you feel the wind? See how it blows the veil and the lady's dress.
Find the little boy below, in the tall grass.

m.q: What is the mood of this day?
o: Fresh and breezy, full of light
Hot and heavy, with no wind
m.w: The sky is blue, the clouds are white and the dress flutters. The day is warm and fresh.

x.q: Where was Monet looking from?
o: From above, on a high balcony
From low down, in the grass
From far away, across the river
x.w: The lady stands on a hill and we look up at her. That is why she seems tall and the sky seems huge.

Q2395218.s: This is Monet's wife Camille with their son Jean. Monet painted quickly, outdoors, to catch the wind and the light.
Q2395218.i: Imagine: what did Jean say to his mum when the wind blew?

f: Find the bright patches of sunlight on the girl's dress and the ground.
Find the little girl and the man beside the young woman. She wears a light dress with blue bows.

m.q: What is the mood of the people in the garden?
o: Hurried, as if they are late
Relaxed, in no hurry at all
m.w: They talk calmly and the sun warms them gently. There is no hurry and no quarrel.

x.q: How did Renoir paint the patches of sunlight?
o: By copying them from a photo
With soft, light dabs of paint
x.w: The strokes are light and small, like droplets. They show how light shines through the leaves.

Q1118456.s: Some critics laughed: they thought the patches of light looked like stains. Today many people love this picture.
Q1118456.i: Imagine: what are these people talking about?

f: Find the big map on the wall.
Look at the officer's wide hat and dark shape. He looks huge!

m.q: What does the girl feel?
o: Shy, as if hiding her face
Bored, waiting for him to leave
m.w: She laughs with her eyes, holds a glass and looks at her guest. Light from the window falls on her face.

x.q: Why does the officer look much bigger than the girl?
o: He sits nearer to us than she
He is much taller than most men
He is the boss, so he is bigger
x.w: He is closer to us, so he looks bigger. It is the same in real life: near things look bigger than far ones.

Q467376.s: Vermeer loved light from a window on the left. It makes the room quiet and the colours bright.
Q467376.i: Imagine: what did the officer tell the girl?

f: Find the sunny patches and the cool blue shadows on the white dresses.
Count the women in the garden. Who is standing and who is sitting?

m.q: What is the mood in this garden?
o: Lazy and sunny, a summer day
m.w: The ladies stroll slowly among the flowers. Light dresses and sunshine make the day soft and warm.

x.q: How did Monet reach the top of his huge picture?
o: He stood on a very tall ladder
He dug a trench for the canvas
A tall friend painted the top
x.w: The picture is taller than a person, and Monet painted it in the garden. He dug a trench and lowered the canvas into it.

Q2734892.s: Monet wanted to paint outdoors, in daylight, not in a studio. Camille, his future wife, posed for almost all the women.
Q2734892.i: Imagine: what are the ladies chatting about in the garden?

f: Find the young knight sleeping under a tree.
Find the two women on either side. What does each one hold?

m.q: What does the knight feel?
o: Restless, tossing in a bad dream
Excited, ready to leap and fight
m.w: He lies still, his face is peaceful and all is quiet. He is having a dream.

x.q: How big is this painting?
x.w: It is tiny: about seventeen by seventeen centimetres. That is smaller than a page of your notebook.

Q552040.s: In his dream the knight is offered two paths: hard work and study, or fun and pleasure. Raphael painted it when he was very young.
Q552040.i: Imagine: which path will the knight choose when he wakes up?

f: Find the golden chain on the philosopher's chest.
Find the white bust and the hand resting on it.

m.q: What is Aristotle's mood?
o: Worried, as if he lost something
Bored, tired of the old bust
m.w: He looks into the distance, not at us, and his hand rests on the bust. You can see he is pondering something.

x.q: Whose bust is the philosopher touching?
x.w: It is Homer, the ancient poet who has been honoured for centuries. Aristotle rests his hand on it as if talking to him.

Q2404992.s: Aristotle was the teacher of Alexander the Great. Rembrandt made the gold chain and the warm light glow out of the dark.
Q2404992.i: Imagine: what would Aristotle say to Homer?

f: Find Mary with her jewelled crown and the baby in her arms.
Look at the tall arches and windows of the church. Where does the light come from?

m.q: What is the mood inside the church?
o: Quiet and tender, full of peace
Lively, with a crowd and music
Dark and gloomy, like a cave
m.w: Mary bows her head to the baby, the church is still and the light is soft. Everything feels peaceful.

x.q: Why is Mary painted so huge?
o: Mary was a very tall woman
The painter ran out of space
To show how important she is
x.w: Mary is almost as tall as the church's columns. The painter made her huge to show how important she is.

Q1747569.s: Van Eyck painted with oil paints, which were new then. He painted every fold and every jewel.
Q1747569.i: Imagine: what quiet song does Mary sing to the baby?

f: Find the table with the red cloth and the open book on it.
Count the men in the picture. Which ones are sitting and which one is standing?

m.q: How do these people look at us?
o: Alertly, as if we just came in
Shyly, looking down at the table
m.w: One seems to rise, the others look up. It feels like the moment a guest enters the room.

x.q: What did these men do?
o: Counted the coins of the town
x.w: They were the heads of a guild that made woollen cloth. They checked that the cloth was good.

Q1170480.s: Rembrandt did not line the men up like a school photo. He caught a lively moment.
Q1170480.i: Imagine: what were these men arguing about before the guest came in?

f: Find the bright moon and the silvery path of light on the water.
Look at the clouds. They glow with moonlight.

m.q: What is the mood of this night?
m.w: The river is calm, all is quiet and the light is soft. It feels as if the night is holding its breath.

x.q: How did Kuindzhi make the moon glow so brightly?
o: He glued silver foil on the moon
He painted it with only white
x.w: Next to the dark land the pale moon seems to burn. This is called contrast.

Q3205872.s: Kuindzhi showed this picture alone in a dark room, and visitors looked for a hidden lamp. But the light was only painted!
Q3205872.i: Imagine: what does the river whisper when the moon shines on it?

f: Find Apollo with the golden glow and the wreath on his head.
Find the blacksmith with a hammer and the glowing forge.

m.q: What do the blacksmiths feel when Apollo comes in?
o: Anger, they want him to go
m.w: They stopped working, turned round and stare. You can see the guest has brought important news.

x.q: Who is Apollo, with the glow around his head?
o: God of fire and the forge
God of the sun and light
God of the sea and storms
x.w: Apollo is the god of the sun, light and the arts. That is why his head glows.

Q247282.s: Velázquez painted an ancient god among simple working men. The smiths have real strong bodies and tired faces.
Q247282.i: Imagine: what news did Apollo bring to the forge?

f: Find the feather and the headband on the woman's head.
Find the quiver and the hatchet beside her. What else lies near?

m.q: What does the woman sitting under the dark sky feel?
o: Joy, as if friends are coming
m.w: She sits alone under a dark sky. The whole picture speaks of sorrow.

x.q: What in the picture shows that the woman is sad?
o: She is alone under dark clouds
She smiles up at a bright sun
x.w: Loneliness, dark clouds and silence make the picture sad. This is how a painter tells feelings without words.

Q1782583.s: Joseph Wright lived in the town of Derby and loved unusual light: candlelight, lamplight, moonlight.

f: Find the two glowing paper lanterns among the flowers.
Find the tall white lilies and the two girls in white dresses.

m.q: What is the mood of the girls?
m.w: The girls light the lanterns seriously and carefully. All around is the hush of a summer evening.

x.q: What time of day is it?
o: Bright midday, the sun is high
x.w: The sky is already dimming and the lanterns are glowing. It is evening twilight, when the light is soft and warm.

Q1560719.s: Sargent painted this picture over two summers. Each evening he had only a few minutes while the light was right.
Q1560719.i: Imagine: what song are the girls humming?

f: Find on the left the fat man riding a barrel. He holds a spit of meat instead of a lance.
Find on the right the thin Lent on a cart. Bread and fish are beside her.

m.q: What do the people on the left, by the barrel, feel?
o: They feast, joke and play games
They work hard in the fields
m.w: They feast, joke and play. It is a noisy party before Lent begins.

x.q: What do Carnival and Lent eat?
o: Carnival: fish. Lent: meat and cake
Carnival: meat. Lent: bread and fish
x.w: During Lent people did not eat meat, so Lent has bread and fish. Carnival has a spit of meat.

Q689236.s: There are more than a hundred people in the picture, and each is busy with something. Brueghel loved to show how people lived in towns and villages.
Q689236.i: Imagine: who will win this funny battle?

f: Find the wheel with spikes next to the young woman. It is the sign of Saint Catherine.
Look where she is looking: not straight at us, but far away.

m.q: What is the look on Catherine's face?
m.w: Her face is steady and serious and her gaze is far away. She looks strong and sure.

x.q: What does the spiked wheel beside her mean?
o: The wheel of her own carriage
A big clock wheel from a tower
Her sign, from an old legend
x.w: In the legend, the wheel meant to punish Catherine broke. So the wheel became her sign.

Q2627034.s: Caravaggio painted real people, not made-up faces. Strong light from the side and a dark background make the figure almost alive.
Q2627034.i: Imagine: what does Catherine see in the distance?

f: Find the black-and-white magpie on the gate.
Look at the shadows on the snow. What colour are they?

m.q: What is the mood of this winter morning?
o: Warm and busy, like a market
Dark and stormy, with a blizzard
m.w: The snow lies soft, the magpie sits calmly and everything is still. You can almost hear the snow creak.

x.q: What colour did Monet paint the shadows on the snow?
x.w: Monet noticed that shadows on snow are not black but coloured, because they reflect the sky. That is why his snow looks alive.

Q4429116.s: Monet went out into the frost to catch the real winter light. His white snow is full of colours.
Q4429116.i: Imagine: what is the magpie chattering about on the gate?

f: Find the soldier with the big banner.
Find Mary with the baby. She sits high up on the steps of the throne.

m.q: What is the mood of this ceremony?
o: Tense, as if before a battle
m.w: People stand and kneel, and Mary looks kindly. Everything moves slowly and festively.

x.q: What unusual thing did Titian do?
o: He put Mary off to one side
He put Mary in the exact middle
He dressed Mary in plain grey
x.w: Before, Mary was painted in the middle. Titian moved the throne sideways, and the scene came alive.

Q572697.s: Titian was the master of Venetian colour. His red cloths and banners glow like fire.
Q572697.i: Imagine: what is the baby whispering to Mary?

f: Find the clock and the candles. What do they show?
Find the hand tucked into the waistcoat.

m.q: What is Napoleon's mood?
m.w: He stands straight and looks stern and calm. You can see he is used to deciding important matters.

x.q: What do the clock and the burnt-down candles tell us?
o: He was waiting for his lunch
He was giving a night party
x.w: The candles are almost burnt out and the clock shows early morning. The painter showed that Napoleon worked through the night.

Q1313605.s: Jacques-Louis David was Napoleon's court painter. He painted him as great and hard-working.
Q1313605.i: Imagine: what important letter did Napoleon work on all night?

f: Find the pearl necklace and the ribbons she is holding.
Find the window on the left and the yellow jacket with white fur.

m.q: What does the woman with the pearls feel?
o: Sad, as if she had cried
m.w: She stands still and her face is calm. She seems to be daydreaming a little.

x.q: Where does the light come from?
o: From the window on the left
From a window on the right
From a candle on the table
x.w: Soft light comes in from the window and lands on her face, her jacket and the pearls. That is why they glow.

Q151143.s: Vermeer painted pearls with little light dots of paint. They look round and shiny.
Q151143.i: Imagine: where is she going, with pearls around her neck?

f: Find the boy being comforted by his mother, and the little boy with a bowl of water.
Find the sheep beyond the door of the workshop.

m.q: What do the grown-ups around the boy feel?
m.w: They bend towards him and look at him closely. His mother hugs and kisses him.

x.q: Where does this scene take place?
o: In a barn full of hay
x.w: Joseph was a carpenter. Wood shavings lie on the floor and a workbench stands by the wall.

Q960157.s: The Pre-Raphaelites painted very sharply and brightly, in tiny detail. Millais painted people and things from real life.
Q960157.i: Imagine: what does his mother whisper to comfort him?

f: Find the huge clay jar. Drops of water shine on it.
Find the glass that the old man hands to the boy.

m.q: What is the mood of the water-seller scene?
m.w: The faces are calm and dignified and nobody hurries. Dark tones make the scene solemn.

x.q: What is in the glass of water?
x.w: People say a fig was put in the water to keep it fresh. Velázquez painted it as a small light spot.

Q2627810.s: Velázquez painted this picture when he was about twenty. He painted ordinary people as proudly as kings.
Q2627810.i: Imagine: what will the boy say when he has finished drinking?

f: Find the stick in the shepherdess's hands.
Find the cows in the meadow and the mountains far away.

m.q: What is the shepherdess's mood?
o: Sad, as if she is lost
m.w: She stands calmly, and around her is a peaceful meadow with cows. There is no hurry and no worry.

x.q: Who is a shepherdess?
x.w: A shepherdess takes cows or sheep to the meadow. She makes sure they do not get lost.

Q512971.s: Bouguereau painted so smoothly that you can hardly see brushstrokes. He liked to paint country children.
Q512971.i: Imagine: what are the shepherdess's cows called?

f: Find the three men sleeping under the tree and the table on the tree.
Find the roast piglet and the egg on little legs.

m.q: What do the lazy men feel?
o: Lively, ready for a long walk
m.w: They lie with their eyes closed, content and still. There is so much food around that they are too lazy even to move.

x.q: What walks up to people by itself in this country?
o: A big fish and a loaf of bread
A roast piglet and a walking egg
A roast cow and a big cheese
x.w: In the fairy-tale land of Cockaigne food comes to your mouth by itself. An egg runs with a spoon and a piglet carries a knife on its back.

Q556553.s: Cockaigne is a fairy-tale land where nobody works. Brueghel joked about how funny laziness looks.
Q556553.i: Imagine: what would you eat first in the land of Cockaigne?

f: Find the old man in the black hooded cloak.
Find the little man inside the glass globe. What does he hold?

m.q: What is the old man's mood?
o: Excited, off to a big party
Friendly, glad to chat with all
m.w: He walks along, grim, wrapped in a dark cloak. He does not look around at all.

x.q: What is the little man in the glass globe doing?
x.w: While the old man is busy with gloomy thoughts, the thief takes his purse. Brueghel shows how important it is to look around.

Q2059447.s: This is a proverb picture. Whoever is cross with everyone does not see what happens right beside him.
Q2059447.i: Imagine: what will the old man say when he notices his purse is gone?

f: Find the yellow, red and blue little squares.
Find the white and pale stripes. They look like city streets.

m.q: What music do you hear when you look at this picture?
m.w: The squares blink and jump like the lights of a big city. It feels as if fast jazz is playing.

x.q: What inspired Mondrian to paint this picture?
o: A map of Paris and church bells
x.w: Mondrian lived in New York and loved the rhythm of boogie-woogie. The streets became like piano keys to him.

Q2915406.s: Earlier Mondrian painted black lines. Here the lines are coloured, like blinking lights.
Q2915406.i: Imagine: which instrument does this picture «play»?

f: Find the knight on horseback who gives half his cloak to a poor man.
Find Mary with her baby and the angels at the top.

m.q: What is the mood of the people in the picture?
o: Fun, a noisy game in the street
m.w: Everyone bends towards those who need help. Some give food, some give drink, some give clothes.

x.q: How many kind deeds are shown in the picture?
x.w: These are the seven works of mercy. They are: food, drink, clothes, shelter, and care for the sick, prisoners and the dead.

Q2626595.s: Caravaggio fitted all seven kind deeds onto one dark street in Naples. Light picks the people out of the darkness.
Q2626595.i: Imagine: what eighth kind deed could the painter add?

f: Find the red four-sided shape on the white field.
Look at its sides. They tilt a little, as if the shape is about to turn.

m.q: What do you feel looking at a red square on white?
o: Cosy and warm, like a home
m.w: There is one colour and one shape. So the picture feels simple and strong, like a signal.

x.q: What is this picture made of?
o: A red door in a white wall
Just a shape and a colour
A tiny red house in snow
x.w: Malevich called his style Suprematism. He wanted to show pure shape and pure colour.

Q17086791.s: Malevich was one of the first to paint pictures with no objects in them. His most famous picture is the «Black Square».
Q17086791.i: Imagine: what would the red square say if it could talk?

f: Find the pomegranate in the woman's hand. A bite has already been taken.
Find the dark green dress and the ivy behind her.

m.q: What is Proserpine's mood?
m.w: She looks aside, her lips are closed and her gaze is serious. You can see she is sad and lost in thought.

x.q: What happened in the myth because of the pomegranate?
o: Part of each year she lives underground
It turned her into a pomegranate tree
She could then fly over the clouds
x.w: This is how people long ago explained the seasons. When Proserpine is underground, the cold time comes.

Q977777.s: Jane Morris, a friend of the painter, posed for this picture. The Pre-Raphaelites loved fairy tales, legends and rich colours.
Q977777.i: Imagine: what does Proserpine dream about as she looks at the pomegranate?

f: Find the red sun low above the trees.
Find Mary on the donkey and Joseph with a saw. They are lost among the village people.

m.q: What is the mood of this winter village?
o: Busy, people go about their day
m.w: People do ordinary things: they walk, work and warm themselves. Nobody notices Mary and Joseph.

x.q: Where does this Bible story take place?
o: In a snowy village of his time
In a hot, sandy desert town
In a shiny marble palace city
x.w: Brueghel set an ancient event in a village of his own time, under snow. This made the story feel close to viewers.

Q375216.s: Brueghel loved to hide the main characters among many people. Try to find them yourself!
Q375216.i: Imagine: what are the people by the house where taxes are collected talking about?

f: Find the girl. She has looked up from her music and gazes right at us.
Find the sheet music on the table and the window on the left.

m.q: What did the girl feel when she was interrupted?
o: Joy, she is about to sing
m.w: She has lifted her eyes from the music and looks straight at us. It seems someone called her.

x.q: Where does the light in the room come from?
o: From the window on the left
From a window on the right
x.w: Light from the window lights the girl's face and the fabrics. The rest of the room is in soft shade.

Q1219698.s: Vermeer left very few paintings, about thirty-five. Each is a quiet scene with soft light.
Q1219698.i: Imagine: what was she asked when she looked up from her music?

f: Find the dove with a flower in its beak.
Find the sundial behind the woman.

m.q: What does the woman with closed eyes feel?
m.w: Her eyes are closed and her head is tilted back. She seems to be seeing a lovely dream.

x.q: What did the dove bring?
x.w: In tales and myths the poppy brings sleep. So the painter spoke of quiet sleep and peace.

Q2712679.s: Rossetti loved heroes from poems. Here he painted Beatrice, the heroine of a book by the great poet Dante.
Q2712679.i: Imagine: what is she dreaming about?

f: Find the sea in the distance. What colour is it?
Find the brightest, sunniest patches in the picture.

m.q: What is the mood of this walk?
m.w: Bright light and warm colours create a light summer mood.

x.q: What kind of light is Joaquín Sorolla famous for?
o: The glow of snowy winter dusk
x.w: Sorolla was born in Valencia, by the Mediterranean Sea. He became famous for his sunny pictures.

Q6065609.s: Sorolla often painted outdoors, quickly, to catch the sun. He is called the painter of light.
Q6065609.i: Imagine: where does this walk lead, and what is there at the end?

f: Find the grey and black horses. They trot along, strong and powerful.
Find the raised hooves and the flying manes.

m.q: What is the mood of the horses?
m.w: The horses stride strongly and their manes fly. You can see they are full of strength.

x.q: How did Rosa Bonheur learn to paint horses so well?
o: She sketched real horses at a market
She copied horses from old books
She practised on a wooden toy horse
x.w: She went to the horse market in Paris and made sketches. She even got permission to wear trousers to work more easily.

Q40432.s: The picture is huge: more than five metres long. The horses look alive.
Q40432.i: Imagine: what are these horses called, and where are they going?

f: Find the bird trap.
Find the tiny skaters on the ice. Who glides along, and who just stands?

m.q: What is the mood of the people on the ice?
m.w: Everyone has come out into the fresh air. People skate, stroll and chat.

x.q: Who skates on the ice in Avercamp's pictures?
o: Rich and poor, side by side
Only rich people in fur coats
x.w: Avercamp painted everyone together: the rich in fine clothes and the poor in plain ones.

Q3373691.s: Hendrick Avercamp painted winter fun. His pictures hold hundreds of tiny people, as if we were looking from a hill.
Q3373691.i: Imagine: which skater is going fastest?

f: Find the saint who holds a model of a city in his hands.
Find the peacock on the balcony, the carpet on the wall and the golden ray from heaven.

m.q: What does Mary feel?
m.w: She folds her hands and bows her head. She calmly accepts the good news.

x.q: What does Saint Emidius hold in his hands?
o: A little model of a town
x.w: It is little Ascoli, a town he protected. Saint Emidius was seen as the guardian of that town.

Q642198.s: Crivelli painted very sharply, brightly and with patterns, with lots of tiny details.
Q642198.i: Imagine: what can be seen from the window of Mary's house?

f: Find Jerome at his desk inside the tall wooden study.
Find the birds in front and a small lion deep in the hall.

m.q: What is Jerome's mood?
m.w: He reads quietly, and all around is order and peace. Nobody disturbs him.

x.q: Why is there a lion painted nearby?
o: It guards the books from thieves
The legend: he healed a lion's paw
The painter needed to fill a corner
x.w: An old legend about the kind Jerome tells so. The lion became his friend and stayed near him.

Q2715353.s: Antonello da Messina painted very finely with oil paints. The light in the windows and arches looks real.
Q2715353.i: Imagine: which book is Jerome reading?

f: Find Copernicus. He stands looking up at the sky.
Find the stars and the bright light above his head.

m.q: What does Copernicus feel?
o: Tired, as it is very late
Worry, as if he is lost
m.w: He looks up and his face glows. He seems amazed at the beauty of the sky.

x.q: What did the scientist Copernicus work out about the Earth?
o: The Sun circles round the Earth
The Earth goes round the Sun
The Earth is a flat plate
x.w: People used to think the Sun moves around the Earth. Copernicus understood it is the other way: the Earth and planets go around the Sun.

Q6609114.s: Jan Matejko, a Polish painter, made large pictures of heroes of his country. Copernicus is a great Polish scientist.
Q6609114.i: Imagine: what did Copernicus see in the sky?

f: Look at the blue dress. It shimmers like silk.
Find the lady's hat.

m.q: What is this lady like?
o: Sad, as if about to cry
m.w: Her face is soft and her look is calm. Her whole bearing speaks of kindness and dignity.

x.q: How did Gainsborough paint the shine of silk?
o: By pressing silver foil on it
With tiny dots, one by one
x.w: Gainsborough painted with a long thin brush, quickly and lightly. The dress looks airy and shimmers.

Q3700536.s: Thomas Gainsborough was an English master of portraits. He loved to paint light, airy dresses.
Q3700536.i: Imagine: where is this lady going?

f: Find the big dark beret and the fur collar.
Find the hand that rests on the stone ledge.

m.q: How does Rembrandt look?
o: Shy, as if wanting to hide
Sad, as if he lost something
m.w: He looks straight at us, his head slightly turned, his pose proud. He looks successful.

x.q: How many times did Rembrandt paint himself?
o: Just three times, as a boy
Dozens of times, all his life
x.w: He often painted himself in a mirror: young, cheerful, and later old. So we can see how his face changed.

Q3630751.s: Rembrandt loved golden light out of the dark: the face is brightly lit and the background is dark.
Q3630751.i: Imagine: what did Rembrandt see in the mirror as he painted this?

f: Find the red tree with curving branches.
Find the deep blue colours around the tree.

m.q: What do you feel looking at a red tree on a blue background?
m.w: Red and blue are very different, so the tree stands out strongly. The branches twist as if the tree were moving.

x.q: What happened to Mondrian's paintings later?
o: He added more and more tiny details
He simplified to lines and squares
He turned to painting only the sea
x.w: First Mondrian painted trees, then simpler and simpler: the branches became lines. That is how his famous grids came about.

Q3818263.s: Mondrian began with trees and became famous for squares and lines. This picture is a step on that road.
Q3818263.i: Imagine: what does the tree see in the evening?

f: Find the garlands of fruit and leaves above Mary.
Find the knight in shining armour who kneels.

m.q: What does the kneeling knight feel?
m.w: He bends his knee and looks at Mary with respect. He is thankful for her help.

x.q: What does the knight thank Mary for?
o: For a good harvest of grapes
For a victory in the battle
x.w: The Marquis Gonzaga believed Mary had helped him in battle. That is why she is called «Madonna of Victory».

Q965822.s: Mantegna painted figures sharply, as if they were made of stone. He loved details: garlands, patterns, armour.
Q965822.i: Imagine: what does the marquis whisper to Mary?

f: Find the headscarf and the shawl on the young woman.
Look at the soft, slightly blurred background around her.

m.q: What is the milkmaid's expression?
o: Bored, in a hurry to leave
m.w: She sits with her head bowed and a gentle gaze. She seems to be dreaming about something.

x.q: Where did Goya paint this picture?
o: In Spain, in a royal palace
In Italy, in the old city of Rome
In Bordeaux, a city in France
x.w: Goya came from Spain but spent his last years in France. There he painted ordinary people from the streets.

Q2088930.s: Goya was over eighty, but he painted freely and boldly, with light strokes.
Q2088930.i: Imagine: what is the milkmaid taking to the market?

f: Look how tenderly Mary holds the baby. Their heads are close together.
Find the see-through veil on Mary's head.

m.q: What feeling does this picture show?
o: Worry, as if danger is near
m.w: Mary holds the baby carefully against her, her head bent. It shows a mother's love.

x.q: What does the word «Madonna» mean in pictures?
o: A name for Mary, Jesus's mother
A name for a kind of angel
x.w: In Italian it means «my lady», a name for Mary. Raphael painted her with the baby many times.

Q2535486.s: Raphael painted soft, beautiful people. His Madonnas are known all over the world.
Q2535486.i: Make up a lullaby that Mary could sing to the baby.

f: Find the sick young man in bed.
Find the doctor beside the bed.

m.q: What does the young man in bed feel?
m.w: He lies without strength, his head tilted back. You can see he feels unwell and sad.

x.q: What did the doctor guess about the cause of the illness?
o: He caught a cold in the rain
He was ill from being in love
He ate something bad at dinner
x.w: When a beautiful woman came in, the young man's heart pounded. The doctor understood it was an illness of feelings, not of the body.

Q3590926.s: David painted this picture when he was young, to win a competition and go to study in Rome. He won!
Q3590926.i: Imagine: what will the doctor tell the young man's father?

f: Find the angel Gabriel and Mary.
Find the clear carafe of water and the bouquet of flowers.

m.q: What is the mood of this scene?
o: Quiet, calm and full of wonder
m.w: The angel and Mary are calm, the room is silent and the light is soft. Everything moves slowly.

x.q: How did Memling show clear glass?
o: He painted it in solid pale blue
He painted glints and water inside
He drew just a thin black outline
x.w: He carefully painted glints on the carafe and the water inside. That is why the glass looks real.

Q9392232.s: Hans Memling, a Netherlandish master, painted fine details and soft colours. His pictures are calm and gentle.
Q9392232.i: Imagine: what news did the angel bring Mary?

f: Find the cart with hay and the tiny people working in the field.
Find the blue sky above the yellow field and the hill in the distance.

m.q: What is the mood of the summer field?
m.w: A hot yellow field, a blue sky, and work going on in the field. It is a hot summer day.

x.q: Which colours did Van Gogh put side by side to make them glow?
x.w: Yellow and blue are very different, and next to each other they look even brighter. Van Gogh loved such pairs.

Q4892867.s: Van Gogh painted this right in the field, in the heat, quickly. He lived then in the south of France, in Provence.
Q4892867.i: Imagine: what is the cart carrying, and where to?

f: Find the woman with a baby in her arms, at the front left.
Find the two men walking in front of everyone.

m.q: What is the mood of the crowd?
m.w: They walk together, step by step, with a straight gaze. They are sure they are doing the right thing.

x.q: What are these people doing?
o: Walking to a big country fair
Marching off to a far-away war
x.w: These are workers who came out together to ask peacefully for fair work and pay. They were called the «fourth estate».

Q1199809.s: The painter worked on this picture for about ten years and painted people from his own village.
Q1199809.i: Imagine: what will the man walking first say aloud?

f: Find the mule that Napoleon is riding.
Find the snow and the narrow mountain track.

m.q: What is Napoleon's mood in the mountains?
m.w: He rides calmly, wrapped in his cloak, his gaze thoughtful. This is not a parade but a hard journey.

x.q: Why does Napoleon ride a mule here, not a handsome horse?
o: His horse ran away that morning
Mules are surer on steep paths
x.w: In the mountains with steep drops a mule is safer than a horse. Napoleon really did cross the Alps on a mule.

Q1224572.s: Delaroche wanted to show the truth without decoration. David painted the hero on a horse, Delaroche showed how it was.
Q1224572.i: Imagine: what does the guide tell Napoleon along the way?

f: Find the apple in the woman's hand.
Find the flowers in her hair and in the green background behind her.

m.q: What is this woman's mood?
o: Sad, as if she had cried
m.w: Her gaze is soft and slightly to the side, her lips are calm. She seems to be dreaming of something.

x.q: Why was this group of painters called the «Pre-Raphaelites»?
o: They were all pupils of Raphael
They loved art from before Raphael
x.w: They wanted to paint honestly and brightly, like the old masters before Raphael. They loved sharp details and rich colours.

Q4936154.s: Rossetti was not only a painter but a poet. He loved to paint beautiful women with flowers and fruit.
Q4936154.i: Imagine: what is the apple for?

f: Find the dark laurel leaves behind the woman.
Find her bright red cloak and her gentle smile.

m.q: What is the mood of the woman in the red cloak?
o: Worried, as if waiting for news
m.w: She has a faint, mysterious smile. The dark greenery behind her makes her face look even lighter.

x.q: Why is a laurel painted behind her?
o: It grew by the painter's house
It marks the town she lived in
x.w: The painter made a hint: the words «laurel» and «Laura» sound alike. A laurel branch was also a sign of fame.

Q595707.s: Giorgione, a master from Venice, loved soft shadows and warm deep colours. Very few of his pictures survive.
Q595707.i: Imagine: what is this woman's secret?

f: Find the man with the big sword in the centre.
Look at the table. Light falls on the faces of the people around it.

m.q: What is the mood of the gathered men?
m.w: They have joined their swords in an oath. Faces are stern and the room is solemn and quiet.

x.q: What are the people at the table doing?
x.w: According to a historian, the Batavians swore to fight for freedom from Rome. Rembrandt showed that moment.

Q2234397.s: The picture was once huge, but it was later cut down, and only part survives. Rembrandt used thick golden paint, and light seems to come from the table.
Q2234397.i: Imagine: what oath are these people taking?

f: Find the tall man on the raised platform: it is George Washington.
Look at the men in wigs and coats in the large bright hall.

m.q: What is the mood of the people in the hall?
m.w: People do important things carefully. They stand, talk and sign the paper.

x.q: What were these people signing?
o: A letter to the king of England
A peace treaty to end a war
x.w: In 1787 in Philadelphia people agreed on the country's main law. It is called the Constitution.

Q2701637.s: The picture was painted in 1940, more than a hundred and fifty years after the event. The painter studied old portraits to show real faces.
Q2701637.i: Imagine: what law would you suggest for your family?

f: Find the maid with the candle. Its light falls on Peter's face.
Find Jesus in the background. He is looking back at Peter.

m.q: What does Peter feel?
o: Proud, as if he had won
m.w: He spreads his hands and his face looks embarrassed. You can see he feels uneasy.

x.q: Where does the light in this dark room come from?
o: A fire burning in the hearth
A lantern held by a soldier
One candle held by the maid
x.w: The candle lights the faces and everything else sinks into the dark. That makes the scene tense.

Q3874247.s: Rembrandt was a master of light and shade. Even a small candle lights a whole scene for him.
Q3874247.i: Imagine: what will Peter say to Jesus when they meet again?

f: Find the table with the white cloth, the bottles and the glasses.
Find the people raising their glasses.

m.q: What is the mood of the friends?
m.w: The friends raise their glasses together and smile. The warm garden makes the party sunny.

x.q: Who are the people in the picture?
o: Fishermen after a day at sea
x.w: They are friends of Krøyer. They gathered in Skagen, in the north of Denmark, and painted side by side.

Q3135789.s: Krøyer loved to paint light: warm evening or midday light. In this picture the garden shines with sun.
Q3135789.i: Imagine: what are the friends toasting?

f: Find the lamb on the table. It has soft wool.
Look at the dark background around it. The lamb seems to glow against it.

m.q: What is the mood of the picture with the lamb?
o: Busy, like a farm at dawn
m.w: The lamb lies calmly and all is quiet. Light falls softly on its wool.

x.q: What does the lamb in the picture mean?
o: A sign of strength and speed
A sign of wool and trading
A sign of kindness and calm
x.w: Jesus is called the «Lamb of God». The lamb is a sign of kindness and gentleness.

Q4693305.s: Zurbarán painted bright light on a dark background, like Caravaggio. The wool and the rope look real.
Q4693305.i: Imagine: what is the lamb thinking about?

f: Find the big dog. The emperor rests his hand on it.
Find the golden chain on the emperor's chest, the sign of the Order of the Golden Fleece.

m.q: What is the emperor's mood?
o: Shy, as if he feels embarrassed
Cheerful, as if about to laugh
m.w: He stands straight and looks stern. His hand rests calmly on the dog.

x.q: Why did the painter put a dog beside him?
o: To show that he loved hunting
To show loyalty and add life
To show how big his house was
x.w: A dog was a sign of loyalty. With it, the emperor looks not only stern but alive.

Q19798137.s: Titian became the favourite painter of Emperor Charles V. He could paint cloth and fur so they look real.
Q19798137.i: Imagine: what is this dog called?

f: Find Sadko. He stands alone and looks at the beauties.
Find the line of girls in delicate dresses walking one after another.

m.q: What does Sadko feel?
o: Fear, he wants to swim away
m.w: He has frozen and gazes at the beauties. You can see he is amazed.

x.q: Where does this fairy tale take place?
o: In a forest, in a wizard's hut
On a mountain, in a snow castle
Under the sea, in a king's realm
x.w: In the old tale Sadko played his gusli and came to the underwater kingdom of the Sea King. Repin showed it in green light, as if through water.

Q4404599.s: Repin, a great Russian painter, painted «Sadko» when he was still young. His underwater light is green and blue.
Q4404599.i: Imagine: which girl will Sadko choose?

f: Find the three disciples sleeping below.
Find the pink sky at dawn.

m.q: How does Jesus feel?
o: Sad and worried, but he prays
m.w: He kneels with folded hands and his gaze lifted. He asks for strength.

x.q: What are Jesus's disciples doing?
o: They are walking to the town
x.w: The disciples were tired and fell asleep. Jesus was left alone with his prayer.

Q1131110.s: Giovanni Bellini was a master of light. His dawn sky is pink and gold, as if a real sun were shining.
Q1131110.i: Imagine: what are the disciples dreaming about?

f: Find Mary in her white dress and blue cloak.
Find the little angels around her and the crescent moon beneath her feet.

m.q: What feeling does Mary show?
o: Worry, as if lost in the sky
m.w: She looks up, her face is bright and her hands are folded. Warm golden light surrounds her.

x.q: What is under Mary's feet?
x.w: In pictures like this the moon is a sign of purity. Mary seems to stand on it as on a cloud.

Q2456003.s: Murillo painted soft, gentle faces and golden light. He was much loved in Spain.
Q2456003.i: Imagine: what are the little angels whispering about?

f: Find the girl in the shiny white dress. She holds the door.
Find the soldier in the black uniform.

m.q: What do the girl and the soldier feel as they part?
o: Excited, as if off to a party
Bored, as if waiting for tea
