x.w: Manet often painted Victorine. She put on a bullfighter's costume, as if for the theatre.

Q72650.s: Manet loved bold flat patches of colour. His paintings were unusual, and viewers did not always understand them.
Q72650.i: Imagine: what does Victorine feel in such a costume?

f: Find Mary and the two little boys beside her.
Find the landscape behind them: hills and distance.

m.q: What is the feeling in this group?
m.w: Mary leans towards the little boys, who play beside her. Everything is soft and peaceful.

x.q: Who is the boy next to the baby Christ?
o: A little shepherd boy with a lamb
A neighbour's son from next door
x.w: John the Baptist was Jesus's cousin. Raphael often painted them together.

Q560057.s: Raphael painted very many Madonnas and each one differently. His faces are soft and his poses calm.
Q560057.i: Imagine: what game are the two little boys playing?

f: Find the hands folded in his lap: there are rings on the fingers.
Find the landscape behind him: hills and trees.

m.q: What does this man look like?
m.w: He sits upright and looks serious. You can tell he is rich and proud of himself.

x.q: What did Agnolo Doni do for a living?
o: A priest in a village church
A cook at the king's court
x.w: Agnolo Doni traded in cloth in Florence and loved buying beautiful paintings.

Q2515309.s: Raphael painted two matching portraits: husband and wife. He took the pose from Leonardo's Mona Lisa.
Q2515309.i: Imagine: what cloths does Agnolo sell?

f: Find Boreas's billowing cloak.
Find the bird and the trees bending in the wind.

m.q: How does the weather look in the picture?
m.w: His clothes tear in the wind, the trees bend and the colours are cold. It seems an icy north wind is blowing.

x.q: Who is Boreas?
x.w: The ancient Greeks thought gods controlled the winds. Boreas brings cold from the north.

Q4944794.s: Waterhouse loved myths and fairy tales, and his pictures are like illustrations for them. He painted handsome heroes and lush nature.
Q4944794.i: Imagine: how do the trees feel when Boreas blows?

f: Find the baby: he is tightly wrapped in swaddling.
Find the stone frame, like a little window.

m.q: What is the feeling in this scene?
m.w: Everyone stands close and keeps silent. The faces are serious and eyes are turned to the baby.

x.q: Where was the baby taken?
o: To the temple, to give thanks
To the palace, to see the king
To the doctor in the next town
x.w: By custom parents brought their first baby to the temple. There the old man Simeon met him.

Q3212033.s: Mantegna painted figures so clearly that they look carved from stone. He admired ancient sculptures.
Q3212033.i: Imagine: what does Simeon whisper to the baby?

f: Find the little statue in his hand.
Find the coin and the tablet with an inscription.

m.q: How does this man seem?
m.w: He looks straight at us with shoulders back, holding interesting things. He clearly knows his own worth.

x.q: Who was Jacopo Strada?
o: A famous general of the king's army
A tailor at the king's court
x.w: He collected old coins and statues. That is why he has a statuette and a coin in the picture.

Q698993.s: Titian was about eighty when he painted this portrait. He painted boldly, with broad brushstrokes.
Q698993.i: Imagine: what story would the statuette tell?

f: Find Joseph's coat in the brothers' hands.
Find the dog: what is it doing?

m.q: What does the father Jacob feel?
m.w: He is told his son is lost and he bows his head. The faces around are bewildered.

x.q: How did the story of Joseph end?
o: He went home and became a farmer
He stayed a shepherd for life
He became an important man in Egypt
x.w: Joseph grew up and became the helper of Egypt's ruler. Later he met his brothers and forgave them.

Q2273901.s: Velázquez painted this in Italy when he was about thirty. There he studied the great masters.
Q2273901.i: Imagine: what will Jacob say when he sees the coat?

f: Find the tiny painter with his easel.
Find the loop of the river, shaped like an ox's yoke.

m.q: What do you feel on the left, where the storm gathers?
o: Worry and the power of nature
Joy, like at a summer picnic
m.w: On the left are dark clouds and rain, and the trees are ruffled. On the right are light and quiet.

x.q: What unusual thing did Cole paint in a corner of the picture?
x.w: The small figure on the hill is the painter himself at his easel. Next to huge nature he looks tiny.

Q3172259.s: Thomas Cole founded the Hudson River School: the name for American painters who painted majestic nature.
Q3172259.i: Imagine: what is the painter thinking as he watches the storm over the river?

f: Find Christ placing the crown on Mary.
Find Mary Magdalene with long loose hair.

m.q: What is the feeling of this scene?
m.w: Mary bows her head while Christ gently places the crown on her. Gold shines all around.

x.q: What is a polyptych?
o: A picture on one huge wall
x.w: A polyptych is made of several boards. Such pictures stood on church altars.

Q3907532.s: Gentile da Fabriano loved gold, bright fabrics and soft faces. His pictures are like jewels.
Q3907532.i: Imagine: what words does Christ say to welcome Mary?

f: Find the sheep that have wandered into the wheat.
Find the girl with a lamb on her lap.

m.q: What does the shepherd feel beside the girl?
o: Fear, he has spotted a wolf nearby
m.w: He shows the girl a moth and does not watch the flock. Meanwhile the sheep go into the field.

x.q: What does the word hireling in the title mean?
o: Someone who sings in the field
x.w: A shepherd must watch his flock, but he is distracted. The picture quietly reminds us: do your job.

Q7739744.s: Hunt and his Pre-Raphaelite friends painted very brightly and in detail: you can see every blade of grass. He painted this outdoors in a field.
Q7739744.i: Imagine: what will the owner say on seeing the sheep in the wheat?

f: Find the road running between the tall rye.
Find the tall pines and the clouds in the sky.

m.q: What do you feel looking at this wide space?
m.w: The rye sways to the horizon and the sky is huge. You breathe easily and widely.

x.q: Which plant grows here like a golden sea?
x.w: Bread is baked from rye. Its ears sway in the wind like golden waves.

Q4396378.s: Shishkin was born in the town of Yelabuga and loved the Russian forest and fields. He was called the singer of the forest.
Q4396378.i: Imagine: where does this road lead?

f: Find the baby on Mary's lap.
Find the soft landscape behind them.

m.q: What is the feeling between mother and baby?
m.w: Mary gently holds the baby, and he nestles trustfully against her. They are happy together.

x.q: How did Raphael make faces soft?
x.w: He blended light and shadow almost invisibly, so the faces look alive and gentle.

Q327780.s: Raphael lived only thirty-seven years, but left a great many beautiful paintings.
Q327780.i: Imagine: what is Mary telling the baby?

f: Find Saint Barbara by the fireplace: she is reading a book.
Find the lamb on the left panel.

m.q: What is the feeling in the room by the fireplace?
m.w: It is warm by the fire, and Barbara reads quietly. Everything is clean and calm.

x.q: What everyday things did the master paint very exactly?
o: A piano, a clock, a sofa
A stove, a sink, a fridge
x.w: Campin painted household things so exactly that it is as if we have looked into the room ourselves.

Q3136106.s: Robert Campin was one of the first masters to paint everyday life and the home, not only golden backgrounds.
Q3136106.i: Imagine: what is Barbara reading in her book?

f: Find the white headdress with little wings.
Find the folded hands and the lowered gaze.

m.q: What is the girl in the bonnet like?
m.w: She looks down and keeps her hands still. You can tell she is quiet and reserved.

x.q: What did the painter paint especially delicately?
o: A heavy fur coat on her shoulders
The thin veil and soft shadows
A big necklace of golden beads
x.w: Rogier van der Weyden painted the light cloth and soft shadows delicately. The face seems alive.

Q3399411.s: Rogier van der Weyden was the city painter of Brussels. He was one of the most famous masters of his time. His pictures are full of feeling.
Q3399411.i: Imagine: what is this girl thinking about?

f: Find the fan in the dancer's hand.
Find her bracelet and fancy dress.

m.q: What is Lola's character?
m.w: She stands with her head up and smiles at us. It seems she knows she is beautiful.

x.q: Where was Lola from?
o: Italy, singing in a grand opera
x.w: A Spanish troupe performed in Paris in 1862. Manet saw Lola on stage and painted her.

Q44124.s: The poet Charles Baudelaire wrote verses about Lola, and they were written on the picture's frame.
Q44124.i: Imagine: what dance has Lola just danced?

f: Find the silver embroidery on the brown costume.
Find the sword at the king's side.

m.q: What does the king look like?
m.w: He stands straight and his gaze is calm and cool. He knows he is a king.

x.q: What was Velázquez at the court of King Philip?
x.w: Velázquez served at court for many years and painted the king several times.

Q1090371.s: Velázquez painted silver and cloth with light strokes. Close up you see only patches, but from afar the embroidery glitters.
Q1090371.i: Imagine: what would you ask the king?

f: Find the red cape and the white lace vestment.
Find the pope's attentive eyes.

m.q: What is the pope's gaze like?
m.w: He looks straight and intently. You can tell he is used to deciding important matters.

x.q: Who is the pope?
o: The mayor of the city of Rome
x.w: Paul V headed the Church in Rome. Caravaggio painted him in 1605, just after his election.

Q1460271.s: Caravaggio painted on a dark background. Light picks out the face and hands like a beam in a dark room.
Q1460271.i: Imagine: what would the pope say as he looked at us?

f: Find the man busy with his work on the bank.
Find the evening sky and the dark hills in the distance.

m.q: How does the evening by the river seem?
m.w: The light fades, and everything around is dark and quiet. It seems night is about to begin.

x.q: What does an earthstopper do before a hunt?
x.w: In the evening he blocked the holes' entrances, and in the morning the hunt began. So the fox could not hide.

Q2397685.s: Joseph Wright of Derby loved painting the light of candles, the moon and fire. He was friends with scientists and inventors.
Q2397685.i: Imagine: what is this man thinking about as he works at dusk?

f: Find Christ on a donkey in the crowd: he is very small.
Find the people in masks: how many are there?

m.q: What do you hear looking at this crowd?
o: The soft ticking of a clock
m.w: A crowd in masks, flags, a band. Everything shouts and booms like a carnival.

x.q: How did Ensor know so many masks?
o: He went to balls every week
A mask-maker taught him at school
His family sold masks in a shop
x.w: His parents' shop in Ostend sold masks and souvenirs. He drew them from childhood.

Q3203172.s: The painting is huge, more than four metres long. Ensor showed a whole city as a parade of masks.
Q3203172.i: Imagine: what are the people in masks shouting?

f: Find the flower in the picture: what is it like?
Find the abundant wavy hair.

m.q: What kind of girl is in the portrait?
m.w: She looks thoughtful and her face is soft. She seems lost in far-off thoughts.

x.q: Which group of painters did Rossetti belong to?
x.w: The Pre-Raphaelites loved medieval fairy tales and the beauty of nature. They painted with bright, pure colours.

Q6901173.s: Rossetti was a painter and a poet at once, and his pictures sound like poems.
Q6901173.i: Imagine: what does she want to do with the flower?

f: Find the white walls of the cottages: they seem to glow.
Find the dark sky with a soft glow.

m.q: How does this night seem?
m.w: The white cottages glow in the dark and all around is still. It seems miracles happen at night.

x.q: How did Kuindzhi amaze viewers?
o: He painted using only his fingers
His light looked real, like a lamp
He used only black and white
x.w: He mixed his paints so that light seems to come from inside the picture.

Q3206123.s: Kuindzhi once showed a single picture in a dark hall, and people queued up to see it.
Q3206123.i: Imagine: who lives in this cottage, and what does he do at night?

f: Find the soap bubble: it is about to break away.
Find the boy with the pipe.

m.q: What does the boy feel?
m.w: He holds still and watches the bubble so as not to pop it. You must blow gently.

x.q: What did soap bubbles mean to painters of that age?
o: That life is fragile, like a bubble
That the boy is from a rich family
x.w: A bubble is beautiful but soon bursts. Painters reminded us how quickly time flies.

Q3231193.s: The boy was called Léon, and Manet painted him more than once. Manet loved dark backgrounds and bright patches of light.
Q3231193.i: Imagine: what wish would you make looking at the bubble?

f: Find the clouds in the sky and their reflection in the water.
Find the far shore of the lake.

m.q: What do you feel on the shore of this lake?
m.w: The water is calm, clouds drift and the shores are far. You want to be quiet and gaze into the distance.

x.q: What does the word Rus in the title mean?
o: The name of a local fisherman
An old name for the homeland
The name of an old boat
x.w: Levitan wanted to show the wide spaces of his homeland. That is why the picture is called Lake. Russia.

Q4332076.s: Levitan was a master of mood: he could show quiet, sadness and joy in a landscape. He was called the singer of Russian nature.
Q4332076.i: Imagine: what sounds can be heard on the shore of the lake?

f: Find the path covered with yellow leaves.
Find the lone woman in dark clothes on the path.

m.q: What kind of autumn is in the picture?
m.w: Leaves yellow and fall, the path is empty and the woman walks alone. It is quiet and a little sad.

x.q: Who helped Levitan paint the figure of the woman?
o: His sister, who posed for him
x.w: Levitan was friends with the Chekhov brothers. The figure on the path was painted by Nikolai Chekhov, brother of the writer Anton Chekhov.

Q4337609.s: Levitan was only nineteen when he painted this. It was bought by the famous collector Pavel Tretyakov.
Q4337609.i: Imagine: where is the woman going, and what is she thinking?

f: Find the bunches of grapes the woman is cutting.
Find the bright sunlight on her face and arms.

m.q: How does the woman feel among the grapes?
o: Fear, she is in a hurry
m.w: She smiles and reaches for the vine while the sun warms her face and arms.

x.q: How did Bryullov show the heat of midday?
o: With cool blues and pale mist
With warm light and deep shadows
x.w: The sun beats down, the skin glows and the shadow is very deep. You feel the heat at once.

Q4205253.s: Bryullov lived in Italy for many years and loved sunny, bright pictures. His The Last Day of Pompeii made him famous across Europe.
Q4205253.i: Imagine: what will the woman make from these grapes?

f: Find the troika of horses pulling the sleigh.
Find the smartly dressed people in the snow in bright coats and scarves.

m.q: What do you feel at this fair?
m.w: Bright colours, jingling bells, people laughing and riding. It is the merriest day of winter.

x.q: What is celebrated at Shrovetide?
o: The start of the new school year
x.w: Shrovetide is a merry week before Lent. People bake pancakes, ride sleighs and see winter off.

Q18683418.s: Kustodiev painted a bright Russia: merchants, fairs and festivals. He kept painting like this even when he was ill and could not walk.
Q18683418.i: Imagine: how many pancakes would you eat during Shrovetide week?

f: Find the woman holding the red, white and blue flag high.
Find the boy with a pistol in each hand. He runs beside Liberty.

m.q: How does the woman with the flag feel?
o: Confused: she has lost her way
Brave: she leads the crowd on
Happy: she is off to a party
m.w: She strides ahead and looks back, calling everyone to follow. The flag is high and her face is determined.

x.q: Who is the woman with the flag?
o: Liberty herself, drawn as a woman
The queen of France in a cap
x.w: She is not a real person. Delacroix drew Freedom as a brave heroine who leads the people.

Q29530.s: Delacroix painted this in the year of a real uprising in Paris. Rich and poor, grown-ups and children fight side by side.
Q29530.i: Imagine: what is the boy with the pistols shouting?

f: Find the little white animal in the lady's arms.
Look at her long fingers: how do they rest on the fur?

m.q: What is the lady's face like?
o: Calm, with a bright, alert look
m.w: She has turned her head to the side and looks there with attention. Her face is quiet, but her eyes are lively.

x.q: What did the ermine mean in a portrait?
o: That she is a great hunter
x.w: In those days a white ermine was a sign of purity and dignity. The little animal is snow white, as it should be.

Q474338.s: The lady and the ermine turn their heads the same way. It is as if the picture caught a living moment.
Q474338.i: Imagine: what are the lady and the ermine looking at? Who just came into the room?

f: Among the blue irises, find one white flower.
Find the long green leaves: they bend like ribbons.

m.q: What is the mood of these flowers?
o: Happy, as if they are dancing
Sleepy, as if they are napping
Sad, as if they are drooping
m.w: The leaves bend and curl, the colours are bright, and the flowers reach up. The irises seem to sway in a dance.

x.q: Where did Van Gogh get the dark outlines and bright flat colours?
x.w: Van Gogh collected Japanese prints and loved their clear lines. Here the irises are outlined like in a Japanese drawing.

Q2282256.s: Van Gogh painted these irises in the garden of the hospital where he was resting. The one white flower among the blue ones stands out at once.
Q2282256.i: Imagine: what does the white iris say to its blue neighbours?

f: Find the white lamb on the altar in the middle.
Find Adam and Eve: they stand at the ends of the top row.

m.q: What is the mood of the people walking to the lamb?
o: Loud fun, like at a fair
Tired, they want to go home
m.w: They come from every side, bow their heads and kneel. Everything around is calm and solemn.

x.q: Why does the altarpiece have so many panels?
o: It closes on weekdays, opens on feast days
It is a giant jigsaw made of many pieces
The painter could not pick just one picture
x.w: The panels were closed on ordinary days and opened on holidays. Then everyone saw the bright colours inside.

Q734834.s: The altarpiece was begun by Hubert van Eyck and finished by his brother Jan. The oil paint is so fine that you can see blades of grass and sparkling jewels.
Q734834.i: Imagine: what gift would you bring to the lamb?

f: Find the big clock on the wall.
Find the lamps: bright circles of light glow around them.

m.q: What is the mood of the night café?
m.w: Red and green seem to quarrel, and the floor slopes steeply away. The people sit slumped and weary.

x.q: What time is it in the café?
x.w: The clock shows just after twelve, and it is dark outside. It is night.

Q674846.s: Van Gogh painted this café over three nights in a row and slept in the daytime. He used red and green to show the restlessness of the night.
Q674846.i: Imagine: what are the people at the tables talking about in the middle of the night?

f: Count the haulers who pull on the straps.
Find the young man in the light shirt: he lifts his head and adjusts his strap.

m.q: How do the barge haulers feel?
o: Happy: they are out for a walk
m.w: Their heads are low, their bodies lean, and the straps cut into their shoulders. It is hard, but they do not stop.

x.q: What are these people doing?
o: Going to market by the river
Hauling in a big fishing net
Pulling a heavy barge by ropes
x.w: There were no engines on barges then, so people pulled them against the current. This work was called hauling.

Q175628.s: Repin travelled to the Volga and painted real barge haulers from life. Each one has his own character: an old man, a young lad.
Q175628.i: Imagine: what does one of the haulers dream about as he walks along the sand?

f: Find Mary with the baby right in the centre.
Find the horsemen on horses far in the distance.

m.q: How do the people look at the baby?
o: Sleepy and calm, as at home
m.w: Many raise their hands, press them to their chests or cover their faces. They are amazed.

x.q: Why is the picture almost all brown?
o: It is unfinished: no colour yet
He ran out of all other paints
It was painted at night by candle
x.w: Leonardo left for Milan and stopped work. We see the beginning: first the drawing and shadows, colour later.

Q1638622.s: The picture stayed unfinished, but it shows how Leonardo worked. He loved to show people's feelings through faces and gestures.
Q1638622.i: Imagine: what would you whisper to the baby if you came closer?

f: Find the musicians with their instruments in the centre.
Find the big jars of wine.

m.q: What is the mood at the feast?
o: Quiet and serious, like in church
m.w: Music plays, guests chat, and everyone is dressed in their best. They came to have fun.

x.q: What miracle happened at this wedding feast?
o: Jesus fed a crowd with bread
Jesus calmed a storm at sea
x.w: When the wine ran out, Jesus turned water into wine. This painting tells that story.

Q185255.s: This is the biggest painting in the Louvre, and it hangs opposite the Mona Lisa. Veronese painted a feast like the ones of his time in Venice.
Q185255.i: Imagine: who would you sit next to, and what would you taste?

f: Find the baby being passed over Mary's shoulder.
Find little John behind the low wall.

m.q: What does the family feel for each other?
o: Warmth: they hold the baby gently
Excitement: they are playing a game
m.w: Mary, Joseph and the baby are pressed close and reach toward each other. Everything in the picture speaks of closeness.

x.q: What is a round painting called?
x.w: In Italian, tondo means round. This picture is a tondo, like a big plate.

Q1473546.s: Michelangelo was above all a sculptor, so his people are strong and solid like statues. His colours are bright and pure.
Q1473546.i: Imagine: what song would Mary sing to the baby?

f: Find the book in her hand.
Find the frilly collar and the ribbon at her neck.

m.q: How does the girl feel?
o: Sleepy: she is about to doze off
Sad: the story makes her cry
At peace: lost in her reading
m.w: Her head is bent, her eyes are on the book, and her shoulders are relaxed. She is cosy.

x.q: How did Fragonard paint the collar?
x.w: Fragonard painted fast, and his strokes show. That is why the lace looks light and alive.

Q2629423.s: Fragonard painted fast and lightly, and you can see his brush marks. The picture seems caught in a moment, like a sketch.
Q2629423.i: Imagine: what story is the girl reading?

f: Find the ruined church wall among the oak trees.
Find the tiny people walking toward the arch.

m.q: What feeling does this wood with a ruin bring?
o: Quiet, misty and a little sad
Busy and cheerful, like a fair
m.w: Bare oaks, mist, grey colours and silence. The people are very small.

x.q: Why are the people so tiny?
o: Because the painter was in a hurry
So the trees and ruins look huge
x.w: Friedrich wanted nature and the old walls to look great, and a person small.

Q334360.s: Friedrich loved quiet, lonely places. The ruins in the picture remind us of Eldena Abbey, which still stands today.
Q334360.i: Imagine: where are the tiny people going, and what will they find beyond the arch?

f: Find the glowing letters on the wall.
Find the king with the jewels: he jerks back.

m.q: How does the king feel?
o: Proud and pleased with his feast
Amused, he thinks it is a joke
Shocked, he jerks back in fear
m.w: He leans back, flings out his arms, and his eyes are wide. The guests jump up and spill their wine.

x.q: What did the mysterious letters warn the king about?
o: That his rule would soon end
That the feast was too noisy
x.w: A hand wrote on the wall that the proud king's days were numbered. The Bible tells it so.

Q1167932.s: Rembrandt was a master of light and shadow. The brightest light in this picture comes from the letters and picks faces out of the dark.
Q1167932.i: Imagine: what would you do if letters began to glow on your wall?

f: Find the big map on the wall behind her.
Look at her blue jacket: how many shades of blue can you see?

m.q: How does she feel as she reads the letter?
o: Quiet hope: she waits for news
m.w: She holds the letter close with both hands, her lips slightly parted. The room is silent.

x.q: Where does the light come from?
o: From a candle on the table
From a big lamp above her
From a window on the left
x.w: Soft light comes from the left, as if from a window. It falls on her face, her jacket and the map.

Q166937.s: Vermeer used a very expensive blue paint. It was made from a precious stone called lapis lazuli.
Q166937.i: Imagine: who wrote this letter, and what does it say?

f: Find the tall dark cypress tree.
Find the bright star and the thin moon on either side of it.

m.q: What is the mood of this night?
m.w: The sky swirls, and the star and moon glow in rings. Everything seems to move.

x.q: What does the cypress look like in this picture?
x.w: It stretches upward like a tongue of flame and reaches for the sky. Van Gogh loved cypress trees.

Q5930190.s: Van Gogh painted this in the south of France. His stars are big glowing rings, and his curly strokes make the sky seem to breathe.
Q5930190.i: Imagine: where are the two walkers going, and what are they talking about?

f: Find the Japanese pictures on the wall behind him.
On the prints, find a mountain with a snowy top and a lady in a kimono.

m.q: What is his face like?
o: Kind and calm, with soft eyes
Strict and stern, like a teacher
Sly, as if he has a secret
m.w: He sits upright, his hands folded, his gaze soft. He looks like a reliable friend.

x.q: Who was Père Tanguy?
o: A paint seller who helped artists
A sailor who had sailed to Japan
A baker who fed hungry artists
x.w: He sold paints in Paris and let artists pay later when they had no money. Van Gogh was his friend.

Q13528770.s: Van Gogh adored Japanese prints and collected many. Here they fill the whole background with bright flat patches.
Q13528770.i: Imagine: which Japanese picture would you hang in your room?

f: Find Mary's long neck, like a swan's.
Find the tiny man with a scroll on the right.

m.q: What is Mary's mood?
o: Cheerful, she is about to laugh
m.w: Her eyes are lowered, and her face is smooth and quiet. The baby lies loosely across her lap.

x.q: Why are the neck and fingers so long?
o: The model was very, very tall
x.w: Parmigianino stretched his figures to make them graceful. Painters of his time loved that look.

Q867403.s: The picture was left unfinished: the row of columns was never completed. The baby and angels are stretched too, like in a fairy tale.
Q867403.i: Imagine: what would the tiny man say, looking up at such a tall lady?

f: Find the calm face of Jesus with closed eyes.
Find Veronica in the lower corner: she holds a cloth.

m.q: How does Jesus feel among the noisy crowd?
m.w: His eyes are closed and his face is quiet, though grimaces surround him. He is the calmest in the picture.

x.q: How do the kind and the unkind people differ in this picture?
o: The kind ones wear very big hats
Unkind faces are twisted, kind ones calm
Only the unkind ones are painted in colour
x.w: Bosch made the unkind people strange and crooked, so we notice the calm, kind faces.

Q680128.s: The picture is almost all faces, like a close-up. Bosch was famous for his imagination: he invented odd creatures and unusual faces.
Q680128.i: Imagine: give the funniest face in the crowd a name and say what it is shouting.

f: Find the two women sitting on the sand.
Find the strip of green-blue sea behind them.

m.q: What is the women's mood?
o: Calm and relaxed, in no hurry
m.w: They sit unhurried, their poses are loose, and their faces are quiet. Nobody is in a rush.

x.q: Where did Gauguin sail to paint pictures like this?
o: To Iceland, an island of ice
To Japan, a land of islands
x.w: Tahiti is an island in the Pacific Ocean. Gauguin liked its bright colours and unhurried life.

Q930535.s: Gauguin painted in big flat patches of bright colour, almost like a poster. He chose colours not as in real life but as he liked them.
Q930535.i: Imagine: what would you talk about with these women, sitting beside them on the sand?

f: Find the lizard clinging to the boy's finger.
Find the rose behind the boy's ear.

m.q: How does the boy feel?
o: Joy: he enjoys playing with it
Calm: he is posing for a portrait
m.w: He snatches his hand back, his eyebrows are raised and his mouth is open. The picture catches one moment.

x.q: How does the light fall in the picture?
o: Soft and even light from every side
From a candle held by the little boy
Strong from one side, dark behind
x.w: The light picks out the face, shoulder and lizard, and the rest is in shadow. Like a stage under a spotlight.

Q585437.s: Caravaggio painted ordinary people from life, not made-up beauties. That is why the scene feels alive, like a snapshot.
Q585437.i: Imagine: what will the boy do a second later: cry or laugh?

f: Find the three people at the cliff edge. One wears a red dress.
Find the little sailing boats on the sea.

m.q: How do the people feel as they look down?
o: Bored, they are waiting for a boat
Sleepy after a long, hot walk
Amazed, but careful at the edge
m.w: One has crept carefully to the edge and peers down. The others admire the view.

x.q: What are these white cliffs made of?
x.w: Chalk is a soft white rock. We also write with it on a school blackboard.

Q1787143.s: Friedrich painted this after a wedding trip to the island of Rügen. The tree branches frame the view like a window.
Q1787143.i: Imagine: what did the three travellers see down there?

f: Find the woman in the black-and-white striped dress with flowers at her chest.
Find the man behind her: he looks up through opera glasses.

m.q: How does the woman in the box behave?
m.w: She sits upright and looks out at the hall. Her face is calm and she is in no hurry.

x.q: What is the man looking at through the glasses?
o: The actors far away on stage
x.w: People went to the theatre not only for the show but to be seen. The man studies the audience above.

Q74339.s: Renoir showed this picture at the very first Impressionist exhibition in 1874. He painted light in quick, light strokes.
Q74339.i: Imagine: whom did the man spot through the glasses?

f: Find the tiny monk on the shore.
Find the narrow strip of sea and the huge sky above it.

m.q: How does the monk feel?
m.w: He stands alone and gazes at the sea. There is nobody around.

x.q: Why does the monk look so small?
o: He is only a small child
The painter ran out of paint
The sky above him is vast
x.w: The sky fills almost the whole picture. Next to it a person is like a dot.

Q693746.s: Friedrich liked to paint people from behind. We look where they look, and feel as if we stand beside them.
Q693746.i: Imagine: what is the monk thinking as he looks at the sea?

f: Find the group of people carrying Jesus.
Find Mary, who is faint with grief: her friends hold her up.

m.q: What do the women beside her feel?
o: Sadness and care for each other
Impatience: they want to leave soon
m.w: One woman has grown weak, and the others hold her gently. The faces are sad and kind.

x.q: Why was this picture ordered?
o: A king wanted it for his big hall
A mother wanted to remember her son
A school wanted it for its classroom
x.w: Atalanta Baglioni asked Raphael to paint it in memory of her son. It is full of quiet sorrow.

Q2500226.s: Raphael arranged the figures in a smooth wave, and your eye follows it. He could make even sad scenes balanced and harmonious.
Q2500226.i: Imagine: what might one of the carriers want to say to the others?

f: Find the mother in the black dress: she stands very straight.
Find the two girls in white pinafores. One sits with her foot tucked under her.

m.q: What is the mood in this family?
m.w: The father sits to one side, the mother stands stiffly, and the girls look at us. They do not look at one another.

x.q: Who are these people?
x.w: Degas stayed with them in Florence and painted a big family portrait.

Q2622172.s: Degas painted no stiff show-off portrait but real life: each person has their own thoughts. The mother wears black.
Q2622172.i: Imagine: what will Dad say when he turns to the family?

f: Find the little unicorn in her arms.
Find the pillars at the sides and the landscape behind her.

m.q: What is the expression of the lady with the unicorn?
o: Stern and proud, like a queen
Calm, soft and a little shy
m.w: She looks at us gently and quietly, without a broad smile.

x.q: What does the unicorn mean in the portrait?
o: That she lives in a forest
x.w: An old legend says only a kind, pure heart can tame a unicorn. It is a sign of gentleness.

Q2344396.s: Later the unicorn was painted over, and the lady turned into a saint with a wheel. Restorers cleaned off the later layers, and the unicorn came back.
Q2344396.i: Imagine: give the unicorn a name and say what it likes.

f: Find the herd of cows coming along the path.
Find the river in the valley and the faraway mountains.

m.q: What kind of day is it in the valley?
m.w: The sky is heavy and grey, the trees are bare, and the people walk slowly. It is late autumn.

x.q: What season is it in the picture?
x.w: The trees have no leaves, the colours are brown and grey, and the herd is heading home.

Q698254.s: Bruegel painted a series of pictures about the seasons, and this is one of them. He loved to show the life of country people.
Q698254.i: Imagine: what sounds can you hear in this valley?

f: Find the golden laurel wreath on his head.
Find the two long sticks in his hands: one ends in a little hand.

m.q: What is Napoleon's face like?
o: Shy and nervous, like a pupil
Proud and stern, like a statue
Cheerful and relaxed, ready to chat
m.w: He looks straight ahead and sits upright like a statue. His face is still and commanding.

x.q: How did the painter show that Napoleon is very powerful?
o: He stands small among his soldiers
He sits at a table in a plain coat
He sits high up, in gold and fur
x.w: Napoleon is huge and in the centre, on a high throne. Gold, fur and velvet glitter around him.

Q1282840.s: Ingres loved smooth, clear lines. He painted so exactly that fur, velvet and gold look as if you could touch them.
Q1282840.i: Imagine: what would you say to this stern emperor if you met him?

f: Find the round mirror behind Circe. Who is reflected in it?
Find the pig near her feet.

m.q: What does Circe feel?
o: Kind and caring, she offers a drink
Sad and lonely, she wants a friend
Sly and pleased: she has a plan
m.w: She smiles and holds out the cup. But the smile hides a trick.

x.q: What was in Circe's cup?
o: A drink that makes men fall asleep
A potion that turns men into pigs
Sweet juice for a thirsty guest
x.w: In the myth, Circe's drink turns travellers into pigs. Ulysses escaped this trick.

Q39537.s: Waterhouse painted heroines of myth in bright colours and with tiny details, like illustrations to a fairy tale.
Q39537.i: Ulysses is clever. Imagine how he will outwit Circe.

f: Find Mary: she reads a book at the table.
Find Joseph's workshop on the right and the mousetrap.

m.q: What is the mood of this room?
o: Gloomy, like a long rainy day
m.w: Mary reads, lilies stand on the table, and the light is soft. Nobody makes a sound.

x.q: What is Joseph doing in the right-hand panel?
x.w: Joseph was a carpenter. Mousetraps lie in his workshop.

Q285392.s: The altarpiece has three panels. The painter set a holy story in an ordinary home of his time, with a table and bench.
Q285392.i: Imagine: what else is Joseph making besides mousetraps?

f: Find the pipe and tobacco on the seat.
Find the red tiled floor and the door behind the chair.

m.q: What feeling does the empty chair give?
o: Busy and cheerful, full of friends
Excited, as if guests are arriving
Quiet, a little lonely: he just left
m.w: The chair is empty and all is still. It feels as if its owner has just left.

x.q: Why does an empty chair look like a portrait of the painter?
o: His paintbrushes lie on the seat
His pipe and tobacco lie on it
His straw hat hangs on its back
x.w: Van Gogh told about himself through things: a plain chair, a pipe, tobacco. It is a portrait without a person.

Q1118295.s: Van Gogh loved yellow and painted in thick paint. The yellow chair glows beside the red floor and the green-blue door.
Q1118295.i: Imagine: where did the chair's owner go, and when will he be back?

f: Find the woman in front of the mirror: she is powdering her face.
Find the big bird on the wallpaper.

m.q: How does the woman carry herself?
o: Shy, as if caught by surprise
m.w: She looks straight at us as if we just walked in. She is not embarrassed at all.

x.q: Why does the picture frame cut off the man on the right?
o: The painter ran out of time to finish
So it looks like a quick glimpse
x.w: It happens when you peek into a room for a moment. Manet painted the scene as if spotted by chance.

Q536024.s: Manet painted modern Paris life in big flat patches and pure colours. The young Impressionist painters learned a lot from him.
Q536024.i: Imagine: who is the man on the sofa, and what will he say?

f: Find the three workers scraping the floor.
Find the bottle by the wall.

m.q: How do the workers feel?
m.w: They are bent over, their backs curved, their hands pressing hard on the tools. Everyone is busy.

x.q: What are the workers doing to the floor?
o: Scraping it to make it smooth
Washing it with soap and water
x.w: They scrape the top layer off the wooden floor with special tools. That makes it even and smooth.

Q1766454.s: Caillebotte looks down at the floor from above, and the boards run away in rows. The official exhibition refused this picture: workers were rarely painted then.
Q1766454.i: Imagine: what song are the workers humming?

f: Find Mary and John: they stand at the sides and look up.
Find the little angels in the sky.

m.q: What feeling do the people's calm faces show?
o: Excited joy, as on a holiday
Worry and hurry, as if running late
m.w: The people stand quietly and their faces are soft. The gentle landscape and clear sky add to the stillness.

x.q: How did Raphael arrange the figures?
o: In a jumble, all piled together
In a long line, one behind another
Evenly: the same on both sides
x.w: Similar groups stand on the left and right, and everything looks even. This balance gives a feeling of peace.

Q598913.s: Raphael painted this when he was very young, about twenty. He learned from the master Perugino, and here are the same soft landscapes and clear light.
Q598913.i: Imagine: what does the little angel see from above?

f: Find the couple under the umbrella: husband and wife hold hands.
Find the baby's tiny hand peeking out from under the cloak.

m.q: What does this couple feel?
o: Cheerful, off on a seaside trip
m.w: They are leaving home. Their faces are serious, but their hands hold each other tightly.

x.q: Where and why are these people going?
o: On a holiday by the seaside
Out fishing on a quiet sea
To a new country, for a new life
x.w: In those days many people sailed abroad to find work and a better life. The white cliffs of England stay behind.

Q958245.s: Brown painted the faces outdoors, on dull days, so the light would be real and not made up.
Q958245.i: Imagine: which three things would you take if you were leaving home?

f: Find the red-orange hair and the attentive gaze.
Find the blue background swirling in waves.

m.q: What is the painter's face like?
m.w: He looks straight at us, his brows drawn together and his lips pressed. His gaze is focused.

x.q: Why did Van Gogh paint himself so often?
o: He loved looking at his face
He had no money to pay models
A museum asked him to do it
x.w: He set up a mirror and painted his own face. That cost nothing.

Q22329831.s: The waves in the background echo the lines of his hair, and the brushstrokes are easy to see. Van Gogh painted not only how a person looks but how they feel.
Q22329831.i: Imagine: what would this man tell you if he could speak?

f: Find John pouring water from a bowl over Jesus's head.
Find the white dove above them.

m.q: What is Jesus's face like?
o: Worried, as if something is wrong
m.w: His eyes are lowered and his hands folded. He stands still like a statue.

x.q: How did Piero make the picture orderly and calm?
o: He filled it with loud, bright colours
He painted a wild, stormy sky
Dove, bowl and Jesus line up straight
x.w: The straight line from top to bottom makes the picture even and quiet.

Q2632688.s: Piero della Francesca was also a mathematician. His people stand still like columns, and the light is clear and soft.
Q2632688.i: Imagine: what sounds can you hear by the river in such quiet?

f: Find the woman at the edge of the picture with a greenish face.
Find the very tall man and the very short man walking together in the distance.

m.q: What is the mood in the cabaret?
o: Noisy and lively, a night out
Calm and orderly, like a lesson
m.w: Many people, bright light and a buzz of voices. The evening is in full swing.

x.q: Why is the woman's face greenish?
o: Bright lamplight in a dark hall
She is feeling a little unwell
The painter mixed the wrong paint
x.w: Under artificial light colours change. Lautrec was not afraid to show it.

Q3607521.s: Lautrec made posters for the Moulin Rouge: bright flat colours and clear lines. He often went to the cabaret and drew performers from life.
Q3607521.i: Imagine: what music is playing in the cabaret, and what are they whispering about at the table?

f: Find the two men: they stand with their backs to us.
Find the old oak tree and the moon in the evening sky.

m.q: What mood are the two men in as they watch the moon?
o: Wild and stormy, like a gale
Excited and lively, like a game
Quiet and dreamy, in no hurry
m.w: The men stand close and gaze calmly at the sky. All around is quiet and dim.

x.q: Why did Friedrich paint the men from behind?
o: He could not paint faces well
So we look at the moon with them
They were hiding from the cold wind
x.w: We cannot see their faces, so we look where they look. It feels as if we stand beside them.

Q232087.s: Dark trees and rocks against a bright sky were a favourite trick of Friedrich's. Moonlight makes the night feel like a fairy tale.
Q232087.i: Imagine: what are the two whispering about under the moon?

f: Find Mary and the baby in the old, tumbledown stable.
Find the crowd of curious people pushing closer.

m.q: What is the mood of the people around?
o: Boredom: they are in a queue
m.w: The people crowd together, stretch their necks and peek over shoulders. Everyone is very interested.

x.q: What gifts did the wise men bring?
x.w: The wise men brought gold, frankincense and myrrh. These were the most precious gifts.

Q4680634.s: Bruegel painted the Bible scene among ordinary people of his own time. They wear Dutch clothes and have funny faces.
Q4680634.i: Imagine: what does a curious man from the crowd say when he sees the baby?

f: Find the little squares of red, blue and yellow.
Find the straight lines: the painting stands on a corner, like a diamond.

m.q: How would this picture sound?
o: Slow and sleepy, like a lullaby
Soft and sad, like falling rain
m.w: The squares hop like notes, and the colours are bright and quick.

x.q: What is boogie-woogie?
o: The name of a big city
A game played with a ball
x.w: Boogie-woogie is fast jazz for dancing. Mondrian loved jazz and dancing.

Q1248830.s: Mondrian painted this in New York and never finished it. Bits of coloured paper are still stuck on it.
Q1248830.i: Imagine: if the picture were a song, which instruments would play in it?

f: Find the white square: it is tilted a little.
Find the edges: the white on white is slightly different.

m.q: What do you feel looking at white on white?
o: Loud and busy, like a street
Quiet and calm, like fresh snow
Cross and fiery, like a bonfire
m.w: Everything is white and soft, and nothing disturbs you. It feels as if silence stands there.

x.q: What is this painting made of?
o: A white square on a white background
A black circle on a grey background
A red square on a yellow background
x.w: Malevich took two almost identical whites. That is why you must look very carefully.

Q579455.s: Malevich invented Suprematism: pictures of pure shapes and colours, with no people or objects. Earlier he had painted the Black Square.
Q579455.i: Imagine: is the white square floating or standing still? What does it feel?

f: Find the tall, stretched figure of Laocoön.
Find the city on a hill far away under a stormy sky.

m.q: What do the figures in the picture feel?
o: Calm: they are resting in the sun
Alarm: they are in great danger
m.w: Their bodies twist and their faces are tense. They are trying to escape.

x.q: What did Laocoön warn the Trojans about?
o: Not to take the wooden horse inside
Not to sail out to sea at night
Not to drink water from the river
x.w: He said the wooden horse was a Greek trick. But nobody believed him.

Q2255224.s: El Greco stretched bodies and painted in strange cold colours. A picture from a myth is a great rarity for him.
Q2255224.i: Imagine: how would you warn the Trojans about the horse?

f: Find the five men in the centre: they are presenting a document.
Find the man at the table who receives the document.

m.q: What is the mood in the hall?
m.w: People stand and sit upright and look at the paper. It is a very important moment.

x.q: What document are they presenting?
o: A letter to the king, with gifts
A list of new taxes on tea
x.w: In 1776 thirteen American colonies announced they would no longer obey the British king.

Q3173195.s: Trumbull painted the faces of real men, many from life. The huge picture hangs in the Capitol, and it appears on the two-dollar bill.
Q3173195.i: Imagine: write the first line of a declaration for your home: what should be free there?

f: Find the little round island with trees.
Find the boats on the water.

m.q: What is the mood of this day?
o: Grey and sleepy, like a rainy day
m.w: People bathe and go boating, and everything is flooded with light. It is good to relax.

x.q: How did Monet paint the sparkles on the water?
o: With smooth paint and no marks
With short, quick dabs of colour
x.w: He put many short strokes of different colours side by side. From far away they blend into shimmering water.

Q941549.s: Monet and Renoir painted La Grenouillère side by side in the summer of 1869. It was a step toward Impressionism.
Q941549.i: Imagine: how does the water feel, and what are the bathers shouting?

f: Find the huge giant behind the mountains and clouds.
Find the tiny people and carts scattering below.

m.q: What do the people below feel?
o: Fear and panic: they run off
m.w: People and animals scatter in all directions. They are in a panic.

x.q: How did Goya show that the giant is huge?
o: He wrote the word 'huge' beside him
Tiny people below, giant above the hills
He painted the giant a shining bright gold
x.w: Next to the giant everything below looks like dots. He rises above the mountains and clouds.

Q2413468.s: Goya was Spain's leading painter and painted both festivals and dark dreams. He went deaf, and his pictures grew more and more fantastic.
Q2413468.i: Imagine: give the giant a name. Is he cruel, or just lost?

f: Find the couple walking side by side: a woman in a light dress and a man.
Find the sunny patches of light on the grass and clothes.

m.q: What is the couple's mood?
o: Sad, saying goodbye on the path
m.w: They walk close together and smile lightly. The day is sunny.

x.q: What colour did Renoir use for shadows?
o: Dark brown, the colour of earth
x.w: Impressionists painted shadows in colour: you can see sky and leaves in them. That is why the picture is bright.

Q3823474.s: Renoir was about thirty when he painted this. He used light strokes and delighted in light and life.
Q3823474.i: Imagine: where is the couple going, and what are they talking about?

f: Find the layers of mountains: the far ones melt into the mist.
Find the tiny trees on the slopes and the water of the river.

m.q: What is the mood of the misty mountains?
o: Quiet and calm, like a deep breath
Loud and busy, like a big city
Tense, like waiting for a storm
m.w: Misty mountains, lots of empty space, no sharp colours. It feels like you can breathe deeply.

x.q: What is this scroll painted with?
o: Only black ink, pale to dark
x.w: The painter mixed ink with water and got many shades of grey.

Q706846.s: The scroll is unrolled bit by bit, as if you walk along the river. It was once nearly burned but was saved, and now it is split into two parts.
Q706846.i: Imagine: you are a fisherman in a boat on this river. What do you see?

f: Find the man in the dark coat and hat gliding on skates.
Find the pale winter sky, the frozen loch and the hills.

m.q: How does the skater look?
o: Worried that the ice might crack
Calm and confident on the ice
Tired and sad, wanting to go home
m.w: His arms are folded, his back is straight, and he glides easily. He is not afraid of falling.

x.q: What is this man doing?
o: Walking his dog on the ice
Fishing through a hole in the ice
x.w: He skates on Duddingston Loch near Edinburgh. He was a minister and loved winter sports.

Q2146810.s: Raeburn painted him in motion, in a winter landscape. It is one of Scotland's best-loved pictures.
Q2146810.i: Imagine: what will he do when he reaches the end of the loch?

f: Find her smile and her sideways glance.
Find her loose black hair and white blouse.

m.q: What is the girl's mood?
o: Strict and stern, like a teacher
m.w: She smiles and looks slightly aside, her eyes sparkling. She seems about to burst out laughing.

x.q: How did Frans Hals paint this picture?
o: With tiny dots of pure colour
x.w: Hals painted fast, and his strokes show on the hair and blouse. That is why the girl looks alive.

Q3206722.s: Frans Hals was a master of laughing faces. The people in his portraits seem caught in a living moment.
Q3206722.i: Imagine: what joke made the girl laugh?

f: Find the lyre: only one string is left on it.
Find the small star in the dark sky.

m.q: What does the girl feel?
o: Proud and happy, ready to dance
m.w: She sits hunched, her eyes covered by a bandage, her head bent to the lyre. But she listens and plays.

x.q: Why does the lyre have only one string?
o: One string still plays: hope stays
A bird flew off with the others
Lyres in the old days had just one string
x.w: The other strings have snapped, but she still plays. That is how the painter showed hope.

Q8874171.s: Watts painted not just people but ideas and feelings: Hope, Love, Life. The colours here are soft and dusky.
Q8874171.i: Imagine: what tune is she playing on one string?

f: Find the three parts of the picture in stone arches.
Find Mary in each of the three parts.

m.q: How does Mary's mood change across the three parts?
o: Sad and tired in all three
m.w: On the left she rejoices over the baby, in the middle she grieves, and on the right she meets her son.

x.q: Why do the frames look like stone arches with little statues?
o: They are real stone cut by builders
They are windows into a real church
Painted to look like carved stone
x.w: Rogier painted tiny statues with paint, but they look like stone. It is a trick on the eye.

Q323032.s: Rogier van der Weyden painted feelings so exactly that you understand them without words. This altarpiece was given to a monastery in Spain.
Q323032.i: Imagine a fourth panel: what happens next?

f: Find the pale blue dress with silvery trim.
Find the flowers next to her.

m.q: What is the Infanta's face like?
m.w: She stands straight, does not smile, and looks polite and stern. A princess was taught to behave with dignity.

x.q: Why was this portrait sent far away to Vienna?
o: To sell it to a rich merchant
To teach students how to paint in Vienna
So relatives could see the princess
x.w: There were no photographs then, and portraits took their place. Relatives in Vienna wanted to see the girl.

Q2264914.s: Velázquez also painted this princess as a little child in Las Meninas. He painted with free strokes: close up they are blotches, and from afar they are silk and lace.
Q2264914.i: Imagine: what would the princess do if she could escape from the palace?

f: Find the baby: he sleeps on Mary's lap.
Find the green meadow and the hills behind.

m.q: What is Mary's face like?
m.w: She looks at the baby, her head slightly bowed. All around is quiet.

x.q: What did Bellini paint behind Mary?
o: A flat gold wall, like an old icon
A dark room with a heavy curtain
A real landscape, hills and sky
x.w: Bellini set Mary in a meadow. Behind her is a wide world with clouds and faraway hills.

Q1115613.s: Giovanni Bellini was Titian's teacher. He painted soft, warm light, like a sunset over Venice.
Q1115613.i: Imagine a lullaby for the sleeping baby: how does it begin?

f: Find the transparent globe in the middle of the picture.
Find the eagle and the three-headed dog.

m.q: How do the gods carry themselves?
o: Nervous, looking for a place to hide
Sleepy and slow, ready for a nap
m.w: They sit and stand at ease, like masters of the world. Nobody is worried.

x.q: Where is this picture?
o: On the floor of a church
On the ceiling of a room
In a tall window of a palace
x.w: It is a ceiling painting: the gods are drawn as if we look up at them from below. You have to raise your head.

Q1122537.s: This is Caravaggio's only ceiling painting. Each god rules his own world: the sky, the sea and the underworld.
Q1122537.i: Which of the three worlds would you choose: sky, sea or underworld?

f: Find the owl peeking out of the conjurer's basket.
Find the man leaning over the table.

m.q: What does the watcher feel?
o: Boredom: he has seen it before
Suspicion: he thinks it is a fake
m.w: He leans forward, his mouth open and his eyes fixed on the trick. He is spellbound.

x.q: What is the sneaky person behind him doing?
o: Helping the conjurer with a trick
Giving him a bunch of flowers
x.w: While the man watches the trick, a thief tugs at his purse. The painter jokes: look where you should!

Q2155289.s: Painters in the Netherlands then liked funny pictures with a lesson: do not let yourself be fooled.
Q2155289.i: Imagine: what is hidden under the cup?

f: Find the woman bent over her book.
Find the patterned wallpaper behind her and the chair.

m.q: What is the atmosphere in the reading woman's room?
o: Tense, as if a storm is on its way
m.w: The woman reads, the room is quiet, and the colours are soft and dark. Nobody disturbs her.

x.q: How did Matisse become a painter?
o: Ill in bed, he was given paints
He was sent to art school at five
He found an old paintbrush outside
x.w: At first Matisse studied law. When he was ill, he was given paints and fell in love with painting.

Q3773123.s: Later Matisse became famous for bright, pure colours. This early picture is quiet and dark.
Q3773123.i: Imagine: what book is the woman reading?

f: Find the big strong oxen pulling the plough.
Find the farmer beside them.

m.q: What kind of day does it seem out in the field?
m.w: The oxen walk steadily, the field is wide, and the autumn sky is soft. All is calm and businesslike.

x.q: Why are the oxen pulling the plough?
o: It turns the soil for sowing seeds
It brings fresh hay to the barn
It clears the big stones from the road
x.w: In autumn the soil is ploughed so grain can be sown in it.

Q14127232.s: Rosa Bonheur was the most famous woman painter of her time. She loved animals so much that she got permission to wear trousers to visit the cattle markets.
Q14127232.i: Imagine: give the oxen names. What is each one called?

f: Find the rider on the white horse with a sword.
Find the beggar below, holding out his hands.

m.q: What is Martin's face like?
o: Proud, looking down on the man
Bored, gazing far into the distance
m.w: He looks gently at the beggar. He is sharing, and there is no anger in his face.

x.q: What is Martin doing with his sword?
o: Cutting his cloak in two to share it
Fighting off a robber on the road
Cutting a branch for a walking stick
x.w: Martin saw a beggar in the frost and gave him half his cloak. Later he was named a saint.

Q6119366.s: El Greco stretched his figures and painted a restless sky. His people and horse are like tongues of flame.
Q6119366.i: Imagine: what will the beggar say to Martin?

f: Find the purple clusters of lilac.
Find the bright green leaves: the strokes are like little dashes.

m.q: What do you feel looking at the blossoming bush?
o: Hot and dry, like late summer
m.w: The colours are light and the bush is in bloom, as if the air smelled of flowers. It is spring.

x.q: In which season does lilac bloom?
x.w: Lilac opens in spring, in May. Van Gogh painted the bush while it was in flower.

Q3832428.s: Van Gogh painted this bush in the garden of the hospital at Saint-Rémy where he was resting. His strokes are short and thick.
Q3832428.i: Imagine: what does this bush smell like, and which insects visit it?

f: Find the archangel Michael: his sword is raised, his wings spread.
Find the dark creatures at his feet.

m.q: What does Michael feel?
o: Courage and calm: he is sure
Worry, he is not sure he will win
m.w: He stands straight, his sword is raised, and his face is clear. He does not shout, he wins with confidence.

x.q: How do the two parts of the background behind him differ?
o: One shows a sea, the other a forest
Both are the same, only a pale blue sky
One is a calm landscape, one is fire
x.w: Raphael showed the struggle of good and evil: in one part there is peace, in the other fire.

Q2415259.s: Raphael painted this picture when he was very young. It was given as a gift to the king of France.
Q2415259.i: Imagine: what would you say to the dragon to make it kind?

f: Find the boy with a fish on a string.
Find the little white dog.

m.q: What do Tobias and the angel feel?
m.w: They walk side by side, and the angel holds the boy's hand. Both are calm.

x.q: What is the fish for in this story?
o: They wanted to fry it for a family supper
Its medicine cured his father's eyes
It was a gift for a rich uncle
x.w: The angel told him to catch the fish. Medicine from it gave Tobias's father his sight back.

Q1635039.s: The picture was painted in Verrocchio's workshop in Florence, where the young Leonardo da Vinci trained. The fish and dog are painted very delicately.
Q1635039.i: Imagine: what will Tobias tell his father when he gets home?

f: Find the king on the throne under a canopy.
Find the white pigeon.

m.q: What is the mood in the square?
m.w: Many people stand and watch the kneeling man. An important ceremony is under way.

x.q: What does the kneeling man promise?
o: To send him a gift of horses
To be loyal to the king of Poland
To give up his castle and go far away
x.w: This is an oath: Duke Albert of Prussia swears to serve the king of Poland.

Q317261.s: Jan Matejko painted huge pictures of Polish history, with bright costumes and real people based on portraits. He is the best-known Polish history painter.
Q317261.i: Imagine: you stand in the crowd. What do you whisper to your neighbour?

f: Look at her face: where does her calm gaze go?
Find her hands: how are they folded?

m.q: What is the young woman's face like?
o: Cheerful, as if about to sing
m.w: She looks slightly aside, her lips closed. Her face is quiet and serious.

x.q: Why is this picture nicknamed «the Silent One»?
o: She looks so quiet, as if silent
She never spoke to the painter
x.w: The Italian name La Muta means the silent woman. Nobody knows for sure who she is.

Q919861.s: Raphael learned from Leonardo. The pose, the hands in the lap and the turn of the body recall the Mona Lisa.
Q919861.i: Imagine: give the young woman a name and say what she likes.

f: Find the bright light bursting into the tent on the left.
Find the shining armour and helmets of the soldiers.

m.q: What is the mood of the scene?
o: Peaceful, like a quiet afternoon nap
Tense and dramatic, light and dark
Funny, like a show at the circus
m.w: Light and dark clash sharply, and people shout and struggle. Something very serious is happening.

x.q: How does Rembrandt guide your eyes?
o: With bright colours at the edges
With a pointing hand in the corner
x.w: The brightest place in the picture is where the main thing happens. Your eyes go there by themselves.

Q1211651.s: Rembrandt was still young when he painted this dramatic picture. Its strong light and deep shadows are like a stage.
Q1211651.i: Imagine: what happened a minute after this scene?

f: Find the angel playing a stringed instrument at Mary's feet.
Find the golden dome above the throne.

m.q: What kind of stillness fills the hall under the golden dome?
m.w: The people stand still, the light is soft, and the angel plays quietly. It is a calm place.

x.q: What did Bellini paint around Mary?
o: A dark forest with tall trees
A quiet hall with arches and a dome
A sunny garden with a stone fountain
x.w: Bellini invented a beautiful hall, like part of the church. The picture seems like a window into another room.

Q2269343.s: Bellini painted this when he was about seventy-five. It still hangs in the church of San Zaccaria in Venice.
Q2269343.i: Imagine: what tune is the angel playing?

f: Find his face: light falls on it from the side, and the background is dark.
Look him in the eyes: how does he look at us?

m.q: What does he look like?
m.w: He sits upright and looks attentive, his face calm and intelligent.

x.q: What did this young man become later?
o: A king ruling a faraway country
The Pope, leader of the Church
A famous captain of a big ship
x.w: Maffeo Barberini grew up and became Pope Urban VIII in 1623. He loved art.

Q2734111.s: Caravaggio placed people in strong light against a dark background, like under a spotlight. He painted living faces, without flattering them.
Q2734111.i: Imagine: what question would you ask the future pope?

f: Find the black dog beside the young man.
Find the painter himself: the young man with dark hair.

m.q: What does the young man feel?
m.w: He sits relaxed and looks straight at us. He is sure of himself.

x.q: Why was this picture important to young Courbet?
o: The very first picture he painted
His first picture at the Paris Salon
A king bought it for his palace
x.w: It was the first of his pictures accepted for the Salon exhibition in Paris. For a painter this was an important step.

Q48651005.s: Later Courbet became the leading master of Realism: he painted ordinary life. Here he is still young but already looks boldly at the world.
Q48651005.i: Imagine: what is the dog's name, and what does it like?

f: Find the thin see-through veil on her hair and shoulders.
Find the fan in her hand.

m.q: What is her face like?
o: Stern and cold, like a statue
Warm and teasing, about to smile
Worried, as if she had heard bad news
m.w: She looks straight at us, her eyes lively. She seems ready to joke.

x.q: Who is this lady?
o: A queen at the royal court
A rich queen who visited the painter
The painter's wife, also an artist
x.w: This is Roslin's wife, Marie-Suzanne Giroust. She also painted pictures.

Q10466368.s: Roslin could paint silk, lace and see-through veils so they look real. He was Swedish and worked in Paris.
Q10466368.i: Imagine: what will she say to her painter husband when he finishes the portrait?

f: Find the blue and purple irises along the path.
Find the house between the trees.

m.q: What is the mood of the garden?
m.w: Many flowers, lots of light, bright colours everywhere. It feels like summer.

x.q: Who planted this garden?
o: A royal gardener sent by a king
His neighbours, as a gift to him
x.w: Monet planted the flowers himself and painted his garden for years. Later he painted the pond with water lilies too.

Q3794124.s: Monet painted outdoors with quick strokes. Little patches of colour blend in your eye, and the garden seems to shimmer.
Q3794124.i: Imagine: which flower from this garden would you like to be, and why?

f: Find the gold chain across his chest.
Find the paper in his hand.

m.q: What is his gaze like?
o: Merry, mischievous, ready for a joke
Stern and furious, ready to shout
m.w: He looks straight, calmly and thoughtfully. He looks like a man who thinks a lot.

x.q: Who gave Holbein a home in England?
o: Thomas More, who found him clients
A family of fishermen by the Thames
x.w: When Holbein came to England, Thomas More took him into his house.

Q5296650.s: Holbein painted faces so exactly that even tiny wrinkles and stubble show. His fur and velvet look real.
Q5296650.i: Imagine: what is written in the letter More is holding?

f: Find the tents of the camp.
Find the riders on horses and the dog.

m.q: What is the mood of the herd?
o: Calm and free, in no hurry
Cross and restless, ready to kick
m.w: The horses graze and wander calmly. Nobody drives or scares them.

x.q: Who painted this picture and where did he work?
o: An Italian at the Chinese court
A Chinese monk on a mountain
A Russian painter at a fair
x.w: Giuseppe Castiglione went to China as a missionary and became the emperor's court painter.

Q28092353.s: This is a long scroll on silk: you unroll it bit by bit, like a journey. Shadows and volume came from Europe, and the mountains and trees are like Chinese painting.
Q28092353.i: Choose one horse and invent a name and a character for it.

f: Find the thatched roofs of the cottages.
Find the sky above the roofs.

m.q: What is the mood of the village?
o: Quiet and cosy, as if dozing
Busy and loud, like a market day
Tense, as if a storm were coming
m.w: The cottages stand peacefully, and the green and ochre patches are soft. The village seems to doze.

x.q: What is a thatched roof made of?
x.w: Straw or reeds are tied in bundles and laid on the roof. Such a roof is warm and light.

Q4497499.s: Van Gogh painted these cottages in Auvers, where he lived in his last months. There he painted almost every day.
Q4497499.i: Imagine: who lives in the cottage, and what is cooking for lunch?

f: Find the baby: he lies right on the floor.
Find the angel flying head down with a ribbon.

m.q: What does Mary look like?
m.w: She sits on the floor and looks at the baby. Her face is tired and warm.

x.q: What unusual thing happened to this painting?
o: It was burnt in a church fire
It was painted over by someone else
x.w: Today we know it only from old photographs. People hope it will turn up.

Q1433194.s: Caravaggio showed a holy story as a scene with ordinary people and strong light from the side. His figures are like living neighbours.
Q1433194.i: Imagine: what is the angel singing, flying down from above?

f: Find her necklace with a pendant.
Find the rings on her fingers and her folded hands.

m.q: What does she look like?
o: Laughing, about to tell a joke
Worried, as if she had heard bad news
m.w: She sits upright and looks straight ahead. Her hands are folded, her face is calm.

x.q: What famous picture did her husband order?
o: A big ship for the city fleet
A giant bell for the church
A round picture, the Doni Tondo
x.w: Maddalena's husband, Agnolo Doni, was a rich merchant. He ordered a round painting from Michelangelo.

Q2607055.s: Raphael learned from Leonardo: the pose, the hands and the landscape behind her recall the Mona Lisa.
Q2607055.i: Imagine: what would you talk about with this lady?

f: Find the nun working with a spade.
Find the glowing sunset sky behind the bare branches.

m.q: What feeling does this quiet evening bring?
o: Quiet, serious and a little sad
Cheerful and noisy, like a holiday
Warm and playful, like a summer fair
m.w: Evening, bare branches, two nuns silently busy with their work. Stillness.

x.q: Where did the painter get such a beautiful evening sky?
o: He invented it in his studio
He painted it outdoors, from life
He copied it from an old painting
x.w: The Pre-Raphaelites tried to paint nature as it really is, straight from life.

Q470541.s: Millais was one of the founders of the Pre-Raphaelites. They painted very clearly, with lots of tiny details.
Q470541.i: Imagine: what are the nuns talking about as the sun sets?

f: Find the baby sleeping on his mother's shoulder.
Find the dog reaching toward the man's hand.

m.q: What does the woman with the paper feel?
o: Anger at the jailer, ready to shout
Tiredness and relief: she did it
Joy: she is dancing with delight
m.w: She is pale and worn out, but she holds the paper firmly. Her husband is free.

x.q: What paper is the woman holding?
o: An order to free her husband
A letter to a friend in the city
A shopping list for the market
x.w: Her husband was in prison, and the paper allows him to be let go. Now the family is together again.

Q822541.s: For the wife Millais used Effie, his future wife, as the model. He painted the faces and the dog very carefully, from life.
Q822541.i: Imagine: what will the family do first when they get home?

f: Find the three little angel musicians at the foot of the throne.
Find the golden mosaic in the dome above the throne.

m.q: How does the hall feel, with everyone gathered around Mary?
o: Loud and jolly, like a feast
Restless, as if everyone is late
m.w: Everyone stands calmly, the music is soft, and the light is gentle. The people seem to listen to silence.

x.q: Why do saints from different times stand together?
o: They happened to meet in a church
They were all neighbours in one town
x.w: The saints lived at different times. The painter gathered them at Mary's throne, and all are calm.

Q1751408.s: Bellini painted warm golden light, and the Venetians were masters of it. He painted such big altarpieces for the churches of Venice.
Q1751408.i: Imagine: which saint would you pick, and what would he say to the baby?

f: Find the boy drinking from the stream.
Find the dog and the sheep at the gate.

m.q: How does this day by the stream feel?
o: Tense, as if a storm is near
m.w: A golden field, a huge sky and a quiet path. Everything breathes summer peace.

x.q: What did Constable draw again and again to learn his craft?
x.w: Constable made many sketches of clouds. He wanted to paint the sky as it really is.

Q2272625.s: Constable painted places he had loved since childhood: the valley of the River Stour. That is why the landscape feels so familiar and dear.
Q2272625.i: Imagine: what did the boy see in the water?

f: Find the red curtain of the bed.
Find the apple on the table.

m.q: How does this scene feel?
o: Peaceful and sleepy, a lazy afternoon
Hurry and secrecy: all moves fast
Dull and quiet, a very boring day
m.w: The two reach and twist, the cloths billow, and the light leaps. Something is happening quickly.

x.q: Where does the brightest light fall?
o: On the pair, apple and white cloth
Evenly across the whole big room
Only on the big red curtain of the bed
x.w: The light picks out the main thing. The rest stays in half-dark.

Q3228069.s: Fragonard painted with a light, quick brush in the Rococo style: lots of light, tender colours, playful scenes.
Q3228069.i: Imagine: who is outside the door, and why did he come?

f: Find the chessboard with the pieces.
Find the elderly maid on the right: she watches the game.

m.q: What is the mood of the sisters?
m.w: They bend over the board, smile and tease each other. The game has caught them.

x.q: What is new about this portrait?
o: Everyone stands stiff in one row
They play and relax, not pose
x.w: Earlier portraits were stiff. Here the sisters play, and we see a living home scene.

Q23008305.s: Sofonisba Anguissola was one of the first women painters to become famous in Europe. She also worked at the court of the Spanish king.
Q23008305.i: Imagine: who is winning, and what will the next move be?

f: Find a kitten.
Find cats of different colours: black, white, striped.

m.q: What is the mood of the cats?
o: Scared, ready to run for the door
Fierce and quarrelsome, ready to fight
m.w: The cats sit and lie at ease, as if they know they are the most important.

x.q: Why is the title of the picture a joke?
o: It shows men who admire the lady
It shows a wedding with many guests
It shows the lady's beloved cats
x.w: The word «lovers» in the title is a joke. The picture shows much-loved house pets.

Q22330063.s: The painter painted the cats one after another, like separate portraits. That is why the picture turned out so big and colourful.
Q22330063.i: Imagine: name three cats and say what each one's job is.

f: Find Miss La La high under the dome: she holds the rope with her teeth.
Find the iron beams of the dome.

m.q: What does Miss La La look like?
o: Frightened, about to let go of it
Sleepy and tired of the show
m.w: She is high above the ground, but her body is straight and calm. She is clearly a master of her craft.

x.q: Where do we look at her from?
o: From above, like a bird in the dome
From the side, from a far seat
From below, with our heads tilted back
x.w: Degas painted the circus from the ground, and the beams meet like threads of a web. We seem to look up, holding our breath.

Q3842349.s: Degas loved painting movement: dancers, horses, acrobats. He often chose an unusual point of view, like in a photograph.
Q3842349.i: Imagine: what do the spectators shout as she swings?

f: Find the polar bears among the ice.
Find the pieces of the ship: a mast and a torn sail.

m.q: What do the bears feel?
o: Curious and calm: this is home
Sad: they feel sorry for the sailors
m.w: They unhurriedly look over the wreckage. For them it is an ordinary place.

x.q: What does the title Man Proposes, God Disposes mean?
o: That ships must be mended before sailing
People make plans, but life decides
That bears are far cleverer than people
x.w: It is an old saying. The picture is about a ship that had bad luck.

Q18209192.s: Landseer was Queen Victoria's favourite painter of animals. He also made the lions at Nelson's Column in London.
Q18209192.i: Imagine: what are the bears talking about as they look at the wreckage?

f: Find the girl at the piano.
Find the older woman in the armchair beside her.

m.q: What is the mood in the room?
o: Noisy and busy: a big dinner party
Quiet and cosy: a family evening
Tense and worried: a stormy evening
m.w: The girl plays, her mother sits nearby, and the wallpaper is patterned. Nobody is in a hurry.

x.q: What music is the girl playing?
o: A lullaby for a sleepy child
An overture by the composer Wagner
A lively march for a brass band
x.w: The title of the picture says so. It is music by the composer Richard Wagner.

Q3929306.s: In his youth Cézanne painted with thick dark paint, spread on with a palette knife. Light, bright colours came later.
Q3929306.i: Imagine: is the music in the room fast or slow?

f: Find the two monkeys sitting in the window arch.
Find the river and the city with a tall cathedral far behind.

m.q: What do the monkeys feel?
o: Playful joy, ready to play a game
m.w: They sit still, one looks down, the other aside. They are chained.

x.q: What did Bruegel paint outside the window?
o: A dark, empty room with a candle
A wide river and a free city
A thick forest with no path
x.w: The monkeys are chained, and outside is open space. Perhaps the picture is about longing for freedom, but nobody knows for sure.

Q231953.s: This is a very small panel, about the size of a book page. Yet it holds both the monkeys and a whole city far away.
Q231953.i: Imagine: what would the monkeys say to the ships on the river?

f: Find Jesus rising with a white banner.
Find the soldiers below: helmets, spears, shields.

m.q: What do the soldiers feel?
m.w: They tumble, shield their eyes from the light, and their spears are scattered. They are stunned.

x.q: How did El Greco show that Jesus is rising?
o: He painted big feathered wings on him
He wrote the word 'flying' above him
A long body and a flying white cloak
x.w: Jesus is long and light, his cloak billows, and the soldiers lie below. Your eye goes up by itself.

Q617629.s: El Greco's real name was Doménikos Theotokópoulos. El Greco means the Greek: he was born on Crete and lived in Spain.
Q617629.i: Imagine: what will the soldiers tell their friends tomorrow?

f: Find the green parasol: it shades the lady from the sun.
Find the little dog in her lap.

m.q: What is this day under the parasol like?
m.w: Everyone is relaxed, the sun shines, and they smile and chat.

x.q: What did Goya paint this picture for?
o: As a pattern for a palace tapestry
To decorate a school classroom wall
To sell at a village market stall
x.w: Weavers used such a picture to weave a big tapestry for the palace. Such patterns are called cartoons.

Q2537138.s: When Goya painted this, he still painted cheerful scenes from Madrid life. Later his pictures grew gloomier.
Q2537138.i: Imagine: what would the little dog say if it could speak?

f: Find Mary: her head is bowed and her hands are folded on her chest.
Find the two who hold the crown over her head.

m.q: What is Mary's expression under the crown?
o: Excited, as if she won a prize
m.w: Her head is bowed and her eyes lowered. She quietly accepts the crown.

x.q: What are the two above Mary doing?
o: Giving her a bunch of lilies
x.w: This is a coronation: Mary becomes the Queen of Heaven. Clouds and angels surround her.

Q3221859.s: Velázquez was the court painter of the king of Spain. He painted mostly portraits, but sacred scenes too.
Q3221859.i: Imagine: what song are the angels around her singing?

f: Find the crying boy.
Find the girl hugging a doll.

m.q: How does the girl with the doll feel?
o: Joy: she hugs her new doll
Sadness: nobody gave her a gift
m.w: She holds the doll tightly and is pleased. She is happy.

x.q: What time of year is this feast?
x.w: In the Netherlands children put their shoes by the fireplace. At night Saint Nicholas leaves presents in them.

Q764831.s: Jan Steen painted such noisy, merry families that in the Netherlands a messy house is «a Jan Steen household».
Q764831.i: Imagine: what would you put in your shoe for Saint Nicholas?

f: Find the baby lying on straw at the very bottom.
Find the shepherds in plain clothes: they bend toward the baby.

m.q: How does Mary look at the baby?
m.w: She bends low over the baby. Her face is warm and weary.

x.q: Why are the people and the baby painted so low, right near the ground?
o: To show a poor stable and bring us close
Because the canvas was too short for more
Because they sit in a deep, dark cellar
x.w: Caravaggio showed a poor stable: everyone is near the ground, and so are we, right beside them.

Q2327715.s: Caravaggio painted this in 1609 in Sicily. The top part is dark and almost empty, so the people below feel closer.
Q2327715.i: Imagine: what would you give the baby, taking it from your pocket?

f: Find the man in the dark frock coat and bow tie.
Find the woman in the wide skirt beside him.

m.q: What do these two feel for each other?
o: Worry, as if waiting for news
m.w: They stand side by side and look gently. You can see they feel good together.

x.q: Who is the man in the picture?
o: A doctor who treated Renoir's family
A rich merchant who bought his paintings
x.w: Alfred Sisley was also an Impressionist. He and Renoir were friends and studied together.

Q3177703.s: Renoir and Sisley studied with Monet under the same teacher in Paris. Then they became Impressionists.
Q3177703.i: Imagine: what is the couple planning for their happy day?

f: Find her light dress with soft folds.
Find the ornament in her hair.

m.q: What does the countess look like?
o: Merry, as if about to laugh
Stern and cold, like a judge
m.w: She looks gently and seriously, her gaze thoughtful. There is no smile.

x.q: How did Goya paint her light dress?
o: With thick, heavy, dark brown paint
With soft, thin strokes of white
