Q3842778.s: This is an early work by Titian: he was about twenty. He learned from Bellini, then found his own style: warm, bright colours.
Q3842778.i: Imagine what Mary tells the baby as she looks at the mountains.

f: Find the priest Skarga: he stands in the pulpit and speaks.
Look at the listeners' faces: who looks worried, who thoughtful?

m.q: What is the mood of the listeners?
m.w: They sit and stand very quietly, their faces stern. Skarga is saying something important and everyone listens.

x.q: What does Skarga warn about in his sermon?
o: People should eat more and also sleep more
A big storm will come here very soon
The country weakens if people quarrel
x.w: He said that important people must think of the country, not only of themselves. Otherwise the state will suffer.

Q4380890.s: Jan Matejko painted huge pictures from Polish history. They contain many real people whom he studied from portraits.
Q4380890.i: Imagine what you would say to the king after hearing the sermon.

f: Find the girl's folded hands.
Find the dark trees and the sky behind her.

m.q: What is the mood of the girl with folded hands?
o: Loud, she is laughing and giggling
m.w: She sits still and looks straight ahead. The soft light and light dress make her calm.

x.q: What helps the girl stand out in the picture?
o: A light dress against a dark background
Bright toys scattered all around her
A big, heavy gold frame around the picture
x.w: A light figure on a dark background catches the eye at once. Reynolds loved such contrast.

Q7712851.s: Joshua Reynolds was the first president of the Royal Academy of Arts in London. He painted children lively and natural.
Q7712851.i: Imagine what the girl is thinking while she sits quietly.

f: Find the sheep on the edge of the cliff.
Find the blue sea in the distance and the bright green grass.

m.q: What is the mood of the shore with the sheep?
m.w: The sheep graze peacefully on the grass while the sea glitters. Bright colours make the day warm and clear.

x.q: How did Hunt get such bright, sharp colours?
o: He painted only from memory at home
He painted outdoors in the sunshine
He painted only at night by candlelight
x.w: He sat on the cliffs beside the sheep and painted what he saw. That is why you can see every blade of grass and strand of wool.

Q18689510.s: The title has a double meaning: the strayed sheep hint that England's coasts are poorly guarded. At that time people in England feared an attack from France.
Q18689510.i: Imagine where the shepherd has gone and what he is doing now.

f: Find the big black circle.
Look at the white background around it: there is nothing extra.

m.q: What is the mood of the black circle on white?
o: Loud and cheerful, like a circus
m.w: One black circle on a white background. Nothing is extra, so the picture feels strict and calm.

x.q: What is Suprematism?
o: Painting of only animals and birds
x.w: Malevich invented a new kind of painting: no people or trees, only a circle, a square, a cross. He thought simple shapes were the purest.

Q4518897.s: In 1915 Malevich painted the ‘Black Square’, and later a black circle and a black cross. These are the three main shapes of his art.
Q4518897.i: Imagine what this circle could be: a moon, a hole, a wheel?

f: Find John the Baptist: he speaks from a raised spot.
Find the people in different hats and clothes sitting and listening.

m.q: What is the mood of John's listeners?
m.w: People sit on the grass and listen. Some lean in, and some are lost in thought.

x.q: Whom did Bruegel paint in the crowd?
o: Ordinary people of his own time
Kings and queens wearing gold crowns
x.w: Bruegel moved the Bible story into his own time. That is why the listeners dress like people of Flanders in his day.

Q257048.s: Bruegel loved painting big crowds of small people and looking down on them. If you look closely, you can find many interesting faces and hats.
Q257048.i: Imagine what John tells the people gathered.

f: Find the little train in the distance with a puff of smoke.
Find the carriage on the road and the flowers in the field.

m.q: What is the mood of these fields and sky?
o: Fresh and bright, as after rain
Anxious, like before a big storm
Dark and cold, like in winter
m.w: The sky is still gloomy, but the fields shine in different colours. The air feels clean and fresh.

x.q: What do the carriage and the train have in common in this picture?
o: Both are going to the same town
Old and new: horses and steam power
They are almost the same size
x.w: Van Gogh set old and new transport side by side. It shows how life was changing in his time.

Q650526.s: The painting is kept in Moscow, in the Pushkin Museum. Van Gogh painted it at Auvers in summer 1890, when he painted almost a picture a day.
Q650526.i: Imagine where the carriage and the train are going and who sits in them.

f: Find Mary and the baby Jesus in her arms.
Find the book near them.

m.q: What is the mood of Mary as she bends over the baby?
o: Anger and a lot of annoyance
m.w: Mary bends towards the baby, her face soft. Quiet warm colours make the picture cosy.

x.q: Why is this painting so small?
o: The painter ran out of big canvas
The painter was in a great hurry
It was made for prayer at home
x.w: Such small pictures were kept at home and people prayed before them. That is why they hold so many fine details.

Q5316837.s: Rogier van der Weyden was very famous in Europe: his Madonnas were copied many times. He showed feelings softly and delicately.
Q5316837.i: Imagine what is written in the book.

f: Find the cheeky angel: he looks straight at you and smiles.
Find the window frame: a landscape can be seen through it.

m.q: What is the angel's mood?
o: Sad, he is about to cry
m.w: He smiles over his shoulder, as if inviting you to join in a secret. It is a very lively face.

x.q: What does the frame in the picture look like?
o: A window to peek into the whole scene
A high stone wall without windows
A big wooden door with a lock
x.w: The painted frame creates depth: we seem to look into a room. And beyond the window you can see nature.

Q1055111.s: Fra Filippo Lippi was a monk and a painter in Florence. His pupil was the famous Botticelli.
Q1055111.i: Imagine what the angel whispers to you with a wink.

f: Find the three Magi with their gifts.
Find the ruined building behind.

m.q: What do the kings feel before the baby?
o: Boredom and wanting to go home
Anger and a lot of annoyance
m.w: They bow and fall quiet. The calm poses and soft light show that this is an important moment.

x.q: What does the ruined building behind mean?
o: The house where the Magi once lived
The old world makes way for a new one
An old shed nobody needs any more
x.w: Painters often drew ruins beside the birth of Jesus. It is a sign that something new is beginning.

Q2741541.s: Hugo van der Goes painted every face in its own way, lively and expressive. This altarpiece was made for a monastery in the Spanish town of Monforte.
Q2741541.i: Imagine what gift the youngest king brought.

f: Find the big white ruff collar.
Find the sword and the hat.

m.q: What is Willem's mood?
o: Sad, he is about to cry
m.w: He stands confidently and looks boldly. That is how people pose when they are pleased with themselves.

x.q: How did Frans Hals paint?
o: Very slowly, one dot at a time
Only with a ruler, in straight lines
x.w: His brushstrokes show, as if everything is happening right now. That is why people in his portraits look alive.

Q880502.s: Hals became famous for painting people lively, laughing and cheerful. In Holland he was considered a master of living faces.
Q880502.i: Imagine what Willem would say if he met you.

f: Find the worker in the blue smock: he looks down over the railing.
Find the dog and the couple walking across the bridge.

m.q: What kind of day is shown on the bridge?
o: A big festival with flags and music
An alarm, people are hurrying away
A calm stroll on an ordinary day
m.w: People walk without hurry, and the worker simply looks down. Nothing has happened; it is a quiet slice of the city.

x.q: What creates depth in the picture?
o: Iron beams meeting in the distance
Heavy grey clouds above the whole city
A big window in the foreground
x.w: The lines of the beams run to a single point, so the bridge seems to go far. This is called perspective.

Q2335560.s: Caillebotte was a wealthy painter and a friend of the Impressionists: he bought their paintings and helped them. He loved painting modern Paris: bridges, streets, trains.
Q2335560.i: Imagine what the worker sees below, on the tracks.

f: Find the king on horseback.
Find the man walking beside the horse.

m.q: What is the king's mood?
m.w: He sits straight and looks confident. The dark clothes and the calm horse make him majestic.

x.q: How did Van Dyck make the king look majestic?
o: Put a huge golden crown on his head
Painted everything around him in gold
Painted from below, so he towers over us
x.w: When you look up from below, a figure seems taller and stronger. King Charles was actually short.

Q3937482.s: Anthony van Dyck came from Flanders and studied with Rubens. King Charles I made him his court painter and knighted him.
Q3937482.i: Imagine where the king is riding.

f: Find the white bandage on Van Gogh's ear.
Find the pipe and the smoke coming from it.

m.q: What is Van Gogh's mood?
o: Cheerful, he is laughing out loud
Angry, he is frowning very hard
m.w: He looks straight at you without a smile. The calm gaze and quiet colours show tiredness.

x.q: Why did Van Gogh paint himself so often?
o: No money for models, but he had a mirror
He thought he was the most handsome man
A museum ordered thirty self-portraits from him
x.w: Models have to be paid, but a mirror is free. He painted himself about thirty-five times.

Q19363214.s: Behind Van Gogh you can see a Japanese print. He loved such pictures: bright, flat, with clear lines.
Q19363214.i: Imagine what Van Gogh thinks about as he looks in the mirror.

f: Find the man with the pipe leaning back in his chair.
Find the dog and the violinist.

m.q: What is the mood of the people at the table?
o: Noisy, everyone is singing and dancing
m.w: They sit relaxed, one smoking, another listening to the violin. The warm dark tones make everything cosy.

x.q: What is unusual about the size of this painting?
o: Tiny, even smaller than a postcard
Huge, yet it shows only ordinary people
Round, like a big dinner plate
x.w: Such big paintings were usually made about kings and heroes. Courbet showed that simple people matter too.

Q12901580.s: Courbet was born in the town of Ornans and painted his friends and his father here. The painting won him a prize at an exhibition, and the state bought it.
Q12901580.i: Imagine what tune the violinist plays.

f: Find Peter: he holds the keys in his hand.
Find Paul: he holds a book.

m.q: What is the mood of the apostles?
o: Sleepy, they are about to doze
m.w: They look thoughtful and their faces are tense. The glowing colours make their gaze strong.

x.q: Why does Peter hold keys?
o: He worked as a doorkeeper for a king
He had lost the keys to his house
Jesus gave him the keys to heaven
x.w: That is why Peter is painted with keys: you recognise him at once. Paul is often painted with a book.

Q9396559.s: El Greco painted stretched-out figures and bright, almost flickering colours. He showed saints as people who think deeply.
Q9396559.i: Imagine what Peter and Paul are discussing.

f: Find the roses on the trellis behind Mary.
Find the birds among the roses and the two angels with a crown above.

m.q: What is the mood of Mary among the roses?
m.w: She looks down at the baby while the birds twitter in the roses. The golden background makes the scene bright.

x.q: Why are there roses around Mary?
o: The rose is Mary's special flower
There were no other flowers that year
It was the painter's neighbour's garden
x.w: Painters have long shown Mary among roses. The delicate flowers speak of beauty and purity.

Q648068.s: Martin Schongauer was a German master of engraving. The young Dürer wanted so much to learn from him that he travelled to him, but Schongauer had already died.
Q648068.i: Imagine what song the birds sing to the baby.

f: Find the royal crown.
Find the lady's fan and the musical instruments.

m.q: What is the mood of the family in this portrait?
o: Sleepy: everyone is about to doze off
m.w: Everyone stands and sits formally and looks at the painter. The silk, jewels and poses show this is a grand portrait.

x.q: What do the violin and the oboe tell us?
o: Children are taught to play here
They were forgotten after a concert
x.w: King Philip V loved music and invited the famous singer Farinelli to his house.

Q3204999.s: The painting is huge: about five metres wide. Van Loo was a court painter in Madrid and could paint silk and velvet.
Q3204999.i: Imagine which child is the naughtiest and what he whispers to his brother.

f: Find the tall tower beside Barbara: it is her sign.
Find the tiny builders and the crane at the building site.

m.q: What is Barbara's mood?
m.w: She sits bent over a book. The calm lines and grey tones make the scene very quiet.

x.q: Why is this picture grey?
o: Van Eyck liked grey best of all
The paint faded over the years
It is unfinished, no colours yet
x.w: It is a brush drawing on wood, and colours were not yet added. So we see how the master began a picture.

Q3464466.s: Van Eyck usually painted in bright oils, but here we see only his drawing. That shows how precisely he planned everything.
Q3464466.i: Imagine which colours you would use to paint this picture.

f: Find the white armband the girl is trying to tie on the man's arm.
Find the ivy leaves on the wall behind them.

m.q: What do these two feel?
m.w: The girl is anxious, while the man gently pushes the band away and holds her hand. They are very close.

x.q: What does the girl ask for?
o: To wear a white band, but he still refuses
To pick her a big bunch of flowers
To sing her a long, sad farewell song
x.w: In those days people quarrelled over faith, and a white band could protect. But the young man stays true to himself.

Q287169.s: Millais was one of the founders of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood: its painters painted every tiny thing precisely and brightly. Here you can see every vein of the ivy leaves.
Q287169.i: Imagine what the man whispers to the girl.

f: Find Venus. What is she standing on? A giant seashell!
On the left, find Zephyr, the wind god: he blows, and roses fly around.

m.q: What is Venus's mood?
o: Cross, she frowns at the wind
Calm and dreamy, with a soft gaze
Joyful, she laughs at the roses
m.w: She stands still with her head tilted and a faraway look. No big smile, no anger.

x.q: In the old myth, what was Venus born from?
x.w: The myth says the goddess rose from the foam of the waves, and the wind blew her to the shore.

Q151047.s: The secret: Botticelli drew with flowing lines, so hair and cloth seem to dance. He mixed his paints with egg yolk.
Q151047.i: Imagine: what did Venus say as she stepped onto the beach? What did the girl with the cloak answer?

f: Find the wanderer. We only see him from behind.
Find the sharp mountain tops poking out of the fog like islands.

m.q: What does the wanderer feel as he looks far away?
o: Tired, he wants to go home
Scared, he wants to run away
m.w: He stands tall, leans on his stick and does not look away. The view takes his breath away.

x.q: Why did the painter show the man from behind?
o: The face was too tiny to paint well
So we can stand there and look with him
He was hiding from the cold wind
x.w: We cannot see his face, so we feel as if we stand on the rock looking at the fog ourselves.

Q311243.s: The secret: Friedrich sketched mountains on his walks and built this picture at home in his studio. That makes the place almost like a dream.
Q311243.i: Imagine: what does the wanderer hear up there: silence, wind or birds? What is he thinking about?

f: Find the three swords in the father's hand and the brothers' arms stretched toward them.
Look to the right: find the women who sit and grieve.

m.q: How do the women on the right feel?
o: Happy, they cheer for the men
Sleepy, they want to go to bed
Sad and worried for the men
m.w: They bend down, hide their faces and cling to each other. They are afraid for the people they love.

x.q: How did the painter show the men and the women differently?
o: All have the same soft, round lines
Men are straight and hard, women soft
The men are painted much smaller
x.w: The brothers stand straight like arrows and the women droop like flowers. You can see who is determined and who is sad.

Q476458.s: The secret: David arranged it like a theatre stage: a bare room, three arches, three brothers. This strict, clear style became the new fashion.
Q476458.i: Imagine: what does the father say after handing out the swords? Give each brother a name.

f: Find the hat with a feather: the boy holds it in his hand.
Look at the suit: see how the blue satin shines!

m.q: How does the boy stand?
o: Lazy, with his eyes half shut
Proud and calm, like a young lord
m.w: He stands tall and looks at us calmly and confidently, like a little lord.

x.q: What kind of clothes are these?
o: The newest fashion of his time
A soldier's uniform with a feather
Clothes from a hundred years ago
x.w: The boy wears clothes from the century before, like a fancy-dress party. Gainsborough loved the old portraits by Van Dyck.

Q604761.s: The secret: people say that painters then thought blue should not be the main colour. Gainsborough wanted to prove it could, and painted a whole blue picture.
Q604761.i: Imagine: where is the boy going in his fine suit? What does he say to the first person he meets?

f: Find the couple walking by the river below.
Find the seven bright stars of the Big Dipper in the sky: they look like a ladle.

m.q: How does the couple feel?
m.w: They walk slowly, side by side, in no hurry. The night around them is warm and calm.

x.q: What colours did Van Gogh use for the night?
o: Mostly black, with small white stars
Bright pink and orange, like dawn
Deep blue and green with golden lights
x.w: Van Gogh wrote that night is richer in colour than day. There is almost no black here: just blues, greens and golden lamps.

Q1464531.s: The secret: Van Gogh painted this at night, right by the river, by the light of gas lamps. He drew the lights in the water as trembling stripes.
Q1464531.i: Imagine: what are the two by the river whispering about? What else do they see in the sky?

f: Look where John's finger points: up, to the sky.
Find the thin cross made of reed in his other hand.

m.q: What kind of smile does John have?
o: Quiet, as if keeping a secret
m.w: The corners of his lips lift a little and his eyes are soft. As if he knows a secret but will not tell.

x.q: What does John's raised finger tell us?
o: Shh! Be quiet, someone is sleeping
Look up, what matters is above
Come closer, I want to tell you
x.w: John points to the sky. It is as if he says: the most important thing will come from there.

Q783215.s: The secret: Leonardo painted in a soft haze with no hard lines, so light melts into shadow. He kept this picture with him until the end of his life.
Q783215.i: Imagine: what would John whisper to you if you came closer?

f: Find the blue statue and the white bird by the old woman.
Find the sleeping baby at the right edge.

m.q: What is the mood of the old woman on the left?
o: Cheerful, she is ready to dance
Cross, she is shouting at someone
Thoughtful, quiet and a little sad
m.w: She sits bent over, as if remembering her whole life. She is calm and a little sad.

x.q: How should you read this picture?
o: From left to right, like a book
From top to bottom, like a ladder
Right to left, baby to old woman
x.w: The baby is on the right, grown-ups in the middle, the old woman on the left. It shows a whole human life.

Q890678.s: The secret: it is huge, almost four metres wide. Gauguin painted it in Tahiti and wrote the title, a question, right in the corner.
Q890678.i: Imagine: how would you answer the three questions in the title?

f: Find the huge wave lifting the boat.
Find the man who looks straight at us: people say he is Rembrandt himself.

m.q: What do the people in the boat feel?
o: Calm, they enjoy a quiet trip
Joy, it is like a sea party
m.w: They grab the ropes and the sides, and their faces are tense. The waves toss the boat.

x.q: What story does the painting tell?
o: Christ calming a storm for his friends
Fishermen racing their boats to shore
A ship sailing home to the harbour
x.w: In the Gospel, Jesus is in the boat with his friends. When they get scared, he tells the wind to be still.

Q2246489.s: The secret: it is Rembrandt's only seascape. It was stolen from a museum in Boston in 1990, and its empty frame still hangs on the wall.
Q2246489.i: Imagine: what do the sailors shout to each other while the boat rocks?

f: Count the bears: how many cubs, and where is their mother?
Look at the morning mist between the tall pines.

m.q: What is the mood of the bear family?
o: Cross and fierce, ready to growl
Sleepy and sad, lost in the woods
m.w: The cubs climb on the log and look around, while mother stays calm beside them. They are having fun and fear nothing.

x.q: Who painted this picture?
o: Shishkin alone, sitting in the forest
Savitsky alone, after visiting a zoo
x.w: Ivan Shishkin painted the forest and trees, and Konstantin Savitsky painted the bears. They worked together.

Q2666439.s: The secret: later, Savitsky's signature was wiped off, and for a long time people thought Shishkin painted it alone. But Savitsky painted the bears.
Q2666439.i: Imagine: what are the cubs called, and what game do they play before breakfast?

f: Count the blind men: they walk in a line, holding shoulders and sticks.
Find the man who has already fallen into the ditch.

m.q: How does the first blind man feel as he falls?
o: Sleepy, he is lying down for a nap
Happy, he is doing a funny dance
Shocked and scared, he is falling
m.w: He has lost his footing and tumbles onto his back, his face baffled. He does not understand what is happening.

x.q: Which old saying is this picture about?
o: Do not count your chickens early
Every cloud has a silver lining
The blind lead the blind, both fall
x.w: If your guide cannot see the road either, you will both fall in the ditch. It is important to choose wise guides.

Q1192570.s: The secret: each blind man has his own face and his own clouded eyes. Bruegel painted real people, not identical dolls.
Q1192570.i: Imagine: what would you shout to the blind men to make them stop?

f: See how the old man hides his face in his hands.
Find the fire in the fireplace: what colour is it?

m.q: What does the old man feel?
o: Sad and tired, he hides his face
Happy and warm by the fire
m.w: He sits bent over with his face in his fists. People do this when they are very sad.

x.q: Which two colours make each other shine most here?
x.w: The old man's blue clothes and the orange fire are opposites. Side by side they glow brighter.

Q500554.s: The secret: Van Gogh made this picture from his own drawing, done many years before. He wanted us to feel kindly towards the old man.
Q500554.i: Imagine: what is the old man thinking about while the fire burns?

f: Look at the young man's hand: it holds a sheet of music.
Find his curly hair and red cap.

m.q: What expression does the young man have?
o: Cheerful, he is about to sing
Sleepy, he is about to nod off
m.w: He looks a little to the side, his brows calm and lips closed. As if he is hearing music inside himself.

x.q: What is unusual about this painting?
o: Every thread is painted perfectly well
Only the red cap is painted well
x.w: Leonardo finished the face but left part of the clothes unfinished. That shows how he worked.

Q2338404.s: The secret: it is thought to be the only portrait of a man painted by Leonardo. He painted skin and eyes in a soft haze.
Q2338404.i: Imagine: what tune did this young man write, and what is it called?

f: Find the sharp slabs of ice stacked into a tall tower.
Find the tiny ship squeezed by the ice on the right.

m.q: What is the mood here?
o: Warm and sunny, like a beach
Busy and noisy, like a fair
m.w: Pale light, sharp ice and emptiness. It feels as if deep silence is all around.

x.q: Why did Friedrich paint the ship so tiny?
o: He ran out of paint for the ship
It really was just a small rowing boat
To show nature is bigger and stronger
x.w: Next to the huge ice the ship is hard to see. That is how the painter showed the power of nature.

Q194137.s: The secret: Friedrich never sailed to the Arctic. He studied real ice floes on the frozen River Elbe near his home.
Q194137.i: Imagine: what can you hear on this ice: cracking, whistling wind or silence?

f: Find the wreath of leaves in Bacchus's hair.
Find the bowl of fruit: can you spot a bruised apple?

m.q: How does Bacchus look?
o: Angry, he is ready to fight
m.w: He lies back with half-closed eyes, a glass lazily held out.

x.q: What did scientists find in the glass carafe of wine?
o: A tiny hidden mouse on the glass
A secret number written in wine
x.w: In the reflection on the carafe you can see the painter at work. It is so tiny that only close study found it.

Q2011510.s: The secret: Caravaggio painted things as they are, even a bruised apple and leaves with holes. He was not afraid of what is not perfect.
Q2011510.i: Imagine: what does Bacchus raise his glass to?

f: Find Manet himself: he stands at the far left edge.
Find the children playing in front.

m.q: What is the mood of the people in the park?
o: Worried, they wait for the rain
m.w: People stand in groups, chat, and the children play. Nobody is in a hurry.

x.q: Whom did Manet paint among the crowd?
o: Only strangers he met that day
Only kings and queens of France
x.w: Many in the crowd were Manet's friends. He wanted to show real life in Paris.

Q210277.s: The secret: Manet painted with quick, loose strokes, and faces far away are just dabs of paint. Many people thought the picture was unfinished.
Q210277.i: Imagine: what is the orchestra playing, a march or a waltz? Who dances to it?

f: Look at the lady's puffy sleeve: so many shiny folds!
Find the thin veil on her hair.

m.q: What kind of lady is in the portrait?
o: Calm and gentle, with a warm look
Angry, she is scowling at us
m.w: Her gaze is warm and steady, and her hand rests on her chest. Her face is relaxed.

x.q: How did Raphael make the sleeve look like real silk?
o: He glued a real piece of silk on it
He painted the whole sleeve one flat colour
He painted light and shadow in each fold
x.w: Where a fold bulges it is bright, where it dips it is darker. That makes the silk shine.

Q948034.s: The secret: Raphael lived only 37 years but became one of the greatest painters. His people look calm and alive.
Q948034.i: Imagine: what would the lady say if she could speak?

f: Find the bright star in the sky with a ring of light around it.
Find the woman near the white house and the glowing windows.

m.q: What is the mood of the night?
o: Noisy, like a party in the street
m.w: The windows glow warm yellow and the sky is deep blue. The house seems to invite you in.

x.q: What is the bright star?
o: The Moon, shining with a halo
The planet Venus, not a star
A lantern hung in the sky
x.w: Astronomers think it is Venus, not a star at all. It looks this bright in the evening and morning.

Q1171740.s: The secret: from Venus's position, astronomers even worked out roughly the day Van Gogh painted it.
Q1171740.i: Imagine: who lives in the white house and what are they doing this evening?

f: Find grapes, peaches and leaves with brown spots in the basket.
Look at how the boy turns his head.

m.q: What look does the boy have?
o: Angry, he glares right at us
Scared, he may drop the basket
m.w: He turns his head a little, lips slightly open, gaze gentle. He seems to be daydreaming.

x.q: Why do the leaves have brown spots?
o: A drop of brown paint spilled there
The painter ran out of green paint
He painted life as it really is
x.w: In real life leaves can be dry and spotted. Caravaggio painted what he saw instead of prettying it up.

Q2610936.s: The secret: Caravaggio painted real people from the streets of Rome. His model was his friend, the young painter Mario Minniti.
Q2610936.i: Imagine: which fruit will the boy hand to you, and what will he say?

f: Find Mary's red dress and blue cloak.
Find the thin glowing rings above their heads: these are halos.

m.q: How does Mary look at her baby?
o: Cross, as if the baby is naughty
Gentle and calm, with a loving look
Bored, as if she wants to go
m.w: She tilts her head a little and her gaze is lowered and soft. Her hands hold the baby gently.

x.q: Why is this called the «Madonna of the Grand Duke»?
o: A grand duke painted it all by himself
A grand duke took it on his travels
It was found in a duke's old castle
x.w: The Grand Duke of Tuscany never parted with this picture and took it on his trips. That is how it got its name.

Q2035209.s: The secret: Raphael painted Madonnas like gentle, real mothers. Against the dark background their colours glow brighter.
Q2035209.i: Imagine: what lullaby does Mary hum to the baby?

f: Find the jug in the woman's hand and the shiny basin on the table.
Find the map on the wall.

m.q: What does the woman feel?
o: Anger, she is cross with someone
Joy, she is laughing out loud
Calm, quietly lost in her thoughts
m.w: She stands still by the window with a quiet gaze. Time seems to stop.

x.q: What hangs on the wall behind the woman?
o: A big clock with golden hands
A big map of the Netherlands
A mirror in a golden frame
x.w: It is a map of the Seventeen Provinces. Dutch homes proudly hung maps on their walls.

Q386453.s: The secret: Vermeer painted soft window light gliding over the headscarf and the wall. He painted very few pictures.
Q386453.i: Imagine: what does the woman see from the window, and why did she pick up the jug?

f: Find the emperor in armour and the spear in his hand.
Look at the sky: it glows with warm sunset light.

m.q: How does the emperor look?
m.w: He sits straight, his face serious and pale, his gaze firm. The horse walks steadily.

x.q: Which victory does this picture celebrate?
o: A horse race won by his horse
A chess game won against a king
x.w: Charles V won the battle of Mühlberg in 1547. Titian painted him as the winner.

Q1123378.s: The secret: Charles V loved Titian so much that he made him a knight. Titian painted with hot, warm colours.
Q1123378.i: Imagine: what is the emperor thinking as he rides along the forest path?

f: Find the angel: he stands with his back to us, playing a violin.
Find the donkey's head behind Joseph's shoulder.

m.q: What do Mary and the baby feel?
o: Fun, they play with the angel
m.w: Mary rests her head and dozes, the baby sleeps in her arms. The music has lulled them.

x.q: What does the angel do for the tired family?
o: Reads a story from a big book
x.w: The angel plays while Joseph holds the music sheet. It is real music: scholars have even found it.

Q745098.s: The secret: Caravaggio painted real musical notes, and scholars recognised an old chant. The angel's white drapery shines.
Q745098.i: Imagine: is the angel playing a cheerful tune or a lullaby?

f: Find the cigarette in the woman's hand and the glass of beer.
Find the bright Japanese prints on the wall behind her.

m.q: What is Agostina's mood?
o: Happy and loud, she is chatting
Angry, she wants everyone to leave
m.w: She leans on her hand and looks past us. She seems lost in her own thoughts.

x.q: What does the stool she sits on look like?
x.w: The café was called «Tambourin», and its stools were made to look like tambourines.

Q2278818.s: The secret: Van Gogh loved Japanese prints and collected them. In this picture he hung them on the wall.
Q2278818.i: Imagine: what is Agostina thinking about as she sits and waits?

f: Find the old man with a hammer: he kneels.
Find the boy with the heavy basket of stones.

m.q: What is the workers' mood?
o: Tired, but they keep on working hard
Cheerful, as if it were a game
Angry, they shout at each other
m.w: Their backs are bent, faces hardly visible, clothes torn. The work is hard and they do it silently.

x.q: Who did painters usually show in huge pictures before Courbet?
x.w: Big pictures were for kings and heroes. Courbet painted ordinary workers life-size, like heroes.

Q2914912.s: The secret: Courbet believed you should paint what you see, not fairy tales. The original was lost in the Second World War, but it is known from photographs.
Q2914912.i: Imagine: what does the boy dream about after work?

f: Find the little fife the boy plays.
Look at the red trousers and the white belts crossing his chest.

m.q: How does the boy fifer look?
o: Proud, with his head held high
m.w: He stands straight, head up, with a bold gaze. He is proud of his job.

x.q: What is painted behind the boy?
o: Almost nothing: a plain light wall
A park with tall green trees
A battlefield with smoke and flags
x.w: Manet left the background smooth and empty, as in Japanese prints. That makes the boy stand out like a cut-out.

Q26250.s: The secret: the exhibition jury turned this picture down for being too flat and too bright. Today it is famous.
Q26250.i: Imagine: what is the boy playing, a march or a merry tune?

f: Find the man who looks straight at us from the dark.
Find the stone slab: its corner sticks out toward us.

m.q: What do Jesus's friends feel?
o: Joy, as if they won a prize
m.w: They bow their heads and carry him carefully. You can see how much they love him.

x.q: How does Caravaggio pull us into the picture?
o: The people turn around and wave to us
A stone corner and a stare reach out
A little dog walks out toward us
x.w: The corner of the stone sticks out and one man looks at us. It feels as if we stand next to them.

Q1213151.s: The secret: Caravaggio lit the scene from the side, like a spotlight in a dark hall. The light picks out faces and hands.
Q1213151.i: Imagine: what kind words would you whisper to Jesus's friends?

f: Find the jester: he sits in an armchair while the others have fun.
Find the brightly lit hall far behind, where the guests dance.

m.q: What does Stańczyk feel?
o: Cheerful, he wants to join the dance
Sleepiness, he is tired of dancing
m.w: He sits alone, frowning, holding a letter. He is not in the mood for a party.

x.q: Why is the jester not dancing with the others?
o: He heard worrying news about his country
He hurt his foot during the last dance
He thinks the music is much too loud
x.w: Stańczyk got worrying news while the guests were enjoying themselves. Jesters could be very wise.

Q6609268.s: The secret: Stańczyk was a real jester at the courts of Polish kings. They say jesters could tell the truth by hiding it in a joke.
Q6609268.i: Imagine: what would you say to Stańczyk to cheer him up?

f: Find the three human heads: an old man, a man and a youth.
Find the three animal heads below: a wolf, a lion and a dog.

m.q: What are the faces of the three men like?
o: Angry, as if they are arguing
Laughing, as if at a joke
m.w: They look to the side with calm brows. They seem to be thinking about something important.

x.q: What do the three ages and three animals stand for?
o: The past, the present, the future
The three seasons of the year
Three old kings who ruled Venice
x.w: The old man is thought to be the past, the man the present, the youth the future. The animals follow the same order.

Q2528145.s: The secret: words written above give advice: learn from the past to act wisely. The old man is thought to be Titian himself.
Q2528145.i: Imagine: what advice would the old man in the picture give you?

f: Find Thomas: he leans forward, his forehead wrinkled.
Count the heads: how many people are in the picture?

m.q: What do the apostles feel?
o: Boredom, they have seen it all before
m.w: They lean in very close, brows raised, eyes wide. They can hardly believe their eyes.

x.q: Why does Thomas touch Jesus's wound?
o: He wanted to heal the sore wound
He doubted and wanted to be sure
He wanted to give him a big hug
x.w: Thomas did not believe that Jesus had come back alive. Jesus let him check, and the doubts disappeared.

Q2419166.s: The secret: Caravaggio painted the apostles as ordinary men with wrinkles and worn clothes. Light falls from the side like a spotlight.
Q2419166.i: Imagine: what did Thomas say when he understood it was true?

f: Find the rainbow in the sky: there are even two!
Find the butterfly on the blind girl's shoulder.

m.q: What does the blind girl feel?
o: Quiet joy, she feels the warm sun
Fear, the storm may come back
Anger, she is cross about the rain
m.w: Her face is lifted to the sky with a faint smile. She basks in the warmth after the rain.

x.q: The girl cannot see the rainbow. How does she still enjoy the world?
o: With warm sun, music and wet grass smell
By touching the colours with her fingertips
By asking the cow what it looks like
x.w: She hears, feels warmth and smells the air. She plays a small accordion and enjoys the sounds.

Q477764.s: The secret: Millais painted grass and sky outdoors, blade by blade. Painters of his group wanted nature exactly as it is.
Q477764.i: Imagine: what tune is the girl playing, and what does she hear around her?

f: Find the boy: he stands beside his mother, her hand on his shoulder.
Look at the duchess's dress: find the golden pattern.

m.q: What is the duchess like in the portrait?
o: Calm and proud, with a firm look
Playful and giggly, full of fun
m.w: She sits straight and looks ahead calmly and sternly. That is how people used to giving orders sit.

x.q: Why did Bronzino paint every thread of the dress so carefully?
o: To show she was rich and important
To make the dress look very old
To show how warm the dress was
x.w: The cloth is woven of silk and gold thread and cost a great deal. The dress tells us she was wealthy.

Q1328065.s: The secret: Bronzino painted people smooth and calm, like porcelain. He was the court painter of the Medici family.
Q1328065.i: Imagine: what is the boy thinking beside his mother? Is he bored?

f: Find the peaches on the table and the knife beside them.
Find the warm patches of sunlight on the table and wall.

m.q: What is Vera's mood?
o: Angry, she is cross with someone
Calm and friendly, a soft smile
m.w: She looks straight at us with a slight smile. She seems comfortable and happy.

x.q: How did Serov show sunlight in the room?
o: He painted warm patches of light
He painted a lamp above the table
x.w: Light falls in patches and the shadows are coloured. That makes the room feel like summer.

Q4156438.s: The secret: Serov was only 22 when he painted this. Vera posed for many days, yet the picture is fresh, as if she just ran in from the garden.
Q4156438.i: Imagine: what did Vera do right after the painter said she could get up?

f: Find Dürer himself: he stands on the right, holding a sheet with his signature.
Find the wreaths of roses held by the angels and Mary.

m.q: What is the mood of the picture?
o: Festive and joyful, full of flowers
Sad and gloomy, like a rainy day
Stormy, with dark clouds and thunder
m.w: Flowers, angels' music and calm faces. It is a real celebration.

x.q: What is being handed out in this picture?
o: Round golden balls to play with
x.w: Mary and the angels crown people with wreaths of roses. The word rosary once meant a rose garland.

Q1170194.s: The secret: Dürer was famous for prints. Here, in Venice, he showed he could handle colour too. He even painted himself.
Q1170194.i: Imagine: which wreath would you choose, and to whom would you give it?

f: Find the window with mountains and a lake behind Dürer.
Look at his curly hair, his cap and his gloves.

m.q: How does Dürer look?
o: Frightened, as if he saw a ghost
Sleepy, as if he just woke up
m.w: He stands straight and looks calm, like a man who knows his worth.

x.q: What is written on the painting itself?
o: How much money the painting costs
That he was 26 and painted himself
A secret recipe for mixing his paint
x.w: The words say he painted this from his own looks at the age of 26. Dürer was proud of his skill.

Q2388965.s: The secret: Dürer was one of the first to draw himself again and again. He made his first self-portrait at 13.
Q2388965.i: Imagine: what would 26-year-old Dürer say about his fashionable clothes?

f: Find the maid: she stands at the window looking outside.
Find the letter and the red sealing wax on the floor.

m.q: What is the lady's mood?
o: Cross, she is annoyed at the maid
Sleepy, she is almost asleep here
m.w: She bends over the letter and does not look up. It seems she has something important to write.

x.q: What does the maid do while the lady writes?
o: Reads the letter over her shoulder
Sits down for a little nap by the wall
Waits and looks out of the window
x.w: The maid stands with her hands folded, looking out of the window. She waits for the letter to be ready.

Q641666.s: The secret: Vermeer loved quiet moments and light from a window on the left. Letters were a big part of life then: it was how people spoke across distances.
Q641666.i: Imagine: who is the lady writing to, and what does the letter say?

f: Find the wreath of olive branches on Pallas's head.
Find the centaur's bow.

m.q: What does the centaur feel?
o: Joy and pride, as if he had won
Anger, he wants to fight Pallas
m.w: He bows his head, his shoulders drop, his face is sad. He no longer wants to rampage.

x.q: What does wise Pallas do to the wild centaur?
o: Calms him by holding his hair
Chases him off with her spear
x.w: Pallas is the goddess of wisdom. She holds the centaur calmly: wisdom tames wild impulses.

Q2426058.s: The secret: Botticelli drew with flowing lines, like ribbons. Pallas's dress is decorated with rings and olive branches.
Q2426058.i: Imagine: what did Pallas say to the centaur?

f: Find Luke: he kneels and draws.
Look through the window: find the town and the river far away.

m.q: What is Mary's mood?
o: Quiet and tender with her baby
Worried, she keeps watching the door
m.w: She sits calmly, holding the baby, her face soft. It is quiet and warm in the room.

x.q: What does Luke draw Mary with?
o: A feather pen and a pot of ink
A big stick of white chalk
A thin stick of silver metal
x.w: He draws with a silver stylus that leaves a thin, light line. Masters drew like that long ago.

Q286096.s: The secret: Luke is the patron saint of painters, so painters loved this story. Every painter could imagine himself in Luke's place.
Q286096.i: Imagine: what do Luke and Mary talk about while he draws?

f: Find the hat with red flowers on the woman's head.
Find the fan in the woman's hand and the man's straw hat.

m.q: What do the dancers feel?
o: Joy, they smile as they spin
Sadness, they say a long goodbye
Anger, they argue as they dance
m.w: She laughs and he holds her firmly. They whirl around and feel good.

x.q: How did Renoir show a sunny garden?
o: With soft dabs of colour and light
With sharp black lines around everything
With flat grey paint, all one tone
x.w: He painted with light strokes, so the light seems to tremble among the leaves.

Q1114718.s: The secret: the woman in the picture later became Renoir's wife. It has a twin, «Dance in the City»: both hang in the same museum.
Q1114718.i: Imagine: what music is playing, and what are they saying as they dance?

f: Find the high walls: the prisoners walk in a circle, like on a merry-go-round.
Find the guards who watch them.

m.q: What do the men in the yard feel?
o: Fun, they are playing a game
Weariness and longing to be free
Joy, they love the fresh air
m.w: They walk round with their heads down. The grey walls press on them.

x.q: Where did Van Gogh get this scene?
o: He dreamed it all up one night
He watched it from his own window
He copied a print and added colour
x.w: Van Gogh liked to paint from prints by other masters, adding his own colours.

Q1132723.s: The secret: Van Gogh painted it in a hospital in Saint-Rémy. He said copying is like a musician playing someone else's music in his own way.
Q1132723.i: Imagine: what do the prisoners dream about when they look up above the walls?

f: Find the little boy: he looks up at his grandfather.
Look through the window: what can you see far away?

m.q: What do they feel for each other?
o: Warmth and love, a tender bond
m.w: The little one looks up trustfully, and the old man gazes at him tenderly. They are close.

x.q: Did the painter make the old man's face prettier than it was?
o: No, he kept the wrinkles and bumpy nose
Yes, he smoothed away every single wrinkle
He hid the bumpy nose behind a hand
x.w: Ghirlandaio showed the old man as he was, with wrinkles. Love shows in the look, not in beauty.

Q23915.s: The secret: young Michelangelo learned in Ghirlandaio's workshop. A view through a window was a favourite trick of painters then.
Q23915.i: Imagine: what is the grandfather telling the boy?

f: Find the parasol and the straw hat with a black ribbon.
Find the patches of leaf shadow on the white dress.

m.q: What is Lise's mood?
o: Cross, she is tired of waiting
Anxious, she is looking for someone
Calm, dreamy, resting in the shade
m.w: She stands still and looks into the distance. It is warm and quiet for her in the shade of the trees.

x.q: Where do the dark patches on the white dress come from?
o: Paint that dripped onto the dress
Shadows of leaves in the sunshine
Little flowers sewn onto the dress
x.w: Sun shines through the leaves and lays soft patches on the dress. Renoir painted shadows bluish and lilac, not grey.

Q2783729.s: The secret: Renoir showed this picture at a big exhibition in Paris, and it brought him success. He painted it in summer near the Forest of Fontainebleau.
Q2783729.i: Imagine: what does Lise hear in the forest: birds, wind, rustling leaves?

f: Find the skull on the table.
See how the red cloak glows brightly in the dark.

m.q: How does Jerome look?
o: Playful, he is about to laugh
m.w: He bends over the page and does not look around. His brow is furrowed, his hand writes.

x.q: What big job did Saint Jerome do?
o: Built a great stone bridge in Rome
Wrote a big book of fairy tales
x.w: Jerome translated the Bible into Latin so that more people could read it.

Q2715177.s: The secret: Caravaggio lit the scene with strong light from the side, like a spotlight. The bald head and red cloak flash out of the darkness.
Q2715177.i: Imagine: what sentence is Jerome writing right now?

f: Find Merlin among the blossoming hawthorn branches.
Find Nimue: she casts the spell while Merlin cannot move.

m.q: What is happening to Merlin?
o: He is laughing at a funny joke
He is spellbound and cannot move
He is rushing to get away
m.w: He stares with a fixed gaze and does not stir. The spell has bound him.

x.q: What did Nimue use to enchant Merlin?
o: A potion in a little bottle
x.w: In the legend she used spells from his own book. A clever pupil outwitted the wise old wizard.

Q4188993.s: The secret: Burne-Jones loved legends of knights and painted them like a beautiful old tapestry. Every flower and leaf is carefully drawn.
Q4188993.i: Imagine: which spell would you cast if you were Merlin?

f: Find the green stripe down the woman's nose.
Find the huge hat with flowers and feathers.

m.q: How does the lady look?
o: Sad, as if she lost something
Calm and stately, head held high
Confused, as if she is lost
m.w: She sits straight, head high, with a confident gaze. Not a hint of fear.

x.q: Why is there a green stripe on the face?
o: He ran out of skin-coloured paint
She had put green powder on her nose
x.w: Matisse thought colour can speak of feelings. So his faces are bright and unusual.

Q1437492.s: The secret: visitors laughed, and a critic called these painters «wild beasts», in French «fauves». The name stuck.
Q1437492.i: Imagine: which colours would you choose for her hat?

f: Find the angel Gabriel: he has multicoloured wings.
Find the golden words: some are written upside down!

m.q: What does Mary feel?
o: Fun, she wants to play a game
m.w: She stands still with her hands together and a serious gaze. She is hearing important news.

x.q: Why are Mary's words written upside down?
o: So God, looking down, can read them
The painter made a mistake there
It is a riddle for children to solve
x.w: The words face the sky, not us. That is how Van Eyck showed that Mary answers God.

Q2734881.s: The secret: Van Eyck painted wonderfully in oil: jewels and gold sparkle in his work. He was one of those who perfected oil paint.
Q2734881.i: Imagine: what did Gabriel say to Mary? And what did she answer?

f: Find the funnel on the «doctor's» head.
Find the book on the woman's head.

m.q: What does the patient feel?
o: Joy, he is having a lovely day
Sleepiness, he is about to doze off
Worry and unease, he looks for help
m.w: He sits and looks straight at us, brows drawn, as if asking for help.

x.q: What is on the «doctor's» head?
o: A funnel worn like a hat
x.w: A funnel is a sign of foolishness. Bosch laughs at tricksters who promised to cut out a «stone of folly».

Q2270768.s: The secret: Bosch loved inventing funny and strange details to tease people's silliness. The «stone» in the head here is a flower!
Q2270768.i: Imagine: what silly «stone of folly» would you pull out of your own head?

f: Find the plum on the table in front of the woman.
Find the hand she leans her head on.

m.q: What is the woman's mood?
o: Angry, she is cross with the waiter
m.w: She stares ahead and seems not to notice anything around her.

x.q: Where is this woman sitting?
o: At a table in a Paris café
In a palace, on a velvet chair
On the deck of a big ship
x.w: Manet painted ordinary Paris life: cafés, parks, passers-by. Painting like this was not usual before.

Q731639.s: The secret: Manet painted the life around him, not ancient legends, and many found that daring. His brushstrokes are quick and free.
Q731639.i: Imagine: who is the woman waiting for, and what is she thinking about?

f: Find the hand resting on the woman's belly.
Look at the soft folds of her sleeves.

m.q: What is the mood of this woman?
o: Quiet and calm, a soft gaze
m.w: She sits straight, her gaze soft and steady. She seems peaceful.

x.q: What does «donna gravida» mean in Italian?
o: A lady in a long green velvet dress
A lady with a big golden ring
A lady who is expecting a baby
x.w: «Donna» is a lady and «gravida» is one who is expecting a child. The hand on her belly says so too.

Q2276546.s: The secret: at this time Raphael lived in Florence studying Leonardo. Her calm pose is a little like the Mona Lisa's.
Q2276546.i: Imagine: what will the baby that this woman is expecting be called?

f: Find the lady's earrings and necklace.
Find her long coppery hair.

m.q: What is this lady like?
o: Angry, she is about to scold someone
Calm and confident, a steady look
m.w: She looks straight at us, calmly and a little proudly.

x.q: Why is reddish-golden hair called «Titian hair»?
o: A hairdresser called Titian invented the colour
It is the colour of the shiny metal titanium
Named after Titian, who painted it so often
x.w: Titian loved painting golden-red hair. The colour was named after him.

Q3784247.s: The secret: Titian was the greatest master of colour in Venice. He used warm, rich colours, and his fabrics shimmer.
Q3784247.i: Imagine: what is the lady's name, and what will she tell about her day?

f: Find the blue curly pattern that runs across the red table and wall.
Find the window with the green garden.

m.q: What is the mood of the red room?
o: Cold and gloomy, like a cellar
Warm and cosy, like a blanket
Quiet and sad, like a rainy day
m.w: Red floods everything like a warm blanket. The room feels hot and festive.

x.q: What colour did Matisse paint this picture first?
x.w: At first the room was blue, and then Matisse repainted it red. The table and the wall merged into one red patch.

Q921429.s: The secret: Matisse believed colour matters more than perspective. So the table and wall seem to lie on one flat surface. A Russian collector, Shchukin, bought it.
Q921429.i: Imagine: what dessert is on the red table?

f: Find the stone ledge at the bottom with letters.
Find the man's big cloth hat.

m.q: How does the man look?
o: Cheerful, about to laugh out loud
m.w: He looks aside, his gaze sharp and calm. He is clearly thinking about something.

x.q: Are the letters on the stone really carved?
o: No, painted to look like carving
No, cut from paper and glued on top
x.w: Van Eyck painted the letters so skilfully that they look like stone. The title means «loyal remembrance».

Q1150782.s: The secret: Van Eyck painted with such patience that tiny lines in the face show. He was one of the first masters of oil paint.
Q1150782.i: Imagine: whom does this man keep a loyal memory of?

f: Find the two women who have met and embrace.
Find the clouds and God the Father above.

m.q: What do the two women feel?
m.w: They reach toward each other and bow their heads. They are happy to see each other.

x.q: Who are these two women?
o: Strangers who just met on the road
x.w: Mary came to visit her relative Elizabeth, and both were expecting babies. It is a story of a joyful meeting.

Q2467082.s: The secret: Giulio Romano was Raphael's best pupil and helped him in the workshop.
Q2467082.i: Imagine: what gift did Mary bring Elizabeth?

f: Find the she-wolf feeding the two babies.
Find the shepherd who found the twins.

m.q: How does the wolf look at the babies?
o: Caring and calm, like a mother
Angry, as if the babies are noisy
Sleepy, as if she wants a nap
m.w: She lowers her head to the babies and stands gently. The wolf guards them like a mother.

x.q: Which city did Romulus found?
x.w: The twins grew up, and Romulus founded a city and gave it his name. It was Rome.

Q3940915.s: The secret: Rubens painted strong, rosy people full of movement. He lived eight years in Italy learning from great masters.
Q3940915.i: Imagine: what did the wolf say to the twins when they grew up?

f: Find the bird trap: a board propped up on a stick.
Find the people skating on the frozen river.

m.q: What is the mood in the village?
o: Scary, like a story about ghosts
Busy and hot, like a summer fair
Calm and quiet, people play on ice
m.w: People skate and play and are in no hurry. It is quiet and cold above the houses.

x.q: How does this trap work?
o: Birds get caught in a net on a pole
Birds are caught in a cage with a door
The stick falls, the board covers the birds
x.w: It is a simple trap: once the birds come for the grain, the board can drop.

Q873639.s: The secret: Bruegel painted from high up, as if looking down like a bird. He made people small, like in a big world.
Q873639.i: Imagine: which game would you play on the ice?

f: Find the young man's cap.
See where his shoulders turn and where he looks.

m.q: How does the young man look?
o: Frightened, as if he heard a noise
Sleepy, as if he had just woken up
m.w: He looks straight out, calmly. That is how someone who knows his worth looks.

x.q: How did Raphael bring the portrait to life?
o: He painted him running down a long road
He turned head and shoulders apart
He painted his eyes closed, dreaming
x.w: The shoulders face one way and the face another. It looks as if someone has just called his name.

Q2422889.s: The secret: this painting went missing during the war and is still being searched for. We know it from photographs and copies.
Q2422889.i: Imagine: what is the young man's name, and what will he become?

f: Find Mary's hand raised toward us.
Find the book on the stand in front of her.

m.q: What does Mary's face express?
o: Anger, she is cross with us
m.w: She raises a hand and lifts her head slightly. As if she heard something extraordinary.

x.q: Where is the angel Gabriel in this picture?
o: Not here: we stand in his place
Tiny, flying in the top left corner
x.w: The angel is not painted. Mary looks at us as if we were the messenger. That puts us inside the picture.

Q3332564.s: The secret: Antonello was among the first in Italy to paint in oil. Oil gives a soft glow.
Q3332564.i: Imagine: what has Gabriel just said to Mary?

f: Find the cat.
Find the bread and the red wine on the table.

m.q: What is the mood of the people in the osteria?
o: Gloomy, as if it rained all day
Sad, as if they all said goodbye
m.w: They sit at the table eating and drinking together. You can see they feel cosy.

x.q: What is an osteria?
o: A simple inn with food and wine
A little school for young painters
A small boat that sails the Tiber
x.w: An osteria is a simple Italian place with food and wine. Friends gather there.

Q16965482.s: The secret: Carl Bloch was a Danish painter who lived in Rome. He mostly painted Bible scenes, but here he painted a merry meal.
Q16965482.i: Imagine: what did these people order, and what are they talking about?

f: Find the girl's butterfly wings.
Find the boy's feathered wings.

m.q: What do the children feel?
o: Tenderness and joy as they hug
m.w: The children hold each other tenderly. It feels warm beside each other.

x.q: What kind of wings does the girl Psyche have?
x.w: In Greek «psyche» means both «soul» and «butterfly». That is why she has butterfly wings.

Q2344593.s: The secret: Bouguereau painted so smoothly that skin looks like porcelain. He disliked visible brushstrokes, unlike the Impressionists.
Q2344593.i: Imagine: where will Cupid and Psyche fly next?

f: Find the angels in blue: each wears a white deer badge.
Find the little banner with a red cross held by an angel.

m.q: What is the mood of Mary and the angels?
o: Calm and kind, a warm welcome
Cross, as if someone was late
Worried, as if danger is near
m.w: They stand quietly and look gently. It is as if they warmly welcome the king.

x.q: Which animal is on the angels' badges?
x.w: The white deer, or hart, was King Richard II's badge. The angels wear it to show the king is under their protection.

Q1813497.s: The secret: this picture is over 600 years old, and its blue was made from a costly stone, lapis lazuli. Nobody knows who painted it.
Q1813497.i: Imagine: what is the king asking for as he kneels?

f: Find the boats with white sails.
Find the people on the shore with parasols.

m.q: What is the mood of the day at the shore?
o: Sunny and merry, like a holiday
Stormy and scary, with huge waves
m.w: Bright sky, blue sea and white sails. Everyone watches the race and enjoys it.

x.q: Where did Monet stand when he painted?
o: In a quiet studio, from memory
On a cloud high above the sea
x.w: Monet liked to paint outdoors to catch real light and wind.

Q734082.s: The secret: Monet painted with quick strokes, and the water sparkles. The word «Impressionism» came from another of his paintings, «Impression, Sunrise».
Q734082.i: Imagine: which boat will win the race, and why?

f: Find the hand the lady rests on her hip.
Find the black lace on her head and shoulders.

m.q: How does the lady carry herself?
o: Shyly, hiding her face a little
Proudly, with her hand on her hip
m.w: Hand on hip, head high, gaze direct. That is how a confident person stands.

x.q: What is the black lace veil on her head called?
x.w: A mantilla is a Spanish lace veil. Goya loved Spanish costume.

Q1585399.s: The secret: Goya was court painter to the King of Spain. He was not afraid to show people as they really were, with character.
Q1585399.i: Imagine: what did the lady say to Goya while posing?

f: Find the bow and arrows beside the sleeping boy.
Find his little wings.

m.q: How does Cupid feel?
o: Angry, he stamps his little foot
Afraid, he hides from the dark
m.w: Eyes shut, hands relaxed, mouth slightly open. He sleeps a deep child's sleep.

x.q: What does Cupid do with his bow?
o: Catches shiny fish in the river
Plays it like a little violin
x.w: Cupid is the god of love, and his arrows make people love. While he sleeps, nobody shoots.

Q2429754.s: The secret: Caravaggio painted the god as a real chubby toddler, not as a symbol. Light falls from the side like a spotlight.
Q2429754.i: Imagine: what does little Cupid dream about?

f: Find Jeanne's smile.
Look at the background: what warm colours does it have?

m.q: What is Jeanne's mood?
o: Lively and cheerful, ready to talk
Gloomy, she has had bad news
Cross, she is annoyed at someone
m.w: Her lips part in a smile and her eyes sparkle. She seems about to speak.

x.q: What was Jeanne's job?
o: A baker in a busy bakery
A sailor on a tall ship
x.w: Jeanne Samary acted at the Comédie-Française in Paris. Renoir painted her cheerful and bright.

Q3807740.s: The secret: Renoir loved cheerful faces and painted with light, feathery strokes. His skin glows like a peach.
Q3807740.i: Imagine: which play is Jeanne about to perform?

f: Find the cat on the floor.
Find the tangled yarn on the floor and the piano.

m.q: What expression does the woman have?
o: Giggly, as if she heard a joke
Serious, as if a thought struck her
Sleepy, as if she is in a dream
m.w: She has jumped up, her eyes wide, gazing into the distance. As if an important thought struck her.

x.q: What is reflected in the mirror behind her?
o: A sunny garden beyond the window
A portrait of an old gentleman
A big clock with golden hands
x.w: The mirror shows a bright garden. Hunt shows that beyond the room's walls there is another, brighter life.

Q7715071.s: The secret: Hunt painted every tiny thing, and each has a hidden meaning, like the tangle of thread and the cat. He was a Pre-Raphaelite: they painted very exactly.
Q7715071.i: Imagine: what will the woman do next, when she walks to the window?

f: Find Mary and the baby on a donkey, with Joseph beside them.
Look into the distance: find mountains and water.

m.q: What is the family's mood?
o: Merry, they are going to a party
Calm but tired after a long way
Angry, they argue about the road
m.w: They travel quietly, in no hurry, but the road is long. Mary holds the baby carefully.

x.q: Why did Bruegel paint the family so small?
o: He ran out of room on the canvas
To show how huge the world is
He wanted to save his paint
x.w: Next to the huge mountains and valley, people look tiny. The world feels wide and endless.

Q1803755.s: The secret: Bruegel travelled across the Alps to Italy, and the mountains later entered his pictures. He loved painting wide landscapes.
Q1803755.i: Imagine: what will the little family see around the bend of the road?

f: Find the cup of hot chocolate and the glass of water on the tray.
Find the girl's white apron and little cap.

m.q: How does the girl look?
o: Cross, she scowls at the tray
Sleepy, she yawns as she walks
m.w: She looks down at the tray and walks carefully. To avoid spilling, she must pay attention.

x.q: What did Liotard make this picture with?
o: Oil paint on a thick wooden panel
A plain pencil on white paper
x.w: It is pastel: coloured chalks that go on very softly and give a velvety surface.

Q445627.s: The secret: Liotard lived in Turkey for several years and grew a long beard. He was nicknamed the «Turkish painter».
Q445627.i: Imagine: who is she carrying the chocolate to, and is it far?

f: Find Mary lying on her bed with her friends standing around.
Find the lake with a bridge and a town in the distance.

m.q: What is the mood of Mary's friends?
m.w: They stand in silence with bowed heads. Each says goodbye in his own way.

x.q: What did Mantegna show beyond the arches?
o: A sandy desert with a camel
A snowy mountain with a castle
A lake with a bridge and a town
x.w: Through the arches you see a calm landscape with water, a bridge and a town. The landscape makes the scene deep and bright.

Q959537.s: The secret: Mantegna loved strict lines and depth. His people look solid, like sculptures.
Q959537.i: Imagine: what do the apostles remember about Mary?

f: Find Mary: she stands high on a pedestal.
Find the little bird-women, the harpies, on the pedestal.

m.q: How does Mary look?
o: Angry, she scowls at the two saints
m.w: She stands straight, holding the baby, and looks quiet. Like a festival picture.

x.q: Why is the picture called «Madonna of the Harpies»?
o: Harpies fly around her head like birds
A rich man called Harpy ordered it
x.w: Harpies are fairy-tale birds with women's faces. Their figures are carved on the stone under Mary's feet.

Q1235695.s: The secret: Andrea del Sarto was called the «faultless painter»: his drawing has almost no mistakes.
Q1235695.i: Imagine: give one little harpy a name and say what it loves to do.

f: Find the boy's red vest.
Find his long arm.

m.q: How does the boy look?
o: Cheerful, he is up to mischief
Cross, he is angry at someone
m.w: He rests his head on his hand and looks aside. He seems to be dreaming.

x.q: What is odd about the boy's arm?
o: It is very long, on purpose
It is far too short, by mistake
It is missing, hidden by his vest
x.w: Cézanne cared about shape and colour balance. The long arm helps the picture feel balanced.

Q2270805.s: The secret: Cézanne is called the father of modern art: Picasso and Matisse learned from him. His models had to pose for a very long time.
Q2270805.i: Imagine: what is the boy in the red vest dreaming about?

f: Find the windmill on the high bank.
Find the sailing boat on the river.

m.q: What is the mood of this landscape?
m.w: Clouds race across the sky and the sails are full. A fresh wind blows, and it is easy to breathe.

x.q: What takes up the most space in the picture?
x.w: Ruisdael painted a huge sky that fills most of the picture. Holland is flat, and the sky above it is like a dome.

Q2881603.s: The secret: Ruisdael is counted among the best Dutch landscape painters. His clouds seem alive.
Q2881603.i: Imagine: which way is the wind blowing, and what is the sailing boat carrying?

f: Find the baby on the ground and Mary beside him.
Find the shepherds: they have come to honour the baby.

m.q: What do the shepherds feel?
m.w: They have come quietly, with respect. You can see this is an important moment for them.

x.q: What in the picture is as important as the people?
o: A huge castle with tall towers
A calm land of hills and trees
A big ship sailing on a wide sea
x.w: Giorgione painted dreamy landscapes. Soft hills and trees are part of the story itself.

Q3605563.s: The secret: Giorgione died young, at about thirty-three, and left very few paintings. His landscapes are like a dream.
Q3605563.i: Imagine: what gift did the shepherds bring the baby?

f: Find the bandage on Van Gogh's ear.
Find the easel with a canvas behind him.

m.q: How does Van Gogh look?
o: Angry, he is ready to shout at us
Calm and serious, a bit tired
m.w: He looks straight out, lips pressed together, dressed warmly. He seems to be gathering his strength.

x.q: How could Van Gogh paint his own face?
o: From a photograph taken by a friend
By looking at himself in a mirror
x.w: He looked in a mirror, so the bandage appears on the opposite side from where it really was.

Q19363211.s: The secret: Van Gogh painted many self-portraits because he could not afford models. Painting himself was cheap.
Q19363211.i: Imagine: what does Van Gogh say to himself in the mirror?

f: Find the rosary: a string of beads.
See where Mary and the child look.

m.q: What is the mood of Mary and the child?
o: Cross, as if they had quarrelled
m.w: Mary holds the baby close and he nestles trustfully against her. All is soft and warm.

x.q: What is a rosary?
o: A small clock to tell the time
Beads on a string to count prayers
x.w: A rosary is a string of beads people use to count prayers. You can see one in this picture.

Q3918296.s: The secret: Murillo of Seville painted gentle Madonnas, and with kind eyes he also painted poor street children.
Q3918296.i: Imagine: what does Mary quietly tell the baby?

f: Find the boats on the beach.
Find the dark clouds above the sea.

m.q: What is the sea like here?
o: Calm, like a smooth shining mirror
Frozen solid, like a big ice rink
m.w: Waves with white crests, a heavy sky, wind. You can tell the weather is turning.

x.q: What got stuck in the paint while Van Gogh worked?
o: Sand blown in by the wind
x.w: Van Gogh painted on the beach in a strong wind, and sand stuck to the fresh paint. Traces of sand remain in the picture.

Q4110564.s: The secret: this is one of Van Gogh's first oil paintings. He painted outdoors, not afraid of bad weather.
Q4110564.i: Imagine: what sounds can you hear on this shore?

f: Find the huge bell: it is being lifted on ropes.
Find the king and queen in fine clothes.

m.q: What do the people around the bell feel?
o: Boredom, they wish it were over
Fear, they think it will fall
m.w: Everyone presses close to look and help, faces intent. It is a big event.

x.q: What is this bell famous for?
o: It is the smallest bell in the world
It is made of pure solid gold
It is one of Poland's biggest bells
x.w: The Sigismund Bell is huge and rings on the most important days.

Q8067460.s: The secret: Matejko painted great events of Poland. He put in real people: kings, craftsmen and even the jester Stańczyk.
Q8067460.i: Imagine: what sound will the bell make the very first time?

f: Find the figure with the violin.
Find the blue sky and the green hill.

m.q: What do the singing figures feel?
o: Sleepiness, they want to lie down
m.w: They stand straight and sing with all their might. You can see the music has swept them away.

x.q: How many colours did Matisse use?
o: Ten: a whole rainbow of colours
Five: red, blue, green and yellow
x.w: Blue sky, green hill and red people. Only three colours, but very bright ones.

Q1999166.s: The secret: Matisse made the figures simple and flat, with no shadows. A Russian collector, Shchukin, ordered it along with «Dance».
Q1999166.i: Imagine: what song are they singing?

f: Find Dürer below: he stands next to a tablet with his name.
Find the dove above in the golden light.

m.q: What is the mood of this celebration?
o: Sad and grey, like a long rainy day
Scary and dark, like a deep cave
Solemn and bright, like a festival
m.w: Golden light, clouds, a multitude of saints and angels. It is like a grand celebration.

x.q: Where did Dürer paint himself?
o: Among the angels flying high above
Dressed as the Pope, at the centre
Down below, near a signed tablet
x.w: Dürer stands as a small figure below, beside a tablet with the year and his signature.

Q688870.s: The secret: the picture is full of people, from the pope and emperor to farmers. Each has a different face.
Q688870.i: Imagine: whom in the crowd would you like to talk to, and about what?

f: Find the two men with clubs.
Look at the ground: where are their legs?

m.q: What mood does Goya create?
o: Gloomy and uneasy, with a grey sky
m.w: Grey sky, heavy tones and angry blows. The picture makes you uneasy.

x.q: Why can the men not run away?
o: They are far too lazy to run away
They are tied together by a long rope
They sank knee-deep into the ground
x.w: They are stuck in the earth and can only fight. Goya showed how foolish and hopeless a fight is.

Q1747282.s: The secret: Goya painted it on the wall of his house when he was old and deaf. Later it was moved onto canvas.
Q1747282.i: Imagine: what words would stop this fight?

f: Find the little round mirror on the table.
Find the scales in the man's hands.

m.q: How does the man with the scales look?
o: Sleepy, he is dozing at his desk
Focused, he is weighing his coins
Cheerful, he is humming a happy tune
m.w: He leans forward and watches the scales closely. He is wholly absorbed by the coins.

x.q: What is reflected in the little round mirror?
o: A man reading by the window
Mountains and a ship at sea
A dark forest with tall trees
x.w: The mirror shows a man reading by a window. Painters loved to hide a piece of the world outside the picture in mirrors.

Q2892964.s: The secret: Massys painted tiny things like the gleam of pearls and coins very carefully. He lived in Antwerp.
Q2892964.i: Imagine: what are the husband and wife talking about?

f: Find Mary with the baby.
Find the angel: look at its face.

m.q: What can you say about Mary's gaze?
o: Soft and a little sad, thoughtful
Hard and sharp, like a scolding
m.w: She looks gently and a little sadly, as if thinking about the baby's future. All is calm.

x.q: Whom did young Botticelli learn from?
o: The monk and painter Filippo Lippi
The great inventor Leonardo da Vinci
The young painter Raphael from Urbino
x.w: His teacher was Fra Filippo Lippi, a monk who painted very tender Madonnas. You can see it in the soft faces.

Q580853.s: The secret: Botticelli's real name was Alessandro Filipepi. «Botticelli» means «little barrel»: it was his brother's nickname.
Q580853.i: Imagine: what does the angel whisper to the baby?

f: Find the card hidden behind the cheat's back.
Look at the eyes: who is looking at whom?

m.q: What does the young man in the feathered hat feel?
o: He is angry: he saw the whole trick
He is scared: he fears he will lose
m.w: He looks at his cards and pays no attention to anything else. Meanwhile the others exchange glances.

x.q: What is the cheat's trick?
o: He is counting the gold coins
He sneaks a hidden ace into play
He is shuffling the whole deck
x.w: The cheat hides an extra ace in his belt and wants to slip it into the game. The others can see it.

Q1193312.s: The secret: La Tour painted people smooth like wooden figures, in warm light. For a long time he was almost forgotten, and then rediscovered.
Q1193312.i: Imagine: what will the young man say when he discovers the trick?

f: Find the glove in the man's hand.
Look at his face and hand: they glow against the dark background.

m.q: How does the man with the glove look?
o: Thoughtful and gentle, a soft gaze
Laughing loudly at a funny joke
m.w: He looks aside, his gaze soft and serious. He seems to be thinking quiet thoughts.

x.q: What glows most against the dark background?
x.w: The clothes and background are dark, so the face and hand seem especially bright. Titian used this as a trick.

Q1848811.s: The secret: Titian was the best painter in Venice. His portraits show not just a face but a person's thoughts.
Q1848811.i: Imagine: what is the man's name, and what does he like to do?

f: Find the white lily in the angel's hand.
Find the blue curtain behind Mary.

m.q: How does Mary feel beside the angel?
m.w: She huddles on the bed, eyes wide. She is both frightened and amazed.

x.q: What does the lily in the angel's hand stand for?
x.w: A white lily is an old sign of purity. The whole picture is nearly white, like this flower.

Q2425901.s: The secret: Rossetti was one of the founders of the Pre-Raphaelites. Mary here is not a stately queen but a frightened girl, which surprised many.
Q2425901.i: Imagine: what news did Gabriel bring, and how will Mary tell it to her mother?

f: Find the soft fur on the collar.
Find the white hair and beard: so many separate hairs!

m.q: How does Mr Holzschuher look?
o: Cheerful, he is about to smile broadly
Stern and sharp-eyed, a firm look
m.w: His gaze is sharp and direct, his brows frown. He looks like a man used to deciding.

x.q: How did Dürer paint the white hair?
o: With a single stroke of grey paint
One hair at a time, thin brush
With a very broad, flat brush
x.w: Dürer painted each hair with a very fine brush, which is why they look real.

Q3937568.s: The secret: Dürer was also famous for prints. He drew a rhinoceros he had never seen, only heard described, and everyone remembered it.
Q3937568.i: Imagine: what question would he ask you with such a stern look?

f: Find the row of trees along the lane.
Find the house among the trees.

m.q: What is the mood of this place?
o: Stormy and scary, with dark clouds
Quiet and sunny, like a summer day
Noisy and busy, like a market
m.w: Warm yellows and greens. It feels quiet and hot, like summer.

x.q: What did Van Gogh paint leaves and grass with?
x.w: He laid paint in short strokes, like stitches. That makes the picture seem to tremble and live.

Q4657634.s: The secret: Van Gogh came to Arles in the south of France for the sun. He painted a great many pictures there in under two years.
Q4657634.i: Imagine: where does the lane lead, and who lives in the house?

f: Find the crab lying on its back.
Find the big claws.

m.q: What is the mood of these crabs?
o: Fast asleep, resting in the sand
Lively, as if about to scuttle off
Sad, as if they miss the sea home
m.w: Legs and claws are spread, as if the crab is about to move. The picture is full of motion.

x.q: Which far-off art did Van Gogh love?
x.w: Van Gogh collected Japanese prints, which often show crabs and fish on a plain background. From them he took a bright, flat style.

Q19356352.s: The secret: Van Gogh liked looking closely at the simplest things: shoes, sunflowers, onions, crabs. And he made each one interesting.
Q19356352.i: Imagine: what are the two crabs called, and what are they arguing about?

f: Find the brightest spot in the sky: where is it lightest?
Find where the warm colours turn into dark ones.

m.q: What is the mood of this sunset?
o: Worried, as if a storm is near
Cheerful and noisy, like a party
m.w: The light fades softly and everything stills. It feels as if silence is all around.

x.q: How do the colours of the sky change at sunset?
o: The whole sky is one flat colour
From yellow to orange, red, dark blue
From green to pink and then purple
x.w: Near the sun the sky is bright and yellow, further away orange and red, and high up it is dark. Friedrich painted these smooth changes.

Q4531523.s: The secret: Friedrich said: close your eyes to see the picture with your inner eye. He painted not only what he saw but what he felt.
Q4531523.i: Imagine: who is watching this sunset, and what do they say?

f: Find the little bird high in the sky.
Look at the wheat: how many different colours did Van Gogh mix in it?

m.q: What is the mood of the field?
o: Lively and fresh, the wheat sways
Scary, like a dark forest at night
m.w: The ears of wheat bend and the strokes run in waves. The field seems to breathe.

x.q: What is the lark famous for?
o: It sings while it flies up high
It dives deep under the water
It glows in the dark at night
x.w: The lark rises high and sings without stopping. You can almost hear that song in the picture.

Q262360.s: The secret: Van Gogh painted this field in Paris, where he learned brighter colour from the Impressionists. He painted wheat all his life.
Q262360.i: Imagine: what song is the lark singing?

f: Find the deer with a cross between its antlers.
Find a bear, a heron and a rabbit in the forest.

m.q: What does Eustace feel?
o: Boredom, he wants to go home
m.w: He has stopped before the wonder, and the hunt is forgotten.

x.q: What did the hunter Eustace see in the forest?
o: A huge brown bear in a cave
A golden castle in the clouds
A stag with a cross in its antlers
x.w: After this vision, Eustace put down his bow, stopped hunting and chose a new way of life.

Q669872.s: The secret: Pisanello was famous for accurate drawings of animals. He painted each bird and beast so you can recognise it.
Q669872.i: Imagine: which animal would you ask for the way through the forest?

f: Find the clouds in the blue sky.
Find the landscape behind Mary.

m.q: How does Mary hold the child?
o: Carelessly, as if to drop him
Crossly, as if about to let go
m.w: She is calm and holds the child gently. All around is stillness, like deep thought.

x.q: What did Bellini show behind Mary's shoulders?
o: A stormy sea with huge waves
A busy city square with a market
Calm countryside and a cloudy sky
x.w: A quiet landscape with sky and clouds opens behind Mary. It makes the picture bright and calm.

Q1762826.s: The secret: Giovanni Bellini was the leading painter of Venice and the teacher of Giorgione and Titian. He painted with soft, glowing oils.
