Q1762826.i: Imagine: what would the baby say if he could talk?

f: Find the dove in the golden glow.
Find the angel Gabriel: his clothes billow.

m.q: How does Mary greet the angel?
o: With boredom, she yawns at him
With fun, she claps her hands
m.w: She throws up her hands and shrinks back. The angel's arrival astonishes her.

x.q: What is special about how old Titian painted this picture?
o: Only pencil, with no paint at all
x.w: In old age Titian painted boldly and broadly. That makes light and fabric seem to tremble.

Q2920183.s: The secret: Titian painted this when he was over seventy. He made the golden light around the angel from bold patches.
Q2920183.i: Imagine: what was the first word Mary said once she recovered?

f: Find the little lyre-guitar in the lady's hands.
Find the wreath in her hair.

m.q: How does the marchioness look?
m.w: She half reclines on the couch, her face soft. She seems cosy and at ease.

x.q: Why did Goya paint her with a lyre and a wreath?
o: She was a famous ship's captain
To show her as a muse of music
x.w: A lyre and a wreath are signs of a muse. Goya was saying: this lady loves the arts.

Q926809.s: The secret: Goya was court painter to the King of Spain. He painted people naturally, without stiff poses.
Q926809.i: Imagine: what tune is the marchioness playing?

f: Find the apples and a lemon among the fruit.
Find the big jug and the folds of the curtain.

m.q: What is the mood of this still life?
o: Quiet and calm, as if thinking
Stormy and noisy, like a fairground
m.w: The objects stand still and the colours are soft and calm. Everything seems lost in thought.

x.q: Why does the table seem a little tilted?
o: The table had a broken leg
The painter was in a big hurry
x.w: He changed his viewpoint and put the objects together. That is why the jug and table seem to slide a little.

Q2349666.s: The secret: Cézanne said he would astonish Paris with an apple, and his apples really did become famous.
Q2349666.i: Imagine: which fruit would you eat first, and which would you keep to paint?

f: Find the hot-air balloon in the sky.
Find the Eiffel Tower.

m.q: How does the painter look?
o: Frightened, he is shaking a little
Sleepy, he is almost nodding off
m.w: He stands straight with brush and palette, like the master of the picture. He is clearly proud of himself.

x.q: What is written on the palette?
o: The price he wanted for the painting
A secret recipe for his bright paints
x.w: The palette bears the names of two women who were dear to the painter.

Q3319184.s: The secret: Rousseau worked as a customs officer and taught himself to paint. Picasso admired him.
Q3319184.i: Imagine: where is the ship sailing, and what flag would you raise on it?

f: Find the man at the helm: he holds the tiller.
Find the woman in the hat and the big white sail.

m.q: What is the mood aboard the boat?
o: Calm and pleasant, a lovely day
Fearful, as if a storm is coming
m.w: They sit relaxed, the wind fills the sail. They feel good on the water.

x.q: What is missing from this picture?
o: The sky and shore, only blue water
The big white sail of the boat
The man and woman on the boat
x.w: The boat fills the picture and the water is like a blue wall. Japanese prints often did this.

Q15290965.s: The secret: Manet painted it in summer at Argenteuil on the Seine, near Monet, who was also working there.
Q15290965.i: Imagine: where is the boat going, and what will they see there?

f: Find the huge blue sleeve.
Find the young man's face: where does he look?

m.q: How does the young man with the blue sleeve look?
o: Frightened, he wants to run away
Roaring with laughter, he is merry
Calm and a little proud, serious
m.w: He looks slightly aside, his face even, his shoulders squared. You can tell he is sure of himself.

x.q: What is the biggest, shiniest thing in the portrait?
o: The dark hat on his head
x.w: The sleeve takes up nearly half the picture and shimmers like silk. Titian showed that the young man is rich.

Q1238886.s: The secret: Titian painted this very young, learning from Giorgione and Bellini. And he lived a very long time.
Q1238886.i: Imagine: what is the young man's name, and what does he dream about?

f: Find the man's hat.
See where the light falls on his face.

m.q: How does this man look?
o: Proud and a little stern, serious
Cheerful, he is about to laugh
m.w: He looks aside, his gaze serious and important.

x.q: What did Rembrandt like to collect?
x.w: Rembrandt collected rare things and dressed people in them for portraits.

Q9351747.s: The secret: Rembrandt painted faces that glow out of the dark. He painted himself many times too.
Q9351747.i: Imagine: where is this gentleman travelling, and what is he carrying?

f: Find the pomegranate.
Find the window behind Mary: what can you see in it?

m.q: What expression does Mary have?
m.w: She looks at the baby with tenderness. Everything in the picture is quiet and loving.

x.q: What can a pomegranate with many seeds mean in old paintings?
o: Life and togetherness in one fruit
A quarrel, the seeds are fighting
x.w: A pomegranate has many seeds in one fruit. That is why it was painted as a sign of life and togetherness.

Q1487435.s: The secret: Lorenzo di Credi learned from Verrocchio in the same workshop as Leonardo da Vinci.
Q1487435.i: Imagine: what does the baby want to do with the pomegranate?

f: Find the golden eagles on the standards.
Find the winged figure in the air.

m.q: What is the mood of the ceremony?
o: Solemn and proud, a grand day
m.w: Everyone stands with raised arms and swords. A solemn ceremony is under way.

x.q: What are the soldiers promising as they raise their weapons?
o: To bring presents back from war
To go home early after the parade
x.w: The eagle standard was the symbol of a regiment. The soldiers swore to protect it.

Q3208312.s: The secret: David was Napoleon's court painter. This picture is over nine metres wide.
Q3208312.i: Imagine: what would you promise if you were given such a standard?

f: Find the three Magi: they brought gifts.
Find the baby Christ.

m.q: What is the mood of this meeting?
o: Festive and tender, a warm welcome
Sad, as if everyone is leaving
Anxious, as if waiting for bad news
m.w: Gold, bright robes and bowed heads. It is like a solemn reception.

x.q: What gifts did the Magi bring?
o: Toys and a little wooden horse
Bread, honey and a jug of milk
x.w: Gold, frankincense and myrrh were the most precious gifts of the time.

Q3605536.s: The secret: Lorenzo Monaco was a monk: his name means «Lawrence the Monk». He loved gold and bright colours.
Q3605536.i: Imagine: what gift would you bring the baby?

f: Find the glow of rainbow colours around Mary's head.
Find the flowers around her.

m.q: What shows in Mary's face?
m.w: She bends over the baby and looks at him with love. It is warm and quiet around them.

x.q: What surrounds Mary's head?
o: A dark and heavy storm cloud
A sparkling crown made of ice
x.w: Grünewald painted a shining ring of rainbow colours, as if a rainbow burned above Mary.

Q315716.s: The secret: Grünewald was a German master who painted glowing colours and strong feelings. His most famous work is the Isenheim Altarpiece.
Q315716.i: Imagine: which flower will the baby like?

f: Find the tall rocky peaks of the mountain.
Find where the summit meets the sky.

m.q: What is the mountain like here?
o: Small and funny, like a little toy
m.w: Huge peaks tower above the ground. It feels as if the mountain is silent and looking down on us.

x.q: Did Friedrich see this mountain with his own eyes?
o: Yes, he lived right at its foot
No, he used a friend's drawing
Only in a dream, once at night
x.w: Friedrich never visited the Watzmann and painted from a drawing made by someone else.

Q1197913.s: The secret: Friedrich wanted us to feel awe before nature and to feel small.
Q1197913.i: Imagine: how would you feel on reaching the summit?

f: Find the line where the sea meets the sky.
Find the sand on the beach: how many colours are in it?

m.q: What is the day like?
o: Dark and stormy, with big clouds
Bright and fresh, a summer day
Cold and snowy, with white ground
m.w: A bright sky, light strokes and the shimmer of water. The day is clear.

x.q: In which colours did Monet paint shadows?
o: Black, like in a pencil drawing
Blue and violet, soft and cool
x.w: Monet saw colour in shadows: blue and lilac. The Impressionists hardly used black.

Q2070487.s: The secret: Monet painted fast, outdoors, to catch light that keeps changing. He painted the same place at different times of day.
Q2070487.i: Imagine: which shells would you find on this beach?

f: Find the four dancers holding hands.
Find the old man with the lyre: he is Time.

m.q: How do the dancers move?
o: Calmly and smoothly, in a ring
m.w: They turn slowly, holding hands. The dance looks like the wheel of life.

x.q: Who are the four dancers?
o: Four seasons of the year, dancing
x.w: They are thought to be Poverty, Labour, Riches and Pleasure: life goes round, and Time plays the music.

Q2513438.s: The secret: Poussin lived in Rome and loved ancient tales. They say he set out little wax figures like on a stage to plan the picture.
Q2513438.i: Imagine: who joins the dance as the fifth dancer?

f: Find the rider in the blue cloak.
Find the white horse and its blue shadow.

m.q: What is the rider's mood?
o: Sad, he is far from home
Sleepy, he nods on the horse
m.w: The cloak flies behind and the horse flies across the meadow. The rider seems free as the wind.

x.q: What did Kandinsky say colours are like?
o: Music, like a song or tune
x.w: Kandinsky thought colours sound like music. That is why his blue is deep and quiet.

Q3793374.s: The secret: later Kandinsky and his friend Franz Marc named their group «The Blue Rider». Kandinsky became one of the first painters of abstract pictures.
Q3793374.i: Imagine: where is the rider galloping, and what will he find there?

f: Find the magic circle on the ground.
Find the cauldron on three legs and the frogs.

m.q: How does the witch look?
o: Playful, as if she is dancing
Sleepy, as if she is dreaming
m.w: Her face is tense and she is absorbed in her work. Magic needs attention.

x.q: Why does the witch draw a magic circle?
o: To play hopscotch with the frogs
To count how many frogs there are
To guard herself from evil spirits
x.w: According to old beliefs, a magic circle guards a witch from evil forces while she works.

Q7749405.s: The secret: Waterhouse loved painting women from legends: the Lady of Shalott, sirens, nymphs. His colours are like jewels.
Q7749405.i: Imagine: what spell is this witch casting, and what is it called?

f: Find the white huts glowing in the sunset.
Find the tall trees beside them.

m.q: What is this evening like?
o: Frosty, with snow on the ground
m.w: The sunset gilds the walls of the huts and everything stills. The evening is like a warm breath.

x.q: Why do the white walls of the huts glow so strongly?
o: The low sun lights them against dark shadows
The walls were painted with glowing paint
A big fire is burning inside each hut
x.w: White against dark always looks brighter. Kuindzhi knew how to show this.

Q4110167.s: The secret: Kuindzhi was a master of light. He once showed one of his paintings in a dark room with a single beam, and it looked magical.
Q4110167.i: Imagine: who lives in a white hut, and what are they cooking for supper?

f: Find the lyre.
Find the little winged Cupid.

m.q: What is the mood of the figures?
o: Angry, they argue with each other
m.w: They stand quietly, heads bowed, everything calm. They seem to be listening to music.

x.q: What was Sappho famous for in ancient Greece?
o: Writing poems and songs for the lyre
Being the fastest swimmer in Greece
Being a brave warrior in many battles
x.w: Sappho was a famous poet. Her poems were sung to the lyre.

Q3473161.s: The secret: the Russian prince Yusupov ordered this picture; it now hangs in the Hermitage in St Petersburg. David painted smoothly and strictly.
Q3473161.i: Imagine: what short poem will Sappho sing to her lyre?

f: Find Mary and the baby in the middle.
Find the people who ordered the picture: they pray beside the Holy Family.

m.q: What is the mood of the family scene?
o: Quiet and peaceful, a calm home
Cheerful and noisy, like a party
m.w: Everyone sits or stands calmly and nobody hurries. It is a quiet, homely scene.

x.q: Who are «donors» in old paintings?
o: People who sell paintings at fairs
People who paid and asked to be painted
People who mop the church floors
x.w: A donor ordered the painting. He paid the painter and asked to be painted next to the saints.

Q5885526.s: The secret: Carpaccio of Venice loved telling stories full of details. The thin-sliced beef dish «carpaccio» was named after him for the red tones of his paintings.
Q5885526.i: Imagine: what do the people who ordered the picture pray for?

f: Look at the faces in the crowd: who is surprised, and who is angry?
Find the calmest person in the picture.

m.q: How does Christ look at the woman?
o: Angrily, as if he is going to scold her
Kindly and calmly, with no blame
Bored, as if he wants to leave
m.w: Jesus does not scold the woman. He looks kindly and calmly.

x.q: What does this story teach?
o: Always win every single game you play
Be kind and forgive, not judge
Be the fastest runner at everything
x.w: It is a story of forgiveness. Jesus shows that we should understand, not condemn.

Q16536549.s: The secret: Semiradsky was born in Poland and lived in Rome. He loved painting the ancient world in sunlight, with white marble.
Q16536549.i: Imagine: what kind words would you say to the sad woman?

f: Find the book.
Find the lightest spot in the picture.

m.q: What is the mood of this scene?
o: Noisy and cheerful, like a party
Quiet and calm, like a library
Anxious, as if waiting for news
m.w: The light is soft, the colours muted, and reading needs quiet. Everything is still.

x.q: Why is this room so quiet?
o: The colours are bright and very loud
Everyone in the room has fallen asleep
Soft, muted colours and calm light
x.w: Fantin-Latour painted with soft, dark colours and even light. That makes the room quiet.

Q25444796.s: The secret: Fantin-Latour was famous for flowers: he painted roses so softly that people loved them in England. In 1870 he also painted a group portrait of Manet's friends.
Q25444796.i: Imagine: what book is being read, and what is it about?

f: Find the painter with a brush and palette beside a huge canvas.
Find the little mirror on the far wall and the man in the open doorway.

m.q: What is the mood of the people in this room?
o: Merry: everyone laughs at a joke
Calm: they look straight at us
Sad: everyone stares at the floor
m.w: The little princess stands calmly, and the painter and others look at us as if we had just walked in.

x.q: Who is reflected in the little mirror?
x.w: They are King Philip IV and Queen Mariana. So they are standing right where we are standing.

Q208758.s: Velázquez painted himself into the picture and set a puzzle: whom is he really painting? Close up the brushstrokes look loose, but from far away they become real lace and silk.
Q208758.i: Imagine: what is the painter drawing on the huge canvas that we cannot see?

f: Find the Cossack with a bandage on his head. He is laughing too!
Find the clerk at the table who is writing the letter.

m.q: What is the mood of the Cossacks?
o: They sing a quiet, sad song
m.w: Mouths are open, eyes are squeezed shut and there are laugh lines around them. They are having great fun.

x.q: Who are the Cossacks writing to?
x.w: The sultan ordered them to obey him. By legend, they answered with a cheeky, joking letter.

Q478271.s: Repin travelled to Ukraine to paint real faces, so every Cossack has his own character. He worked on the picture for about ten years.
Q478271.i: Imagine: what was the funniest joke the Cossacks added to the letter last?

f: Find little Cupid at the top, with a blindfold. He is aiming his bow!
Find Flora in her dress of flowers, scattering roses.

m.q: What is the mood of the dance of the three Graces?
m.w: Three girls in see-through dresses dance hand in hand. Everything moves smoothly and quietly.

x.q: Where does the action of Primavera take place?
x.w: Behind the figures grow orange trees with golden fruit, and a carpet of flowers covers the grass.

Q549847.s: Botticelli painted so many flowers that botanists have counted about 190 kinds of plants. The figures are drawn with thin, flowing lines, so they seem to dance.
Q549847.i: Imagine: what song is Flora humming as she scatters the flowers?

f: Find the green boots of the trapeze artist in the top left corner.
Find the bowl of oranges and the bottles on the counter.

m.q: What does the girl behind the bar feel?
o: She is thoughtful and a little sad
She is cross with a customer
m.w: She does not smile and looks a little aside, as if far away. A noisy crowd is behind her.

x.q: What is odd about the mirror behind the girl?
o: It shows no bottles at all
It shows the hall completely empty
Her reflection is off to one side
x.w: The girl stands straight, but her reflection is moved to the right. People still argue about why.

Q1245354.s: This is one of Manet's last big paintings. The girl really worked at this Paris café-theatre, and she posed for him in his studio.
Q1245354.i: Imagine: what is the girl thinking, and what will she say to the man in the top hat?

f: Find the people holding on to the broken mast.
Find the sun: what colour is the sky around it?

m.q: What do the people on the wreckage feel when they see the sunrise?
o: Tiredness and a wish to sleep
m.w: The warm golden sun breaks through the clouds. It looks like a sign that the storm is ending.

x.q: What is the «ninth wave»?
o: The ninth day of the storm
The biggest wave of the storm
The name of the sunken ship
x.w: Sailors believed waves come one after another and the ninth is the mightiest. In the picture it towers over the people.

Q1070896.s: Aivazovsky painted the sea from memory, in his studio, not on the spot. His waves look clear as glass and glow from inside.
Q1070896.i: Imagine: what happened to the ship, and how will these people be rescued?

f: Find the lightning in the dark sky above the little town.
Find the woman with a baby and the man with a staff at the two edges.

m.q: What is the mood of the young mother?
o: She fears the storm and hurries off
She is calm, though a storm looms
She plays merrily with her baby
m.w: She sits quietly and feeds her baby as if the storm does not scare her. That makes the picture mysterious.

x.q: What is the biggest puzzle of this painting?
o: How many dark clouds it has
x.w: The picture had no title, and experts still argue about who the two people are and why they are here.

Q930137.s: Giorgione was one of the first to make nature and weather the star, not people. X-rays show another figure under the paint: the painter changed his mind.
Q930137.i: Imagine: who are these two people, and what happens when the storm arrives?

f: Follow the beam of light from the top right: where does it fall?
Find the hand of Jesus pointing at a man at the table.

m.q: What does the man who is pointed at feel?
o: Anger: he scowls at the visitors
m.w: One man points at himself, as if asking, «Me?». The others freeze and stare too.

x.q: What are the people at the table wearing?
x.w: The men are dressed as in Italy around 1600. So the painter shows that a miracle can happen in our own day.

Q969377.s: Caravaggio lit his scene like a spotlight in a dark room, and everything else sank into shadow. That makes his pictures lively and a little tense.
Q969377.i: Imagine: what did the man at the table answer, and where did he go next?

f: Find the white tiare flower behind the ear of the woman in front.
Look at the bright yellow and green patches behind them.

m.q: What is the face of the woman in front like?
m.w: She is not smiling and looks slightly aside. The question in the title seems to have made her think.

x.q: What kind of colours did Gauguin paint with in Tahiti?
o: Bright ones, not as in real life
x.w: He liked flat patches of strong colour, like the pink ground. They make the island feel even hotter and brighter.

Q3869871.s: Gauguin left France for Tahiti to live simply and paint with bright colours. This picture was later sold as one of the most expensive in the world.
Q3869871.i: Imagine: how will the woman answer the question in the title?

f: Find the little bird, a goldfinch, in the baby's hand.
Look into the two little windows: what can you see behind them?

m.q: What does Mary feel as she looks at her baby?
o: Sadness: she is about to cry
Tenderness and love for her son
m.w: She tilts her head and looks at her son with a soft smile. Her hands hold him gently.

x.q: How did Leonardo make the faces look so soft?
x.w: Light melts smoothly into shadow with no hard edges, so the faces seem alive. It was Leonardo's favourite trick.

Q1327676.s: The painting is named after the Litta family of Milan, who once owned it. Now it hangs in the Hermitage, and experts argue whether a pupil helped Leonardo.
Q1327676.i: Imagine: what lullaby is Mary quietly singing to her baby?

f: Find the little bunch of white snowdrops in the angel's hand.
Find the boy who is looking straight at us.

m.q: What do the boys who carry the angel feel?
o: Joy and a wish to play
m.w: The boys walk slowly and look serious. They hold the stretcher carefully so the angel will not be hurt.

x.q: How do Finns feel about this painting?
o: Chose it as the nation's favourite
Gave it to a neighbouring country
Decided they do not like it
x.w: Finland loves this picture very much. It hangs in the National Gallery in Helsinki.

Q471289.s: Simberg never explained what happened to the angel, so everyone sees something different. He painted it near Töölö Bay in Helsinki.
Q471289.i: Imagine: what happened to the angel, and where are the boys taking it?

f: Find the goldfinch in little John's hands.
Find the open book in Mary's hand.

m.q: How does the baby Jesus treat the little bird?
o: He is scared and turns away
He tries to catch it and run
m.w: The baby reaches out and touches the bird with his fingertips. His face is calm, and Mary looks on kindly.

x.q: What shape do Mary and the two little boys make?
o: A circle, like a big wheel
A straight line, like a fence
x.w: Mary's head is at the top and the boys are low on each side. That makes a steady triangle, and everything feels calm.

Q2344505.s: Long ago the house where the painting was kept collapsed, and it broke into many pieces. It was glued together, and later restorers brought back its bright colours.
Q2344505.i: Imagine: how did the bird come to the boys, and what is its name?

f: Find the three men: a young one, a grown-up and an old one.
Find the dark cave in the rock on the left.

m.q: What is the mood of these three?
m.w: They are quiet and look in different directions. Soft evening light makes the picture still and mysterious.

x.q: What do experts think these three may be studying?
x.w: The old man holds a sheet with drawings of the stars. The young man has a compass and a square. So they are probably thinking about the sky.

Q877191.s: Nobody knows exactly who the three are: maybe wise men or the three ages of man. Giorgione lived only about thirty years and left few paintings.
Q877191.i: Imagine: what did these three discover when they looked at the stars?

f: Find the falling snow: white flakes all over the picture.
Find Mary with the baby and the Magi in the lower left part.

m.q: What is the mood of the winter day in the picture?
o: Hot: everyone hides from the sun
Noisy: everyone dances at a feast
Cold and quiet: all in snow
m.w: Grey-white tones, bare trees and snow. It feels quiet and cold all around.

x.q: Where did Brueghel place this Bible scene?
o: In a hot desert among the sands
In a big harbour city by the sea
x.w: Brueghel moved the Bible story to winter Flanders, where he lived himself. People are dressed as they were in his own time.

Q1211030.s: Brueghel liked to move Bible scenes into his own Flanders. That makes the story closer and easier to understand.
Q1211030.i: Imagine: what do the villagers say to each other, not noticing the wonder beside them?

f: Find the two angels behind Mary's shoulders.
Find the baby: where is he looking?

m.q: What is the mood of Mary, the baby and the angels?
o: Noisy: the angels sing at full voice
Tender and quiet, heads bent low
m.w: Heads are bowed, faces are soft and gazes are calm. It seems everyone is busy with the baby.

x.q: What do the golden circles above the heads mean?
o: Golden hats worn by the rich
x.w: A golden circle over a head is called a halo. In old pictures it showed saints.

Q2268013.s: This picture is painted softly and finely, when Botticelli was still young. Later he created Primavera and The Birth of Venus.
Q2268013.i: Imagine: what are the names of the two angels?

f: Find Christopher: he wades through the water carrying the baby on his shoulder.
Find the odd little details around: Bosch loved riddles.

m.q: What does Christopher feel?
o: Joy: he feels light as a feather
Tired, but he keeps on walking
Fear: he dreads the deep water
m.w: He leans on a thick staff and walks with bowed head. You can see carrying is hard, but he is determined.

x.q: Why was the baby so heavy, by legend?
o: He was cast in heavy gold
His sack was full of stones
x.w: By legend, the giant Christopher carried the baby across a river, and he grew heavier and heavier. It was Jesus, who carries the whole world.

Q2565646.s: Bosch liked to add strange fantastic creatures and tiny riddles to his pictures. Even in this calm scene you can look for them.
Q2565646.i: Imagine: what did the baby say to Christopher when they reached the shore?

f: Find the big red square.
Find the small blue and yellow rectangles.

m.q: What is the mood of Mondrian's picture?
o: Calm: everything is in its place
m.w: The lines are straight, the shapes even and the colours pure. Nothing trembles or hurries.

x.q: How many basic colours did Mondrian use?
o: Ten, like fingers on two hands
x.w: Mondrian took only the purest paints: red, blue and yellow. He added black lines and white to them.

Q19609193.s: Mondrian first painted trees and flowers, then simplified everything to lines and coloured rectangles. He called his style «Neoplasticism».
Q19609193.i: Imagine: if this is a city map, where are the park, the river and your house?

f: Find the sorceress: where is she looking?
Find the brightest light in the picture: what does it light up?

m.q: What is the sorceress's mood?
o: Merry: she is about to dance
Cross: she is frowning at us
m.w: She is busy with something secret and looks very attentively. That makes the whole scene feel mysterious.

x.q: Where did Waterhouse take the subjects of his pictures from?
o: From old myths, legends and poems
From the daily news of his own time
x.w: He loved old tales about sorceresses, nymphs and princesses. Reading them, he invented pictures.

Q7765329.s: Waterhouse was an English painter who loved mystery: his heroines often cast spells or wait for something magical. He painted softly, as in a dream.
Q7765329.i: Imagine: what spell is the sorceress saying, and what will come of it?

f: Find the boy Bartholomew: he stands with his hands folded on his chest.
Find the old monk in dark clothes.

m.q: What does the boy feel?
o: Anger: he is cross with someone
Boredom: he has nothing to do
m.w: He stands still, hands folded and head slightly bowed. You can see he is moved and very attentive.

x.q: What kind of nature is in this picture?
o: A hot tropical forest with palms
Quiet Russian nature and a field
x.w: Nesterov loved to paint Russian nature: quiet, tender and a little sad. Here it seems to listen too.

Q4110588.s: Nesterov painted this at Abramtsevo, where artists lived, and the landscape in it is real. The famous collector Pavel Tretyakov bought the painting.
Q4110588.i: Imagine: what did the old man say to the boy, and what did the boy answer?

f: Find the stone with writing: it shows three roads.
Find the knight on the white horse: he is lost in thought.

m.q: What does the knight feel?
o: Joy: he has found a treasure
Thoughtful: he is choosing a road
Impatience: he wants to gallop off
m.w: He has halted his horse and looks at the stone without hurry. You can see the choice is not easy.

x.q: What is written on the stone?
o: The knight's own name and his horse's
The year the road was built
What awaits a traveller on each road
x.w: The stone is a warning. Go left and lose your horse, go right and you will marry, go straight and meet great danger.

Q4112530.s: Vasnetsov loved Russian heroic songs and fairy tales and painted heroes as if they stepped off the pages. He worked on this picture for several years.
Q4112530.i: Imagine: which road will the knight choose, and what will happen to him?

f: Find the moon in the sky.
Find the mermaids in pale clothes.

m.q: What is the mood of this night?
o: Anxious: the sky is full of dark clouds
m.w: Everything is silvery blue, soft and still. Moonlight makes the night mysterious.

x.q: Which work is this painting based on?
o: Pushkin's tale of the Golden Fish
x.w: Kramskoi was inspired by Gogol's tale «May Night, or the Drowned Maiden», in which mermaids come ashore by moonlight.

Q4400244.s: Kramskoi painted moonlight in silvery and bluish colours, and the picture seems to glow from within. He is best known for portraits, such as «Unknown Woman».
Q4400244.i: Imagine: what do the mermaids sing on a moonlit night?

f: Find the shield with the face of Medusa.
Find where light falls on the face and hands: the rest is in half-dark.

m.q: What is Athena's look like?
o: Playful: she is about to giggle
Sad: she looks close to tears
m.w: She sits straight, her face is serious and thoughtful, and there is strength in her hands. She is neither afraid nor in a hurry.

x.q: Who is Athena?
o: Goddess of the sea and ships
x.w: In Greek myths Athena is the wise protector of heroes and cities. That is why she is in armour but looks calm.

Q3610098.s: Rembrandt was a master of light and shadow. Faces and hands seem to glow from the half-dark, and gold shines warmly.
Q3610098.i: Imagine: what wise advice would Athena give you?

f: Find the samovar on the table.
Find the watermelon and the cat.

m.q: What is the merchant's wife's mood?
o: Sad: she is lonely and bored
Cross: the tea is cold and nasty
m.w: She sits relaxed, rosy and calm. Tea, watermelon and a warm day make her happy.

x.q: What does the merchant's wife drink her tea from?
o: From a silver goblet, as at a feast
From a saucer, as merchants did
x.w: In old Russia tea was often poured into a saucer so it would cool faster. This was thought cosy and homely.

Q18683417.s: Kustodiev loved to paint a bright, juicy Russia: fairs, festivals, merchants. He kept painting even when walking was hard for him.
Q18683417.i: Imagine: what is the cat thinking as it looks at the watermelon and the samovar?

f: Find the boats and ships on the water.
Find where the light is brightest: in the sky or on the water?

m.q: What is the mood of the River Seine in the picture?
o: Gloomy: a dark night over the river
Quiet and golden, in a haze
m.w: Warm light and a light haze soften everything around. It feels like a quiet morning or evening on the river.

x.q: How did Turner paint air and mist?
o: With thick paint put on with a knife
x.w: He laid paint in thin, see-through layers, and the borders between sky and water blur. So the air seems to glow.

Q25445077.s: Turner loved to travel and paint light, rivers, sea and weather. His glowing pictures later inspired the Impressionists.
Q25445077.i: Imagine: what are the boats carrying along the river, and where are they sailing?

f: Find the girl's reflection in the window glass.
Find the bowl of fruit on the table and the green curtain.

m.q: What does the girl feel as she reads the letter?
m.w: Her lips are slightly parted and her face is calm and bright. She seems to be reading something important and pleasant.

x.q: What did restorers find on the wall behind the girl?
o: A hidden door, covered with paint
A Cupid hidden under the paint
An old map hidden under the paint
x.w: The Cupid had been painted over: someone added the paint after Vermeer. Restorers removed it, and Cupid is visible again. He hints that the letter is about love.

Q700251.s: Light pours in from the window on the left and makes the room quiet and warm. Only about thirty-five paintings by Vermeer have survived.
Q700251.i: Imagine: what is written in the letter, and who is it from?

f: Find the young man in the hat with a feather.
Find the girl in the white headscarf: where is she looking?

m.q: What is the young man's mood?
o: He is scared of bad fortune
He is charmed and trusts her
He is bored and wants to leave
m.w: He looks into her face and smiles a little. He is pleased and suspects nothing.

x.q: What is the girl doing while she reads his palm?
o: Giving him a flower for luck
x.w: With one hand she holds his palm, and with the other she secretly tugs at his ring. He looks into her eyes and sees nothing.

Q2610675.s: Caravaggio painted ordinary people from the street, not only heroes and saints. He set them in strong side light, so they look completely alive.
Q2610675.i: Imagine: what will the young man say when he notices the ring is gone?

f: Find the globe on top of the cupboard.
Find the compasses in the geographer's hand.

m.q: What does the geographer feel?
o: Absorbed in work, lost in thought
m.w: He has looked up from the map and gazes out of the window. A new idea seems to have come to him. His face is focused.

x.q: Which other painting by Vermeer is a pair to this one?
x.w: The Astronomer shows a similar room and a scholar by the window. Vermeer painted these two at almost the same time.

Q45130.s: Vermeer loved to show how light from a window on the left lies softly on things. Only about thirty-five of his paintings have survived.
Q45130.i: Imagine: which faraway country does the geographer dream of visiting?

f: Find the three musicians: who is playing, and who is singing?
Find the black and white tiles on the floor.

m.q: What is the mood in the music room?
m.w: The musicians play and sing calmly together. Soft light and quiet make the room cosy.

x.q: What happened to this painting in 1990?
o: It was painted all over again
It was given to a school
It was stolen from a museum
x.w: Thieves took it from a museum in Boston, and it has never been found. An empty frame still hangs on the museum wall.

Q1169395.s: Vermeer painted slowly and carefully, so very few of his pictures remain. That makes it sadder that this one is missing.
Q1169395.i: Imagine: what tune are these three playing?

f: Find the cards hidden in the belt of the trickster on the right.
Find the glove of the older man: its fingertips are bare.

m.q: What does the young player feel?
o: He is absorbed, sees no cheating
He cheats too and hides cards
He is upset: he keeps losing
m.w: He looks at his cards and thinks only about the game. His face is open, and he notices nothing.

x.q: What does the older man behind the young player do?
o: He teaches the youth fair play
He peeks at the youth's cards
He pours the youth some wine
x.w: He peeks at the young man's cards and signals with his fingers to the other player. Together they cheat the boy.

Q663133.s: This painting made Caravaggio famous: a rich cardinal bought it. The painter showed a street scene as if it were happening before our eyes.
Q663133.i: Imagine: how will the game end when the young man spots the cheating?

f: Find Jesus in the centre, under the biggest arch.
Count the people at the feast: they are on the stairs and on the balconies too.

m.q: What is the mood at this feast?
o: Noisy and merry, like a feast
Quiet and solemn, like a church
m.w: Guests talk and wave their hands while servants carry dishes. There is movement and bright clothing everywhere.

x.q: Why did Veronese have to change the title of the painting?
o: The monks wanted a shorter, simpler title
Church judges disliked the noisy guests
It was mixed up with another painter's work
x.w: At first it was called «The Last Supper», but the judges thought that was unsuitable. Veronese repainted nothing, he simply gave the picture a new title.

Q951105.s: The painting is huge: almost thirteen metres wide. Veronese loved grand feasts, beautiful buildings and bright silk clothes.
Q951105.i: Imagine: what are the guests on the stairs talking about?

f: Find the red cap and the red armchair.
Find the folded paper in the pope's hand.

m.q: What can you see in the pope's face?
o: He is sad and about to cry
He is stern and very watchful
m.w: His brows are drawn together and his sharp eyes look straight at us. He seems to see right through us.

x.q: What did the pope reportedly say when he saw his portrait?
o: «It is far too true to life!»
x.w: They say he exclaimed that the portrait was too truthful. Velázquez did not flatter him, he showed his real character.

Q1240092.s: Velázquez painted many shades of red, from dark to almost glowing, with quick, free brushstrokes. Many people think this is one of the best portraits in the world.
Q1240092.i: Imagine: what would the pope say to us if we walked into the room?

f: Find the little girl with a hoop on the left.
Find the young woman with a basket at the front on the right.

m.q: What is the mood of the passers-by?
o: Merry: everyone dances in the rain
m.w: People go in different directions and huddle under umbrellas. There is lots of movement: an ordinary rainy day in a big city.

x.q: Why do the left and right parts of the painting look a little different?
o: Half was painted by his friend
It was once cut in two pieces
Renoir painted it in two stages
x.w: He began it around 1881 and finished it several years later, by which time his style had changed. So the lines are sharper on the left and softer on the right.

Q1114571.s: Renoir loved painting people in the soft light of Paris. The painting now hangs in Dublin, in the Hugh Lane Gallery.
Q1114571.i: Imagine: where is the girl with the basket hurrying, and what is in her basket?

f: Find Jesus placing a crown on Mary's head.
Find the tomb full of flowers below.

m.q: What do the apostles below feel?
m.w: They look up, and at the flowers in the tomb, with amazement. You can see a miracle has happened.

x.q: What did the apostles find in the tomb instead of Mary?
x.w: By legend, when the tomb was opened there were only flowers. Mary is already in heaven, where Jesus crowns her.

Q2344357.s: Raphael painted this picture very young, at about twenty. He learned from the master Perugino, and the picture is full of air and light.
Q2344357.i: Imagine: what music are the angels playing up above?

f: Find the man with a ney flute in his hand.
Find the tortoises on the floor around him.

m.q: What is the mood of the tortoise trainer?
m.w: He looks at the tortoises calmly and patiently. You can tell it is not easy to teach them.

x.q: What do many people see in this picture?
o: A tale of tortoise and hare
An advert for a tortoise show
x.w: Tortoises are very slow, and their teacher is patient. Many think it is a smile at slow change and at patience.

Q7769644.s: Osman Hamdi Bey was not only a painter but also an archaeologist. He founded an art school in Istanbul and directed a museum.
Q7769644.i: Imagine: what dance will the tortoises dance to the flute?

f: Find the emperor on the raised platform among the guests.
Find the rain of pink petals falling from above.

m.q: What does the emperor feel as he watches the petals?
o: He is bored and nearly asleep
He is curious: it is his idea
He is cross with the guests
m.w: He calmly watches the petals from his couch as if it were a game. You can see everything goes to his plan.

x.q: How did Alma-Tadema prepare for this picture?
o: He ordered real roses for months
He copied petals from paper flowers
He copied the roses from an old book
x.w: For several months fresh roses were brought to him from Nice so that he could see every petal.

Q276174.s: Alma-Tadema adored ancient Rome and painted marble, cloth and flowers so well you want to touch them. Here he shows a feast of a Roman emperor from an old legend.
Q276174.i: Imagine: how will the guests get out from under the petals, and what will they say?

f: Find the angel's big dark wings.
Find his face and look at his eyes.

m.q: What does the fallen angel feel?
o: Pride: he is pleased with himself
Hurt and sorrow: eyes full of tears
m.w: His face is tense, his eyes shine with tears and his body is curled tight. You can tell he is very bitter.

x.q: Whom did the painter show?
o: A knight who lost his sword
An angel cast out of heaven
x.w: In the old story, this angel was thrown out of heaven. The painter shows how lonely and hurt he feels.

Q107486133.s: Cabanel liked to paint smoothly and softly, as if everything were polished. In his day the public loved such pictures.
Q107486133.i: Imagine: where will the angel go now, and what will he do?

f: Find the lady's white dress and the boat on the river.
Find the cloth hanging over the side of the boat.

m.q: What does the lady feel?
o: Joy: she is sailing to a party
Boredom: she has nothing to do
m.w: Her face is sad and her gaze is far away. Her lips are slightly parted, as if she were singing softly. The autumn colours around her are calm.

x.q: Why did the lady get into the boat?
o: She saw life and sailed to Camelot
She wanted to gather river lilies
She was lost and tired in the woods
x.w: In Tennyson's poem, the lady lived in a tower and saw the world only in a mirror. When she saw the knight Lancelot, she sailed to Camelot.

Q2445726.s: Waterhouse loved pictures from fairy tales and poems and painted «The Lady of Shalott» three times. The 1888 version is the best known.
Q2445726.i: Imagine: what song did the lady sing as she floated down the river?

f: Find the sunburnt shepherds who have come to the baby.
On a side panel, find Saint Margaret with a little dragon.

m.q: What do the shepherds feel when they see the baby?
o: Fear: they want to run and hide
Awe and joy, hands folded in prayer
Tiredness: they want to go home
m.w: The shepherds have knelt and folded their hands, and their faces are moved. They look at the baby with joy.

x.q: What is painted with great care in the foreground?
x.w: Irises, lilies and other flowers are painted so exactly that you can see every petal. The painter gave each flower its own meaning.

Q18686031.s: The banker Portinari ordered this altarpiece, and it was shipped from Flanders to Florence. Italian painters studied it and learned how to paint faces and flowers.
Q18686031.i: Imagine: what are the shepherds whispering to each other as they bend over the baby?

f: Find Actaeon pushing aside the red curtain on the left.
Find the goddess Diana and her nymphs by the water.

m.q: What does Diana feel when she notices Actaeon?
m.w: Diana has turned sharply, covers herself and looks angry. The nymphs around her are frightened too.

x.q: What hangs above them on the arch as a sign of trouble to come?
x.w: In the myth, Actaeon is turned into a stag. The skull on the arch hints to us what will happen to him.

Q2528177.s: Titian painted this for King Philip II of Spain when he was about seventy. His late pictures seem woven out of colour and light.
Q2528177.i: Imagine: what did Diana say to Actaeon?

f: Find the inkwell held by an angel.
Find the crown above Mary's head, held up by angels.

m.q: What is the mood of Mary and the angels with the crown?
o: Tender and quiet, heads bent close
Noisy: the angels shout and argue
m.w: Heads are bowed and lines are soft and round. Everyone seems to wrap the baby in care.

x.q: What shape is this painting?
x.w: Round paintings like this are called a «tondo». Botticelli's figures also fit in a circle, and flowing lines echo its shape.

Q2551625.s: Mary writes a joyful prayer, the «Magnificat», in a book. The picture is named after it. Botticelli drew in flowing lines, as if music were playing.
Q2551625.i: Imagine: what is the baby whispering to his mother and the angels?

f: Find Mary and the baby: where are they looking?
Find Mary's hands: how do they hold the baby?

m.q: What does Mary feel as she holds the baby?
m.w: Her face is soft, her head tilted and her hands hold the baby gently. Everything in the picture is calm.

x.q: How did Raphael paint his Madonnas?
o: As gentle mothers in soft light
As merry girls at a party
x.w: Raphael made Mary kind and beautiful and the light soft and warm. People have loved his Madonnas for centuries.

Q602813.s: The painting is named after an English collector, Solly, who once owned it. Raphael was very young then, about eighteen.
Q602813.i: Imagine: what is Mary quietly telling the baby?

f: Find the sleeping Jacob: what is his head resting on?
Find the golden glow in the sky above.

m.q: What is the face of sleeping Jacob like?
m.w: His face is lit, his eyes are closed and his lips almost smile. He is having a good dream.

x.q: What did Jacob dream of, in the old story?
o: A ladder to heaven with angels
A tall tower up to the clouds
A golden bridge across the sea
x.w: In the Bible, Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven with angels on it. When he woke, he knew he was not alone.

Q2052008.s: Ribera lived in Naples and painted with strong contrasts of light and shadow, like Caravaggio. He knew how to make faces warm and alive.
Q2052008.i: Imagine: what did the angels say to Jacob in his dream?

f: Find the tall rock with a windmill on top.
Find Jesus with the cross: he is small, in the middle of the crowd.

m.q: What do the loved ones of Jesus, standing at the bottom right, feel?
o: Impatience: they want to go home
m.w: The women in blue lean toward each other and their faces are sad. They are worried for Jesus.

x.q: Why is Jesus so hard to find in the picture?
o: He is hidden behind a big tree
He is painted in the far corner
He is small among many people
x.w: Brueghel shows that ordinary life goes on around, and people hardly notice what matters. So we have to look for him.

Q686107.s: Brueghel painted more than five hundred tiny people, each busy with something. He dressed them like people of Flanders in his own time.
Q686107.i: Imagine a story about one little person in this crowd.

f: Find the earring in the girl's ear.
Find the green leaves behind her.

m.q: What is the mood of Renoir's girl?
m.w: She sits quietly and looks thoughtful. Her face is soft and her pose is relaxed.

x.q: Who sat in front of Renoir while he painted this picture?
x.w: Lise posed for Renoir for several years, and he painted her many times. Here she wears light summer clothes.

Q1659469.s: Renoir loved soft light, patches of leaf shadow and warm colours. He became one of the first Impressionist painters.
Q1659469.i: Imagine: what is the girl dreaming about as she sits in the shade?

f: Find the glass in the man's raised hand.
Find his broad hat, tilted to one side.

m.q: What is the mood of the militiaman with the glass?
o: Sad: he looks about to cry
Merry: he smiles and calls to us
m.w: He has turned to us, smiles and lifts his glass. He seems to be calling us to the table.

x.q: What is Frans Hals famous for?
x.w: Hals painted fast, the strokes stay visible, and the faces seem about to move. He could catch a smile in a single moment.

Q650635.s: Hals painted not only grand people but also townsfolk, militiamen and jolly fellows. Few painters caught laughter so vividly.
Q650635.i: Imagine: what is this cheerful fellow raising his glass to?

f: Find the woman in red shaking the big sieve.
Find the boy in the picture.

m.q: What is the mood of the woman at work?
o: Focused and calm, busy with work
Cross: they argue about the grain
m.w: She looks down at the grain and moves smoothly. Her face is calm: she is busy with her task.

x.q: Why do the women shake the sieve?
o: To grind the wheat into flour
To sift the rubbish out of wheat
To dry the grain in the sun
x.w: The sieve is shaken so dust and rubbish fall through and clean grain stays. Courbet showed ordinary farm work.

Q2561558.s: Courbet painted ordinary people on big canvases, the way only heroes and kings had been painted before. At the time that seemed bold.
Q2561558.i: Imagine: what will the boy say when the grain is ready?

f: Find the baby: he is asleep on Mary's lap.
Find Duke Federico: he is in armour, kneeling with folded hands.

m.q: What is the mood of the scene around Mary?
o: Quiet and solemn: all stay silent
m.w: The saints stand in a half-circle and say nothing, and the baby sleeps. The light is even, and everything is calm.

x.q: How did Piero make the hall look so deep?
o: He painted a light mist over the hall
He used exact perspective: arches recede
He painted the walls very dark brown
x.w: Piero was also a mathematician. The lines of the arches meet in one point, and it feels like a real tall vault above the saints.

Q1796098.s: Piero della Francesca painted calmly and strictly, and his figures look like carved stone. He also wrote books about mathematics.
Q1796098.i: Imagine: what is the baby dreaming about?

f: Find the white tablecloth with food on the grass.
Find the patches of sunlight and leaf shadow.

m.q: What is the mood of the company?
m.w: People sit and stand at ease, chatting, and nobody hurries. Light clothes and sunny patches make the day festive.

x.q: What happened to Monet's huge painting?
o: It got damp and was cut up
It was painted over by someone
It was shipped overseas and lost
x.w: Monet gave it to his landlord to settle a debt, and it got damp in a cellar. Later the painter cut it up, and the surviving pieces were kept.

Q1167912.s: Monet wanted to paint a huge picture right among the trees and show light shining through leaves. That is how he learned to paint patches of sun.
Q1167912.i: Imagine: what is in this group's picnic basket?

f: Find the two mirrors: she holds one, the man behind her holds the other.
Find the girl's golden hair and her white blouse.

m.q: What does the girl feel?
o: She is merry and winks at us
She is cross at her reflection
m.w: Her gaze is quiet and turned aside, and her pose is calm. She is in no hurry.

x.q: Why are there two mirrors in the painting?
o: To make the room seem brighter
To show her from different sides
To stop the wall looking empty
x.w: Thanks to the mirrors we see the girl not only from the front. Titian showed that painting can show a person from several sides at once.

Q23922.s: Titian was the greatest master of colour in Venice. His golden-red hair became so famous that this shade is called «Titian red».
Q23922.i: Imagine: what does she see in the mirror, and what is she thinking about?

f: Find the dancer's long white dress and long gloves.
Find the plants with big leaves behind the couple.

m.q: What is the mood of the couple?
o: Cross: they argue as they dance
Dull: waiting for the dance to end
m.w: The man holds his partner gently, and she tilts her head back a little. The dress flows, and everything moves softly.

x.q: Which paired painting did Renoir make in the same year?
x.w: In Dance in the Country a simple couple dance, the woman in a straw hat. Here a smart couple dance at a city ball.

Q3633456.s: Suzanne Valadon posed for this picture, and she later became a famous painter herself. Renoir loved to show people moving in soft light.
Q3633456.i: Imagine: what music is playing at this ball?

f: Find the little bunch of violets on her chest.
Find her big dark eyes: where is she looking?

m.q: What is Berthe's face like?
o: Merry, she is about to laugh
m.w: Her gaze is attentive and deep and her mouth is calm. She seems about to speak.

x.q: Who was Berthe Morisot besides being a model?
o: An actress at a Paris theatre
A painter, a friend of Manet
x.w: Berthe was a well-known Impressionist painter. She was Manet's friend, posed for him many times and later married his brother.

Q2899286.s: Almost the whole picture is black, yet it is not gloomy. The strokes are quick and free, and the face glows. Manet could show character in just a few strokes.
Q2899286.i: Imagine: what does Berthe want to paint tomorrow?

f: Find the sunshade in the girl's hands.
Find the greenery and flowers behind her.

m.q: What is the mood of Manet's spring portrait?
o: Fresh and joyful, like a morning
m.w: Light, soft colours, greenery and flowers, and the girl's calm face. It feels as if real spring has come.

x.q: What was the idea behind this painting?
o: A copy of an old Italian painting
A wedding present for a friend
One of the pictures of the seasons
x.w: Manet planned four portraits of women, one for each season, but only finished Spring and Autumn.

Q18620351.s: Manet painted quickly and freshly, and the brushstrokes stay visible. A Paris actress, Jeanne Demarsy, posed for him.
Q18620351.i: Imagine: where is the girl going with her sunshade on the first warm day?

f: Find the bride with a crown in the boat.
Find the tall mountains around the fjord.

m.q: What is the mood of the wedding journey?
o: Solemn and joyful, a festive day
m.w: The people wear festive clothes and glide along together quietly. The water is calm, and everything looks peaceful.

x.q: How did people get to a wedding in Norway at that time?
x.w: In the mountains there were few roads, but water was close, so the wedding party travelled by boat.

Q2841473.s: Two painters made this picture: Tidemand painted the people and Gude painted the mountains and water. It became one of the symbols of Norway.
Q2841473.i: Imagine: what song do they sing in the boats at the wedding?

f: Find the shepherds peeking from the roof of the stable.
Find the Magi in their rich golden clothes.

m.q: What do the Magi feel as they look at the baby?
m.w: The Magi bow or kneel, with gifts in their hands. Their faces are serious and respectful.

x.q: What gifts did the Magi bring the baby?
x.w: Frankincense is a fragrant resin and myrrh is a sweet-smelling oil. Gold, frankincense and myrrh were very costly gifts.

Q2276130.s: Bosch lived in the Netherlands and became famous for odd, fantastic creatures. Here the scene is calm, but the details hold many puzzles.
Q2276130.i: Imagine: what are the shepherds whispering to each other as they peek from the roof?

f: Find the girl's striped jacket.
Find the oleander sprig in her hand.

m.q: What is the girl's face like?
m.w: She sits straight and looks serious, as if shy. Her hands lie calm and she is not smiling.

x.q: Whom did Van Gogh imagine when he painted this girl?
o: A princess from an old fairy tale
A young Spanish dancer from a play
A girl from Japan, as he imagined
x.w: Van Gogh had read a book about Japan in which young girls were called «mousmé». He adored Japanese prints, though he lived in France.

Q948894.s: Van Gogh was crazy about Japanese prints: bright flat patches of colour and clear lines. You can see that in La Mousmé.
Q948894.i: Imagine: what is the girl's name, and what is she thinking about?

f: Find the green Christ.
Find the women in dark clothes and white bonnets.

m.q: What is the mood of the people near the green Christ?
o: Quiet and sad, like a prayer
m.w: The women stand quietly with bowed heads. Their calm poses make the scene thoughtful.

x.q: Why is Christ green in the picture?
o: The paint turned green with age
The statue is overgrown with moss
x.w: Gauguin loved bright, unusual colours: he also painted a «Yellow Christ». His colour carries the mood.

Q2504917.s: Gauguin lived in Brittany, in France, then, where people prayed at stone crosses called calvaries. He painted in flat patches of colour, simply and boldly.
Q2504917.i: Imagine: what are the women praying about by the stone cross?

f: Find the red poppies in the vase.
Find the thick, heavy brushstrokes: you can see them even from far away.

m.q: What is the mood of the bouquet?
o: Gloomy, like a grey rainy day
m.w: The red patches of the poppies catch your eye at once. The strokes are quick and energetic, and the bouquet seems to tremble.

x.q: What unusual thing has happened to this painting?
o: It was found in an old chest
It was stolen twice from a museum
A flood nearly washed it away
x.w: It was stolen in 1977 and later found. It was stolen again in 2010 and has not been found since.

Q4118041.s: In Paris Van Gogh painted more brightly than before: he was learning from the Impressionists. He laid paint on thickly, so the strokes show like relief.
Q4118041.i: Imagine: who will you give such a bouquet to, and what will you say?

f: Find the wreath of flowers on Saskia's head.
Find the staff decorated with flowers in her hand.

m.q: What is Flora's mood?
o: Soft and gentle: a quiet smile
Stern: she looks down on us
m.w: Her face is warm and calm and her eyes look kindly. She seems tender and welcoming.

x.q: Whom did Rembrandt show as the goddess?
x.w: Saskia, Rembrandt's wife, posed for the picture. He liked to dress up those close to him and paint them as heroes of myths.

Q2225699.s: Rembrandt was a master of light and shadow: the bright face seems to glow against the dark background. Saskia posed for him often.
Q2225699.i: Imagine: which flowers did Flora pick this morning?

f: Find the tall black top hat and the long cloak.
Find the bottle and the glass near the man.

m.q: What is the mood of the man in the top hat?
o: Proud: he is off to a party
m.w: He stands alone, shoulders sagging, his gaze turned aside. His clothes are worn, and he does not seem happy.

x.q: Why did the exhibition jury refuse to accept this painting?
o: The picture was much too small for the hall
Its hero was a poor man off the street
The painter handed it in too late
x.w: At that time big pictures were about kings and heroes. Manet chose an ordinary Parisian, and the jury found that strange.

Q1192090.s: Manet painted city people without prettying them up. He was bold enough to put a poor man at the centre of a big picture.
Q1192090.i: Imagine: what is this man thinking about as he stands in the street?

f: Find the soldiers in shining armour.
Find Mary on the left, reaching out her hands to her son.

m.q: What do the women on the left feel?
o: Joy: they walk to a festival
Impatience: they want to go home
m.w: They bend toward Jesus and reach out to him, and their faces are sad. You can see how much they want to help.

x.q: What, according to the story, happened to this picture on its way to Sicily?
o: The ship arrived but the picture faded
The ship sank but the picture survived
Pirates took it, then gave it back
x.w: The ship was wrecked near Genoa, and the waves carried the crate with the painting to shore. The picture was taken out unharmed.

Q2664637.s: Raphael painted this for a church on the island of Sicily. There are many people in it, all in motion, as if the scene is happening right now.
Q2664637.i: Imagine: what words does the man who helps carry the cross use to cheer Jesus on?

f: Find the cross in the saint's hand.
Look at how light falls on her face: the background behind her is dark.

m.q: What is Saint Praxedis's face like?
m.w: She looks upward, and her face is soft and serious. You can tell she is busy with something important and kind.

x.q: How is this painting different from the usual paintings of Vermeer?
o: It shows a saint, not a quiet room
It shows only flowers and fruit
It shows a sea battle with ships
x.w: Later Vermeer became famous for quiet home scenes with a window and light. This is an early picture on a religious subject.

Q94006.s: The painting carries the date 1655. It may be one of Vermeer's earliest pictures, though experts still argue about it.
Q94006.i: Imagine: what would you ask Praxedis if you met her?

f: Find the oldest king kneeling before the baby.
Find the star above the stable.

m.q: What do the Magi feel?
o: Respect and joy: came from far away
Confusion: not sure where to go
m.w: The oldest king kneels, and the others look serious and respectful. You can tell they have long waited for this meeting.

x.q: What do the three panels of the altarpiece tell about?
o: Three events from the baby's life
x.w: On the left an angel brings Mary good news. In the centre the Magi arrive, and on the right the baby is brought to the temple.

Q874058.s: Rogier van der Weyden painted very finely and exactly, and his faces are full of feeling. The altarpiece is named after the church of St Columba in Cologne.
Q874058.i: Imagine: what do the Magi say to each other on the way home?

f: Find George's white horse.
Find the little princess running away in the distance on the left.

m.q: What does George feel?
o: Tiredness: he wishes to go home
m.w: He looks straight at the dragon and holds his weapon firmly. The horse rears up, yet he sits steady.

x.q: What did Raphael do to make the picture full of movement?
o: Everyone stands straight, as on parade
He painted thick fog all around
The horse rears, all rushes forward
x.w: The horse, the cloak and the lance point one way, like a rush. So it feels like the fight is happening right now.

Q2529918.s: By legend, Saint George beat a dragon, so he was painted often. This picture is quite small, and Raphael was young then.
Q2529918.i: Imagine: what will the princess say to George when the dragon is beaten?

f: Find the crutches and the wooden leg.
Find the unusual hats on the people's heads.

m.q: What do the people in the picture feel?
o: Joy: they are off to a festival
Tiredness: walking is hard for them
Boredom: they have nothing to do
m.w: The people walk with difficulty, leaning on crutches, and their heads are bowed. You can see it is not easy for them.

x.q: What is unusual about the size of this painting?
o: It is huge, like a barn door
It is huge, filling a wall
It is tiny, like a book
x.w: The picture is small, but it has very many exact details. You have to look at it up close.

Q3772184.s: Brueghel liked to paint ordinary people, not only grand ones. His pictures are full of careful little details.
Q3772184.i: Imagine: where are these people going, and what are they talking about?

f: Find the architect: he sits on a huge column holding a scroll.
Find buildings with a dome, columns and pointed towers: buildings of different ages.

m.q: What does the architect feel?
o: Worry: he fears for the city
A calm dream about his city
Boredom: he is tired of drawing
m.w: He reclines at ease and gazes at the city in the distance. The golden sunset light makes it all look like a dream.

x.q: What kind of city does the architect see in his dream?
o: A city of only wooden houses
A city of only glass towers
A city of buildings of all ages
x.w: Buildings of different ages stand side by side: with columns, domes and pointed towers. So the architect dreams of gathering the best of all times.

Q17512050.s: Thomas Cole was an American painter who loved huge landscapes and bright sunsets. A real architect ordered this picture from him.
Q17512050.i: Imagine: which building would you add to this dream city?

f: Find the two little boys: little Jesus and little John.
Find Mary bending toward the children.

m.q: What is the mood of this family?
o: Warm and quiet: all gaze at the children
m.w: All eyes are on the children, and the poses are soft and close. Everything looks calm and warm.

x.q: Who were the Canigiani, after whom the picture is named?
o: Monks from a monastery in Rome
x.w: Raphael lived in Florence then and painted pictures for noble families. For the Canigiani family he painted this Holy Family.

Q2713671.s: Raphael joined the figures into one flowing group, like a round dance: everyone is linked by glances and gestures.
Q2713671.i: Imagine: what are the little boys playing while the grown-ups watch them?

f: Find the see-through veil that Mary lifts.
Find the baby: he lies on a pillow.

m.q: What does Mary feel as she shows the baby?
o: Pride: she is showing off to guests
Worry: she fears he will wake up
m.w: She tilts her head and gently lifts the cloth with two fingers. Her face is soft and kind.

x.q: Why does Mary lift the veil?
o: To wipe the baby's little face
To hide the baby from the guests
x.w: She carefully uncovers the baby to show him to those nearby. The baby sleeps and does not notice.

Q2427320.s: Raphael painted the thin see-through cloth so well that it looks almost real. This is one of his most tender pictures of Mary.
Q2427320.i: Imagine: what will the baby say when he wakes up?

f: Find Mary's face: it is dark and calm.
Find the shining gold and silver cover around her.

m.q: What is Mary's face like?
m.w: Her gaze is soft and her face calm. She seems to comfort everyone who comes.

x.q: Where is this icon kept?
o: In a big museum in central Paris
In a hilltop castle near Prague
In a chapel above Vilnius's gate
x.w: The icon is kept over a gate of the old town, and people come there to pray. The gate is known as the Gate of Dawn.

Q2721080.s: The icon is painted on oak boards, and a silver cover hides almost everything except the face and hands. People of different countries and faiths come to it.
Q2721080.i: Imagine: what kind wish would you make for all people?

f: Find the dog in the foreground.
Find Isabella in the pale dress at the table: whom is she looking at?

m.q: What do Isabella's brothers feel?
o: Dislike and anger at her friend
m.w: They frown and look sideways, and one even kicks the dog. You can see the mood at the table is heavy.

x.q: What does this painting tell about?
o: A dinner at the painter's own house
A royal ball at the palace
A scene from a poem by Keats
x.w: Millais took a scene from John Keats's poem about the love of Isabella and a young man, Lorenzo. Isabella's brothers were against it.

Q822535.s: Millais was only about twenty when he and his friends founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood. They wanted to paint honestly, in bright colours and with lots of detail.
Q822535.i: Imagine: what are Isabella and Lorenzo whispering to each other at the table?

f: Find the stone parapet she leans on.
Find her hairstyle and see how she looks at us.

m.q: What is this woman's gaze like?
o: Sad, as if about to cry
m.w: She has turned to us over her shoulder and looks straight at us without looking away. Her face is calm and her pose is relaxed.

x.q: What does the nickname «La Schiavona» mean?
o: A singer from a Venice theatre
A countess from a hill castle
A Slavic girl from across the sea
x.w: She was perhaps given this name because of her dress and hairstyle. Nobody knows who she really was.

Q1633898.s: Titian painted portraits so well that the person seems about to speak. Here he used soft, warm colours, like a true master of Venice.
Q1633898.i: Imagine: what is this woman going to say to you?

f: Find the coin in the Pharisee's hand.
Find the hands of Jesus and the Pharisee: how do they differ?

m.q: What can you see in the face of Jesus?
o: Anger: he is cross with the Pharisee
Fear: he is afraid of the Pharisee
Calm, with great wisdom in his eyes
m.w: His face is even and soft and his gaze is attentive. He is not angry, he answers calmly.

x.q: What are these two arguing about?
o: How much this old coin is worth
Whether to pay the emperor's tax
Where they should go after lunch
x.w: The Pharisee shows a coin and wants to catch Jesus out. Jesus answers: «Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's».

Q2459887.s: Titian was about thirty when he painted this. There are only two faces, but they tell a whole story.
Q2459887.i: Imagine: what would you answer the Pharisee?

f: Find the green stripe running down the middle of the face.
Find the patches of colour behind her: they are nothing like real life.

m.q: What is Madame Matisse's face like?
o: Sad, as if about to cry
m.w: Her lips are closed and her gaze is straight and firm. This restrained seriousness suits her.

x.q: Why is the face in the picture multicoloured?
o: He was in a hurry and smudged it
x.w: Matisse believed colour could be bold and need not look realistic. The green stripe divides the face into a light part and a dark part.

Q2902188.s: When such pictures were shown, viewers were surprised. A critic called these painters «Fauves», «wild beasts», for their bold colours.
Q2902188.i: Imagine: what colour would you paint a friend's face, and why?

f: Find the dark cypress that looks like a flame.
Find the clouds in the sky: they curl like waves.

m.q: What is the mood of the field, sky and cypress?
o: Calm and clear, like a postcard
Sleepy and still, as if frozen
Lively: it all sways and trembles
m.w: The field, sky and tree sway as if a strong wind were blowing. That makes it all seem to breathe.

x.q: How did Van Gogh show the wind?
o: He painted leaves flying in the sky
He painted a weathervane on a pole
x.w: He laid paint in short, winding strokes. So the field, the sky and the cypress seem to tremble in the wind.

Q9391004.s: Van Gogh painted this at Saint-Rémy in the south of France, where he was being treated. He loved cypresses and wrote that they were as beautiful as Egyptian obelisks.
Q9391004.i: Imagine: what sound does this wind make?

f: Find the six angels at the sides: three on the left and three on the right.
Find the golden background: it has no sky and no trees.

m.q: What is the mood of the Madonna on her throne?
o: Noisy: all the angels sing and dance
Solemn and calm, like a ceremony
m.w: Mary sits straight on the throne, the angels stand still, and everything is hushed. The gold makes the scene festive and quiet.

x.q: Why is the background of the painting gold?
o: It showed a heavenly, special world
They ran out of blue paint for the sky
Gold was the cheapest paint then
x.w: In old pictures gold meant heavenly light. An ordinary landscape with sky and trees was not painted then.

Q948745.s: The painting is huge, over four metres high. Duccio lived in Siena and was one of the first to make figures more lifelike and rounded.
Q948745.i: Imagine: what are the angels whispering to each other at the edges?

f: Find the knife and the fruit in the boy's hands.
Find his white shirt: it is light against the dark background.

m.q: What is the boy's face like?
o: Playful: about to toss the fruit
Sad: he looks about to cry
m.w: He looks down at the fruit with his brows slightly drawn. All his attention is on the job.

x.q: How did Caravaggio light the boy?
o: With even light and no shadows
With strong side light, dark behind
With daylight from a window behind
x.w: The pale skin and shirt stand out from the darkness. So the boy looks almost alive and very close.

Q2574120.s: This is one of Caravaggio's earliest paintings, from when he was young and lived in Rome. He liked to paint ordinary boys from the street.
Q2574120.i: Imagine: who is the boy peeling the fruit for?

f: Find the owl on the woman's shoulder.
Find the big mug in her hand.

m.q: What is Malle Babbe's mood?
o: Loud fun: she roars with laughter
Quiet sadness: she remembers old days
Tiredness: she is about to nod off
m.w: Her mouth is wide open and her eyes sparkle, and you almost hear her loud laugh. She is all movement.

x.q: How did Hals paint laughter?
o: With quick strokes, catching the moment
With slow finishing of every hair
With smooth paint and no strokes at all
x.w: Hals painted fast, and the strokes stay visible. So the face seems to flicker and is about to burst out laughing.

Q474198.s: Hals lived in the city of Haarlem and could paint laughter so vividly that you seem to hear a voice.
Q474198.i: Imagine: what joke did Malle Babbe tell?

f: Find Mary, Joseph and the baby in the landscape.
Find the tall trees and the building in the distance.

m.q: What is the mood of the family on the road?
o: Quiet and solemn, even on the road
Merry: the family goes to a festival
m.w: The light is soft, the trees are calm, and the figures move unhurriedly. Even on the road you can feel peace and hope.

x.q: Why did the Holy Family go to Egypt?
o: To escape from a wicked king
x.w: In the Gospel, an angel warned Joseph of danger. The family went to Egypt and came back when it was safe.

Q970808.s: Nicolas Poussin was a French painter who lived in Rome. He loved order: trees, buildings and figures stand clearly and calmly, like music.
Q970808.i: Imagine: what are Joseph and Mary talking about on this road?

f: Find the biggest coloured rectangle.
Find the thin stick-like lines among the shapes.

m.q: What is the mood of the shapes on the white ground?
o: Heavy and gloomy: all presses down
m.w: The shapes lie on white as if in the air and seem to move along a diagonal. That gives a feeling of flight.

x.q: What is the movement that Malevich invented called?
x.w: He invented «Suprematism» in 1915: pictures of simple shapes and colours, with no people or objects.

Q1523466.s: Malevich's most famous picture is the «Black Square». He wanted a picture not to tell a story but to be pure shape and colour.
Q1523466.i: Imagine: if these shapes are spaceships, where are they flying?

f: Find Lazarus: he has just been raised from the tomb.
Find the hand of Jesus: he is calling Lazarus.

m.q: What do the people around feel?
m.w: Hands are raised, faces turn to Lazarus, eyes are wide open. Everyone is stunned by what they see.

x.q: How did Caravaggio make the scene dramatic?
o: He added lots of gold and colour
Light picks people out of the dark
He blurred everyone, as in fog
x.w: The figures seem to grow out of the dark into a beam of light. So everything looks tense and very alive.

Q2277635.s: Caravaggio liked light like a spotlight in a dark room. It picks out the main thing, and the rest sinks into shadow. This painting is very large.
Q2277635.i: Imagine: what did Lazarus say when he opened his eyes?

f: Find the riders on horses: they are entering the city.
Find the people in the foreground: they are bowing before the riders.

m.q: What do the people of the city feel?
m.w: People kneel and stretch out their hands to the riders. You can see they are frightened and ask for mercy.

x.q: What did Delacroix like to show in his big pictures?
o: Quiet still lifes of fruit and jugs
Calm portraits in soft grey tones
x.w: Delacroix was the leading Romantic painter. He liked everything in a picture to move, glow with colour and stir the feelings.

Q3055367.s: The event he showed happened in 1204, more than six hundred years before the painting. Delacroix painted history as if he had seen it with his own eyes.
Q3055367.i: Imagine: what will the people of this city say when peace comes?

f: Find the two girls: one in a pink dress, the other in blue.
Find their long, fluffy hair.

m.q: What is the mood of the sisters in pink and blue?
o: Calm, and a little bit shy
m.w: They stand side by side and look at us calmly, a little timidly. Their poses are quiet, with no fuss.

x.q: How did Renoir paint the dresses?
x.w: The dresses are painted in soft patches of colour. Renoir liked cloth to look light and fluffy.

Q6251405.s: Renoir painted portraits of children from rich Paris families. He loved tender pink and blue, soft as petals.
Q6251405.i: Imagine: what will the girls play when the painter lets them go?

f: Find the hat on the lady's head.
Find the patterns on the dress and the background: they almost merge.

m.q: What is the lady's mood?
m.w: She stands straight and looks out with confidence. Her pose and gaze look calm and dignified.

x.q: What makes Klimt's pictures recognisable?
o: Thick black outlines, like a comic
Soft mist instead of any outlines
x.w: Klimt loved beautiful ornaments. His patterns almost turn the figure and the background into one mosaic.

Q4681871.s: Klimt painted two portraits of Adele Bloch-Bauer. The first, the golden one, is the most famous, and the second has less gold but just as many patterns.
Q4681871.i: Imagine: where is this lady in the hat going?

f: Find the huge arches of the arena.
Find the little people in the foreground.

m.q: What is the mood of the day by the arena?
o: Gloomy: night is falling over the arena
Empty and silent: not a soul about
m.w: Bright sun, a deep blue sky and the colourful clothes of the people. Everything looks lively and warm.

x.q: What did the Romans build such an arena for?
o: To keep grain, oil and wine
x.w: The Romans built the arena at Arles almost two thousand years ago. In Van Gogh's time, shows with bulls were held there.

Q2269835.s: Van Gogh lived in Arles, in the south of France, for just over a year. He painted a great many pictures there. He loved the bright southern light and pure, rich colours.
Q2269835.i: Imagine: what show is on in the arena today?

f: Find the scene where the baby is born: people bend around him.
Find the riders on the road: they are the Magi with their company.

m.q: What is the mood of this long story in colour?
o: Stern and dull: everyone is silent
m.w: There are many bright colours, angels and scenes of joy. The title speaks of the seven joys of Mary.

x.q: How did Memling tell a whole story in one picture?
o: He painted one scene and added labels
He put many scenes in one landscape
He wrote a long text on the frame
x.w: In one long landscape scenes follow one after another: the news, the birth, the visit of the Magi and more. It reads like a comic strip.

Q369913.s: Memling lived in Bruges and painted very finely and exactly. This painting has a multitude of tiny figures, and you can look at each one on its own.
Q369913.i: Imagine: which scene would you add to this long story?

f: Find the wrinkles around the cardinal's eyes.
Find his thin lips and attentive gaze.

m.q: What kind of character does the cardinal's face show?
o: Cross and forever displeased with all
Clever and attentive, a little tired
m.w: His gaze is sharp and calm, his lips are pressed together and there are lines around his eyes. You can tell he has thought and seen a lot.

x.q: What is striking about this portrait?
o: Its huge size, a portrait filling a wall
x.w: Van Eyck painted very finely in oil. So you can see every wrinkle and little spot on the skin.

Q3399498.s: Van Eyck was one of the masters who developed oil painting. Oil let him paint tiny details and soft light.
Q3399498.i: Imagine: what is the cardinal thinking about, and what will he say to a visitor?

f: Find the two girls in black dresses and hats.
Find the light blouses: they stand out against the black.

m.q: What is the girls' mood?
m.w: They sit quietly and look calmly. Their poses are relaxed and nobody is in a hurry.

x.q: What did Renoir reportedly say about the colour black?
o: That black is the queen of colours
That black is just dirt on the palette
That black is only good for night
x.w: Many Impressionists avoided black, but Renoir thought it beautiful and used it boldly. Here the black dresses are soft and alive.

Q613390.s: Renoir loved painting children, and his portraits are tender. He painted the black dresses softly and lively, not as a flat patch.
Q613390.i: Imagine: what are the two girls talking about at the table?

f: Find the big lone tree.
Find the distant blue mountains in the morning haze.

m.q: What is the mood of the morning Friedrich painted?
m.w: Soft light, haze in the distance and a big still tree. It feels very, very quiet around.

x.q: What did Friedrich like to tell about in his pictures?
o: Merry festivals in a busy town square
Nature's silence and how small we are
x.w: Friedrich was a German Romantic. His landscapes are silent and make you stop and think.

Q1198515.s: Friedrich painted landscapes with few people or none at all. He painted light and mist so that you seem to hear the silence.
Q1198515.i: Imagine: what does the lone tree see in a whole day?

f: Find the chimneys on the roofs.
Find the snow on the roofs and the grey-blue sky.

m.q: What is the mood of winter Paris in the picture?
o: Quiet and cold: the city is hushed
