Hot and noisy, like high summer
Festive: everyone off to a carnival
m.w: Grey-blue tones, white snow and quiet wisps over the chimneys. The city seems to have fallen silent.

x.q: Where did Caillebotte look at the roofs from?
o: From a balloon high over Paris
From the top of Notre-Dame cathedral
From the window of his Paris flat
x.w: He painted the view from his flat window. The Eiffel Tower did not exist yet, it was built later.

Q1857132.s: Caillebotte was rich and supported his Impressionist friends by buying their paintings. He himself liked unusual views from above.
Q1857132.i: Imagine: who lives under these snowy roofs, and what are they doing?

f: Find the boy Jesus in the centre: where are his hands pointing?
Find the elderly teachers with books and look at their faces.

m.q: What do the teachers feel?
o: Anger: they are cross with the boy
Surprise: the boy is very wise
Joy: they are enjoying the lesson
m.w: They wrinkle their foreheads, bend over books and argue. You can see they did not expect such wisdom from a boy.

x.q: In how many days did Dürer paint this picture?
o: In a whole year of hard work
In five days, as it says on it
In one single hour, very fast
x.w: The picture has a Latin inscription: «Work of five days». Dürer painted it very fast, in Venice.

Q2448065.s: Dürer came from the German city of Nuremberg and was one of the most famous painters. He loved to draw every face and every hand very exactly.
Q2448065.i: Imagine: what question did the boy ask the teachers?

f: Find the powder puff in the woman's hand.
Find the vase of flowers on the little table.

m.q: What does the woman at the dressing table feel?
o: Delight: she is hurrying to a ball
m.w: She has bent her head and carefully powders her face. Her movements are smooth, and it is quiet around.

x.q: Who was the woman at the little table whom Seurat painted?
x.w: Madeleine Knobloch was the painter's companion. He painted her in his studio.

Q3766163.s: Seurat painted not with strokes but with thousands of tiny dots of colour. In the picture they blend into soft colour. He worked slowly and very carefully.
Q3766163.i: Imagine: what party is this woman getting ready for?

f: Find Mary with the baby.
Find the Magi and the people of their company: they came from far away.

m.q: What is the mood of the Adoration of the Magi?
o: Quiet and reverent, all gazing down
Anxious: everyone is afraid of something
m.w: People have gathered around the baby and look at him quietly and seriously. Nobody is noisy or in a hurry.

x.q: How many famous masters worked on this painting?
o: One: Fra Angelico on his own
x.w: Two Florentine masters worked on it together. It seems one began it and the other helped finish it.

Q3531531.s: Fra Angelico was a monk and painted in very light, tender colours. His name means «angelic brother».
Q3531531.i: Imagine: what does the youngest of the Magi say when he sees the baby?

f: Find the girl's white dress.
Find the patterns in the background: they are in an Eastern style.

m.q: What is Elisabeth's mood?
o: Sad: she looks close to tears
m.w: She stands straight and looks out calmly, with still hands. The pale dress underlines her softness.

x.q: What is unusual about the background of this portrait?
o: It is painted like a dark forest
It is completely empty and pale grey
x.w: Klimt loved Japanese and Chinese art and collected Eastern fabrics. The bright patterned background makes the white dress look even lighter.

Q136433749.s: Elisabeth was the daughter of Klimt's friends and patrons. He painted her when she was about twenty.
Q136433749.i: Imagine: which ball is Elisabeth going to in such a dress?

f: Find the arches that run into the distance like a corridor.
Find the people bending over the tombs.

m.q: What is the mood of the scene in the dim hall?
o: Tense and mysterious, in dim light
Sleepy and dull: all wait for morning
m.w: The hall is dim, and the figures bend and move fast. It seems something very important is happening.

x.q: How did Tintoretto make the picture deep, like a theatre stage?
o: He painted a mirror on the far wall
He filled the hall with thick fog
Floor and arch lines meet far away
x.w: The lines of the floor tiles and arches meet at a faraway point. So the hall seems huge and runs far back.

Q3937806.s: Tintoretto worked fast and boldly. His name means «little dyer»: his father was a silk dyer.
Q3937806.i: Imagine: what are the people whispering about in this dim hall?

f: Find the house in the middle of the field.
Find the golden-yellow field and the blue sky.

m.q: What is the mood of the summer day on the farm?
o: Cold: the first snow falls on the fields
Anxious: a storm gathers over the field
Warm and calm: summer on the farm
m.w: Yellow and green colours, a bright sky and nobody around. It feels like a hot, quiet day.

x.q: In which town in the south of France did Van Gogh live when he painted this?
x.w: In 1888 he went to Arles for the southern sun and bright colours. There he painted a great many pictures.

Q5435849.s: Van Gogh painted in thick, easily seen strokes, so a field seems to sway. He chose bright, pure colours, like those of Japanese prints.
Q5435849.i: Imagine: who lives in this house, and what do they do at sunset?

f: Find the tall painter with a palette: it is Bazille himself.
Find the pianist at the piano.

m.q: What is the mood of the friends in the studio?
o: Dull: all wait for the day to end
Cross: they have all fallen out
m.w: Friends stand and sit at ease, talking, and someone plays music. You can see they feel good together.

x.q: Who is in the picture next to Bazille?
o: Only his family and their servants
His friends: painters and a writer
Famous ministers and generals of France
x.w: Bazille painted his studio where friends gathered. For example, Manet, Monet, the writer Zola and the musician Maître.

Q15877622.s: This is a picture about the friendship of the future Impressionists. Bazille lived only twenty-eight years but managed to paint many pictures.
Q15877622.i: Imagine: what tune is the pianist playing while the friends argue about paintings?

f: Find the girl's light smile.
Find the blush on her cheeks.

m.q: What is Gabrielle's mood?
o: Kind and gentle: a quiet smile
Sad: she looks about to cry
Proud and cold, looking down on us
m.w: The corners of her lips are slightly raised, and her gaze is warm and open. She looks at us in a friendly way.

x.q: How did Bouguereau show that the girl is alive, not a statue?
o: Rosy cheeks, bright eyes, warm skin
He stood her on a tall stone pedestal
He painted her grey, like marble
x.w: Pink cheeks, sparkling eyes and warm skin colour make the face alive. Every small thing is painted very tenderly.

Q19826371.s: Bouguereau disliked visible brushstrokes: he painted so smoothly that his portraits look like porcelain. He taught in Paris, and many painters learned from him.
Q19826371.i: Imagine: what is Gabrielle thinking about as she smiles?

f: Find the huge hall with a high ceiling and chandeliers.
Find the men in uniforms: they sit and stand in rows.

m.q: What is the mood of the gathering?
o: Sleepy: everyone is bored and dozing
Solemn and serious, a big occasion
m.w: Everyone is in dress uniform, sitting or standing straight, and the hall is strict. You can see the event is important.

x.q: How many people did Repin paint in this picture?
x.w: Repin painted each official on his own. His pupils helped, among them the young Boris Kustodiev.

Q13381307.s: The painting is huge, almost nine metres wide. Repin painted it with helpers because there was so much work.
Q13381307.i: Imagine: what are two officials in the same row whispering about?

f: Find Hercules: he sits in the middle, thinking.
Find the steep rocky path and the winged horse Pegasus at the top.

m.q: What does Hercules feel?
o: Anger: he is arguing with the women
Joy: he is having fun with them
m.w: He sits between two women and looks serious. You can see the decision is not easy for him.

x.q: What choice does Hercules face?
o: Choosing the best sword for battle
Choosing where to sail a ship
Easy life or a hard road to glory
x.w: One woman calls him to pleasure and ease, the other points to the hard road to courage. In the myth, Hercules chose the road of effort.

Q283665.s: Annibale Carracci, with his relatives, founded a school in Bologna where artists learned to draw from life. His pictures were a start of Italian Baroque.
Q283665.i: Imagine: which road would you choose, and why?

f: Find the sorceress Medea: what is she doing?
Find Jason: how does he look at her?

m.q: What is the mood of the meeting of Jason and Medea?
o: Dull: they have nothing to do
m.w: The sorceress is busy with something magical, and Jason looks at her seriously. Everything around is quiet and mysterious.

x.q: Why did Jason come to Medea, in the myth?
o: He was looking for his lost ship
He wanted to buy medicine from her
x.w: In the myth, Jason sailed on the ship Argo for the Golden Fleece. The sorceress Medea helped him with magic.

Q6163843.s: Waterhouse loved painting heroines of myths and fairy tales, beautiful and mysterious. He worked in England and drew on legends and poems.
Q6163843.i: Imagine: what magic did Medea make?

f: Find the crescent moon under Mary's feet.
Find the little cherubs, the putti, around her.

m.q: What is Mary's mood?
o: Anxiety: she fears she will fall
Tiredness: she wants to sit down
m.w: She stands lightly, her hands folded and her gaze lifted to the sky. Soft golden light is all around.

x.q: What do the mirror and fountain held by the cherubs mean?
o: That the cherubs are about to wash
A sign of wealth: fine things
A sign of purity: spotless mirror
x.w: In old pictures a spotless mirror and clean water were signs of purity and light. This is how the painter says it without words.

Q5916308.s: Tiepolo was a Venetian and painted with ease: his figures float in a bright sky as if weightless. The King of Spain invited him to Madrid.
Q5916308.i: Imagine: what are the cherubs singing about around Mary?

f: Find Mary: she is rising upward on a cloud.
Find the apostles below: they look up in amazement.

m.q: What do the apostles feel as they watch Mary rise?
o: Anger: they argue with each other
m.w: Hands are raised, faces turned up and eyes wide open. They are seeing a miracle.

x.q: How did Rubens show that Mary is rising?
o: He painted a bird flying beside her
Lines and cherubs all lift upward
He painted a long ladder below her
x.w: Figures and clouds spiral upward, and cherubs support Mary. Your eye slides up to the sky by itself.

Q2067336.s: Rubens was the leading painter of Antwerp and painted very energetically: bodies, cloth and clouds seem to swirl. This picture hangs over the high altar of the cathedral.
Q2067336.i: Imagine: what do the apostles say to each other as they look up?

f: Find Mary: she lies on a couch with the apostles around her.
Find the angels at the top of the picture.

m.q: What do the apostles around Mary's couch feel?
m.w: They bend over Mary, their faces serious and tender. Everything is quiet, as at a farewell.

x.q: What old kind of picture does this painting look like?
o: A bright picture from a storybook
An old map of faraway seas
x.w: The young El Greco grew up on Crete, where icons were painted. This early picture still looks very much like an icon.

Q3078569.s: El Greco was born on Crete and later went to Spain, where he became famous. This is an early work from his homeland, and it is signed in Greek.
Q3078569.i: Imagine: what do the apostles whisper to Mary as a farewell?

f: Find the shadow on the floor under the man's feet.
Find his raised hand: he seems to be making a speech.

m.q: What is the mood of the court jester?
o: Lost: he has forgotten his part
Sad: he is in no mood for jokes
m.w: His head is raised, one arm is stretched out and his stance is firm. He looks like a performer before an audience.

x.q: What is unusual about the background of this painting?
o: A thick dark forest behind him
A heavy red curtain behind him
x.w: Velázquez painted no wall, furniture or landscape. The space is seen only through the shadow and a slight change of colour.

Q1113763.s: Pablo de Valladolid was a court jester and actor. Many painters, including Manet, admired this portrait.
Q1113763.i: Imagine: what speech is Pablo making?

f: Find the old blind Belisarius and the boy who helps him.
Find the soldier: he is amazed to see his former commander.

m.q: What does the soldier feel?
o: Joy: he is glad to meet him
Anger: he is angry at the old man
m.w: He has thrown up his hands and froze, staring at the old man. You can see he is shaken.

x.q: Who is Belisarius in the old story?
o: A wise monk from a mountain cave
A general who ended up poor
A famous shipbuilder of his day
x.w: Belisarius was a famous general of Byzantium. By legend, in old age he went blind and begged for alms.

Q2698149.s: David loved clear, strict pictures with noble heroes, as in ancient Greece and Rome. His figures are arranged clearly and look like sculptures.
Q2698149.i: Imagine: what will the soldier say to his former commander?

f: Find Pierrot in his white costume: he stands straight and looks at us.
Find the donkey and the other actors behind Pierrot.

m.q: What does Pierrot feel?
o: Mischief: he is up to a prank
Impatience: he is due on stage
m.w: His arms hang down, his pose is still and his gaze is soft and sad. Around him everyone moves, but he is silent.

x.q: Which theatre do the figures of this picture come from?
x.w: Pierrot is a hero of old Italian comedy, where actors played in masks and bright costumes.

Q3387944.s: Watteau was a French painter of tender, slightly sad scenes of festivals and theatre. Here Pierrot stands full-length, almost like a monument.
Q3387944.i: Imagine: what is Pierrot sad about, and what would cheer him up?

f: Find the church and bell tower: they stand as a dark silhouette at sunset.
Find the reflections in the water.

m.q: What is the mood of the evening over Venice?
o: Noisy: a carnival on the canals
Anxious: a big storm is on its way
Quiet and dreamy, all in a haze
m.w: Pink and violet tones, soft haze and still water. It seems the day is slowly falling asleep.

x.q: In which city did Monet paint this picture?
o: In the French city of Rouen
x.w: In 1908 Monet came to Venice and painted many pictures there of canals and palaces.

Q3947218.s: Monet painted the same place at different times of day to show how light changes. Here the sunset sky is pink, orange and violet.
Q3947218.i: Imagine: who is sailing on the water in a boat this evening?

f: Find the mirror behind her: it shows her hairstyle from the back.
Find the opera glasses on the little table.

m.q: What is the countess's mood?
o: Playful: she is about to giggle
Tired: she longs to be in her bed
m.w: She stands straight with her hand at her chin, her gaze steady and attentive. Her pose is calm and noble.

x.q: What could Ingres paint especially skilfully?
x.w: The blue satin dress gleams and shimmers softly, as if real. Every fold is painted very exactly.

Q17189258.s: The countess was a real woman, the daughter of a duke. Ingres worked on the portrait for several years and made many sketches.
Q17189258.i: Imagine: which theatre is the countess going to with these opera glasses?

f: Find Mary and the baby: how close are their faces?
Find the opening behind them with a landscape in it.

m.q: What does Mary feel?
o: Tiredness: she wants to sit down
Worry: she fears for the baby
m.w: She has bent her head to the baby, and her look is soft. Everything in her pose speaks of care.

x.q: What is a «loggia», after which the painting is named?
o: A tall tower with a big bell
A stone well in a small courtyard
x.w: A loggia is an open gallery with arches. In the picture Mary is at such an opening.

Q2717478.s: Botticelli was about twenty-two when he painted this. He learned from the master Filippo Lippi, and his teacher's softness shows in it.
Q2717478.i: Imagine: what story will Mary tell the baby this evening?

f: Find Mary: she is huge, calm and has opened her cloak.
Find the small people kneeling under her cloak.

m.q: What do the people under the cloak feel?
o: Calm and deep trust in her
Worry: they fear being sent away
m.w: The people kneel with folded hands and peaceful faces. They feel protected.

x.q: What does Mary's wide cloak mean?
o: That a heavy rain has just begun
Protection and care for her people
That she is setting off on a journey
x.w: Mary covers the people with her cloak like a big shelter. That is why she is called the «Madonna of Mercy».

Q2247307.s: Piero painted calmly and strictly, and his figures look like stone statues. He came from the town of Sansepolcro, where this picture is kept even today.
Q2247307.i: Imagine: what kind word will Mary say to the people under the cloak?

f: Find George Washington on his horse.
Find the British officer who is handing over his sword.

m.q: What is the mood of the surrender ceremony?
o: Panic: everyone runs in all directions
m.w: Soldiers stand in neat rows and nobody shouts. An important moment passes strictly and quietly.

x.q: Who helped the Americans in this battle?
o: The Chinese, who came by ship
The French, shown on the left
x.w: At Yorktown French troops helped the Americans. In the picture the French are on the left and the Americans on the right.

Q3212180.s: This painting hangs in the Capitol building in Washington. Trumbull fought in that war himself and painted portraits of the people who took part from life.
Q3212180.i: Imagine: what did the British officer think as he came forward with the sword?

f: Find the baby: he lies in front of Mary.
Find the shepherds: they came to bow.

m.q: What do the shepherds feel?
o: Fear: they want to run to the flock
Awe and a quiet joy, hands folded
m.w: They bow with folded hands, and their faces are calm and happy. You can see this meeting is very important to them.

x.q: How did Mantegna paint the rocks?
o: Soft and fluffy, like cotton wool
Sharp and hard, like cut stone
x.w: Mantegna loved ancient statues and stones. His rocks look like stone sculptures.

Q3605556.s: Mantegna, from northern Italy, painted as if his figures were carved from stone. He built space and perspective very exactly.
Q3605556.i: Imagine: what gift did the shepherds bring to the baby?

f: Find Mary and the baby: how do they look at each other?
Find the soft landscape behind them.

m.q: What is the mood of Mary and the baby?
m.w: Mary and the baby are close, the figures are soft and the colours warm. It seems quiet and peaceful all around.

x.q: How many years did Raphael live?
o: Fifty, until his hair turned grey
x.w: Raphael died young, in 1520, but managed to create many famous paintings.

Q323188.s: The painting is named after the Diotallevi family of Rimini, who once owned it. Raphael painted it young, at about nineteen.
Q323188.i: Imagine: what does the baby want to tell his mother?

f: Count the people sitting at the table. Find the steam rising from the potatoes.
Find the lamp above the table, then look at the big, hard-working hands.

m.q: How do these people feel at their supper?
o: Tired, but warm and calm together
Cheering at a party round the lamp
Arguing about who gets the potatoes
m.w: Their faces look tired, and the lamp glows softly. They sit close together, so it feels cosy.

x.q: Why did Van Gogh choose such dark, earthy colours?
o: His bright paints had just run out
To look earthy, like their hard life
The room with the lamp was very dark
x.w: Van Gogh wrote that the colour should be like a dusty potato, still in its skin. He wanted everything to look like earth, just like these people's lives.

Q154469.s: Van Gogh wanted to show that these people eat with the same hands they used to dig the earth. The painting is dark and honest, with no pretending.
Q154469.i: Imagine what these five are quietly talking about at the table.

f: Find the pitchfork in the farmer's hand. Its prongs are copied in the stitching of his overalls.
Above them, find the pointed window on the house.

m.q: What do the faces of these two look like?
m.w: Their lips are pressed together and they stare straight at us. Nobody is smiling.

x.q: Why is the painting called 'American Gothic'?
o: From a scary story in the picture
From the cathedral where it was painted
From the pointed window on the house
x.w: Pointed windows like this belong to old Gothic churches. The painter spotted one on a small country house.

Q464782.s: The models were the painter's sister and his dentist, posing separately. Grant Wood imagined them as a farmer and his daughter.
Q464782.i: Imagine what they would say if you knocked on their front door.

f: Find the shadows of the clouds on the town and the sunny roofs far away.
Find the tiny people on the shore and the boats on the water.

m.q: What is the mood of this morning?
m.w: The water is smooth like a mirror and the people stand still. The sky above the town is peaceful.

x.q: How did Vermeer paint the sparkles of light on the roofs and boats?
o: With tiny dots of light paint
He glued glitter on the canvas
With a white pencil on the roofs
x.w: Vermeer put small light dots of paint on the roofs and boats. From far away they look like sparkling sunshine.

Q523974.s: The writer Marcel Proust called this the most beautiful painting in the world. Vermeer painted his hometown, Delft, in soft light.
Q523974.i: Imagine you are standing on the shore. What sounds can you hear in this town?

f: Find the flower the baby is looking at.
See how seriously he studies it, like a tiny scientist.

m.q: What is Mary's mood?
o: Sad, about to burst into tears
m.w: Mary smiles and plays with her son, like any young mother.

x.q: Why is the picture called the 'Benois Madonna'?
o: After the baby in Mary's arms
After the family that owned it
After the town where it was painted
x.w: The Benois family in Russia owned it for a long time, then sold it to the Hermitage. It was painted by Leonardo da Vinci.

Q1142058.s: Leonardo painted softly, with no hard outlines, so the faces look alive. He painted this one when he was still young.
Q1142058.i: Imagine what the baby is thinking while he studies the flower.

f: Look closely at the edges of the square: they are not perfectly straight.
Find the thin cracks in the black paint.

m.q: What feeling does this black square give you?
m.w: A dark square on a pale background is quiet and still. It is like a closed door with something behind it.

x.q: Where did Malevich hang it at its first show?
o: In the middle of the biggest wall
High in a corner, like an icon
x.w: In Russian homes icons hang in the 'red corner'. Malevich showed that this new picture mattered just as much to him.

Q1170315.s: Malevich believed a picture can be just shape and feeling, without showing any objects. He called this Suprematism.
Q1170315.i: Imagine what is hidden behind the black square, like behind a door.

f: Find the patterns on the golden dress that look like eyes. How many can you count?
Find Adele's face and hands. The painter made them look just like real life.

m.q: How does Adele seem?
m.w: Her gaze is soft and deep, and her head tilts slightly. She seems lost in her own thoughts.

x.q: What is the shining background made of?
x.w: Gustav Klimt used thin leaves of real gold and silver, as in icons and mosaics. That is why the painting glows.

Q354396.s: The painting is nicknamed 'The Woman in Gold'. For many years it was far from Adele's family, until her niece won it back.
Q354396.i: Imagine what Adele is dreaming of in her golden room.

f: Find the red poppies and other flowers floating on the water.
Find the little robin on the branch above the water.

m.q: What is Ophelia's face like?
o: Quiet, as if she is singing
Cheerful, she is about to laugh
m.w: Her mouth is slightly open as if she is softly singing, and her palms are open. Everything around her is calm, like a dream.

x.q: How did Millais paint the river bank?
o: Made it up from memory, indoors
Copied it from a big photograph
x.w: Millais sat by the river for months with his easel and painted every leaf. That is why the plants look so real.

Q1065493.s: This is a sad scene from Shakespeare's play about a girl called Ophelia. The model, Elizabeth Siddal, posed lying in a bath of warm water.
Q1065493.i: Invent the little song that Ophelia is softly singing.

f: Find the dark curtain on the left and the framed pictures on the wall.
Find the white cap on her head and her hands resting calmly in her lap.

m.q: What is this woman's mood?
m.w: She sits straight and still with her hands folded. You can see she is in no hurry.

x.q: What is the painting's real title?
o: 'A Lady in Black by a Grey Wall'
'Mother Waiting for Her Son at Home'
x.w: Whistler thought of colours like music. 'Arrangement' is a word from music, just like 'nocturne'.

Q687182.s: Whistler named his pictures like pieces of music: 'Symphony', 'Nocturne', 'Arrangement'. For him, colours and how they fit together mattered most.
Q687182.i: Imagine what she is remembering while she sits so quietly.

f: Find the red carnation in Mary's hand.
Find the clear glass vase of flowers by the window.

m.q: What does the baby feel?
o: Bored, he gazes out of the window
m.w: The baby stretches out his little hand and stares at the flower.

x.q: What did Leonardo paint through the windows?
o: Rocky peaks in a blue haze
A blue sea with white sails
x.w: Through the windows you see far-off rocky mountains, like in a fairy tale. Leonardo loved nature and studied mountains and water.

Q698015.s: Leonardo was young when he painted this. He even painted a see-through glass vase very exactly.
Q698015.i: Imagine what the baby does once he grabs the carnation.

f: Find the dog on the bank and the little house on the left.
Find the cart and horses crossing the river.

m.q: What is the mood of this summer day?
m.w: The water is calm and the sky is soft. Nobody is in a hurry. It is just an ordinary country day.

x.q: What is the cart with horses doing?
o: Waiting on an old stone bridge
Crossing the river at a ford
x.w: The horses walk right through shallow water, because there is no bridge. This kind of crossing is called a ford.

Q2366825.s: Constable painted the place where he grew up: the River Stour in England. The white flecks of light on leaves and water were nicknamed 'Constable's snow'.
Q2366825.i: Imagine where the cart is going and who is waiting for it.

f: Find the lamp hidden behind the boy's back. The light comes from it.
Find the machine in the middle with rings and little balls.

m.q: What do the people around feel?
m.w: Their faces glow and their eyes are wide open. Everyone watches the machine, holding their breath.

x.q: What does the machine in the middle show?
o: What time it is, like a clock
x.w: It is a model of the Solar System. The lamp in the middle plays the Sun, and the little balls are planets.

Q1651874.s: Joseph Wright loved painting bright lamp or candle light in dark rooms. He painted the science of his time as if it were magic.
Q1651874.i: Imagine the question a child would ask the philosopher.

f: Look at the stormy sky: what colours can you see in the clouds?
Find the bridge and the tall buildings on the hill above the river.

m.q: What is the mood of this city?
m.w: Dark clouds hang over the hill, and a strange light falls on the ground. It feels as if a storm is about to break.

x.q: What did El Greco do with the buildings of Toledo?
o: Moved some to make it prettier
Drew each one exactly like a map
Made up a town that isn't real
x.w: El Greco shifted some buildings so the picture worked better. He cared about more than exactness.

Q883994.s: El Greco was a very unusual painter. He painted very few landscapes, and this is the most famous one.
Q883994.i: Imagine what happens a minute later: rain, wind or a rainbow?

f: Look at the scales in her hand: is there anything in the little pans?
Find the pearls and the gold on the table.

m.q: What is the woman feeling?
o: Anger, she is in a hurry
Joy, she is about to laugh
m.w: She stands very still and looks carefully at the scales. The soft light from the window makes everything quiet.

x.q: What is she doing with the scales?
x.w: The pans are empty. She is waiting for the scales to hang level. This is how Vermeer showed calm and balance.

Q969367.s: On the wall behind her hangs a picture of the Last Judgement, where people's deeds are weighed. Vermeer liked hiding meanings in everyday things.
Q969367.i: Imagine what she will weigh once the scales settle.

f: Find the three women bending down to pick up ears of wheat.
Look into the distance: find the huge haystacks and the person on a horse.

m.q: What do these women feel?
o: Merry, as if at a festival
Hiding from rain in the field
m.w: They are bent to the ground and silent. You can see the work is hard, but they keep going.

x.q: Who are 'the gleaners'?
o: The owners, checking on the whole harvest
Women hired by the farmer to reap
Poor women picking up leftover wheat
x.w: When the harvest is in, a few ears of wheat are left on the field. Poor people picked them up so they would have bread.

Q1368055.s: Jean-François Millet grew up in a farming family. He painted these ordinary workers as strong and important, like heroes.
Q1368055.i: Imagine what the women will do with the ears they gathered, back at home.

f: Find the bright light inside the glass flask.
Find the moon in the window. Who is kneeling in front of the flask?

m.q: What does the alchemist feel?
m.w: He has raised his hands and stares at the glowing flask. Something wonderful has just happened.

x.q: What did the alchemist discover?
o: Phosphorus, it glows in the dark
A way to turn lead into gold bars
A magic potion for a long life
x.w: He was looking for a way to make gold, and found phosphorus instead. It glows in the dark.

Q1652023.s: Joseph Wright of Derby loved painting bright light in dark rooms. Here the light comes from the discovery itself.
Q1652023.i: Imagine what the alchemist says to his helpers.

f: Find the mirror above the instrument. What does it show?
Find the window on the left, where the light pours in.

m.q: What is the atmosphere in this room?
m.w: The girl stands by the instrument and listens. The room is silent.

x.q: What does the mirror above the instrument show?
o: The window and the street outside
The girl's face and an easel
A portrait of a king in a frame
x.w: We see the girl from behind, but the mirror shows her face. You can also spot part of the painter's easel.

Q2336984.s: On the instrument is a Latin saying: 'Music is the companion of joy and medicine for sorrow'. Vermeer liked to hide clues like this in his paintings.
Q2336984.i: Invent the tune that the girl is playing.

f: Find the man who is sleeping under the tree.
Find what the other workers are eating for lunch.

m.q: What do the people feel while they rest?
m.w: They sit and sleep in the shade after hard work. Everything around is calm.

x.q: What time of year is it?
x.w: The wheat is golden and ripe and people are cutting it. That happens in late summer.

Q776175.s: Bruegel painted a whole series of pictures about the seasons, and this is one of them. He painted village life with love and care.
Q776175.i: Imagine what the man sleeping under the tree is dreaming.

f: Look up: find Jesus floating in bright light.
Look down: how many people are pointing upwards?

m.q: What do the people below feel?
m.w: They wave their hands and look up, then at each other. It is noisy and anxious below, with quiet light above.

x.q: How did Raphael divide the picture?
o: Calm light above, busy dark below
Light on the left, dark on the right
Dark and busy above, light below
x.w: A bright calm floats above while hurry fills the bottom. Two worlds in one picture.

Q2344437.s: This is Raphael's last painting, and he did not finish it. His pupils completed it, and it was displayed next to him when people said goodbye.
Q2344437.i: Imagine what the people pointing upwards can see.

f: Find the young man on the left: he smiles and looks straight at us.
Find the red and yellow colours and the stringed instrument, a cittern.

m.q: What is the mood in this tavern?
o: Anxious, as if trouble is near
m.w: People smile and music plays. The bright clothes make the scene warm and lively.

x.q: Who do many people think the smiling young man might be?
o: A boy from next door in Delft
x.w: Many think Vermeer painted himself here. Nobody knows for sure.

Q63692.s: This is one of Vermeer's early paintings, and he put the year on it. The colours are bright and warm, not quiet like in his later rooms.
Q63692.i: Imagine the song the young man is singing.

f: Look at the young man's dark beret and his long hair.
Find his eyes: where are they looking?

m.q: What is his face like?
m.w: His face is smooth and his gaze is kind and quiet. He is not smiling or frowning.

x.q: About how old was Raphael in this portrait?
x.w: Raphael painted himself young, a little over twenty. He started working very early.

Q555821.s: Raphael lived only 37 years, but he became one of the most loved painters. He knew how to paint soft, kind faces.
Q555821.i: Imagine what Raphael wants to paint next.

f: Find the girl's long golden hair.
Find the flowers in her hand.

m.q: What is Flora like in the picture?
m.w: Her head is tilted slightly and her gaze is soft. The white blouse and flowers make her look gentle.

x.q: Who is Flora?
o: Goddess of the sea and ships
Goddess of the hunt and forests
x.w: In Roman myths Flora is the goddess of flowers and spring. That is why she holds flowers.

Q2046100.s: Titian was a master of colour. He could paint warm skin, golden hair and soft light.
Q2046100.i: Imagine which flowers Flora is picking today.

f: Find the lamp near the ceiling: its smoke turns into angels.
Find the servants and the basket at the front.

m.q: What do the apostles feel?
o: Boredom, wanting to go to sleep
Joy, playing a game at the table
m.w: They lean in, whisper and gesture. You can tell they have heard something very important.

x.q: How did Tintoretto place the table?
o: Straight across, as in most pictures
At a slant, leading deep inside
Round, in the middle of the hall
x.w: The table runs into the distance on a diagonal, so the picture is full of movement. It feels like it is happening right now.

Q2472983.s: 'Tintoretto' means 'little dyer', because his father dyed cloth. He painted fast, boldly and with huge energy.
Q2472983.i: Imagine what the servants whisper while the apostles talk.

f: Find the gods sitting on the grass, feasting under the trees.
Find the little donkey and the wine jugs.

m.q: How is the feast going?
o: Angry, everyone quarrels over the wine
Sad, everyone is silent and sighing
Merry, the gods relax on the grass
m.w: The gods sit on the grass and drink wine, with no hurry. It is a party in the woods.

x.q: Who began painting this picture?
x.w: The old master Giovanni Bellini began it, and his pupil Titian finished it and repainted the landscape.

Q15008032.s: Bellini was over eighty when he took on this painting. Titian continued his teacher's work and added his own landscape.
Q15008032.i: Imagine a funny story one of the gods is telling.

f: Find the long ribbon with knots in the angels' hands.
Find Mary in the middle, with many angels around her.

m.q: How does Mary deal with the knots?
o: Kind and calm, in no hurry
Puzzled, not sure what to do
m.w: Mary bends over the ribbon and takes her time. It is as if she is saying, 'I will help.'

x.q: What do the knots in the ribbon mean?
o: Sweets and gifts hidden for children
Troubles of people that Mary unties
A pretty trim for a festive dress
x.w: The knots stand for people's troubles and problems. In the picture, Mary helps to untangle them.

Q472799.s: The painting hangs in a church in Augsburg, Germany. The future Pope Francis saw it there and took a postcard of it home to Argentina.
Q472799.i: Imagine which 'knot' you would like to untie.

f: Find the swirls in the background that look like waves.
Find the red beard and moustache.

m.q: What is Van Gogh's face like?
m.w: His face is pale, his brows are drawn together and his gaze is watchful. He looks tired and thoughtful.

x.q: Why did Van Gogh paint so many self-portraits?
o: He really liked his own face
He wanted to hand them to friends
He had no money to pay models
x.w: Models had to be paid, and Van Gogh had little money. So he often painted himself in a mirror.

Q3630735.s: Van Gogh painted around thirty-five self-portraits. Here he used thick brushstrokes, and the background seems to ripple like waves.
Q3630735.i: Imagine what Van Gogh is thinking as he looks at himself in the mirror.

f: Find Jesus's bright red robe in the centre.
See how tightly the people crowd around him: how many faces can you see?

m.q: What is Jesus like in the picture?
o: Scared, looking for a way to escape
Stern and angry, shouting at all
m.w: The crowd is noisy around him, but he stands quietly and looks up. His calm makes him strong.

x.q: How did El Greco make Jesus the main figure?
o: His red robe glows against the dark
He painted him a giant, taller than all
He hid him away in a dark corner
x.w: The bright red patch pulls your eye at once, among the dark crowd.

Q2714617.s: 'El Greco' means 'the Greek': he came from the island of Crete but worked in Toledo, Spain. He painted this for Toledo Cathedral.
Q2714617.i: Imagine what people in the crowd whisper to each other.

f: Find the girl in the light dress: she stands with her back to us.
Find the cloud of white steam and the little dog in the woman's lap.

m.q: What is the woman's face like?
o: Cheerful, about to laugh out loud
m.w: She has looked up from her book and gazes at us. Her look is calm and a little absent-minded.

x.q: Where is the girl looking?
o: Up at birds and clouds in the sky
Through the railings at the trains
At the puppy on the woman's lap
x.w: The girl holds the railings and looks at the tracks. She is probably waiting for a train to pass.

Q1212098.s: There is hardly any train in the picture, only white steam. Manet knew the Saint-Lazare station well: his studio was nearby.
Q1212098.i: Imagine where the train will go and who sits inside.

f: Find the bearded man with a stick and painting gear on his back: it is the painter himself.
Find the man who is lifting his hat and bowing.

m.q: What does the painter look like?
o: Shy, hiding his eyes from all
m.w: He stands straight with his head up and his beard forward. You can see he is sure of himself.

x.q: Why is the picture called 'Bonjour, Monsieur Courbet!'?
o: It was the street where he lived
A friend greets the painter, bowing
x.w: Courbet's rich friend Alfred Bruyas lifts his hat and greets the painter. That is the 'meeting'.

Q3642171.s: Courbet painted only what he saw in real life. He painted ordinary roads and ordinary people on huge canvases, as if they were heroes.
Q3642171.i: Imagine how the painter answers the greeting.

f: Find the god Bacchus: he leaps from the chariot in a pink cloak.
Find the two spotted animals pulling the chariot.

m.q: What does Ariadne feel?
o: Amused, she is laughing at him
Bored, she wants to go home
m.w: She has drawn back and stares at Bacchus. A ship sails away on the horizon, and she is confused.

x.q: What is the blue of the sky made from?
o: A rare blue stone, lapis lazuli
Juice of blue berries and flowers
Blue clay from a river bank
x.w: Ultramarine was made from lapis lazuli, brought from far away. It cost a great deal.

Q1206860.s: Titian painted the huge glowing sky with expensive blue paint. Bacchus and his merry crowd burst into the picture like a whirlwind.
Q1206860.i: Imagine what Bacchus says to Ariadne when they meet.

f: Find the coloured stained-glass window: a woman is painted in it.
Find the glass the young woman is drinking from, and the chair.

m.q: What does the young woman feel?
o: Laughing out loud with the man
m.w: She drinks with her eyes lowered while the man leans toward her. She seems a little awkward.

x.q: What is painted on the coloured window?
o: A tall ship on the sea
x.w: The window shows a woman holding reins. It is a hint to know your limits in everything.

Q782639.s: Dutch painters of the 1600s loved painting everyday life in homes. Their pictures often hide little clues.
Q782639.i: Imagine what the man and the young woman are talking about.

f: Find the dog that barks at the traveller.
Look at his clothes and shoes: they are ragged and do not match.

m.q: How does the traveller feel?
o: Carefree and merry, humming a tune
Tired and wary, but he walks on
m.w: He glances back at the dog and still steps forward. His clothes are torn: the road has been long.

x.q: Who is the 'prodigal son' of the old story?
o: A king disguised as a poor traveller
A shepherd who lost his sheep
A son who left home and came back
x.w: This story has been told for centuries. Some people think the traveller in the picture is that son.

Q2400652.s: The picture is round, like a big coin. Experts argue whether he is the prodigal son or just a travelling pedlar.
Q2400652.i: Imagine where the traveller is going and what is in his bundle.

f: Find the dog's head peeking up from below.
Look at the huge empty sky above it: what colour is it?

m.q: What does the dog feel?
o: Happy, about to jump and play
m.w: The dog is tiny in the corner and everything around is empty. It looks up as if waiting for someone.

x.q: Why does the dog look so small and lonely?
o: A huge empty ochre sky around it
It is hiding behind a big rock
It was painted on a separate canvas
x.w: Goya left a huge empty space and put the dog at the bottom. That makes it look small and alone.

Q500936.s: Goya painted this dog straight onto the wall of his house. Later the picture was carefully moved onto canvas, and now hangs in the Prado.
Q500936.i: Imagine what the dog is looking at and who it is waiting for.

f: Find the women with rakes walking across the meadow.
Find the cart with horses and the village on the hill far away.

m.q: What is the mood of the workers?
o: Sad, everyone sighs and says nothing
m.w: People work in the field together and do not argue. The sun shines and the day is warm.

x.q: In what season is hay made?
x.w: The grass is tall, and people cut it and dry it as hay. This happens in June and July.

Q1213437.s: Bruegel painted peasants at work in different months of the year. He was nicknamed 'Peasant Bruegel' because he loved village life.
Q1213437.i: Invent the song the women with rakes are singing.

f: Find the white caps of the Breton women and their black dresses.
Find the two wrestlers far off: a man and an angel.

m.q: What do the women feel?
o: Merry, they play a game of tag
Scared, they want to run away
m.w: The women sit still with their heads bowed. They are so focused that they see the vision as if it were real.

x.q: Why is the ground in the picture bright red?
o: The soil in that village is red
He had run out of green paint
Gauguin chose it for a feeling
x.w: Gauguin wanted to show the power of the vision, not the true colour of the ground. The bright colour makes the scene strange and magical.

Q1764395.s: The wrestling man and angel are the women's vision, not something truly in front of them. Gauguin painted flat bright patches with dark outlines.
Q1764395.i: Imagine how the wrestling in the vision ends.

f: Find the dark curtain at the left: it feels as if we peek through a half-open door.
Find the slippers and the broom on the floor, and the musical instrument in the woman's lap.

m.q: What does the lady feel?
o: She does not care about it at all
Amused, she is about to laugh
Surprised and hoping for good news
m.w: She looks up at the maid with the letter. Her gaze is questioning and a little uneasy.

x.q: From where do we look into the room?
o: As if through a half-open door
Through a window from the street
x.w: The dark frame of curtain and floor makes the room look like a picture in a window. We seem to be peeking.

Q735061.s: In the 1600s, the Dutch loved pictures with letters, because they told little stories. Vermeer could show them without words.

f: Find Mary and the baby in the golden glow above.
Find the little angel in the middle holding a blank tablet.

m.q: How do the people below look at Mary?
o: With love and a lot of hope
m.w: They look up, and some kneel. You can see they gaze at Mary with love and hope.

x.q: How did Raphael arrange Mary and the people?
o: Everyone in one row, like a photo
Mary up on a cloud, people below
x.w: Mary floats in a golden circle on the clouds, as in the sky, while the people stand on earth. Light joins the top and the bottom.

Q2610709.s: At the bottom you can see the little town of Foligno with a bright flash above it. It was probably ordered in thanks, because the patron's house survived a strike from the sky.
Q2610709.i: Imagine what the little angel was going to write on the tablet.

f: Find the old man with a violin in the middle.
Find the tall man in a top hat and the child.

m.q: What is the mood of these people?
o: Festive, noisy and full of fun
Quiet, a little sad and thoughtful
Angry, as if they had quarrelled
m.w: Nobody is smiling and everyone looks serious. This shows a poor life as it is, without pretending.

x.q: Whom did Manet choose as the heroes of this picture?
x.w: Manet painted not kings but people he met on the streets of Paris. He thought their lives deserved a big picture too.

Q59815.s: Manet liked to learn from old masters, but he painted ordinary people of his own time.
Q59815.i: Imagine the tune the old man is playing.

f: Find Mary on the high throne with the baby on her lap.
Find the angels around the throne and the golden halos.

m.q: What is Mary like in this picture?
o: Merry and playful, like a girl
Cross, as if upset with the world
Calm and important, like a queen
m.w: She sits straight and still on a high throne. Calm and gold make her look majestic.

x.q: What new thing did Giotto do compared with earlier paintings?
o: His figures look solid and real
He painted everything only in gold
He made every figure flat, like icons
x.w: Before Giotto, figures were often flat, like on icons. His folds, shadows and throne look solid, as if you could touch them.

Q2016193.s: Giotto is called the father of European painting. He taught painted figures to stand on the ground and have weight.
Q2016193.i: Imagine what the angels whisper to each other by the throne.

f: Find the baby: bright light comes from him.
Look up: find the ring of angels in the bright sky.

m.q: What do the people around the baby feel?
m.w: Their faces glow in the baby's light. Everyone looks at him with tenderness and wonder.

x.q: What is the source of light in this picture?
o: A big lamp under the ceiling
It comes from the baby himself
The full moon shining in the window
x.w: The light comes from the infant and lights the faces around. It is a bold and beautiful idea by the painter.

Q1527541.s: Correggio loved soft light and tender faces. The picture is called 'The Night' for this glow in the dark.
Q1527541.i: Imagine a lullaby for the baby.

f: Find the young woman: she sits at a keyboard instrument and looks at us.
See how soft light falls on her face.

m.q: What is the face of the girl at the virginal like?
o: Cross, as if we disturbed her
Calm and friendly, she sees us
Sad, her eyes are full of tears
m.w: She has turned to us and looks straight at us without fear. It seems she has noticed us and is waiting.

x.q: What is a virginal?
x.w: A virginal has keys like a piano, but its strings are plucked. It is an instrument from the 1600s.

Q4660880.s: Vermeer left only about thirty-five paintings, all small. He loved quiet rooms and soft light.
Q4660880.i: Imagine what she says if we walk into the room.

f: Find the big flowers on her dress.
Find the mirror behind her: it shows her from the side.

m.q: What is her expression?
o: Calm, dreamy and a little proud
Cheerful, about to laugh out loud
m.w: She rests her head on her hand and looks slightly aside. Her pose is calm, as if lost in thought.

x.q: How long did Ingres work on this portrait?
x.w: Ingres began the portrait in 1844 and finished it in 1856. He tried very hard to make everything perfect.

Q3137278.s: Ingres loved smooth lines and shiny fabrics. He painted silk and flowers so well that you want to touch them.
Q3137278.i: Imagine what Madame Moitessier is thinking, resting her head on her hand.

f: Find the woman and the fan in her hands.
Look at the bright patterned background: what colours and patterns do you see?

m.q: What is the mood of this portrait?
o: Dreamy and calm, like a dream
Playful, like a game of tag
m.w: The woman looks thoughtful, and the bright patterns around her are like a beautiful dream.

x.q: What did Klimt love to add to his paintings?
x.w: Klimt decorated his pictures with rich ornaments, often with gold. That makes them look like carpets or mosaics.

Q106522623.s: This is one of Gustav Klimt's last paintings: he died in 1918. To the end of his life he painted women among bright patterns.
Q106522623.i: Imagine what party the woman with the fan is going to.

f: Find the dancing people: they whirl in the middle of the picture.
Find the bright red clothes: there are many.

m.q: What is the mood at this party?
m.w: People dance, hop and hold hands. You can see everyone is having a great time.

x.q: What celebration is shown?
o: A wedding party in the village
A Christmas party in the village
A royal ball in a big palace
x.w: The title says it: a wedding dance. Bruegel loved painting village celebrations.

Q3702434.s: Bruegel loved the parties of simple people: dances, weddings, fairs. He painted every figure with humour and care.
Q3702434.i: Invent the tune that the guests are dancing to.

f: Find the girl's big eyes: where do they look?
Find the dark clouds and the last light of sunset in the sky.

m.q: What does the girl feel?
o: Happy, ready to play a game
m.w: Her eyes are big and sad, and her shoulders droop. She is alone, and the sky is dark.

x.q: Why did Delacroix paint a twilight sky?
o: He was only able to work at night
The dark sky shows her sadness
He ran out of bright blue paint
x.w: The dark clouds and sunset match her feelings. That is how colour helps tell about mood.

Q3119110.s: Delacroix was a leader of Romanticism: he believed feelings and colour matter more than strict lines. His paintings are full of emotion.
Q3119110.i: Imagine who comes to the girl and what they say.

f: Find the big red turban on the man's head.
Find the words written on the picture's frame.

m.q: How does the man in the turban look at us?
o: Sleepy, about to shut his eyes
m.w: He looks out of the picture straight at us without blinking. His brows are slightly drawn together.

x.q: What does the motto 'Als ich can' on the frame mean?
x.w: It was the painter's motto: 'as I can', or 'as best I can'. It is also a play on his name.

Q2392901.s: Many think this is Jan van Eyck himself. He painted so finely in oil that every fold and wrinkle shows.
Q2392901.i: Imagine what he is thinking as he looks at us.

f: Find the embroidered signs on the sleeve: arrows, bees and flames.
Find the tilted hat and the curled moustache.

m.q: What is his expression?
o: Sad, as if about to cry
m.w: One eyebrow is slightly raised and the moustache curls up. He looks at us with a hint of mischief.

x.q: Is he really laughing?
o: Yes, he is roaring with laughter
No, he is only feeling bored
x.w: It is really a slight smile. People gave the picture the name 'Laughing Cavalier' many years later.

Q965124.s: Frans Hals painted with quick, lively strokes. The cavalier's sleeves are embroidered with signs of love: arrows, flames and bees.
Q965124.i: Imagine what joke he is smiling about.

f: Find the print of 'Olympia' on the wall and the Japanese screen.
Find the books on the desk and the feather pen in the inkwell.

m.q: What is Zola's mood?
m.w: He looks aside and does not notice us. You can see he is thinking of his own things.

x.q: Why are there so many pictures and books around Zola?
o: His study is a small bookshop
They show what Zola likes best
He had no time to tidy up
x.w: Zola wrote in defence of Manet's paintings. Manet put around him things they both liked: books, prints and 'Olympia'.

Q2529703.s: Émile Zola was a famous French writer. He boldly wrote in a newspaper that Manet's pictures were good, when many critics attacked them.
Q2529703.i: Imagine what Zola is about to write.

f: Find King Stanisław August among the crowd.
Find the people who are cheering and waving hats and handkerchiefs.

m.q: What do the people feel?
o: Fear, they hide and run away
Boredom, they yawn and drift off
m.w: People smile, wave their arms and congratulate each other. It is a celebration and a time of great hope.

x.q: What is a constitution?
o: A festive cake with a flag
A building plan for a palace
The main law of a country
x.w: A constitution is a country's main law. Poland adopted one on 3 May 1791, one of the first in the world.

Q4231515.s: Jan Matejko painted this for the 100th anniversary of that day, in 1891. He painted huge pictures of Polish history so that people would remember it.
Q4231515.i: Imagine the main rule you would write for your own family.

f: Find the two women walking along the garden path.
Find the bright flowers against the dark green background.

m.q: What is the mood in this garden?
o: Quiet and dreamy, like a memory
m.w: The women walk slowly, and the flowers and path curve like in a dream. Everything is soft and calm.

x.q: Why is the picture called 'Memory of the Garden'?
o: It is a garden that never existed
He painted it on the spot, from life
x.w: Van Gogh lived in Arles, but remembered the garden in Etten where his parents lived. He said the two women were his mother and sister.

Q4126322.s: Van Gogh chose colours and lines by feeling, not only by how things look. That is why the path and flowers curve and the colours are bright.
Q4126322.i: Imagine what the two women are talking about in the garden.

f: Find the angel swooping in from above.
Find Mary: she bows her head and crosses her arms on her chest.

m.q: What does Mary feel?
o: Loud joy, she wants to dance
Anger, she is cross with him
m.w: Her head is bowed and her arms are folded on her chest. She listens to the angel quietly and carefully.

x.q: Where does the light in the picture come from?
o: From above, from a big lamp
From the side, like a spotlight
From below, from a tiny candle
x.w: Light strikes out of the darkness from one side, like a spotlight. The figures flare with light and the rest sinks into shadow.

Q1448728.s: Caravaggio became famous for sharp contrast of light and shadow, like a stage in a theatre. This is called 'tenebrism'.
Q1448728.i: Imagine what the angel told her.

f: Look at his hands: they rest confidently on his knees.
Find the white collar, the necktie and the waistcoat.

m.q: What does Monsieur Bertin look like?
o: Timid, and rather shy of us
Sleepy, as if he just woke up
m.w: He sits heavily and firmly, with broad shoulders. His gaze is direct, like a man used to making decisions.

x.q: Who was Bertin?
o: The captain of a big ship
A musician in a royal band
The owner of a big newspaper
x.w: Louis-François Bertin owned a big Paris newspaper. Many people listened to what he said.

Q2985455.s: They say Ingres could not find the pose for a long time. Then he saw Bertin sitting with his hands on his knees and knew at once how to paint him.
Q2985455.i: Imagine what news he has just read in his paper.

f: Find the smiling faces of the musicians.
Find the bread and the glass of wine on the table.

m.q: What is the mood in the tavern?
m.w: The faces smile and the eyes sparkle. You can see the friends are having a great time.

x.q: What was unusual about this picture for its time?
o: Ordinary people, painted as they are
A grand portrait of a crowned king
There are no people, only the food
x.w: Back then, saints and kings were painted more often. Young Velázquez painted ordinary people and food on the table very truthfully.

Q389198.s: Velázquez was about nineteen when he painted this. Later he became the court painter to the King of Spain.
Q389198.i: Imagine the merry song they are singing.

f: Find the huge wine barrel and the people around it.
Find the people holding mugs.

m.q: What is the mood at the festival?
o: Noisy and merry, the crowd cheers
Quiet and sad, all standing silent
Sleepy, all dozing by the barrel
m.w: There are many people, standing close around the barrel. You can see everyone has been waiting for the feast.

x.q: What is Saint Martin known for?
o: Building a bridge over a big river
Giving half his cloak to a beggar
Winning many battles for the king
x.w: Saint Martin shared his cloak with a freezing beggar. On his day, 11 November, people tasted the new wine.

Q1198007.s: Bruegel loved painting big merry crowds. He painted this one in water-based paint on thin linen.
Q1198007.i: Imagine what the smells are like at this feast.

f: Find the cardinal's red hat and red cape.
Find his eyes: what is their look?

m.q: What is the cardinal's gaze like?
o: Sleepy, as if just woken up
m.w: His eyes are narrow and sharp, as if he notices everything. There is no smile on his face.

x.q: Who is a cardinal?
o: The head of the royal guard
The chief cook at the palace
A top leader in the church
x.w: A cardinal is a high church official. Red clothes were his sign.

Q2535563.s: Nobody knows for certain who this man is, but Raphael made him look very alive. You can read his character in his face.
Q2535563.i: Imagine what the cardinal thinks as he looks at us.

f: Find the thick curving roots: they twist together like snakes.
Find the light patches of yellow, orange and green.

m.q: What is the mood of these roots?
o: Sleepy, as if the roots are napping
Alive, as if the roots are moving
m.w: The roots wriggle in every direction. The strokes are quick, and everything seems to move.

x.q: What is missing from the picture?
o: A path and a fence far away
x.w: Van Gogh filled the whole picture with roots and trunks. There is no sky at the top, which makes them look huge.

Q4233325.s: This is one of Van Gogh's last paintings: he painted it in 1890 in Auvers. His roots almost dance.
Q4233325.i: Imagine what the roots look like: snakes or giant hands?

f: Find the white horse tied to a post.
Find the red seals: collectors stamped them.

m.q: What is this horse's character?
o: Fiery and strong, tugging his rope
Sleepy and lazy, dozing on his feet
Timid and shy, pressing to the post
m.w: The horse has tossed his head, tensed his legs and pulled the rope tight. You can see he is full of strength.

x.q: Whose favourite horse was this?
x.w: This was the favourite horse of Emperor Xuanzong. His name was 'Night-Shining White'.

Q28092249.s: The painting is over a thousand years old and is made with ink on paper. The red seals are marks of collectors who kept it.
Q28092249.i: Imagine where the horse would gallop if he were untied.

f: Find the hands clutching the hair.
Find the wide-open eyes.

m.q: What does the painter's face show?
o: Boredom and a wish to doze off
m.w: His eyes are wide open and his hands clutch his hair. He seems to have seen something terrifying or astonishing.

x.q: Who is in the picture?
x.w: It is a self-portrait: Courbet painted himself. He often painted himself in different roles, as if acting in front of a mirror.

Q3222585.s: Courbet painted this when he was very young. Later he became a famous realist and painted ordinary life.
Q3222585.i: Imagine what has surprised or frightened the painter so much.

f: Find the bowl in the sorceress's hand: she pours something into the water.
Look at the colour of the sea: what shades of green and blue do you see?

m.q: What does Circe feel?
m.w: Her brows are drawn together and her gaze is sharp. She wants to cast a spell on her rival.

x.q: What does the Latin word 'Invidiosa' in the title mean?
x.w: 'Invidiosa' means 'envious'. In the myth, Circe was jealous of her rival and angry at her.

Q5121363.s: John William Waterhouse loved the heroines of myths and legends. He painted them in detail and bright colour, in the Pre-Raphaelite spirit.
Q5121363.i: Invent the spell that Circe whispers.

f: Find the low sun in the middle and the sparkles on the water.
Find the big buildings and the ships in the harbour.

m.q: What is the mood of this golden light over the city?
o: Uneasy and dark, like deep night
Sad and grey, like a rainy day
m.w: Golden light floods the city and the water. It feels as if the day has just begun and lots of good lies ahead.

x.q: What are the people building in this picture?
o: A royal castle by the sea
A stone bridge over a river
x.w: In the myth, Dido founded the city of Carthage. Turner painted it being built in golden light.

Q3027255.s: Turner asked in his will for this painting to hang next to pictures by his favourite painter, Claude Lorrain. They still hang side by side in the National Gallery in London.
Q3027255.i: Imagine what Carthage will look like when it is finished.

f: Find the cross on the top of the mountain.
Find the dark fir trees and the sunset rays spreading across the sky.

m.q: What is the mood of these mountains?
o: Noisy and merry, like a fair
m.w: The mountains are silent, the firs stand still and the sky glows. You want to speak in a whisper.

x.q: What was unusual about this picture for an altar?
o: It is painted in pure gold
It is as small as a postcard
x.w: Altars were usually decorated with people and saints. Friedrich painted mountains, firs and a sunset, with the cross standing in nature. Many people were surprised.

Q884782.s: Friedrich designed the golden frame himself. It is carved with ears of wheat, grapes and little angel heads.
Q884782.i: Imagine who will climb up this mountain.

f: Find Mary on the high throne and, below, the soldier in shining armour with a banner.
Find the calm landscape with a little town behind them.

m.q: What is Mary like on her high throne?
m.w: Her head is bowed and her gaze lowered. She seems far from the noise, as if thinking about something important.

x.q: What new thing did Giorgione add to an altarpiece?
o: Lots of gold around the saints
x.w: Earlier, there was often a golden background behind Mary. Giorgione shows a quiet landscape with sky and soft mist.

Q1720631.s: Giorgione lived only about thirty-three years, and just a few of his paintings survive. He is famous for soft colours and misty landscapes.
Q1720631.i: Imagine what Mary is thinking as she looks down.

f: Find the two babies: one with Mary, the other is little John.
Find the carnation flower near the children.

m.q: How does Mary look at the children?
o: Gentle, she looks at them lovingly
Strict, she is frowning at them
Tired, she is nearly falling asleep
m.w: Mary holds the baby and looks at the children lovingly. It is quiet, with soft light.

x.q: Who is the second baby in the picture?
o: Baby John, the cousin of Jesus
A neighbour's boy from the village
x.w: It is John the Baptist, who will grow up to be a preacher. The children are friends, and Raphael loved to paint them together.

Q2503581.s: Raphael learned from Leonardo how to make pictures calm and harmonious. He placed Mary and the children in the shape of a triangle.
Q2503581.i: Imagine what the babies say to each other.

f: Find the boy in the bright red suit.
Find the magpie on a string and the cage with little birds.

m.q: What does the boy look like?
o: Tearful, about to burst into crying
Calm and serious, like a grown-up
m.w: The boy stands straight and looks at us calmly. He is not afraid and not noisy.

x.q: What are the cats in the shadows planning?
o: To play a game with the boy
To sleep in the warm shade
x.w: Three cats stare at the birds without blinking. They seem to wait for the moment to pounce.

Q3035829.s: In its beak the magpie holds a card with Goya's name. It is Goya's playful way of signing the portrait.
Q3035829.i: Imagine how the boy will save the little birds from the cats.

f: Find the red-orange glow of sunset near the horizon.
Find the wisp of smoke from the bonfire of leaves.

m.q: What is the mood of this autumn evening?
o: Merry, like a big children's party
Quiet, a little sad and dreamy
m.w: It is getting dark and the girls are silent. An autumn evening is hushed and a little wistful.

x.q: What are the girls doing?
o: Raking leaves into a pile to burn
Playing catch on the lawn at home
x.w: In autumn, people raked leaves into heaps and burned them. The girls are busy with this quiet job.

Q4148585.s: Millais thought twilight was the most poetic time of day. He tried to capture the pink-gold sky and the quiet light.
Q4148585.i: Imagine what the girls talk about as it gets dark.

f: Find the paper lantern hanging above the table.
Find the carafe on the white tablecloth and see how light and shade fall on it.

m.q: What is the mood of this company?
o: Uneasy, all waiting for a storm
m.w: People sit together at the table and are in no hurry. You can see they enjoy chatting in the shade.

x.q: What did the painter especially love to show in this picture?
o: Only the sharp outlines of people
Light and shade among the leaves
A dark night with stars above
x.w: Sunlight breaking through leaves falls in patches on the table and dresses. Gierymski loved to paint such lively light.

Q23688702.s: Aleksander Gierymski was a Polish painter who loved light: sun, shade and evening lamps. In Polish the picture is called 'Altana', which means an arbour.
Q23688702.i: Imagine what the people in the arbour are talking about.

f: Find the big round eyes and the open mouth.
Find the spread wings and the curly hair.

m.q: What does the angel look like?
o: Merry, laughing with a wide mouth
m.w: The eyes are huge, the mouth is slightly open and the wings are spread. He seems to have seen something important.

x.q: How did Klee paint the angel?
o: With simple shapes, like a child
x.w: Klee loved children's drawings and learned simplicity from them. That is why the angel looks funny and touching.

Q537640.s: This picture is quite small, just a little bigger than a school exercise-book page. The philosopher Walter Benjamin bought it and hung it in his home, because he loved this angel.
Q537640.i: Imagine what the angel wants to tell us.

f: Find the blossoming trees with white and pink flowers in the front.
Find the town of Arles far away.

m.q: What is the mood of this spring day?
m.w: The trees are in bloom, the sky is bright and the colours are vivid. It feels as if spring has woken up.

x.q: What season did Van Gogh show?
o: Autumn, when the leaves turn gold
x.w: Fruit trees are blooming, so it is spring. Van Gogh painted this in Arles in April.

Q3314658.s: In Arles Van Gogh discovered bright southern light and pure colours. He lived there for more than a year and painted many pictures.
Q3314658.i: Imagine where you would walk on this spring day.

f: Find Mary Magdalene with long hair: she reaches towards Jesus.
Find the sheep and the houses on the hill far away.

m.q: What does Magdalene feel?
o: Boredom, she does not care much
Anger, she turns away from him
m.w: She has knelt down and reaches towards Jesus. She did not recognise him at first, and now she is very happy.

x.q: What do the Latin words 'Noli me tangere' mean?
x.w: According to the Gospel, that is what Jesus said to Magdalene. He stopped her when she wanted to come close.

Q3877895.s: Titian painted a wide landscape with hills, sheep and sky. He was still young, but he already knew how to paint rich colours and living light.
Q3877895.i: Imagine what Magdalene tells her friends.

f: Find the woman in a hat with a parasol.
Find the man leaning towards her, and the green plants around.

m.q: What is the mood of this couple?
m.w: Each looks in their own direction and is silent. Both seem lost in their own thoughts.

x.q: Where does the scene happen?
o: On a ship, in a big cabin
In a forest, on a quiet glade
x.w: A conservatory is a glassed-in garden where plants grow in winter. People could stroll and relax there.

Q481454.s: Manet loved painting Parisians at leisure, on walks and at rest.
Q481454.i: Imagine what they are quietly saying.

f: Find old Jacob in bed: his hands rest on his grandsons' heads.
Find the warm golden light falling on the faces.

m.q: What is the mood of this blessing?
o: Angry, everyone argues by the bed
m.w: People stand quietly with heads bowed. The golden light makes the scene warm.

x.q: What unusual thing does Jacob do?
o: Puts his right hand on the younger
x.w: Usually the eldest got the main blessing. Jacob chose the younger boy, and the boys' father was surprised.

Q1679544.s: Rembrandt painted warm golden light in a dark room, and the faces seem alive. In old age he painted especially softly and deeply.
Q1679544.i: Imagine what the grandfather wished for the boys.

f: Find the lovely flowers and butterflies on the dark background.
Find the princess's high forehead and hairstyle.

m.q: What is the princess's face like?
m.w: She sits straight and looks aside. Her face is calm, as if thinking of something important.

x.q: Why is the princess painted from the side, in profile?
o: Profile was in fashion, like on coins
The princess felt shy and turned away
It was simply easier for the painter
x.w: Profile was fashionable in portraits and medals. Pisanello was a famous maker of medals.

Q2478403.s: Nobody knows for sure who the princess is: perhaps Ginevra d'Este. Pisanello painted flowers and butterflies very finely, like in a picture book.
Q2478403.i: Invent a name for the butterfly and where it will fly.

f: Find Homer in the centre: he sits in front of a temple.
Find the winged woman crowning him with a laurel wreath.

m.q: What is Homer's mood?
o: Sleepy, as if he dozed off
m.w: He sits straight and still, and it is quiet around him. Everything speaks of honour and respect.

x.q: Who was Homer?
o: A Roman emperor and brave general
A French painter and a sculptor
x.w: Homer composed poems about the Trojan War and Odysseus's journey. People have been reading them for thousands of years.

Q3202169.s: Ingres gathered great people of different centuries in one picture: ancient Greeks and French writers like Molière and Racine. It shows how art joins people across time.
Q3202169.i: Imagine what story Homer tells his guests.

f: Find the teacher with a long stick.
Find the mirror on the wall and the dancers in white dresses.

m.q: What do the dancers feel?
m.w: The girls stand, sit and adjust their dresses. You can see it is ordinary work, not a party.

x.q: What is unusual about this picture?
o: A stage with lights and applause
A royal ball with music and gowns
It is a rehearsal, not a show
x.w: Degas painted what is usually hidden: how dancers practise and rest. The audience never sees this.

Q3821820.s: Degas painted hundreds of pictures about ballet. He liked to catch ordinary movements when nobody is posing.
Q3821820.i: Imagine what the teacher says to the dancers.

f: Find the fly on the frame at the bottom of the picture.
Find the monk's white robe and the stubble on his face.

m.q: What does the monk look like?
o: Merry, about to laugh out loud
m.w: He looks straight out and his face is soft and quiet. You can see he is used to silence.

x.q: What is painted on the frame?
x.w: The fly is painted so well that it looks real. This trick is called trompe l'oeil, or 'fooling the eye'.

Q7232319.s: Carthusians are monks who live quietly and speak little. Petrus Christus painted stubble and shadows so well that the monk seems alive.
Q7232319.i: Give the fly a name and say where it is flying.

f: Find the row of tall trees with golden and orange leaves.
Find the stone tombs along the avenue and the tiny people strolling.

m.q: What is the mood of this autumn walk?
o: Warm and calm, like an autumn walk
Uneasy and dark, like a storm
Noisy, like a busy city market
m.w: The leaves are golden, the light is soft and people are in no hurry. It feels as if autumn has stood still.

x.q: What is Alyscamps?
o: An old royal palace in Arles
An old avenue with stone coffins
A wide river that runs through Arles
x.w: It is an ancient place near the town of Arles with stone coffins. Now it is a quiet avenue for walks.

Q4924524.s: Van Gogh painted Alyscamps in autumn 1888 in Arles, with Gauguin working beside him. He loved oranges and yellows, which glow brightly.
Q4924524.i: Imagine what the people strolling along the avenue are talking about.

f: Find the orange-red crab: it lies on its back.
Find the claws and legs sticking up.

m.q: How does the crab seem?
o: Fierce, as if it will pinch you
Helpless, with legs in the air
m.w: The crab is upside down and cannot get up. Its legs dangle in the air, which is a little funny.

x.q: What influenced Van Gogh when he painted the crab?
o: Old maps of far seas and lands
x.w: In Paris Van Gogh collected Japanese prints and loved their bright colours and bold shapes. You can see it in the crab too.

Q17511613.s: Van Gogh liked to put opposite colours side by side, such as orange and blue. That makes both colours glow brighter.
Q17511613.i: Imagine how the crab will turn over and where it will scuttle.

f: Find the tall Gothic church with arches in the middle of the picture.
Find the angels holding scrolls in different colours.

m.q: What is the mood in the middle of the picture?
o: Noisy and merry, like a bazaar
Quiet and sad, by the cross
m.w: People stand silently with heads bowed. Everything around is solemn and quiet.

x.q: What are the seven sacraments?
o: Seven big paintings for a church
x.w: Sacraments are important church ceremonies: baptism, marriage and others. Each one is shown in its own part of the church.

Q434461.s: Rogier van der Weyden painted a church of his own time and dressed people in clothes of his day. It all looks as if it is happening right now.
Q434461.i: Imagine what one of the angels is quietly telling.

f: Find the calm face of Jesus.
Find the crowd of faces around: they are pressed tightly together.

m.q: How does Jesus look against the crowd?
o: Quiet and calm in all the noise
m.w: Around him are many harsh, noisy faces, but he looks quiet. His calm stands out.

x.q: How did Bosch show the difference between Jesus and the crowd?
o: Crowd faces rough, Jesus's face soft
He painted all the faces the same
He painted Jesus very, very tiny
x.w: The crowd's faces are grotesque and angry, like masks, while the face of Jesus is lighter and gentler. That shows who matters most here.

Q2328603.s: Bosch painted strange faces and fantastic creatures, so his pictures cannot be mistaken for anyone else's. He lived in the Dutch town of 's-Hertogenbosch.
Q2328603.i: Imagine a kind word you could say to him.

f: Find her big dark eyes.
Find her earrings and the river and trees behind her.

m.q: What is her face like?
o: Sad, with tears in her eyes
m.w: Her gaze is kind and the corners of her lips lift slightly. She looks gentle and modest.

x.q: How old is the girl in the portrait?
x.w: Caroline Rivière was about thirteen. Ingres painted her very young.

Q24011.s: Ingres loved smooth, flowing lines and tender colours. He painted this portrait when he was young, about twenty-five.
Q24011.i: Imagine what Caroline is thinking about.

f: Find the red cloth: it is the brightest patch in the picture.
See how light falls from the side onto the saint's face and shoulders.

m.q: What does Saint Jerome feel?
o: Angry, as if cross with someone
m.w: He bows quietly and his gaze is serious. He is thinking and praying.

x.q: From which side does light fall on the saint?
o: From above, through a roof window
From the side, like a spotlight
x.w: Light picks the figure and the red cloth out of the dark. Everything else stays in shadow.

Q626791.s: Caravaggio painted as if he had switched on a spotlight in a dark room. This strong light from one side is easy to recognise.
Q626791.i: Imagine what Jerome is quietly praying.

f: Find the white collar and the dark clothes of the friar.
Find the book and the armchair.

m.q: What does the friar seem like from his gaze?
o: Sleepy, about to give a yawn
m.w: His eyes are big and lively, and he looks closely. You can see he is a man who reads and thinks a lot.

x.q: Who was Paravicino?
o: A priest and poet, El Greco's friend
The King of Spain, who loved art
A sailor who sailed to far lands
x.w: Ortensio Paravicino was a priest, preacher and poet. He was a friend of El Greco.

Q949323.s: Paravicino wrote a poem in honour of El Greco. El Greco liked to paint people long and slender, with lively eyes.
Q949323.i: Imagine what he is reading and thinking about.

f: Find the spoon, the bowl of beans and the bread on the table.
Find the glass of wine nearby.

m.q: What is his mood?
o: Busy with his food, enjoying it
Sad, he does not want to eat
m.w: His mouth is open and the spoon is at his lips. He looks at us as if about to speak. You can tell the food is tasty.

x.q: Whom did Carracci choose as the hero of the picture?
o: A king in a golden crown
A saint with a golden halo
x.w: Carracci painted an ordinary man with an ordinary meal. This was rare then; painters usually showed saints and noble people.

Q1232131.s: Annibale Carracci, with his brother and cousin, founded an art school in Bologna. He taught drawing from real life, lively and simple.
Q1232131.i: Imagine what the man says when he looks up from his plate.

f: Find the garlands of fruit hanging from above.
Find Mary with the baby on the throne and the angels at her feet.

m.q: What is the mood of this altarpiece?
m.w: The figures stand calmly and majestically, and gold and fruit add a festive touch.

x.q: What new idea did Mantegna have?
o: Painted everything on a golden background
Made all the figures flat, like icons
Painted columns that continue the frame
x.w: The painted columns look like a continuation of the real frame. It seems you could step inside, like into a hall.

Q2066739.s: Mantegna adored ancient Rome and painted figures like stone statues. He painted folds, stone and marble very exactly.
Q2066739.i: Invent the song the angels are singing.

f: Find the apple in the young man's hand.
Find the river and mountains behind him.

m.q: What is the face of the young man with the apple like?
o: Sad, with tears in his eyes
m.w: He looks straight at us. His face is soft and open.

x.q: What is behind the young man?
o: A calm landscape, river and hills
A dark wall and a heavy curtain
A big city with tall towers
x.w: Behind him opens a quiet landscape. Leonardo also liked to paint people against nature, and Raphael learned from him.

Q2713823.s: Raphael painted this portrait very young, around twenty. Nobody knows for sure who the young man is: maybe Francesco Maria della Rovere.
Q2713823.i: Imagine whom the young man wants to give the apple to.

f: Find the dancers kicking up their legs together.
Find the musicians at the bottom, and see how the lines race upward.

m.q: What is the mood of this dance?
m.w: The dancers' legs fly up in time and their faces smile. You can almost hear the music.

x.q: How did Seurat paint this picture?
o: With tiny dots of pure paint
With thin lines of black pencil
x.w: Seurat put tiny coloured dots side by side. From far away they blend into one colour, and the picture seems to shimmer.

Q3835761.s: Seurat believed that lines going upward make a picture cheerful. Here the dancers' legs and the lines in the background all go up.
Q3835761.i: Invent the music for this cancan.

f: Find the fur hat and the red clothes of the rider.
Find the arrows in the quiver and the castle on the hill far away.

m.q: What is the rider's mood?
o: Sleepy, about to doze in the saddle
