m.w: A hand on his hip, a sideways glance. He rides boldly forward and notices everything.

x.q: What do people know about the rider?
o: He is a famous Polish king
He is Rembrandt himself in costume
Nobody knows for sure who he is
x.w: The rider's name remains a mystery. Experts argue about who he is: a young warrior or a hero from a story.

Q3663892.s: Rembrandt painted a bright rider against a dark landscape. This contrast of light and shadow makes the picture mysterious.
Q3663892.i: Imagine where the rider is galloping and why.

f: Find the little prince with a baton in his hand.
Find the person beside him with a rattle and an apple.

m.q: What does the little prince look like?
o: Serious and proud, like a grown-up
m.w: He stands straight and holds the baton like a real commander. The little boy tries hard to look important.

x.q: How old is the prince in the picture?
x.w: Balthasar Charles was about two years old. The grown-up costume and baton make him look like a tiny commander.

Q3138273.s: Velázquez was court painter to King Philip IV of Spain. He often painted the royal children and courtiers.
Q3138273.i: Imagine what the prince and his friend will play.

f: Find the basket of apples and the bottle.
Find the plate of biscuits and the folds of the tablecloth.

m.q: What is the mood of this still life?
m.w: The things stand still and nobody makes a sound. The apples and cloth look heavy and peaceful.

x.q: What is unusual about how the table and objects are painted?
o: All of it is exactly like a photo
The table and bottle seem tilted
All of it is painted in thick fog
x.w: Cézanne looked at objects from several viewpoints at once. That is why the table edges do not match and the bottle seems to lean.

Q3956440.s: They say Cézanne dreamed of astonishing Paris with a single apple. He painted apples in very simple, solid shapes.
Q3956440.i: Imagine what you would cook from these apples.

f: Find the girl in the white dress in the middle of the field.
Find the tall grass and the ears of wheat around her.

m.q: What is the mood of this field?
o: Calm and bright, like a summer day
Noisy, like a busy building site
m.w: The girl stands calmly, the grass sways around her, and the colours are light and soft.

x.q: What kind of strokes did Van Gogh use for the grass around the girl?
x.w: Van Gogh painted with thick, short strokes, and the field seems alive. That is why the grass seems to sway.

Q5564475.s: Van Gogh painted this in Auvers in 1890. In his last two months or so there he made around seventy paintings.
Q5564475.i: Imagine the girl's name and what she is doing in the field.

f: Find the pale greenish face of the man in the foreground.
Find the couple in the garden far behind.

m.q: What does the man in the foreground feel?
o: Joy, he is happy for the couple
Calm, he does not mind at all
Jealousy, he is hurt and anxious
m.w: His face is pale and his eyes are wide and gloomy. Behind him in the distance is a couple, and it hurts him.

x.q: How did Munch show the feeling of jealousy?
o: With colour and a face, not words
He painted a big black thunderstorm
x.w: Munch painted feelings: the pale face and huge eyes tell of jealousy. No words are needed.

Q16939042.s: Edvard Munch was a Norwegian painter, the author of 'The Scream'. He painted not things but feelings: fear, love, jealousy.
Q16939042.i: Imagine what could help this man stop feeling sad.

f: Find the saint's white beard.
Look at his face: how many wrinkles the painter drew!

m.q: What is the mood in the saint's room?
m.w: The old man looks calm and focused. It is as quiet as a scholar's study.

x.q: Who posed for Dürer's Saint Jerome?
o: His younger brother, still a boy
A very old man, about ninety
A rich merchant from next door
x.w: In Antwerp Dürer met a 93-year-old man and drew his face. Later he painted the saint from that drawing.

Q1989202.s: Dürer was a German master of the tiniest details: he drew every hair and wrinkle. His prints and paintings are studied with a magnifying glass.
Q1989202.i: Imagine what book the saint is reading.

f: Find the big family in the shade of the chestnut tree: everyone looks at us.
Find the painter himself: he painted himself into the picture.

m.q: What is the family's mood?
m.w: Everyone sits and stands quietly, as before a photograph. It is a peaceful family day.

x.q: What is unusual about how this picture is painted?
o: Family outdoors, in patches of sun
Everybody is painted in black paint
It was painted at night by candle
x.w: Bazille painted people outdoors, in patches of sun and the shade of leaves. The future Impressionists loved painting this way.

Q325981.s: Frédéric Bazille was a friend of Monet and Renoir. He painted his own family on the terrace of their house near Montpellier.
Q325981.i: Imagine what the family was talking about before they froze for the picture.

f: Find the king in golden armour: he sits low.
Find the girl in a simple dress above him, on the steps of the throne.

m.q: What does the king feel?
m.w: The king sits lower and looks up at the girl. His gaze is gentle and respectful.

x.q: What is unusual about where the king and the girl sit?
o: The king sits highest on his throne
The king sits lower than the girl
They both stand back to back
x.w: Normally kings sit above everyone. Here the king bows before a poor girl because he has fallen in love with her.

Q6411359.s: Edward Burne-Jones loved old tales and legends. He painted them dreamily in golds and blues, like a dream.
Q6411359.i: Imagine what the king says to the girl.

f: Find Mary in the centre: her robes billow in waves.
Find the angels around her: there are many.

m.q: How does Mary look in the glow?
o: Noisy and merry, like a fair
Quiet and humble, all in light
m.w: Mary is calm and humble, with light shining around her. Angels surround her.

x.q: Why are the figures in the picture so stretched out?
o: The canvas got stretched out of shape
The painter could not draw very well
El Greco liked long, flame-like figures
x.w: El Greco lengthened figures to make them seem light and rising upward. It was his signature trick.

Q5966323.s: El Greco painted for Spanish churches, and his colours burned bright and strange. He loved dramatic light and swirling clouds.

f: Find the riders on horses: they ride in a line.
Find the colourful hats and rich clothes of the judges.

m.q: What is the mood of this procession?
o: Uneasy, as if in a hurry
m.w: The riders ride slowly and with dignity. Everything around is quiet and beautiful, like a solemn procession.

x.q: What happened to this panel of the altarpiece?
o: It was stolen in 1934, never found
Mice ate it in an old church cellar
It went to a king as a gift
x.w: The real panel vanished, and a copy hangs in its place. Nobody has ever found out where it is.

Q2157202.s: The Ghent Altarpiece was painted by the brothers Jan and Hubert van Eyck. They were masters of oil paint: even jewels and fabrics sparkle like real ones.
Q2157202.i: Imagine where these riders are going.

f: Find the yellow straw hat.
Find the pipe, the bottle and the clay pot.

m.q: What is the mood of this still life with a hat?
o: Quiet and simple, like a calm home
Merry and noisy, like a big feast
Uneasy, like just before a storm
m.w: The things lie plainly and quietly. There is nothing festive about them, but they feel warm and alive.

x.q: What objects did Van Gogh like to paint in still lifes?
o: Simple things: shoes, a hat, a pipe
Only flowers in big fancy vases
x.w: Van Gogh painted what was at hand: shoes, a hat, a pipe. He found beauty in simple things.

Q7617094.s: Van Gogh painted this in Nuenen, where he worked in dark, earthy colours. Bright colours came later, in the south of France.
Q7617094.i: Imagine whose hat this is and where its owner is.

f: Find the fan in the lady's hands.
Look at her calm, direct gaze.

m.q: What does the lady look like?
o: Shy, she is hiding her eyes
Proud, calm and sure of herself
Sleepy, she is about to yawn
m.w: She holds herself straight and looks straight at us. There is no fear in her gaze.

x.q: What was a fan for?
o: To play music, like a guitar
To catch flies and little moths
To cool oneself, and for style
x.w: In hot weather people fanned themselves, and a fan was also a fashionable accessory. The lady holds it as a sign of taste.

Q1211943.s: Up close Velázquez's strokes look like bold patches, but from a distance they turn into real fabric and skin. That is why his pictures are best seen from afar.
Q1211943.i: Imagine where the lady is going and what she whispers behind her fan.

f: On the left find Mary with the child, on the right the young man at prayer.
Find the windows with a view of a garden or field.

m.q: What is the mood of these two panels?
o: Noisy and hurried, like a market
Quiet and prayerful, like a church
m.w: Mary and the young man are still and quiet. Everything around is silent, like in a church.

x.q: What is a diptych?
o: A picture of two panels, like a book
A picture in ten parts, like a puzzle
A huge painting on a church wall
x.w: A diptych is two joined panels. They can be opened and closed like a book. Together they tell one story.

Q2711706.s: Maarten van Nieuwenhove is twenty-three in the picture, and it says so on the frame. Hans Memling painted faces and objects very finely.
Q2711706.i: Imagine what Maarten is praying about.

f: Find the soap bubble the boy is looking at.
Find his curly hair and the velvet suit with a lace collar.

m.q: What does the boy feel?
o: Boredom, he is tired of the game
m.w: He looks up with wide-open eyes. The bubble seems magical to him.

x.q: How was this picture used later?
x.w: A soap company bought the picture and made a famous advertisement out of it. That is how the whole world got to know it.

Q4147036.s: The boy was William, the painter's grandson. Millais first called the picture 'A Child's World'.
Q4147036.i: Imagine what the boy is thinking as he looks at the bubble.

f: Find the girl's hat and dress.
Find the stones on the beach and the sea in the distance.

m.q: What is the mood of this shore?
o: Noisy, like a crowded beach party
Quiet and dreamy, like a dream
m.w: The girl by the sea is in no hurry. Everything around is quiet, like in a dream.

x.q: Who is Inger in this picture?
o: A friend of the Queen of Norway
A neighbour girl from the village
x.w: Inger is the painter's younger sister. Munch often painted people close to him.

Q18748731.s: Edvard Munch was born in Norway and loved the northern sea and shore. Later he painted the famous 'Scream'.
Q18748731.i: Imagine what Inger is thinking as she looks at the sea.

f: Find the boyarina in black: she sits in the sleigh and raises a hand with two fingers.
Find the barefoot man in ragged clothes sitting in the snow, and the crowd of people.

m.q: What is the boyarina like?
o: Brave and firm, her eyes burn
Merry, she is about to dance
Sleepy, she is about to doze off
m.w: Her face is pale, her eyes burn and her hand is raised high. She is not afraid and stays true to her beliefs.

x.q: How did Surikov show the winter air?
o: Pure white snow, with no shades
Snow with blue and lilac shadows
Only grey paint, with no other colours
x.w: Surikov's snow is not just white: it has blue and lilac shadows and sleigh tracks. That is why you almost feel the frost.

Q4095553.s: Surikov painted snow and people's faces from life, making many studies. He was born in Siberia, in Krasnoyarsk, and loved bright, lively crowds.
Q4095553.i: Imagine what the people in the crowd say to each other.

f: Find the stone bridge with an arch and the river.
Find the dark clouds and the bright light falling on the land.

m.q: What is the mood of this landscape?
m.w: Dark clouds hang over the land while sharp light falls on the fields. It feels as if a storm is about to hit.

x.q: What most attracts the eye?
o: Lots of tiny people on the road
A pretty golden frame around it
x.w: Light and shadow clash, and that makes the picture feel alive and dramatic. Rembrandt loved such contrasts.

Q4211284.s: Rembrandt painted only a few landscapes, mostly painting people. But even in a landscape he remained a master of light and shadow.
Q4211284.i: Imagine who is walking across the bridge and where to.

f: Find the donkey carrying Mary and the baby.
Find the quiet river and the hills far away.

m.q: What is the mood of this journey?
o: Noisy and merry, like a fair day
Quiet and peaceful, like a walk
m.w: It is a quiet morning, the light is soft and the landscape is calm. The travellers walk without hurry.

x.q: What is more important in the picture: the people or the landscape?
o: The people, the scenery is minor
Only the sky, with hardly any land
x.w: The people are quite small among hills, rivers and trees. Such a picture is called a 'historical landscape'.

Q1115595.s: Annibale Carracci loved ideal landscapes, beautiful and calm. They later inspired Poussin and Claude Lorrain, masters of such pictures.
Q1115595.i: Imagine what Mary sings to the baby on the way.

f: Find the man in the centre standing on a table and reading the oath.
Find the white curtains billowing in the wind by the big windows.

m.q: What do the people in the hall feel?
o: Boredom, everyone wants to go home
Fear, everyone wants to run away
m.w: Hands reach up and people look in one direction. You can see they have decided to do something together.

x.q: What do the people promise in the oath?
o: To build a beautiful new palace
Not to part without a constitution
To eat a festive dinner together
x.w: The deputies swore not to disperse until they had given France a constitution, the main rules of the country.

Q3227124.s: David planned a huge painting but never finished it. A large sketch survives, with wind in the curtains and raised hands.
Q3227124.i: Imagine a promise the whole family could make together.

f: Find the dark beret and the brightest spot in the picture: the face.
Look at the thick brushstrokes on the forehead and cheeks.

m.q: What are Rembrandt's eyes like?
m.w: There are wrinkles around the eyes, but the gaze is soft and honest. He seems to look into your soul.

x.q: How many self-portraits did Rembrandt make?
o: Only two or three in all
About ten or twelve in all
x.w: Rembrandt portrayed himself all his life, from youth to old age. That is how we see how he changed.

Q3630743.s: Rembrandt did not flatter himself: he painted wrinkles, eye bags and a soft nose. This honesty and the warm golden light make the portrait special.
Q3630743.i: Think of one question you would ask Rembrandt.

f: Find the dark barge on the river.
Find the tiny lights on the far bank and the small boat with a fisherman.

m.q: What is the mood of this night on the river?
o: Noisy and merry, like a ball
m.w: Blue mist wraps the river and everything is still. It feels as if you can hear only the splash of water.

x.q: Where does the word 'nocturne' come from?
o: From music: a quiet night piece
From the theatre: a late-night show
From astronomy: a name for night stars
x.w: A nocturne is a calm musical piece for the night. Whistler decided to give this name to his night pictures.

Q720602.s: Whistler often painted evening scenes from memory, back in his studio. He wanted to capture the mood, not exact details.
Q720602.i: Invent a melody that floats over the river.

f: Find Mary with the baby on the throne.
Find the painted patterned carpet in front of the throne.

m.q: What is the mood of this gathering of saints?
o: Cross, as if they had quarrelled
m.w: The saints stand and kneel quietly, and gold and bright colours make it festive.

x.q: Who was Fra Angelico?
o: A sailor who drew sea maps
x.w: Fra Angelico was a monk and an artist. He was called 'angelic' because his colours are so soft and pure.

Q1215809.s: Fra Angelico loved bright pure colours and gold. He also painted the cells of the San Marco monastery.
Q1215809.i: Imagine what Mary tells the baby.

f: Find the golden halos above their heads and the thin, see-through veil.
See how gently the mother holds the baby.

m.q: What is Mary like as she holds the baby?
m.w: Her head is bowed and her gaze is soft. She holds the baby carefully and seems to be thinking of him.

x.q: What is Mary holding in her hands?
x.w: Mary is reading a book: this is how painters showed her wisdom. The baby is beside her, and they are together.

Q2269585.s: Botticelli loved thin, flowing lines, so his figures look light and almost dancing. His most famous painting is 'The Birth of Venus'.
Q2269585.i: Imagine what is written in the book.

f: Find Mary holding the baby on her lap.
Find the soft light on the faces of Mary and the baby.

m.q: What is Mary like with the baby on her lap?
m.w: She looks tenderly and holds the baby carefully. Her face is soft and quiet.

x.q: How did Raphael arrange Mary and the baby?
o: In a triangle, like a low hill
x.w: Together the figures look like a triangle. This arrangement makes the picture calm and steady.

Q2607065.s: Raphael painted many pictures of Mary and the baby, and each came out new. He was famous for tender, calm faces.
Q2607065.i: Imagine what the baby says to his mother.

f: Find the tree trunk and the branches curving like a web.
Look at the pale grey background behind.

m.q: What is the mood of this grey tree?
o: Quiet and serious, in grey tones
m.w: Grey and dark lines on a pale background create a calm and slightly sad mood.

x.q: What did Mondrian do with the tree?
o: Painted it exactly like a photograph
Turned it into a pattern of lines
Painted only the leaves, no branches
x.w: He drew the tree in thin lines, almost like a pattern. So the tree became almost abstract.

Q5598238.s: Mondrian painted the same kind of tree many times, until it became almost a pattern. Later he painted only straight lines and squares of red, yellow and blue.
Q5598238.i: Imagine what bird will land on these branches.

f: Find Mary's face: it is gentle and calm.
Find the baby and see how his mother holds him.

m.q: What is Mary like in Bellini's picture?
m.w: Her gaze is lowered and her face is soft. She seems to be thinking of the baby.

x.q: What is Bellini famous for?
x.w: The Venetian Giovanni Bellini painted soft golden light and warm colours. His pictures feel very calm.

Q3842705.s: Bellini was the teacher of two great painters, Giorgione and Titian. He painted Mary and the baby many times, and each picture is different.
Q3842705.i: Imagine what mother and baby are quietly saying.

f: Find the blue shadows on the snow.
Find sunlight on the wall of the house and the bare trees.

m.q: What is the mood of this March day?
o: Gloomy and cold, like deep midwinter
Joyful, snow melts, spring is near
m.w: The sun is bright, the snow is already melting and the sky is blue. You can feel the first warmth.

x.q: How did Levitan show that the snow is melting and spring has come?
o: He painted flowers on the snow
x.w: In March the sun already warms, but snow still lies. Levitan showed this with blue shadows on the snow and warm light.

Q4282465.s: Levitan is called a master of the 'landscape of mood': his pictures express feelings. His close friend was the writer Anton Chekhov.
Q4282465.i: Imagine what sounds you hear on this March day: dripping, birds or wind?

f: Find the bright yellow and orange aspens.
Find the winding blue river and the light clouds in the sky.

m.q: What is the mood of this golden autumn?
o: Warm and calm, like a goodbye
Uneasy, as if a storm will break
m.w: Golden trees glow in the sun and the river is quiet. Autumn is hushed and a little wistful.

x.q: Which colours in the picture make each other stronger?
o: A grey sky and brown ground
Golden trees and the blue river
x.w: Yellow and orange beside blue look even brighter. That is why the autumn in the picture shines.

Q4193277.s: 'Golden Autumn' is one of Isaac Levitan's best-known paintings. He loved Russian nature and could capture its mood.
Q4193277.i: Imagine what the leaves on the aspens whisper about.

f: Find the tall pole with a serpent on top.
Find the people reaching out and looking up.

m.q: What do the people by the pole feel?
o: Fear and hope, they beg for help
Boredom, nothing to do all day
m.w: The people are exhausted and reach towards the pole. They look up because they hope for help.

x.q: According to the legend, what did people have to do to get well?
o: Drink a bitter medicine from herbs
Go up into the mountains to rest
Look at the bronze snake on the pole
x.w: In the legend Moses raised a bronze serpent on a pole. Those who looked at it with faith got well.

Q20829114.s: Fyodor Bruni painted this huge picture for many years. He studied in Italy and painted strictly, with attention to every figure.
Q20829114.i: Imagine what the people feel once they get better.

f: Find Jesus: he speaks calmly to the crowd.
Find the woman who was brought to Jesus.

m.q: What does the woman who was brought to Jesus feel?
o: Joy, she has come to a festival
Boredom, none of it interests her
Fear and shame, but she is defended
m.w: She stands with her head lowered and waits for a decision. Jesus speaks up for her.

x.q: What did Jesus say to the people who wanted to condemn her?
o: Let the sinless throw the first stone
Let every one of you go away now
Bring me some water, I am thirsty
x.w: In this way Jesus reminded them that nobody is perfect. The people were embarrassed and left, one by one.

Q26781788.s: Polenov travelled to Egypt, Syria and Palestine to paint on the spot. That is why the buildings, light and clothes in the picture look real.
Q26781788.i: Imagine what the people thought when they heard these words.

f: Find the angels bending close.
Find the stone tomb.

m.q: What do the people and angels feel?
m.w: Everyone bends down and speaks softly. You can see they are saying goodbye to someone very dear.

x.q: What moment is shown in the picture?
o: The birth of Jesus in a cosy stable
Loved ones lay Jesus in a tomb
A festive dinner with his friends
x.w: This is the entombment: loved ones gently lay Jesus in a stone tomb. The picture is called the 'Deposition'.

Q17390181.s: Tiepolo was a Venetian master of light, airy colours and big angels on clouds. He loved painting the ceilings of palaces and churches.
Q17390181.i: Imagine what one of the angels whispers.

f: Find the lightest, warmest place in the picture: where does the warmth come from?
Look at the colours: which of them speak of warmth?

m.q: What is the mood of a picture with this title?
o: Warm and calm, like a sunny day
Noisy, like a circus or a fair
m.w: The title speaks of a warm land where the sun shines. So the mood of the picture is soft and warm.

x.q: Who were the 'Wanderers', the group Yaroshenko belonged to?
o: Wandering traders with cloth and ribbons
Boatmen who carried people along rivers
Painters who took shows to many cities
x.w: The Wanderers held exhibitions not only in the capitals but also in other towns. That way all kinds of people saw their pictures.

Q84723020.s: Nikolai Yaroshenko was a soldier who rose to the rank of major general, but he painted all his life. He was one of the leading Wanderers.
Q84723020.i: Imagine where this warm land is and who lives there.

f: Find Mary: she holds the baby with great care.
See how closely the people stand, shoulder to shoulder in one row.

m.q: What is the mood among the people around the baby?
m.w: The faces are calm and thoughtful. Nobody is laughing or shouting, as if something important is happening.

x.q: Where have the parents brought baby Jesus in this painting?
o: To the doctor for a check-up
To the temple, to thank God
To visit family in a village
x.w: By custom, parents brought a baby to the temple forty days after the birth. They thanked God for their child.

Q3910910.s: Bellini painted people large, down to the waist, right at the edge of the picture. It feels as if you could talk to them.
Q3910910.i: Imagine what Mary whispers to the baby in the temple.

f: Find the man's face: Titian lit it so that your eyes go straight to it.
Look into his eyes: where is he looking?

m.q: How does this man seem?
m.w: He looks steadily and seriously, with no smile. He seems to be thinking about something.

x.q: In which city did Titian live and work?
o: In Rome, the city of seven hills
In Paris, the city by the Seine
In Venice, the city on the water
x.w: Venice stands in a lagoon, and its painters were famous for colour and soft light. Titian was the most famous of them.

Q3937410.s: Titian painted portraits so that people look alive. Rich people all over Europe asked him to paint their faces.
Q3937410.i: Give this man a name and say what he does for a living.

f: Find Mary: she is the biggest figure in the picture.
Find the people standing under her wide cloak.

m.q: What does Mary feel towards the people under her cloak?
m.w: She has opened her cloak over the people, and her face is calm and gentle. She seems ready to protect everyone.

x.q: Why does Mary open her cloak in pictures like this?
o: To show off her beautiful cloak
To keep herself warm in the cold
x.w: In pictures of the Madonna of Mercy, the cloak is like a big house. People who need help shelter under it.

Q5965524.s: El Greco painted tall, stretched-out figures, like flickering flames. That is why his pictures feel full of movement.
Q5965524.i: Imagine what help the people under the cloak are asking for.

f: Find the angels: there are very many, and they seem to swirl round.
Find the brightest spot: it looks as if a glow pours out of it.

m.q: What do the angels and people in this picture feel?
m.w: The figures swirl in shining light, like a huge round dance. It is a celebration in heaven.

x.q: How big is this painting?
o: The size of a dining table
The size of a big double door
A whole wall of a great hall
x.w: The painting is about twenty-two metres wide. Tintoretto painted it with helpers, because one person could not cover such a wall.

Q5996597.s: This is one of the biggest oil paintings in the world. It hangs in the Doge's Palace in Venice.
Q5996597.i: Imagine what song the angels sing in this shining round dance.

f: Find the shining armour: see how the light slides over the metal.
Look at Cosimo's face: is he smiling?

m.q: How does Cosimo want to look?
m.w: He looks stern and does not smile, and he wears armour. That is how a ruler looks who fears nothing.

x.q: Why did Cosimo have himself painted in armour?
o: To show he was a strong ruler
He had just come back from hunting
He had been given shiny new armour
x.w: Cosimo was the Duke of Florence. The armour told everyone he could defend his city.

Q3625842.s: Bronzino painted so smoothly and sharply that faces look like porcelain. His people are always calm and hide their feelings.
Q3625842.i: Imagine what order the duke gives once the portrait is finished.

f: Find the two people: they stand very close to each other.
Look at the faces and necks: how long and stretched they are.

m.q: What do these two feel for each other?
m.w: They stand very close together. It seems they feel calm and happy being together.

x.q: Who was Jacques Lipchitz, one of the people in the picture?
o: A doctor who cared for the painter
A cook in the painter's house
x.w: Jacques Lipchitz made sculptures and was Modigliani's friend. The couple ordered this portrait after their wedding.

Q3806044.s: Modigliani painted long faces, long necks and narrow, almond-shaped eyes. He liked African masks.
Q3806044.i: Imagine what these two talked about while the painter was painting them.

f: Find the bride: what is her face like?
Find the groom: he is much older than the bride.

m.q: How does the bride feel during the wedding ceremony?
m.w: She has lowered her head, and her face is pale and sad. You can see she is not happy at all.

x.q: What does the title The Unequal Marriage mean?
o: She is much younger than he is
They arrived late for the wedding
x.w: The bride is very young, and the groom is old and rich. The painter wanted to show that marrying a girl off like this is unfair.

Q3918079.s: Everyone in Russia knew this picture: people argued about it and wrote about it in the papers. It showed life as it really was.
Q3918079.i: Imagine what the bride will say when she is alone.

f: Find Saint George: see how his armour shines.
Find the garland of leaves and the dragon beside George.

m.q: What does George feel after his victory?
m.w: He stands straight and looks calm, while the dragon lies beside him. George is not afraid of anything.

x.q: How did Mantegna show that George is a saint?
o: He put a golden crown on him
A glowing halo above his head
He painted wings on his back
x.w: A thin golden ring over the head is called a halo. In paintings it marks a saint.

Q3947210.s: Mantegna painted figures as if carved from stone: hard and sharp, down to every fold. He loved the art of ancient Rome.
Q3947210.i: Imagine what George tells the people about his victory.

f: Find the orange trees: what colour are their leaves?
Look for where the sun falls in the picture and where the shade is.

m.q: What is the mood of this corner of the garden?
m.w: Sun, greenery and warm colours make a calm day. You do not want to hurry anywhere here.

x.q: How did Caillebotte help his painter friends?
x.w: Caillebotte was rich and bought paintings by Monet, Renoir and other friends. Thanks to him, work was easier for them.

Q4067988.s: Caillebotte loved to paint gardens, boats and the city. He left his collection of his friends' paintings to France.
Q4067988.i: Imagine what people do in a garden like this on a hot summer day.

f: Find the black dress with the fur collar.
Look at Christina's face: how lifelike it is.

m.q: What is Christina's mood?
m.w: She looks straight out without a smile, and her face is quiet. She carries herself with dignity.

x.q: Why is Christina dressed in black?
o: She just liked the colour black
Black was the usual ball colour
x.w: Christina was sixteen, but she was already a widow. The black dress was a sign of mourning.

Q4373334.s: Holbein made a sketch of her in just three hours. Later he used it to paint the big portrait.
Q4373334.i: Imagine what Christina would answer if she got a letter from the King of England.

f: Find the girl's thick, red-gold hair.
Find the violin in her hands.

m.q: What does the girl seem to be thinking about?
o: About what to have for lunch
About music she is listening to
m.w: Her look is dreamy, as if she is listening to music. That makes the picture feel quiet.

x.q: Who was Alexa Wilding, the woman shown here?
o: A famous singer of a grand theatre
A music teacher from next door
A model who posed for the painter
x.w: A model sits in front of the painter while he works. Alexa posed for Rossetti in many paintings.

Q5015478.s: Rossetti and his friends called themselves the Pre-Raphaelites. They loved pure, bright colours and tiny details, like in old paintings.
Q5015478.i: Imagine the tune the girl is playing: a fast one or a slow one?

f: Find baby Mary: women are bustling around her.
Find the angels at the top, in the golden light.

m.q: What is the mood in this room?
m.w: The women lean over the baby and handle her gently. Warm golden light pours down from above.

x.q: Whose birthday does this painting show?
x.w: Mary later became the mother of Jesus. Here she has just been born herself, and everyone cares for her.

Q5792618.s: Murillo lived in Seville and painted children and angels tenderly, in warm golden light. People loved his pictures for their kindness.
Q5792618.i: Make up a lullaby for baby Mary.

f: Find the lamb beside John.
Find the river and the trees around: it is a wild, empty place.

m.q: How does John feel in the wilderness?
m.w: He looks strong and calm, and all around is quiet. He is not afraid to be alone with nature.

x.q: Why is there a lamb next to John?
o: The lamb is his favourite pet
The lamb reminds us of Jesus
x.w: John called Jesus the Lamb of God. That is why paintings put a lamb next to him.

Q7401482.s: Titian painted nature as seriously as people. His sky, trees and river glow with warm colours.
Q7401482.i: Imagine what John tells the lamb.

f: Find the woman among the greenery.
Find the patches of sunlight: where do they lie?

m.q: What is the mood of this spring day?
m.w: There is a lot of light, fresh green and flowers. Everything feels calm and gentle.

x.q: How did Monet show the play of light?
o: With one smooth coat of paint
x.w: He put small patches of light and shade side by side. From far away they shimmer, like sun through leaves.

Q7581196.s: The word Impressionism comes from Monet's painting Impression, Sunrise. He wanted to catch a moment, like a quick snapshot.
Q7581196.i: Imagine what song is playing in this garden in spring.

f: Find the young man: we see him from behind.
Look out of the window: what can you see in the street?

m.q: What is the young man thinking about?
o: He is nervously waiting for a friend
He wants to run out and dance
He is calmly watching the street
m.w: He stands still and looks at the street. We cannot see his face, but his pose is calm and thoughtful.

x.q: Why do we see the young man from behind?
o: The painter did not finish his face
So we look at the street with him
He is shy and turned away
x.w: We stand at his shoulder and see the city through his eyes. That is how the picture invites us into the room.

Q8058274.s: Caillebotte loved unusual points of view, like a photographer: from above, from behind, from a window. He painted modern Paris.
Q8058274.i: Imagine what the young man sees in the street and what he dreams about.

f: Find Mary: she is embroidering a flower.
Find Anne, Mary's mother: she sits close by.

m.q: How is the day going for Mary and Anne?
o: Quiet and calm, they are busy
m.w: Mary and Anne bend over their work, and nobody hurries. The light is soft and the room is quiet.

x.q: Why is there a lily in the picture?
o: A white lily is a sign of purity
The lily just decorates the room
The lily is a gift from neighbours
x.w: A white lily has long been a sign of purity and kindness. That is why it is often painted near Mary.

Q9248672.s: Rossetti painted this picture when he was very young, about twenty. He and his friends wanted to paint honestly, with bright colours and tiny details.
Q9248672.i: Imagine what Anne is teaching Mary.

f: Find the pine trees: some are sharp, others hardly visible.
Find the empty space in the picture: that is the fog.

m.q: What is the mood of this picture?
m.w: The trees sink into the fog, and all is silent. It feels as if you can hear only the breathing of the forest.

x.q: What is this picture painted with?
x.w: Tohaku used only ink, dark and pale. By thinning it with water he got shades of grey, like fog.

Q11531476.s: The empty space in this picture tells a story too: it becomes the fog. In Japan these screens are a national treasure.
Q11531476.i: Imagine who lives in the fog behind the pines.

f: Find the candle: almost all the light comes from it.
Find Jesus among the people around the table.

m.q: What is the atmosphere of this night scene?
m.w: Candlelight picks the faces out of the dark, and thick shadow lies all around. Everyone is serious, as if something important is being decided.

x.q: Where does the light in this picture come from?
o: From the sun through a big window
From a torch on the wall
x.w: The candle lights the faces, and everything else sinks into shadow. This makes you look where it matters most.

Q11690349.s: Honthorst learned in Italy to paint night scenes lit by candles. The Italians nicknamed him Gerard of the Nights.
Q11690349.i: Imagine what the people in the shadows whisper to each other.

f: Find the bride in the green dress: she is lifting her veil.
Find the bridesmaids and the boy with flowers.

m.q: What does the bride feel?
m.w: She holds her veil a little shyly, with friends and flowers all around her. You can see this day is special for her.

x.q: What celebration does this picture show?
x.w: The bride in the green dress walks along, and her bridesmaids walk beside her. The picture is about love and a wedding day.

Q16275077.s: Rossetti packed the picture so full of faces and bright colours that hardly any space is left. It looks like a fancy bouquet.
Q16275077.i: Imagine what the bride will say to the groom when she reaches him.

f: Find the little bird in the child's hand.
Find the little dog next to him.

m.q: What is the atmosphere in this family?
m.w: The grown-ups beside the child are calm, and he is busy playing. It is all simple and cosy.

x.q: How did Murillo show the Holy Family?
o: As a royal family in a palace
As travellers walking on a road
As an ordinary family at home
x.w: In the picture they play as in any family: a child, a bird and a dog. That is why it feels close and familiar.

Q16627776.s: Murillo lived in Seville and painted children and families very tenderly. His pictures were much loved in Spain.
Q16627776.i: Give the little bird a name and say what it chirps.

f: Find the two women: they walk along the beach arm in arm.
Look at the sky and the sea: what colour are they?

m.q: What do the women feel on this evening?
m.w: They walk slowly, side by side, with only the sea and sky around them. The evening seems to stand still.

x.q: What do we call the time after sunset when everything turns blue?
x.w: The blue hour comes after sunset. The sky and sea become almost the same blue. Krøyer loved to paint it.

Q18085208.s: Krøyer lived in Skagen, at the very north of Denmark. In summer the evenings there are long and light, and painters painted them on the beach.
Q18085208.i: Imagine what the two friends are quietly talking about on their walk.

f: Find the stars in the dark sky.
Find the sea: where does it meet the sky?

m.q: What kind of night is in this picture?
m.w: Dark blues and a few tiny stars make it hush. It feels as if everything around is asleep or listening.

x.q: What colour did Munch make the sky and the sea?
x.w: Blue and dark blue are the colours of night by the sea. The stars glow on it like small lights.

Q18209775.s: Munch is famous for The Scream, but he also painted quiet night landscapes by the sea. In summer he lived in the small town of Åsgårdstrand on the fjord.
Q18209775.i: Imagine what the stars whisper to the sea.

f: Find the couple on the shore: they are the painter himself and his wife Marie.
Find the dog beside them and the sailing ship at sea.

m.q: How is this evening walk going?
m.w: The husband and wife walk side by side without hurrying, and the dog goes with them. Moonlight makes the evening soft and quiet.

x.q: Where does the soft silvery light in this picture come from?
o: From the moon over the sea
From a lantern on a boat
From a fire on the beach
x.w: It is moonlight: silvery, with soft shadows. Pictures of the night with this kind of light are called nocturnes.

Q18386245.s: Krøyer painted himself in the picture with his wife. He was one of the Skagen painters who gathered by the sea in Denmark every summer.
Q18386245.i: Think of a name for the dog and say what it has sniffed out on the beach.

f: Find Madame de Pompadour: see how elegantly she is dressed.
Find the lightest, softest colours in the picture.

m.q: How does Madame de Pompadour want to look?
m.w: She sits upright, her face is calm and her dress is arranged beautifully. That is how a true lady of the court looks.

x.q: Who was Madame de Pompadour?
o: The wife of an English king
The head cook of the royal palace
x.w: She was a friend of King Louis XV and helped painters and writers. People admired her good taste.

Q18552705.s: Boucher was Pompadour's favourite painter. He painted in the Rococo style: light and gentle, with soft colours, like sweets.
Q18552705.i: Imagine what Pompadour would say if she invited you to tea.

f: Find the woman and the wallpaper behind her.
Find the warm colours that remind you of autumn.

m.q: What is the look on Méry Laurent's face?
m.w: She sits quietly, her look is soft, as if she is daydreaming a little. Nothing disturbs the peace.

x.q: Why is the picture called Autumn?
o: A woman here stands for autumn
It was painted late one October
It shows a forest in autumn
x.w: Manet wanted to paint the seasons as beautiful women. Méry Laurent posed for Autumn.

Q18625546.s: Manet painted this picture two years before he died. He painted quickly and freely, with broad strokes.
Q18625546.i: Imagine what autumn song this woman is humming.

f: Find the people in dark clothes: they are coming out of the church.
Find the little church and the path in front of it.

m.q: What is the mood of the people leaving church?
m.w: The people in dark clothes walk in silence, and the colours are grey and brown. It shows the quiet of a Sunday.

x.q: Whose church was it?
o: Van Gogh's father was the pastor
x.w: Van Gogh's father was a pastor in Nuenen. Vincent painted the church where his father served.

Q19833792.s: Later Van Gogh painted in bright colours. But in Nuenen his colours were dark and earthy, like village life itself.
Q19833792.i: Imagine what the people are quietly saying on their way home.

f: Find the girl with the parasol.
Find the girl with the basket, the cows and the dog.

m.q: What feeling comes from this village stroll?
m.w: The young ladies walk without hurry, the cows graze, and all is peaceful. Nobody is rushing anywhere.

x.q: Who are the young ladies Courbet painted?
x.w: Courbet painted his sisters on a walk in his home village of Ornans. He painted ordinary people, not kings.

Q19911495.s: Courbet believed you should paint only what you see: people, cows, a village. This kind of painting was called Realism.
Q19911495.i: Imagine what the young ladies said to the girl with the basket.

f: Find Hercules: see how he braces himself and pushes the rocks apart.
Find the two mountains on the sides: now there is sea between them.

m.q: What does Hercules feel at this moment?
m.w: His muscles are tense, and he pushes the rocks apart with all his might. His face is focused.

x.q: What did Hercules do, according to the legend?
o: He built a huge bridge over the sea
He pushed mountains apart for the sea
He fought a lion on a mountaintop
x.w: The Greeks told how Hercules pushed apart mountains at the edge of Europe and Africa. That made a strait, and the mountains were called the Pillars of Hercules.

Q24843240.s: Zurbarán often painted on a dark background, and light picked out the figures from the darkness. This painting was made for the royal palace in Madrid.
Q24843240.i: Imagine what Hercules says when the mountains move apart.

f: Find Washington's face: it is the most finished part.
Find the places where the canvas is almost bare: the picture is unfinished.

m.q: What look does Washington have on his face?
m.w: His lips are pressed together, and his gaze is steady and stern. That is how a man looks who is used to being responsible for others.

x.q: Where can you see this face today?
o: On a box of fine English tea
x.w: Stuart's portrait became the basis of the face on the US dollar bill. Millions of people see it every day.

Q28796116.s: Stuart never finished this painting. He kept it for himself and painted copies from it, which he sold.
Q28796116.i: Imagine what Washington would say if he could speak.

f: Find Maria's fine collar and jewellery.
Look at her face: how softly it is lit.

m.q: What can you say about Maria's mood?
o: She is tired and a bit bored
m.w: She looks straight out, gently, and her face is bright and clear. You can see calm confidence.

x.q: What does this portrait say about the Trip family?
x.w: The Trip family in the Netherlands traded in metals and was very rich. Maria's splendid dress shows it.

Q4373336.s: Rembrandt could paint light so that a face looks alive and warm. He lived in Amsterdam in the Golden Age of Dutch painting.
Q4373336.i: Imagine where Maria is going in such a splendid dress.

f: Find the white rabbit.
Find the shepherd with his flock far away and the sunset sky.

m.q: How is this evening going for Mary and the baby?
o: Gentle and calm, like a game
Tense, like just before a storm
m.w: Mary and the baby are playing with the rabbit. Soft evening light surrounds them, and all is calm.

x.q: What time of day did Titian show?
x.w: The sky is warm, as at sunset, and far away you can see a shepherd with his flock. That makes the picture soft and cosy.

Q24249.s: Titian was a master of colour: his reds, blues and golds glow. Venetians loved him for his warm light and lively colours.
Q24249.i: Give the rabbit a name and say what it thinks about the baby.

f: Find the remains of the ancient bridge: what is left of it?
Find the river below and the mountains far away.

m.q: What is the mood of this landscape?
m.w: Soft light, a calm river, wide open space. Nothing here is in a hurry.

x.q: How old is the bridge Corot painted?
x.w: The Romans built the bridge under Emperor Augustus, so it is called the Bridge of Augustus. It is more than two thousand years old.

Q24283.s: Corot liked to paint out in nature, under the open sky. That way he caught real light, and the Impressionists learned a lot from him.
Q24283.i: Imagine who once walked across this bridge and where they were going.

f: Find the painter's father and mother: they sit side by side.
Find the woven basket.

m.q: How do Manet's parents look?
m.w: They sit upright and look serious. They seem strict and respected people.

x.q: What was Manet's father by profession?
o: A doctor in a big hospital
A captain of a trading ship
x.w: Auguste Manet was a judge, an important official. He wanted his son to be a lawyer, not a painter.

Q126467.s: Manet painted Parisians and his own family without flattery. He loved black and bright patches of light, and for his time he was very bold.
Q126467.i: Imagine what Manet's mother is thinking while the painter paints the portrait.

f: Find the toy Noah's Ark.
Find the olive branch and the big dog: an Irish wolfhound.

m.q: What do the parents and the girls feel?
m.w: Everyone is together, the girls are playing, and the grown-ups look calm. The hard time is behind them.

x.q: What does the title Peace Concluded mean?
o: The war was over, peace had come
The family moved to a new house
Neighbours made up after a quarrel
x.w: In 1856 the Crimean War ended. The picture shows a family glad that the trouble is over.

Q266435.s: The olive branch has long been a sign of peace. Millais hid peace in small things: the Ark also tells of the end of trouble.
Q266435.i: Imagine what game the girls are playing with the toy Ark.

f: Find the dove: it has an olive twig in its beak.
Find the girl who is kissing the dove.

m.q: What do the girls feel when the dove has come back?
m.w: One girl kisses the dove, and the other holds it gently. The dove has returned, so the water is going down.

x.q: What does the twig in the dove's beak mean?
o: That the dove found a nest
That the water is going down
x.w: Noah sent out the dove to find out if there was dry land. The twig says: trees are growing again!

Q465894.s: Millais painted every straw and every strand of hair so carefully, as if looking through a magnifying glass. The Pre-Raphaelites loved small details.
Q465894.i: Imagine what the dove would tell about where it flew.

f: Find Goethe: he is resting in a wide hat and cloak.
Find the ruins and the broken piece of a column beside him.

m.q: How does Goethe feel?
o: He is in a great hurry
m.w: He sits at ease, looks into the distance and hurries nowhere. Around him are beautiful ruins and quiet.

x.q: Why did Goethe come to Italy?
o: To take a job with a king
To sell his books to the rich
x.w: Goethe was a poet and dreamed of seeing ancient Rome and Italian art. Later he wrote a book about it.

Q481447.s: This is the most famous portrait of Goethe. Tischbein painted it in Rome, where the friends lived together.
Q481447.i: Imagine what poem Goethe is composing as he looks at the ruins.

f: Find the biggest iceberg: what colour is it?
Find the tiny broken mast at the bottom of the picture.

m.q: How do the mountains of ice seem?
m.w: Blue and white ice, cold light and silence. The icebergs seem huge and solemn.

x.q: Why did the painter paint a tiny mast?
o: Just to make the picture prettier
To show how huge the icebergs are
To show that a steamship passed by
x.w: Next to the small mast you can see how enormous the ice is. It is lonely, which makes the ice look even bigger.

Q575573.s: Church sailed north to see real icebergs, and made many sketches. Later the painting was shown to the public as a great spectacle.
Q575573.i: Imagine how the icebergs talk to each other at night.

f: Find the tall wooden bridge.
Find the golden sparks far away: that is fireworks.

m.q: What do you feel looking at the river at night?
o: The heat of the midday sun
m.w: Blue mist and dark outlines make everything soft and quiet. Only the golden lights sparkle a little.

x.q: What did Whistler take from Japanese pictures?
x.w: He loved Japanese prints, which have few details and much air. That is why the bridge is just a dark silhouette.

Q589002.s: Whistler called the picture a nocturne, like a piece of music about the night. He wanted colours to sound like music.
Q589002.i: Imagine the tune you can hear on this river at night.

f: Find Sebastián: he sits right on the floor.
Look into his eyes: where is he looking?

m.q: What can you feel in Sebastián's gaze?
o: He is about to laugh at us
m.w: He looks straight out, seriously, and holds himself proudly. Velázquez showed him not as funny but as a strong, important man.

x.q: What was Sebastián's job at court?
o: A jester who amused the prince
A general in the royal army
A cook in the royal kitchen
x.w: Jesters made kings and princes laugh. Sebastián served Prince Baltasar Carlos, the king's son.

Q729194.s: Velázquez painted court jesters with respect and dignity. That was unusual: more often people just laughed at them.
Q729194.i: Imagine what joke Sebastián told the prince.

f: Find the little prince: he is only two years old.
Find the little dog on the chair beside him.

m.q: What is the look on the little boy's face?
m.w: The little boy stands straight and looks seriously, like a grown-up. His face is quiet and a little sad.

x.q: Why was the little prince hung with charms?
x.w: The boy was dear to the whole family, and they wanted to keep him from illness. The charms were thought to protect him.

Q3225899.s: Velázquez painted with quick, soft strokes. From far away you see the shimmer of cloth, but close up only patches of paint.
Q3225899.i: Imagine what the dog is called and what it is waiting for.

f: Find the angel Gabriel: he has wings.
Find Mary with her book and the little garden outside the window.

m.q: How does Mary greet the angel?
o: She is frightened and wants to run
She laughs and claps her hands
m.w: Mary listens to the angel closely and quietly. Nobody shouts or hurries.

x.q: What news did Gabriel bring?
o: That Mary would have a son, Jesus
That a festival was coming to town
That guests would soon visit her
x.w: The word Annunciation means good news. Gabriel told Mary she would have a son, Jesus.

Q1114806.s: Botticelli loved flowing lines, light clothes and delicate faces. His figures seem to dance, even when they stand still.
Q1114806.i: Imagine what the angel whispers to Mary as he comes into the room.

f: Find Mary: how gently does she hold the baby?
Find the brightest spot: that is where the light falls.

m.q: What does Mary feel for the baby?
m.w: She bends towards the baby and holds him gently. The light makes them warm and close.

x.q: What did Artemisia learn from Caravaggio?
o: To paint only bunches of flowers
To paint strong light and shadows
To paint everything in one blue
x.w: Her light falls like a spotlight in a dark room. That makes the figures look solid and alive.

Q3842443.s: Artemisia Gentileschi was one of the first famous women painters in Italy. She became famous when it was hard for women to become painters.
Q3842443.i: Make up a lullaby that Mary sings to the baby.

f: Find Mary and the baby Jesus.
Look at their faces: how soft and beautiful they are.

m.q: What is the mood of this group of people?
m.w: The faces are soft and kind, and nobody hurries. They are all close together, which feels peaceful.

x.q: What shape did Raphael build out of the people?
o: A circle, like a big round sun
A square, like a tall window
x.w: Heads and bodies form a triangle. This shape makes the picture calm and steady.

Q3842605.s: Raphael lived only thirty-seven years, but became one of the best-loved painters in the world. You can recognise his Madonnas by their soft, kind faces.
Q3842605.i: Imagine what the baby wants to say to his mum.

f: Find Mary and the baby Jesus.
Look at the faces: how serious and calm they are.

m.q: What is Mary's face like?
m.w: She looks calmly, without a smile. That is how faces were painted on old icons too.

x.q: Why is this painting called the Greek Madonna?
o: A Greek girl posed for it
It was found on a Greek island
x.w: Bellini painted it on the model of Byzantine, Greek icons that were brought to Venice. That is why the faces are so grave and calm.

Q3842748.s: In Venice Bellini worked with many young painters. They say even Titian learned from him.
Q3842748.i: Imagine what Mary is thinking as she looks at the baby.

f: Find the untied laces.
Find the scuffs on the old leather.

m.q: What do you feel looking at these boots?
o: The joy of a festive ball
The tiredness of a long road
m.w: The leather is scuffed and creased, so the boots have walked a lot. They look as tired as their owner.

x.q: Why did Van Gogh paint his own boots?
o: He needed a drawing for a lesson
He saw character in old things
x.w: For Van Gogh ordinary things mattered. In old boots he saw a whole story, like in a person's face.

Q956738.s: Van Gogh painted boots several times. For him even an old thing could be the hero of a picture.
Q956738.i: Imagine where these boots walked and what they saw.

f: Find the table: how many people sit at it?
Look at the friends' faces around the table: are they serious or laughing?

m.q: How do the friends listen to Jesus at the table?
m.w: The friends sit close and listen, and nobody jokes. The talk is important.

x.q: What is the Last Supper?
o: A harvest feast in the fields
A wedding feast at a friend's house
x.w: It is the last meal Jesus shared with his twelve disciples. He broke bread and said important words to them.

Q3208041.s: El Greco was born on the island of Crete, studied in Venice and then lived in Spain. Later he painted stretched-out figures and unusual colours.
Q3208041.i: Imagine what the disciples whispered around the table.

f: Find the hat with the wide brim.
Look Rubens in the eyes: he looks straight at us.

m.q: How does Rubens want to look?
m.w: He holds himself straight and looks straight at us. That is how a man looks who respects himself.

x.q: Besides being a painter, what else was Rubens?
o: A captain of a big ship
A doctor at the queen's court
x.w: He knew many languages and travelled on the errands of kings, helping them to agree on peace. That is why he is dressed like a nobleman in the portrait.

Q3630731.s: Rubens had a big workshop with helpers, and he made hundreds of paintings. He loved bright colours and soft, rounded shapes.
Q3630731.i: Imagine what Rubens will say if you walk into his studio.

f: Find the young soldier: look at his cap and clothes.
Look at how he stands: confident and proud?

m.q: How does the young man look?
m.w: He looks straight out, sure of himself. That is how a man looks who is proud of his duty.

x.q: Who is a halberdier?
o: A soldier with a halberd, a spear-axe
A musician with a long shiny trumpet
A cook with a huge wooden cooking spoon
x.w: A halberd is a weapon on a long pole with a small axe and a point. Halberdiers often guarded a town or a palace.

Q3607621.s: Pontormo lived in Florence and loved long, stretched figures and pure bright colours. This style is called Mannerism.
Q3607621.i: Imagine what this young man is guarding and who his friends are.

f: Find the musicians with wind instruments on the platform.
Find the gas lamps up above: they light the stage.

m.q: What is the atmosphere at this circus before the show?
m.w: The people stand still, and the light is yellow and dim. It seems everyone froze before the show.

x.q: What did Seurat paint this picture with?
o: Broad strokes of a palette knife
x.w: Seurat put tiny dots of different colours side by side. The eye mixes them, and the picture shimmers.

Q3823444.s: This way of painting is called pointillism. Seurat developed it, and first studied the science of colour for a long time.
Q3823444.i: Imagine what wonder the performers will show when the show begins.

f: Find the red cherubs around Mary.
Find Mary and the baby she is holding.

m.q: How does Mary seem in this picture?
m.w: Her face is soft and serious, and her hands hold the baby gently.

x.q: Who are the cherubim?
x.w: Cherubim are often painted as little heads with wings. Bellini made them red.

Q3842596.s: Bellini painted Madonnas large, down to the waist, so they are very close to us. Their faces are quiet and kind.
Q3842596.i: Think of names for the red cherubs and say what they sing about.

f: Find the roses on the trellis behind Mary.
Find Mary and the baby: they are sitting in the garden.

m.q: What is the mood of this garden?
m.w: Soft colours, roses and calm faces. It is like a quiet garden on a warm day.

x.q: What do roses mean in pictures of Mary?
o: That bees live in the garden
A sign of love and beauty
That it is a hot summer
x.w: Roses have long been a sign of love and beauty. That is why Mary is often painted in a rose garden.

Q3842633.s: Luini worked in Milan, where Leonardo da Vinci lived, and learned a lot from him. That is why his faces are soft, with delicate shadows.
Q3842633.i: Imagine what these roses smell like and what Mary tells the baby.

f: Find the crowd of people: where are they going?
Look at the faces: how pale they are, with big eyes.

m.q: What do these people feel?
o: Worry and loneliness in a crowd
The joy of a festive stroll
m.w: The faces are pale, the eyes are big, and everyone walks in silence. Each person seems to be alone, though they are close.

x.q: What street is shown in the picture?
x.w: Karl Johan street is the most famous street in Oslo, which was then called Kristiania. People loved to stroll there in the evening.

Q3955717.s: Munch painted not only what he saw, but feelings. That is why the faces are so unusual and frozen, like masks.
Q3955717.i: Imagine what each person in this crowd is thinking.

f: Find Mary and the baby Jesus.
Find the other boy: that is little John.

m.q: What can you feel in this group of relatives?
m.w: Mary, Elizabeth and the little ones sit close together. That is how family usually sits.

x.q: Who is little John?
o: An angel sent down from heaven
x.w: John's mother, Elizabeth, was Mary's relative. So the little boys were family too.

Q538243.s: Raphael worked with pupils: his workshop had helpers who painted part of a picture. This one was made together too.
Q538243.i: Imagine what the two little boys, Jesus and John, are playing.

f: Find the people carrying flowers up the marble steps.
Find the brightest flowers and the brightest clothes.

m.q: What is the mood of this festival?
m.w: The people go along together with flowers, the clothes are bright, and the marble is white like spring. It is a celebration.

x.q: From what time is this scene?
o: From the time of knights and castles
From the age of the first trains
From ancient Rome, long, long ago
x.w: The painter showed a festival in ancient Rome. He studied real ruins and finds so that everything would look true.

Q732011.s: Alma-Tadema painted marble so exactly that you feel you could touch it. He showed the ancient world as if he had been there himself.
Q732011.i: Imagine what song the people in this procession are singing.

f: Find the princess: she leads the dragon on her belt, like a leash.
Find the knight on the white horse.

m.q: What is the princess like in this picture?
m.w: She stands straight and holds the dragon on a leash. You can see she trusts the knight.

x.q: What was Uccello most fascinated by?
x.w: Uccello learned to paint so that things seem to go off into the distance. He loved lines that lead the eye deep into the picture.

Q780466.s: Uccello painted like a fairy tale: clear lines, pretty patterns, a cloud shaped like a circle. The picture looks like a page from a storybook.
Q780466.i: Imagine how the princess made friends with the dragon.

f: Find Mary with the baby in her arms.
Find the fountain and the little garden behind her.

m.q: What is the mood of this little picture?
m.w: Mary stands calmly with the baby, and around her is a quiet, walled garden. All is peaceful.

x.q: How small do you think this painting is?
o: As big as a school blackboard
As big as our room's door
A little bigger than your palm
x.w: It is a tiny painting, only 19 by 12 centimetres. Van Eyck painted it in the tiniest detail.

Q838074.s: Van Eyck painted in oil paint in very thin layers, so cloth shines like silk. He is one of the first great masters of oil painting.
Q838074.i: Imagine what the water sings in this little fountain.
